```rust
/// Names the field whose parse refused a decoded value (LLR-7yu2xy).
/// postcard drops the message of an error raised inside `Deserialize`, so a
/// record with a fallible field is decoded as its `Raw…` mirror and parsed
/// here, field by field, instead.
pub(crate) fn parse_field<T, E: core::fmt::Display>(
    field: &'static str,
    parsed: Result<T, E>,
) -> Result<T, OrgNodeError> {
    parsed.map_err(|e| OrgNodeError::InvalidField { field, reason: e.to_string() })
}

/// Each of `raw`, parsed by `parse`, the first refusal naming `field`.
fn parse_each<R, T, E: core::fmt::Display>(
    field: &'static str,
    raw: Vec<R>,
    parse: impl Fn(R) -> Result<T, E>,
) -> Result<Vec<T>, OrgNodeError> {
    raw.into_iter().map(|value| parse_field(field, parse(value))).collect()
}

/// One to three distinct preferred Handles, each parsed (LLR-7yu2xy,
/// LLR-rjphn4): the count or a repeat is refused naming `count_field`, a
/// Handle that does not parse naming `handle_field`.
pub(crate) fn parse_preferred_handles(
    handle_field: &'static str,
    count_field: &'static str,
    raw: &[String],
) -> Result<Vec<Handle>, OrgNodeError> {
    let handles = raw.iter().map(|handle| parse_field(handle_field, Handle::parse(handle))).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
    check_preferred_handles(count_field, &handles)?;
    Ok(handles)
}

/// One to three pairwise distinct Handles, else `InvalidField` naming `field`.
pub(crate) fn check_preferred_handles(field: &'static str, handles: &[Handle]) -> Result<(), OrgNodeError> {
    if handles.is_empty() || handles.len() > 3 {
        return Err(OrgNodeError::InvalidField {
            field,
            reason: format!("expected one to three preferred handles, got {}", handles.len()),
        });
    }
    for (index, handle) in handles.iter().enumerate() {
        if handles[..index].contains(handle) {
            return Err(OrgNodeError::InvalidField { field, reason: "a preferred handle is repeated".to_owned() });
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// A Persona: the one identity a store holds, bound to at most one
/// Organisation for its life (LLR-pv2rdy, LLR-qqqg4b). The member seed is
/// crate-private and redacted under `Debug`; the record is not `Serialize`
/// outside test builds, and the store encodes it through
/// `PersonaRecordEncoding`. The record holds the Device public key, never the
/// Device seed.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct PersonaRecord {
    pub persona_id: PersonaId,
    pub org_id: Option<OrgId>,
    pub name: Name,
    pub surname: Surname,
    /// Set for a founder at founding, and on a first admission to the Handle
    /// the adopted record gives the Persona's MemberId; `None` for a
    /// provisional Member (LLR-pv2rdy).
    pub handle: Option<Handle>,
    pub(crate) member_seed: MemberSeed,
    pub device_key: DevicePublicKey,
    pub member_id: Option<MemberId>,
    pub status: PersonaStatus,
}

/// Every field of a `PersonaRecord`, public, for tests that build one
/// (test builds only).
#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
pub struct PersonaRecordParts {
    pub persona_id: PersonaId,
    pub org_id: Option<OrgId>,
    pub name: Name,
    pub surname: Surname,
    pub handle: Option<Handle>,
    pub member_seed: MemberSeed,
    pub device_key: DevicePublicKey,
    pub member_id: Option<MemberId>,
    pub status: PersonaStatus,
}

#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
impl From<PersonaRecordParts> for PersonaRecord {
    fn from(parts: PersonaRecordParts) -> Self {
        Self {
            persona_id: parts.persona_id,
            org_id: parts.org_id,
            name: parts.name,
            surname: parts.surname,
            handle: parts.handle,
            member_seed: parts.member_seed,
            device_key: parts.device_key,
            member_id: parts.member_id,
            status: parts.status,
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
impl PersonaRecord {
    /// The stored Member seed (test builds only).
    pub fn member_seed_for_test(&self) -> &MemberSeed {
        &self.member_seed
    }
}

/// A `PersonaRecord` as decoded, before parsing (LLR-7yu2xy).
#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct RawPersonaRecord {
    persona_id: PersonaId,
    org_id: Option<OrgId>,
    name: String,
    surname: String,
    handle: Option<String>,
    member_seed: MemberSeed,
    device_key: [u8; 32],
    member_id: Option<MemberId>,
    status: PersonaStatus,
}

impl TryFrom<RawPersonaRecord> for PersonaRecord {
    type Error = OrgNodeError;

    fn try_from(raw: RawPersonaRecord) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
        Ok(Self {
            persona_id: raw.persona_id,
            org_id: raw.org_id,
            name: parse_field("persona.name", Name::parse(&raw.name))?,
            surname: parse_field("persona.surname", Surname::parse(&raw.surname))?,
            handle: raw.handle.map(|handle| parse_field("persona.handle", Handle::parse(&handle))).transpose()?,
            member_seed: raw.member_seed,
            device_key: parse_field("persona.device_key", DevicePublicKey::parse(&raw.device_key))?,
            member_id: raw.member_id,
            status: raw.status,
        })
    }
}

/// A `PersonaRecord` decoded on its own goes through the same parse.
impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for PersonaRecord {
    fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        let raw = RawPersonaRecord::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        PersonaRecord::try_from(raw).map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum PersonaStatus {
    Proposed,
    Active,
    Revoked,
}

/// The current record of the Persona's Organisation (spec §4.3). The
/// Organisation private key is crate-private and the record is not
/// `Serialize` outside test builds; the store encodes it through
/// `OrgRecordEncoding`. It always holds the private key of the epoch it
/// adopted, and no earlier one (LLR-78jfrd).
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct OrgRecord {
    pub org_id: OrgId,
    pub root_hash: RootHash,
    pub org_pub_key: OrgPublicKey,
    pub epoch: Epoch,
    pub last_seq: SequenceNumber,
    pub trie_members: Vec<MemberSnapshot>,
    /// The proxy account recorded for a founding, held opaquely and only
    /// handed back (LLR-x5asbx); `None` on a record a first admission made.
    pub proxy_account: Option<ChainAccount>,
    /// The Organisation's X25519 private key, required, as its plain 32
    /// bytes with no option tag (LLR-78jfrd). Renders under `Debug` as its
    /// redacted secret type.
    pub(crate) org_private_key: OrgPrivateKey,
    /// The Change set the adopted epoch was reached by (LLR-p8vpgz).
    pub kept_change_set: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    /// The postcard `Vec<MemberSnapshot>` of the record the kept Change set
    /// extends (LLR-p8vpgz).
    pub kept_base_snapshot: Option<Vec<u8>>,
}

/// Every field of an `OrgRecord`, public, for tests that build one (test

#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]

    pub surname: Surname,
    pub member_key: PersonPublicKey,
    pub device_keys: Vec<DevicePublicKey>,
}

/// A `MemberSnapshot` as decoded, before parsing (LLR-7yu2xy).
#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct RawMemberSnapshot {
    id: MemberId,
    handle: String,
    name: String,
    surname: String,
    member_key: [u8; 32],
    device_keys: Vec<[u8; 32]>,
}

impl TryFrom<RawMemberSnapshot> for MemberSnapshot {
    type Error = OrgNodeError;

    fn try_from(raw: RawMemberSnapshot) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
        Ok(Self {
            id: raw.id,
            handle: parse_field("member.handle", Handle::parse(&raw.handle))?,
            name: parse_field("member.name", Name::parse(&raw.name))?,
            surname: parse_field("member.surname", Surname::parse(&raw.surname))?,
            member_key: parse_field("member.member_key", PersonPublicKey::parse(&raw.member_key))?,
            device_keys: parse_each("member.device_keys", raw.device_keys, |key| DevicePublicKey::parse(&key))?,
        })
    }
}

/// Each raw member snapshot, parsed (`member.*`).
pub(crate) fn parse_members(raw: Vec<RawMemberSnapshot>) -> Result<Vec<MemberSnapshot>, OrgNodeError> {
    raw.into_iter().map(MemberSnapshot::try_from).collect()
}

/// The bound on one Organisation's provisional changes, provisional
/// organisations and kept revocation notices in their stored form: 1 MiB
/// (LLR-m76r4k). A separate constant from `wire::MAX_MESSAGE`, so changing
/// one is a decision about the other.
pub const MAX_PROVISIONAL_BYTES: usize = 1 << 20;

/// An Admin's change, recorded and not yet calculated (LLR-b2hgd4): it
/// holds no Membership root, no Change set, no Sequence number and no key.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub enum ProvisionalChange {
    /// Admit the kept admission request for `invite_id` under `handle`.
    Admit { invite_id: InviteId, handle: Handle },
    /// Delete the member `member_id`.
    Revoke { member_id: MemberId },
}

/// A `ProvisionalChange` as decoded, before parsing.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub(crate) enum RawProvisionalChange {
    Admit { invite_id: InviteId, handle: String },
    Revoke { member_id: MemberId },
}

impl TryFrom<RawProvisionalChange> for ProvisionalChange {
    type Error = OrgNodeError;

    fn try_from(raw: RawProvisionalChange) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
        Ok(match raw {
            RawProvisionalChange::Admit { invite_id, handle } => {
                ProvisionalChange::Admit { invite_id, handle: parse_field("provisional.handle", Handle::parse(&handle))? }
            }
            RawProvisionalChange::Revoke { member_id } => ProvisionalChange::Revoke { member_id },
        })
    }
}

/// Where a provisional organisation came from (LLR-s3vq6d). Origin plays no
/// part in the match that adopts one (LLR-8528ud).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub enum Origin {
    Own,
    Received { from: DevicePublicKey },
    Answer { from: DevicePublicKey },
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub(crate) enum RawOrigin {
    Own,
    Received { from: [u8; 32] },
    Answer { from: [u8; 32] },
}

impl TryFrom<RawOrigin> for Origin {
    type Error = OrgNodeError;

    fn try_from(raw: RawOrigin) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
        let parse = |key: [u8; 32]| parse_field("provisional.origin", DevicePublicKey::parse(&key));
        Ok(match raw {
            RawOrigin::Own => Origin::Own,
            RawOrigin::Received { from } => Origin::Received { from: parse(from)? },
            RawOrigin::Answer { from } => Origin::Answer { from: parse(from)? },
        })
    }
}

/// One calculated next epoch, kept until verification adopts or drops it
/// (LLR-s3vq6d). Its identity is `(root, org_pub_key)`; `org_pub_key` is the
/// X25519 public half of `org_private_key`, which is crate-private
/// (LLR-qw8tyu). Not `Serialize` outside test builds.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ProvisionalOrganisation {
    pub epoch: Epoch,
    pub base_root: RootHash,
    pub members: Vec<MemberSnapshot>,
    pub root: RootHash,
    pub org_pub_key: OrgPublicKey,
    pub(crate) org_private_key: OrgPrivateKey,
    pub change_set: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    pub base_snapshot: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    pub origin: Origin,
    pub applied: Vec<ProvisionalChange>,
}

/// One Persona's view of one Organisation (LLR-d925uu), in encoding order:
/// the Persona, the current record, the Organisation name and the epoch
/// state beside the record. `behind` is the one field that is not encoded:
/// it lives in the open store and is `None` after `unseal` (LLR-zk7fx2). Not
/// `Serialize` outside test builds: it holds the member seed and
/// Organisation private keys; `seal` encodes it through `StoreDataEncoding`.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct StoreData {
    pub persona: PersonaRecord,
    pub record: Option<OrgRecord>,
    pub org_name: String,
    pub provisional_changes: Vec<ProvisionalChange>,
    pub provisional_organisations: Vec<ProvisionalOrganisation>,
    pub founding: Option<ProvisionalFounding>,
    pub member: Option<ProvisionalMember>,
    pub kept_admission_requests: Vec<KeptAdmissionRequest>,
    pub kept_revocation_notices: Vec<RevocationNotice>,
    pub expected_admissions: Vec<ExpectedAdmission>,
    pub outstanding_invites: Vec<OutstandingInvite>,
    pub revoked_devices: Vec<RevokedDevice>,
    pub address_book: Vec<(DevicePublicKey, EndpointAddresses)>,
    pub behind: Option<Epoch>,
}

impl StoreData {
    /// A store holding `persona` and nothing else: no record, an empty
    /// Organisation name and no epoch state.
    pub fn new(persona: PersonaRecord) -> Self {
        Self {
            persona,
            record: None,
            org_name: String::new(),
            provisional_changes: Vec::new(),
            provisional_organisations: Vec::new(),
            founding: None,
            member: None,
            kept_admission_requests: Vec::new(),
            kept_revocation_notices: Vec::new(),
            expected_admissions: Vec::new(),
            outstanding_invites: Vec::new(),
            revoked_devices: Vec::new(),
            address_book: Vec::new(),
            behind: None,
        }
    }
}

/// The store plaintext as decoded, before parsing (LLR-7yu2xy).
#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct RawStoreData {
    persona: RawPersonaRecord,
    record: Option<RawOrgRecord>,
    org_name: String,
    provisional_changes: Vec<RawProvisionalChange>,
    provisional_organisations: Vec<RawProvisionalOrganisation>,
    founding: Option<RawProvisionalFounding>,
    member: Option<RawProvisionalMember>,
    kept_admission_requests: Vec<RawKeptAdmissionRequest>,
    kept_revocation_notices: Vec<RevocationNotice>,
    expected_admissions: Vec<ExpectedAdmission>,
    outstanding_invites: Vec<OutstandingInvite>,
    revoked_devices: Vec<RawRevokedDevice>,
    address_book: Vec<([u8; 32], Vec<String>)>,
}

impl TryFrom<RawStoreData> for StoreData {
    type Error = OrgNodeError;

    fn try_from(raw: RawStoreData) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
        Ok(Self {
            persona: PersonaRecord::try_from(raw.persona)?,
            record: raw.record.map(OrgRecord::try_from).transpose()?,
            org_name: raw.org_name,
            provisional_changes: raw
                .provisional_changes
                .into_iter()
                .map(ProvisionalChange::try_from)
                .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?,
            provisional_organisations: raw
                .provisional_organisations
                .into_iter()
                .map(ProvisionalOrganisation::try_from)
                .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?,
            founding: raw.founding.map(ProvisionalFounding::try_from).transpose()?,
            member: raw.member.map(ProvisionalMember::try_from).transpose()?,
            kept_admission_requests: raw
                .kept_admission_requests
                .into_iter()
                .map(KeptAdmissionRequest::try_from)
                .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?,
            kept_revocation_notices: raw.kept_revocation_notices,
            expected_admissions: raw.expected_admissions,
            outstanding_invites: raw.outstanding_invites,
            revoked_devices: raw.revoked_devices.into_iter().map(RevokedDevice::try_from).collect::<Result<_, _>>()?,
            address_book: raw
                .address_book
                .into_iter()
                .map(|(key, addresses)| {
                    Ok((
                        parse_field("org.address_book", DevicePublicKey::parse(&key))?,
                        parse_field("org.address_book", EndpointAddresses::parse(addresses))?,
                    ))
                })
                .collect::<Result<_, OrgNodeError>>()?,
            behind: None,
        })
    }
}

/// A `StoreData` decoded on its own goes through the same parse as `unseal`.
impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for StoreData {
    fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        let raw = RawStoreData::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        StoreData::try_from(raw).map_err(serde::de::Error::custom)
    }
}

/// `StoreData` as the store encodes it: every field but `behind`.
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct StoreDataEncoding<'a> {
    persona: PersonaRecordEncoding<'a>,
    record: Option<OrgRecordEncoding<'a>>,
    org_name: &'a str,
    provisional_changes: &'a [ProvisionalChange],
    provisional_organisations: Vec<ProvisionalOrganisationEncoding<'a>>,
    founding: Option<ProvisionalFoundingEncoding<'a>>,
    member: &'a Option<ProvisionalMember>,
    kept_admission_requests: &'a [KeptAdmissionRequest],
    kept_revocation_notices: &'a [RevocationNotice],
    expected_admissions: &'a [ExpectedAdmission],
    outstanding_invites: &'a [OutstandingInvite],
    revoked_devices: &'a [RevokedDevice],
    address_book: &'a [(DevicePublicKey, EndpointAddresses)],
}

impl<'a> From<&'a StoreData> for StoreDataEncoding<'a> {
    fn from(data: &'a StoreData) -> Self {
        Self {
            persona: PersonaRecordEncoding::from(&data.persona),
            record: data.record.as_ref().map(OrgRecordEncoding::from),
            org_name: &data.org_name,
            provisional_changes: &data.provisional_changes,
            provisional_organisations: data.provisional_organisations.iter().map(ProvisionalOrganisationEncoding::from).collect(),
            founding: data.founding.as_ref().map(ProvisionalFoundingEncoding::from),
            member: &data.member,
            kept_admission_requests: &data.kept_admission_requests,
            kept_revocation_notices: &data.kept_revocation_notices,
            expected_admissions: &data.expected_admissions,
            outstanding_invites: &data.outstanding_invites,
            revoked_devices: &data.revoked_devices,
            address_book: &data.address_book,
        }
    }
}

/// Test builds encode the store's data as `seal` does.
#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
impl Serialize for StoreData {
    fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        StoreDataEncoding::from(self).serialize(serializer)
    }

/// A sealed Persona store: `nonce(24) ‖ ciphertext`, the bytes org-io writes
/// to and reads from that Persona's file (LLR-bg538c).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SealedStore(Vec<u8>);

impl SealedStore {
    pub fn from_bytes(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Self {
        Self(bytes)
    }

    pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        &self.0
    }
}

/// One store's change, sealed: the bytes org-io writes to the file of the
/// Persona whose Device key it names.
#[must_use = "org-io must write the sealed store before reporting success (org-io's write-before-success requirement)"]
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct StoreWrite {
    pub device_key: DevicePublicKey,
    pub sealed: SealedStore,
}

/// The nonce, then the authentication tag: the shortest sealed store.
const NONCE_LENGTH: usize = 24;
const TAG_LENGTH: usize = 16;

/// The HKDF info string of the store key (LLR-2qqqx6): versioned, so a
/// change of derivation is a new label.
const STORE_KEY_INFO: &[u8] = b"ods/persona-store/v1";

/// One Persona's open store: the store key, held only as the cipher
/// (LLR-2qqqx6), and the data. No path: org-node touches no file.
pub struct PersonaStore {
    key: XChaCha20Poly1305,
    data: StoreData,
}

/// The store encryption key (LLR-scgk5j): private to this file, no
/// `Display`, not `Copy`, redacted `Debug`, wiped on drop.
struct StoreKey(Zeroizing<[u8; 32]>);

impl core::fmt::Debug for StoreKey {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("StoreKey([REDACTED])")
    }
}

/// HKDF-SHA-256 of the device seed, salted with the Device public key, under
/// `STORE_KEY_INFO` (LLR-2qqqx6).
fn derive_key(secret: &DeviceSecret, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> Result<StoreKey, OrgNodeError> {
    let mut key = Zeroizing::new([0u8; 32]);
    Hkdf::<Sha256>::new(Some(device_key.as_bytes()), secret.seed())
        .expand(STORE_KEY_INFO, key.as_mut())
        .map_err(|_| OrgNodeError::Chain("store key derivation failed".into()))?;
    Ok(StoreKey(key))
}

/// The cipher of the store key `secret` derives for `device_key`.
pub(crate) fn cipher(secret: &DeviceSecret, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> Result<XChaCha20Poly1305, OrgNodeError> {
    let key = derive_key(secret, device_key)?;
    XChaCha20Poly1305::new_from_slice(key.0.as_ref()).map_err(|error| OrgNodeError::Chain(format!("bad key length: {error}")))
}

/// The `Debug` rendering of the store key `secret` derives (LLR-scgk5j).
#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
#[doc(hidden)]
pub fn store_key_debug_for_test(secret: &DeviceSecret) -> Result<String, OrgNodeError> {
    Ok(format!("{:?}", derive_key(secret, &secret.device_key())?))
}

/// Whether `StoreKey` implements `Display` and whether it is `Copy`, in that
/// order (LLR-scgk5j).
#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
#[doc(hidden)]
pub fn store_key_traits_for_test() -> (bool, bool) {
    (crate::implements_display!(StoreKey), crate::implements_copy!(StoreKey))
}

/// `nonce(24) ‖ ciphertext` of `plaintext`, with a fresh random nonce.
pub(crate) fn seal_bytes<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
    key: &XChaCha20Poly1305,
    plaintext: &[u8],
    rng: &mut R,
) -> Result<SealedStore, OrgNodeError> {
    let mut nonce = [0u8; NONCE_LENGTH];
    rng.fill_bytes(&mut nonce);
    let ct = key
        .encrypt(XNonce::from_slice(&nonce), plaintext)
        .map_err(|e| OrgNodeError::Chain(format!("encrypt failed: {e}")))?;
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(NONCE_LENGTH + ct.len());
    out.extend_from_slice(&nonce);
    out.extend_from_slice(&ct);
    Ok(SealedStore(out))
}

impl PersonaStore {
    /// Open the sealed store of the Persona whose Device key is `device_key`
    /// with its secret, which is consumed (LLR-bg538c, LLR-7yu2xy). Refused,
    /// each with its own error and opening nothing: a secret of another
    /// Device (`DeviceSecretMismatch`, before any decryption); fewer bytes
    /// than a nonce and a tag (`TooShort`); a ciphertext that does not
    /// authenticate (`NotAuthentic`); a plaintext that does not decode
    /// (`Undecodable`) or holds a value its type's parse refuses
    /// (`InvalidField`); and a store whose Persona names another Device
    /// (`DeviceSecretMismatch`). The behind marker opens `None`.
    pub fn unseal(sealed: &SealedStore, device_key: DevicePublicKey, secret: DeviceSecret) -> Result<Self, OrgNodeError> {
        if secret.device_key() != device_key {
            return Err(OrgNodeError::DeviceSecretMismatch);
        }
        let bytes = sealed.as_bytes();
        if bytes.len() < NONCE_LENGTH + TAG_LENGTH {
            return Err(OrgNodeError::StoreRefused(StoreRefusal::TooShort));
        }
        let key = cipher(&secret, &device_key)?;
        drop(secret);
        let (nonce, ciphertext) = bytes.split_at(NONCE_LENGTH);
        let plaintext = Zeroizing::new(
            key.decrypt(XNonce::from_slice(nonce), ciphertext)
                .map_err(|_| OrgNodeError::StoreRefused(StoreRefusal::NotAuthentic))?,
        );
        let raw: RawStoreData =
            postcard::from_bytes(&plaintext).map_err(|_| OrgNodeError::StoreRefused(StoreRefusal::Undecodable))?;
        let data = StoreData::try_from(raw)?;
        if data.persona.device_key != device_key {
            return Err(OrgNodeError::DeviceSecretMismatch);
        }
        Ok(Self { key, data })
    }

    /// An open store over `data`, keyed from `secret`, whose Device key must
    /// be `data`'s Persona's. The secret is borrowed: the operation that
    /// adds a store returns it to its caller.
    // Called by the test fixtures only until T9's `propose_founding`.
    #[cfg_attr(not(feature = "test-support"), allow(dead_code))]
    pub(crate) fn create(secret: &DeviceSecret, data: StoreData) -> Result<Self, OrgNodeError> {
        if secret.device_key() != data.persona.device_key {
            return Err(OrgNodeError::DeviceSecretMismatch);
        }
        let key = cipher(secret, &data.persona.device_key)?;
        Ok(Self { key, data })
    }

    /// The Device public key of this store's Persona.
    pub fn device_key(&self) -> DevicePublicKey {
        self.data.persona.device_key
    }

    pub fn data(&self) -> &StoreData {
        &self.data
    }

    pub fn data_mut(&mut self) -> &mut StoreData {
        &mut self.data
    }

    /// This store, sealed with a fresh 24-byte nonce.
    // Called by the test fixtures only until T9's `propose_founding`.
    #[cfg_attr(not(feature = "test-support"), allow(dead_code))]
    pub(crate) fn seal<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(&self, rng: &mut R) -> Result<StoreWrite, OrgNodeError> {
        self.seal_data(&self.data, rng)
    }

    /// `data`, sealed under this store's key as this store's write: what a
    /// change would write, before it is adopted.
    pub(crate) fn seal_data<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(&self, data: &StoreData, rng: &mut R) -> Result<StoreWrite, OrgNodeError> {
        let plaintext = Zeroizing::new(
            postcard::to_allocvec(&StoreDataEncoding::from(data))
                .map_err(|error| OrgNodeError::Chain(format!("store encode: {error}")))?,
        );
        Ok(StoreWrite { device_key: self.device_key(), sealed: seal_bytes(&self.key, &plaintext, rng)? })
    }
}
```

Add, after `struct EndpointAddresses`:

```rust
impl EndpointAddresses {
    /// Accepts zero to sixteen entries of at most 256 bytes; refuses any
    /// other list (LLR-h4gwns).
    pub fn parse(addresses: Vec<String>) -> Result<Self, EndpointAddressesError> {
        if addresses.len() > MAX_ENDPOINT_ADDRESSES {
            return Err(EndpointAddressesError::TooMany { count: addresses.len() });
        }
        if let Some((index, address)) =
            addresses.iter().enumerate().find(|(_, address)| address.len() > MAX_ENDPOINT_ADDRESS_BYTES)
        {
            return Err(EndpointAddressesError::TooLong { index, length: address.len() });
        }
        Ok(Self(addresses))
    }

    /// The entries, in the order given.
    pub fn as_slice(&self) -> &[String] {
        &self.0
    }
}
```

```rust
//! The Invite and the endpoint addresses (SDD-xexu3k): the Invite a Member
//! sends, as a Blob (Base64 of postcard), parsed here, naming the field that
//! fails; and the endpoint addresses one Device keeps for another
//! (`EndpointAddresses`, LLR-h4gwns). The Invite reply is gone: an admission
//! request takes its place (LLR-96z2k5).
//! org-io runs the exchange, and the service
//! keeps the outstanding pairs in the sealed store (`OrgService::build_invite`
//! and the operations beside it). Nothing here is verified: an Invite's
//! sender and its Organisation name are whatever the sender chose.

use base64::{engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, Engine};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use org_members::DevicePublicKey;

pub use crate::ids::{
    EndpointAddresses, EndpointAddressesError, InviteId, MAX_ENDPOINT_ADDRESSES, MAX_ENDPOINT_ADDRESS_BYTES,
};
use crate::ids::OrgId;
use crate::store::parse_field;
use crate::OrgNodeError;

/// An Invite as parsed: what the inviter typed, the Organisation it names,
/// the inviter's Devices, and the identifier its reply must echo.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Invite {
    pub org_name: String,
    pub org_id: OrgId,
    pub invitee_name: String,
    pub inviter_device_keys: Vec<DevicePublicKey>,
    pub invite_id: InviteId,
}

#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct WireInvite {
    org_name: String,
    org_id: Vec<u8>,
    invitee_name: String,
    inviter_device_keys: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
    invite_id: Vec<u8>,
}

/// Exactly `N` bytes, else `InvalidField` naming `field`.
fn exact<const N: usize>(field: &'static str, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; N], OrgNodeError> {
    bytes.try_into().map_err(|_| OrgNodeError::InvalidField {
        field,
        reason: format!("expected {N} bytes, got {}", bytes.len()),
    })
}

/// The value inside the Blob `blob`, else `InvalidField` naming `what`
/// (`invite`).
fn unarmour<T: for<'de> Deserialize<'de>>(what: &'static str, blob: &str) -> Result<T, OrgNodeError> {
    let bytes = STANDARD
        .decode(blob.trim())
        .map_err(|error| OrgNodeError::InvalidField { field: what, reason: format!("not a Blob: {error}") })?;
    postcard::from_bytes(&bytes)
        .map_err(|error| OrgNodeError::InvalidField { field: what, reason: format!("does not decode: {error}") })
}

fn armour<T: Serialize>(value: &T) -> Result<String, OrgNodeError> {
    postcard::to_allocvec(value)
        .map(|bytes| STANDARD.encode(bytes))
        .map_err(|error| OrgNodeError::Chain(format!("blob encode: {error}")))
}

/// `bytes` armoured as a Blob, whatever they hold, so a fuzz target reaches
/// the decode behind the armour (test builds only).
#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
pub fn armour_for_test(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    STANDARD.encode(bytes)
}

impl Invite {
    /// Parse an Invite Blob, naming the field that fails (LLR-b7wgpf).
    pub fn parse(blob: &str) -> Result<Self, OrgNodeError> {
        let wire: WireInvite = unarmour("invite", blob)?;
        Ok(Self {
            org_name: wire.org_name,
            org_id: OrgId::new(exact("invite.org_id", &wire.org_id)?),
            invitee_name: wire.invitee_name,
            inviter_device_keys: wire
                .inviter_device_keys
                .iter()
                .map(|key| {
                    parse_field(
                        "invite.inviter_device_keys",
                        DevicePublicKey::parse(&exact("invite.inviter_device_keys", key)?),
                    )
                })
                .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?,
            invite_id: InviteId::new(exact("invite.invite_id", &wire.invite_id)?),
        })
    }

    /// This Invite as a Blob.
    pub fn encode(&self) -> Result<String, OrgNodeError> {
        armour(&WireInvite {
            org_name: self.org_name.clone(),
            org_id: self.org_id.as_bytes().to_vec(),
            invitee_name: self.invitee_name.clone(),
            inviter_device_keys: self.inviter_device_keys.iter().map(|key| key.as_bytes().to_vec()).collect(),
            invite_id: self.invite_id.as_bytes().to_vec(),
        })
    }

    /// A Blob from raw parts, so a test can present one this software never
    /// writes (test builds only).
    #[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
    pub fn wire_for_test(org_name: &str, org_id: &[u8], invitee: &str, keys: &[[u8; 32]], invite_id: &[u8]) -> String {
        armour(&WireInvite {
            org_name: org_name.into(),
            org_id: org_id.to_vec(),
            invitee_name: invitee.into(),
            inviter_device_keys: keys.iter().map(|key| key.to_vec()).collect(),
            invite_id: invite_id.to_vec(),
        })
        .unwrap_or_default()
    }
}
```

```rust
//! OrgService: one sealed Persona store per Persona (LLR-f9x3vf), each one
//! Persona's view of one Organisation (SDD-undd7q).
//!
//! It reads no chain: the one operation that judges against the chain takes
//! the Organisation's state as a value (LLR-7en38k). It binds no endpoint and
//! sends and receives nothing: org-io receives a body and its sender and
//! hands them to `check_received`, and sends the messages org-node builds.
//!
//! It writes no file: every operation that changes a store returns at most
//! one `StoreChange` for org-io to write (LLR-ay8nvu). A refusal changes
//! nothing: each change is made on a copy of the store's data, sealed, and
//! only then adopted.
//!
//! *Stripped 2026-10-21 (T5 of docs/plans/2026-10-21-org-io-domain-api.md):*
//! the commit path and every operation this change supersedes are removed;
//! the proposal, verification and receive operations that replace them come
//! in the tasks after T5.
//!
//! Gated on the `app` feature.
use org_members::hasher::Blake3Hasher;
use org_members::trie::OrgTrie;
use org_members::{DevicePublicKey, MemberLeaf, PersonPublicKey};
use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};

use crate::error::OrgNodeError;
use crate::ids::OrgId;
use crate::invitation::{Invite, InviteId};
use crate::revocation::{Acknowledgement, RevocationNotice, VerifiedAcknowledgement};
use crate::store::{
    parse_members, ExpectedAdmission, MemberSnapshot, OrgRecord, OutstandingInvite, PersonaRecord, PersonaStore,
    RawMemberSnapshot, StoreData, StoreWrite,
};
use crate::types::{ChainAccount, PersonaId};
use crate::wire::{decode_message, WireMessage};

type Trie = OrgTrie<Blake3Hasher>;

/// A trie mirror rebuilt from persisted member snapshots.
fn trie_from_snapshots(snapshots: &[MemberSnapshot]) -> Result<Trie, OrgNodeError> {
    let leaves = snapshots
        .iter()
        .map(|s| {
            MemberLeaf::new(s.id, s.handle.clone(), s.member_key, s.name.clone(), s.surname.clone(), s.device_keys.clone())
        })
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
        .map_err(OrgNodeError::Trie)?;
    Trie::genesis(leaves).map_err(OrgNodeError::Trie)
}

/// The record a first admission extends, decoded from the snapshot its
/// Organisation-information message carries (REQ-d9g6nt, LLR-j6j95z),
/// refusing a value its type's parse refuses with `member.*` (LLR-7yu2xy).
// Public only for the fuzz target `fuzz_first_admission_base`; not API.
#[doc(hidden)]
pub fn first_admission_base(record_snapshot: &[u8]) -> Result<Trie, OrgNodeError> {
    let raw: Vec<RawMemberSnapshot> = postcard::from_bytes(record_snapshot)
        .map_err(|e| OrgNodeError::Chain(format!("record snapshot decode: {e}")))?;
    trie_from_snapshots(&parse_members(raw)?)
}

/// The one store change an operation returns (LLR-ay8nvu): the store,
/// sealed again. No variant removes a store: org-io deletes a store's file
/// and keychain item.
#[must_use = "org-io must write the store before reporting success (org-io's write-before-success requirement)"]
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum StoreChange {
    Sealed(StoreWrite),
}

/// Holds one `PersonaStore` per Persona (LLR-f9x3vf). It holds no chain and
/// no endpoint, so it runs headless on values a test passes.
pub struct OrgService {
    stores: Vec<PersonaStore>,
}

impl OrgService {
    /// A service over `stores`, one per Persona; two stores with one Device
    /// key are refused with `DuplicatePersonaStore` (LLR-f9x3vf).
    pub fn new(stores: Vec<PersonaStore>) -> Result<Self, OrgNodeError> {
        for (index, store) in stores.iter().enumerate() {
            if stores[..index].iter().any(|earlier| earlier.device_key() == store.device_key()) {
                return Err(OrgNodeError::DuplicatePersonaStore);
            }
        }
        Ok(Self { stores })
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // The receive path (chain-free).
    // ----------------------------------------------------------

    /// The check of a received body: `sender` is the Device the transport
    /// authenticated for it. The body is bounded and decoded first
    /// (`MessageTooLarge`, `MalformedMessage`); then an acknowledgement is
    /// decided against the store holding its Organisation's record, only
    /// from the Device it names (LLR-5azhry); a revocation notice passes
    /// `check_notice` (LLR-r7zm39) and the sender rule; Organisation
    /// information about a held Organisation passes the sender rule
    /// (`SenderNotListed`). Writes nothing.
    ///
    /// *Transitional (T5 until T11/T13):* Organisation information and a
    /// revocation notice that pass these refusals are refused as
    /// `MalformedMessage`: the arms that keep them come with T11's
    /// `check_received`.
    pub fn check_received(&self, sender: DevicePublicKey, body: &[u8]) -> Result<Checked, OrgNodeError> {
        match decode_message(body)? {
            WireMessage::Acknowledgement(ack) => self.check_acknowledgement(sender, ack).map(Checked::Acknowledged),
            WireMessage::Revocation(notice) => {
                let index = self.notice_index(&notice)?;
                if let Some(record) = &self.stores[index].data().record {
                    sender_listed(record, notice.org_id, &sender)?;
                }
                Err(OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage)
            }
            WireMessage::OrgInformation { envelope, .. } => {
                let org_id = envelope.org_id;
                if let Some(index) = self.record_index(org_id) {
                    if let Some(record) = &self.stores[index].data().record {
                        sender_listed(record, org_id, &sender)?;
                    }
                }
                Err(OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage)
            }
        }
    }

    /// `revocation::check_acknowledgement` against the store holding the
    /// Organisation's record; `AcknowledgementNotHeld` when none does
    /// (LLR-5azhry).
    fn check_acknowledgement(
        &self,
        sender: DevicePublicKey,
        ack: Acknowledgement,
    ) -> Result<VerifiedAcknowledgement, OrgNodeError> {
        let org_id = ack.org_id;
        let index = self.record_index(org_id).ok_or(OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementNotHeld { org_id })?;
        crate::revocation::check_acknowledgement(self.stores[index].data(), sender, ack)
    }

    /// The store whose Persona a notice is for (`revocation::notice_store`,
    /// LLR-r7zm39).
    fn notice_index(&self, notice: &RevocationNotice) -> Result<usize, OrgNodeError> {
        crate::revocation::notice_store(self.stores.iter().map(PersonaStore::data), notice)
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // Reads.
    // ----------------------------------------------------------

    /// The proxy account the record of `org_id` holds, unchanged and
    /// uninterpreted (LLR-x5asbx); `OrgNotHeld` when no store holds it.
    pub fn proxy_account(&self, org_id: OrgId) -> Result<Option<ChainAccount>, OrgNodeError> {
        let index = self.record_index(org_id).ok_or(OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { org_id })?;
        Ok(self.stores[index].data().record.as_ref().and_then(|record| record.proxy_account))
    }

    /// The Persona's Member-as-a-group key, from its seed, and its
    /// DevicePublicKey, as the store holds it, and no dialling address
    /// (LLR-437fvx).
    pub fn persona_public_keys(&self, persona_id: &PersonaId) -> Result<(PersonPublicKey, DevicePublicKey), OrgNodeError> {
        let persona = &self.stores[self.persona_index(persona_id)?].data().persona;
        Ok((persona.member_seed.x25519_keypair().member_key()?, persona.device_key))
    }

    /// One record per store, in store order (LLR-f9x3vf).
    pub fn list_personas(&self) -> Vec<&PersonaRecord> {
        self.stores.iter().map(|store| &store.data().persona).collect()
    }

    /// Every current record the stores hold, in store order.
    pub fn list_orgs(&self) -> Vec<&OrgRecord> {
        self.stores.iter().filter_map(|store| store.data().record.as_ref()).collect()
    }

    /// The first admissions the stores expect, in store order.
    pub fn expected_admissions(&self) -> Vec<ExpectedAdmission> {
        self.stores.iter().flat_map(|store| store.data().expected_admissions.iter().copied()).collect()
    }

    /// The store data of `device_key`'s Persona, read only, refusing an
    /// unknown key with `PersonaNotHeld` through the lookup every per-store
    /// operation shares (LLR-f9x3vf; test builds only).
    #[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
    pub fn store_data(&self, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> Result<&StoreData, OrgNodeError> {
        Ok(self.stores[self.store_index(device_key)?].data())
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // The Invite (until T8's `build_invite`).
    // ----------------------------------------------------------

    /// An Invite for `org_id` from the Persona bound to it, carrying that
    /// Persona's Device public key and a fresh 32-byte identifier, which its
    /// store keeps as an outstanding invite with `invitee_name`; returns the
    /// Invite and that store's write. An Organisation no Persona is bound to
    /// is refused (`OrgNotOnChain`), writing nothing.
    pub fn build_invite<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
        &mut self,
        rng: &mut R,
        org_id: OrgId,
        org_name: &str,
        invitee_name: &str,
    ) -> Result<(Invite, StoreWrite), OrgNodeError> {
        let index = self.bound_index(org_id).ok_or(OrgNodeError::OrgNotOnChain)?;
        let mut bytes = [0u8; 32];
        rng.fill_bytes(&mut bytes);
        let invite_id = InviteId::new(bytes);
        let ((), write) = self.change(index, rng, |data| {
            data.outstanding_invites.push(OutstandingInvite { org_id, invite_id, invitee_name: invitee_name.into() });
            Ok(())
        })?;
        let invite = Invite {
            org_name: org_name.into(),
            org_id,
            invitee_name: invitee_name.into(),
            inviter_device_keys: vec![self.stores[index].device_key()],
            invite_id,
        };
        Ok((invite, write))
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // The stores as org-io's files hold them.
    // ----------------------------------------------------------

    /// Put `store` in place of the held store with its Device key, or add it
    /// when none is held: org-io's reload of a Persona from its file. One
    /// store per Device key is kept (LLR-f9x3vf); nothing is sealed, no other
    /// store changes and no store is removed.
    pub fn restore_store(&mut self, store: PersonaStore) {
        match self.stores.iter().position(|held| held.device_key() == store.device_key()) {
            Some(index) => self.stores[index] = store,
            None => self.stores.push(store),
        }
    }

    /// Remove the store of `device_key` from the in-memory service, returning
    /// whether one was held: org-io's local-IO exception (LLR-9jn3z8). It
    /// touches no file and no keychain item.
    pub fn drop_store(&mut self, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> bool {
        let before = self.stores.len();
        self.stores.retain(|held| &held.device_key() != device_key);
        self.stores.len() != before
    }

    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // Private helpers.
    // ----------------------------------------------------------

    /// The index of the store of `device_key`'s Persona, else
    /// `PersonaNotHeld` (LLR-f9x3vf): the lookup of every per-store operation.
    // Read only by `store_data` (test builds) until T8's `build_invite`.
    #[cfg_attr(not(feature = "test-support"), allow(dead_code))]
    fn store_index(&self, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> Result<usize, OrgNodeError> {
        self.stores.iter().position(|store| &store.device_key() == device_key).ok_or(OrgNodeError::PersonaNotHeld)
    }

    /// The index of `persona_id`'s store, else `PersonaNotHeld`.
    fn persona_index(&self, persona_id: &PersonaId) -> Result<usize, OrgNodeError> {
        self.stores
            .iter()
            .position(|store| &store.data().persona.persona_id == persona_id)
            .ok_or(OrgNodeError::PersonaNotHeld)
    }

    /// The index of the store holding the current record of `org_id`.
    fn record_index(&self, org_id: OrgId) -> Option<usize> {
        self.stores.iter().position(|store| store.data().record.as_ref().is_some_and(|record| record.org_id == org_id))
    }

    /// The index of the first store whose Persona is bound to `org_id`.
    fn bound_index(&self, org_id: OrgId) -> Option<usize> {
        self.stores.iter().position(|store| store.data().persona.org_id == Some(org_id))
    }

    /// Make `change` to a copy of the data of the store at `index`, seal
    /// the copy, and only then adopt it: a refusal, of the change or of the
    /// seal, leaves the store as it was and returns no write.
    fn change<T, R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
        &mut self,
        index: usize,
        rng: &mut R,
        change: impl FnOnce(&mut StoreData) -> Result<T, OrgNodeError>,
    ) -> Result<(T, StoreWrite), OrgNodeError> {
        let mut data = self.stores[index].data().clone();
        let result = change(&mut data)?;
        let write = self.stores[index].seal_data(&data, rng)?;
        *self.stores[index].data_mut() = data;
        Ok((result, write))
    }
}

/// The member-sender rule: `sender` must be in some member snapshot's
/// `device_keys` of `record`, else `SenderNotListed`.
fn sender_listed(record: &OrgRecord, org_id: OrgId, sender: &DevicePublicKey) -> Result<(), OrgNodeError> {
    if record.trie_members.iter().any(|member| member.device_keys.contains(sender)) {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(OrgNodeError::SenderNotListed { org_id })
    }
}

/// One recipient's body (LLR-rsjs8e): the Device it goes to and the encoded
/// Wire message. Not `Clone`: an Organisation-information body carries the
/// Organisation private key (REQ-y7tsft); its `Debug` renders the recipient
/// and the body's length only.
pub struct OutgoingMessage {
    pub recipient: DevicePublicKey,
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for OutgoingMessage {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        formatter
            .debug_struct("OutgoingMessage")
            .field("recipient", &self.recipient)
            .field("body_len", &self.body.len())
            .finish()
    }
}

/// What `check_received` decided. *Transitional (T5 until T11):* an
/// acknowledgement it accepted (LLR-5azhry), decided against the store alone,
/// nothing written.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum Checked {
    Acknowledged(VerifiedAcknowledgement),
}
```

```rust
/// The Persona a notice is for, decided with no Organisation state: the
/// store must hold the Organisation, and a Persona bound to it must be the
/// notice's Member on the notice's Device. LLR-r7zm39.
#[cfg(feature = "app")]
pub fn check_notice<'a>(store: &'a StoreData, notice: &RevocationNotice) -> Result<&'a PersonaRecord, OrgNodeError> {
    let org_id = notice.org_id;
    if store.record.as_ref().is_none_or(|record| record.org_id != org_id) {
        return Err(OrgNodeError::RevocationNotHeld { org_id });
    }
    let persona = &store.persona;
    if persona.org_id == Some(org_id) && persona.member_id == Some(notice.member_id) && persona.device_key == notice.device
    {
        Ok(persona)
    } else {
        Err(OrgNodeError::RevocationNotForThisDevice { org_id })
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Decides a notice against the Organisation state the caller read: the
/// state must exist, be no older than the record, hold the record's root
/// when at the record's epoch, and the notice's proof
/// must show the Device absent under its root. On success the secret source
/// is called, with the Device keys of the bound Personas, and the
/// acknowledgements are signed and returned; nothing is deleted here and the
/// store is borrowed unchanged. On any refusal the error alone is returned
/// and the secret source is never called. LLR-tx8ruv, LLR-r7zm39.
#[cfg(feature = "app")]
pub fn accept(
    store: &StoreData,
    notice: &RevocationNotice,
    chain: Option<OrgState>,
    device_secrets: impl FnOnce(&[DevicePublicKey]) -> Vec<DeviceSecret>,
) -> Result<Vec<Acknowledgement>, OrgNodeError> {
    check_notice(store, notice)?;
    let org_id = notice.org_id;
    let chain = chain.ok_or(OrgNodeError::OrgNotOnChain)?;
    let record = store.record.as_ref().ok_or(OrgNodeError::RevocationNotHeld { org_id })?;
    if chain.epoch < record.epoch {
        return Err(OrgNodeError::StaleChainState { org_id, chain_epoch: chain.epoch, record_epoch: record.epoch });
    }
    // At the record's own epoch the chain must hold the record's root, as
    // `reconcile` requires (owner ruling R3: false deletion extremely unlikely).
    if chain.epoch == record.epoch && chain.root_hash != record.root_hash {
        return Err(OrgNodeError::ChainStateConflict { org_id });
    }
    notice
        .proof
        .verify::<Blake3Hasher>(&chain.root_hash, &notice.member_id, &notice.device)
        .map_err(|cause| OrgNodeError::RevocationProofRefused { org_id, cause })?;
    // Every refusal check has passed: only now are the device secrets read.
    sign_acknowledgements(store, org_id, &chain, device_secrets(&bound_devices(store, org_id)))
}
```

```rust
/// One acknowledgement per Persona bound to `org_id` with a MemberId, naming `verified`'s epoch and root and signed with the
/// secret in `device_secrets` whose Device key is that Persona's. Refuses
/// with `DeviceSecretNotSupplied` when such a Persona has no secret there.
/// The secrets are moved in and dropped, zeroised, on return. LLR-hby4jr.
/// A store holds one Persona, so at most one acknowledgement.
#[cfg(feature = "app")]
pub fn sign_acknowledgements(
    store: &StoreData,
    org_id: OrgId,
    verified: &OrgState,
    device_secrets: Vec<DeviceSecret>,
) -> Result<Vec<Acknowledgement>, OrgNodeError> {
    let persona = &store.persona;
    if persona.org_id != Some(org_id) {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    }
    let Some(member_id) = persona.member_id else { return Ok(Vec::new()) };
    let device = persona.device_key;
    let keypair = device_secrets
        .iter()
        .find(|secret| secret.device_key() == device)
        .map(DeviceSecret::signing_keypair)
        .ok_or(OrgNodeError::DeviceSecretNotSupplied { org_id })?;
    let mut acknowledgement = Acknowledgement {
        org_id,
        member_id,
        device,
        epoch: verified.epoch,
        root: verified.root_hash,
        signature: Signature64([0; 64]),
    };
    acknowledgement.signature = Signature64(keypair.sign(&acknowledgement.signed_bytes()).to_bytes());
    Ok(vec![acknowledgement])
}
```

```rust
/// Checks a received acknowledgement against the store alone, cheapest
/// first: the store holds the Organisation's record; `sender`, the Device
/// the transport authenticated for the delivering connection, is the Device
/// the acknowledgement names; the acknowledgement's epoch is not above that
/// record's; no Member of the record lists its Device; its signature
/// verifies strictly under that Device. The store is not changed.
/// LLR-5azhry.
#[cfg(feature = "app")]
pub fn check_acknowledgement(
    store: &StoreData,
    sender: DevicePublicKey,
    ack: Acknowledgement,
) -> Result<VerifiedAcknowledgement, OrgNodeError> {
    let org_id = ack.org_id;
    let record = store
        .record
        .as_ref()
        .filter(|record| record.org_id == org_id)
        .ok_or(OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementNotHeld { org_id })?;
    if sender != ack.device {
        return Err(OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementNotFromItsDevice { org_id });
    }
    if ack.epoch > record.epoch {
        return Err(OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementFromFuture { org_id });
    }
    if record.trie_members.iter().any(|member| member.device_keys.contains(&ack.device)) {
        return Err(OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementForListedDevice { org_id });
    }
    let signature = ed25519_dalek::Signature::from_bytes(&ack.signature.0);
    ack.device
        .verifying_key()
        .verify_strict(&ack.signed_bytes(), &signature)
        .map_err(|_| OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementSignatureInvalid { org_id })?;
    Ok(VerifiedAcknowledgement(ack))
}
```
