```rust
//! Story helpers shared by org-node's service-level test targets. Not a test
//! target: each target that uses it declares `mod support;`.
//!
//! The story steps — `create_persona`, `found`, `prepare_to_join` — are the
//! only place a test performs one, so a change to the service API changes
//! their bodies and not the tests that call them.
//!
//! *Rewritten 2026-10-21 (T5 of docs/plans/2026-10-21-org-io-domain-api.md):*
//! the operations the stories ran (`create_persona`, `create_organisation`,
//! `commit_genesis`, `admit_member`, `revoke_member`, `commit_update`,
//! `commit_checked`, `reconcile`, `expect_admission`) are removed. Each step
//! now builds the store it leaves directly, in the single-Organisation layout
//! (LLR-d925uu), seals it as an operation would and hands it to the service
//! with `restore_store`; a founding writes its slot through `ChainSlots`, the
//! stand-in for org-io's chain write. The admission and revocation stories
//! and their send and receive come back with verification and the messages
//! of the current epoch (T14 onwards).
//!
//! A [`Node`] plays org-io's part: its [`Keychain`] keeps each secret's
//! bytes, and its [`Disk`] keeps the latest sealed store per Persona, updated
//! from every returned write. What "reached the disk" is what the writes
//! carried: `reopen_store` unseals the [`Disk`] with the [`Keychain`].
#![allow(dead_code, clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, LazyLock, Mutex};

use org_members::{DevicePublicKey, Handle, MemberId, MemberLeaf, Name, PersonPublicKey, Surname};
use org_node::chain::OrgState;
use org_node::error::OrgNodeError;
use org_node::ids::OrgId;
use org_node::keys::{DeviceSecret, SigningKeypair, X25519Keypair};
use org_node::service::{Checked, OrgService, StoreChange};
use org_node::store::{
    ExpectedAdmission, MemberSnapshot, OrgRecord, OrgRecordParts, OutstandingInvite, PersonaRecord, PersonaRecordParts,
    PersonaStatus, PersonaStore, SealedStore, StoreData, StoreWrite,
};
use org_node::test_fixtures::{device_keypair, seal_for_test, store_for_test, ChainSlots, Trie};
use org_node::wire::{decode_message, encode_message, WireMessage};
use org_node::{ChainAccount, Epoch, OrgPrivateKey, PersonaId, SequenceNumber};
use rand::rngs::OsRng;
use rand::RngCore;
use zeroize::Zeroizing;

/// org-io's keychain, played by the test: each Persona's device seed bytes,
/// by Device key. Clones share one map.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct Keychain(Arc<Mutex<HashMap<[u8; 32], Vec<u8>>>>);

impl Keychain {
    /// Keep `secret`'s bytes, as org-io writes a new Persona's keychain item.
    pub fn keep(&self, secret: &DeviceSecret) {
        let mut bytes = vec![];
        secret
            .lend_to_keychain(|seed| {
                bytes.extend_from_slice(seed);
                Ok::<(), std::convert::Infallible>(())
            })
            .unwrap();
        self.0.lock().unwrap().insert(*secret.device_key().as_bytes(), bytes);
    }

    /// The secret of `device_key`, read back as org-io reads a keychain item.
    pub fn secret(&self, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> Option<DeviceSecret> {
        let bytes = self.0.lock().unwrap().get(device_key.as_bytes()).cloned()?;
        Some(DeviceSecret::from_keychain_bytes(Zeroizing::new(bytes)).unwrap())
    }

    /// The seed bytes of `device_key`.
    pub fn seed(&self, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> [u8; 32] {
        self.0.lock().unwrap().get(device_key.as_bytes()).expect("a keychain item").as_slice().try_into().unwrap()
    }

    /// The secrets of `device_keys` this keychain holds: org-io's
    /// `device_secrets` closure.
    pub fn secrets(&self, device_keys: &[DevicePublicKey]) -> Vec<DeviceSecret> {
        device_keys.iter().filter_map(|key| self.secret(key)).collect()
    }
}

/// The store files of one party: each Persona's latest sealed store, by its
/// Device key's bytes.
type StoreFiles = BTreeMap<[u8; 32], (DevicePublicKey, SealedStore)>;

/// org-io's store files, played by the test: the latest sealed store of
/// each Persona, by Device key. Clones share one map.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct Disk(Arc<Mutex<StoreFiles>>);

impl Disk {
    pub fn write(&self, write: StoreWrite) {
        self.0.lock().unwrap().insert(*write.device_key.as_bytes(), (write.device_key, write.sealed));
    }

    pub fn apply(&self, change: StoreChange) {
        match change {
            StoreChange::Sealed(write) => self.write(write),
        }
    }

    /// Every sealed store, unsealed with `keychain`'s secrets.
    pub fn unseal(&self, keychain: &Keychain) -> Vec<PersonaStore> {
        self.0
            .lock()
            .unwrap()
            .values()
            .map(|(device_key, sealed)| {
                PersonaStore::unseal(sealed, *device_key, keychain.secret(device_key).expect("a keychain item")).unwrap()
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// Every sealed store, by its Device key.
    pub fn sealed(&self) -> Vec<(DevicePublicKey, SealedStore)> {
        self.0.lock().unwrap().values().cloned().collect()
    }

    /// Every sealed byte, in Device-key order (to prove nothing was written:
    /// each write draws a fresh nonce).
    pub fn bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.0.lock().unwrap().values().flat_map(|(_, sealed)| sealed.as_bytes().to_vec()).collect()
    }
}

/// One party's org-io storage in a test: its keychain and its store files.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct Party {
    pub keychain: Keychain,
    pub disk: Disk,
}

/// Every party's storage, by test tag and party name: `open_store` starts
/// one afresh, `reopen_store` and `store_bytes` read it back.
static PARTIES: LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap<(String, String), Party>>> = LazyLock::new(Default::default);

/// A fresh, empty storage for `party` in test `tag`, replacing any earlier
/// one.
pub fn open_store(tag: &str, party: &str) -> Party {
    let fresh = Party::default();
    PARTIES.lock().unwrap().insert((tag.to_string(), party.to_string()), fresh.clone());
    fresh
}

/// `party`'s storage in test `tag`, as `open_store` registered it.
pub fn party(tag: &str, party: &str) -> Party {
    PARTIES.lock().unwrap().get(&(tag.to_string(), party.to_string())).cloned().expect("open_store first")
}

/// What reached `party`'s disk in test `tag`: every Persona store it holds,
/// unsealed, merged in one view.
pub fn reopen_store(tag: &str, party_name: &str) -> Reopened {
    let party = party(tag, party_name);
    Reopened::of(&party.disk.unseal(&party.keychain))
}

/// The raw bytes of a party's store files (to prove nothing was written).
pub fn store_bytes(tag: &str, party_name: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
    party(tag, party_name).disk.bytes()
}

/// A service over what reached `party`'s disk in test `tag`.
pub fn reopened_service(tag: &str, party_name: &str) -> OrgService {
    let party = party(tag, party_name);
    OrgService::new(party.disk.unseal(&party.keychain)).unwrap()
}

/// Make `change` to the store of `persona_id` that reached `party`'s disk in
/// test `tag`, and seal it back there as org-io would hold it: a store this
/// software never writes. Reopen it with `Node::reopened`.
pub fn tamper(tag: &str, party_name: &str, persona_id: &PersonaId, change: impl FnOnce(&mut StoreData)) {
    let party = party(tag, party_name);
    let stores = party.disk.unseal(&party.keychain);
    let store = stores.iter().find(|store| &store.data().persona.persona_id == persona_id).expect("the Persona's store");
    let mut data = store.data().clone();
    change(&mut data);
    let secret = party.keychain.secret(&store.device_key()).expect("a keychain item");
    let rewritten = store_for_test(&secret, data);
    party.disk.write(seal_for_test(&rewritten, &mut OsRng));
}

/// Every Persona store of one party, merged: the Personas, current records,
/// expectations and outstanding invites in store order.
pub struct Reopened {
    pub personas: Vec<PersonaRecord>,
    pub orgs: Vec<OrgRecord>,
    pub expected_admissions: Vec<ExpectedAdmission>,
    pub outstanding_invites: Vec<OutstandingInvite>,
}

impl Reopened {
    fn of(stores: &[PersonaStore]) -> Self {
        Self {
            personas: stores.iter().map(|store| store.data().persona.clone()).collect(),
            orgs: stores.iter().filter_map(|store| store.data().record.clone()).collect(),
            expected_admissions: stores.iter().flat_map(|store| store.data().expected_admissions.clone()).collect(),
            outstanding_invites: stores.iter().flat_map(|store| store.data().outstanding_invites.clone()).collect(),
        }
    }

    /// The merged view itself, so `reopen_store(..).data().orgs` reads as it
    /// did when one store held every Persona.
    pub fn data(&self) -> &Self {
        self
    }
}

/// An `OrgService` and the chain view its org-io reads through, with the
/// keychain and store files org-io keeps. Derefs to the service for every
/// read.
pub struct Node {
    pub svc: OrgService,
    pub view: CountingChain,
    pub keychain: Keychain,
    pub disk: Disk,
    /// The Device this node's sends come from, when a test names one
    /// (`sending_as`); else the first Persona bound to the Organisation.
    pub sends_as: Option<DevicePublicKey>,
}

impl std::ops::Deref for Node {
    type Target = OrgService;
    fn deref(&self) -> &OrgService {
        &self.svc
    }
}

impl std::ops::DerefMut for Node {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut OrgService {
        &mut self.svc
    }
}

impl Node {
    /// A node with no Persona over `party`'s storage.
    pub fn new(party: Party, view: impl Into<CountingChain>) -> Self {
        Self::over(OrgService::new(vec![]).unwrap(), party, view)
    }

    /// A node over what reached `party`'s disk: its stores unsealed with its
    /// keychain.
    pub fn reopened(party: Party, view: impl Into<CountingChain>) -> Self {
        Self::over(OrgService::new(party.disk.unseal(&party.keychain)).unwrap(), party, view)
    }

    fn over(svc: OrgService, party: Party, view: impl Into<CountingChain>) -> Self {
        Self { svc, view: view.into(), keychain: party.keychain, disk: party.disk, sends_as: None }
    }

    /// This node's sends come from `device`'s Device.
    pub fn sending_as(self, device: &SigningKeypair) -> Self {
        Self { sends_as: Some(device.device_key().unwrap()), ..self }
    }

    /// The Device a send of this node about `org_id` comes from: the one
    /// `sending_as` named, else the first Persona bound to `org_id`.
    pub fn sender_for(&self, org_id: OrgId) -> DevicePublicKey {
        self.sends_as.unwrap_or_else(|| {
            self.svc
                .list_personas()
                .into_iter()
                .find(|persona| persona.org_id == Some(org_id))
                .map(|persona| persona.device_key)
                .expect("a Persona bound to the Organisation")
        })
    }

    /// A new Persona with a fresh member seed and Device secret, its store
    /// holding it alone: the secret kept in the keychain, the sealed store
    /// on the disk and in the service.
    pub fn create_persona<R: rand_core::RngCore + rand_core::CryptoRng>(
        &mut self,
        rng: &mut R,
        handle: Handle,
        name: Name,
        surname: Surname,
    ) -> Result<PersonaId, OrgNodeError> {
        let member = X25519Keypair::generate(rng);
        let secret = DeviceSecret::generate(rng);
        let persona_id = persona_id_for(&member.member_key()?);
        let persona = PersonaRecord::from(PersonaRecordParts {
            persona_id: persona_id.clone(),
            org_id: None,
            name,
            surname,
            handle: Some(handle),
            member_seed: member.member_seed(),
            device_key: secret.device_key(),
            member_id: None,
            status: PersonaStatus::Proposed,
        });
        self.keychain.keep(&secret);
        self.put(StoreData::new(persona));
        Ok(persona_id)
    }

    /// Seal `data` as an operation would, write it to the disk and hold it
    /// in the service in place of the store with its Device key.
    pub fn put(&mut self, data: StoreData) {
        let secret = self.keychain.secret(&data.persona.device_key).expect("a keychain item");
        let store = store_for_test(&secret, data);
        self.disk.write(seal_for_test(&store, &mut OsRng));
        self.svc.restore_store(store);
    }

    /// The store data of `persona_id`, read only.
    pub fn store_of(&self, persona_id: &PersonaId) -> &StoreData {
        let device_key = persona_of(&self.svc, persona_id).device_key;
        self.svc.store_data(&device_key).expect("the Persona's store")
    }

    /// What org-io does on a receive, as far as T5 keeps it:
    /// `check_received(sender, body)`.
    pub fn receive_from(&self, sender: DevicePublicKey, body: &[u8]) -> Result<Checked, OrgNodeError> {
        self.svc.check_received(sender, body)
    }

    /// `receive_from` the body posted to `inbox`.
    pub fn receive_posted(&self, inbox: &Inbox) -> Result<Checked, OrgNodeError> {
        let (sender, body) = inbox.take();
        self.receive_from(sender, &body)
    }
}

/// A Persona identifier from its Member key: the first 16 bytes, in hex.
pub fn persona_id_for(member_key: &PersonPublicKey) -> PersonaId {
    PersonaId::new(member_key.as_bytes().iter().take(16).map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect())
}

/// Where a send is delivered: the value-driven stand-in for the address a
/// sender dialled. A send posts the sending Device's key and the body; the
/// receiving side takes the first posted. Clones share one queue.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Inbox {
    posts: std::sync::mpsc::Sender<Post>,
    queue: Arc<Mutex<std::sync::mpsc::Receiver<Post>>>,
}

/// One delivery: the sending Device's key and the body.
type Post = (DevicePublicKey, Vec<u8>);

impl Default for Inbox {
    fn default() -> Self {
        let (posts, queue) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
        Self { posts, queue: Arc::new(Mutex::new(queue)) }
    }
}

impl Inbox {
    /// Deliver `body` as sent by `sender`'s Device.
    pub fn post(&self, sender: DevicePublicKey, body: Vec<u8>) {
        self.posts.send((sender, body)).unwrap();
    }

    /// The first body posted and its sender; none is a failed test.
    pub fn take(&self) -> (DevicePublicKey, Vec<u8>) {
        self.queue.lock().unwrap().try_recv().expect("nothing was delivered")
    }
}

/// A receive a test runs after the send it waits for.
pub struct Deferred<T>(Box<dyn FnOnce() -> T + Send>);

impl<T> Deferred<T> {
    pub fn run(self) -> T {
        (self.0)()
    }
}

/// A Device that relays what it is handed: the value-driven stand-in for an
/// endpoint bound from that Device's secret.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Relay {
    device_key: DevicePublicKey,
}

impl Relay {
    pub fn new(device: &SigningKeypair) -> Self {
        Self { device_key: device.device_key().unwrap() }
    }

    pub fn from_seed(seed: [u8; 32]) -> Self {
        Self::new(&device_keypair(seed))
    }

    pub fn device_key(&self) -> DevicePublicKey {
        self.device_key
    }

    /// Post `msg`, encoded, to `to` as sent by this Device.
    pub fn send(&self, to: Inbox, msg: &WireMessage) -> Result<(), OrgNodeError> {
        to.post(self.device_key, encode_message(msg)?);
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The rogue relay's device seed — a third device, neither A's nor B's.
pub const ROGUE_SEED: [u8; 32] = [0x33u8; 32];

pub fn h(s: &str) -> Handle {
    Handle::parse(s).unwrap()
}
pub fn nm(s: &str) -> Name {
    Name::parse(s).unwrap()
}
pub fn sn(s: &str) -> Surname {
    Surname::parse(s).unwrap()
}

/// One party's scratch directory, unique per target, test and process.
pub fn store_dir(tag: &str, party: &str) -> PathBuf {
    std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
        "ods-{}-{tag}-{party}-{}",
        env!("CARGO_CRATE_NAME"),
        std::process::id()
    ))
}

/// A persona's record, cloned.
pub fn persona_of(svc: &OrgService, persona_id: &PersonaId) -> PersonaRecord {
    svc.list_personas()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|p| &p.persona_id == persona_id)
        .expect("persona not found")
        .clone()
}

/// The device keypair of a persona, from its secret in `node`'s keychain.
pub fn device_kp(node: &Node, persona_id: &PersonaId) -> SigningKeypair {
    device_keypair(device_seed_of(node, persona_id))
}

/// `svc`'s record of `org_id`, cloned.
pub fn rec_of(svc: &OrgService, org_id: OrgId) -> OrgRecord {
    svc.list_orgs().into_iter().find(|o| o.org_id == org_id).expect("record").clone()
}

/// The record of `org_id` as it reached the disk, cloned.
pub fn disk_rec_of(store: &Reopened, org_id: OrgId) -> OrgRecord {
    store.orgs.iter().find(|o| o.org_id == org_id).expect("record on disk").clone()
}

/// The MemberId of the member with `handle` in `rec`.
pub fn id_by_handle(rec: &OrgRecord, handle: &str) -> MemberId {
    rec.trie_members.iter().find(|m| m.handle.as_str() == handle).expect("member in the record").id
}

/// A Device (from `seed`) that captures the first message sent to it: the
/// inbox a sender delivers to, and the capture yielding that Device as a
/// [`Relay`], the sender's Device and the message.
pub fn spawn_recv_one(seed: [u8; 32]) -> (Inbox, Deferred<(Relay, DevicePublicKey, WireMessage)>) {
    let inbox = Inbox::default();
    let posted = inbox.clone();
    let capture = Deferred(Box::new(move || {
        let (sender, body) = posted.take();
        (Relay::from_seed(seed), sender, decode_message(&body).expect("a Wire message"))
    }));
    (inbox, capture)
}

/// The proxy account a founding records in these tests.
pub fn test_proxy() -> ChainAccount {
    ChainAccount::new([0x5a; 32])
}

/// The persisted snapshot of a trie member.
pub fn snapshot_of(m: &MemberLeaf) -> MemberSnapshot {
    MemberSnapshot {
        id: *m.id(),
        handle: m.handle().clone(),
        name: m.name().clone(),
        surname: m.surname().clone(),
        member_key: *m.p2p_key(),
        device_keys: m.p2p_devices().to_vec(),
    }
}

/// Story 1: `pid` founds an Organisation. The store a founding's adoption
/// leaves is built directly (T5: no operation founds yet): a founding record
/// at epoch 1 listing `pid` alone under a drawn MemberId, a fresh
/// Organisation key pair, the test proxy; the Persona bound and Active. The
/// slot is written through `chain` at epoch 1.
pub fn found(svc: &mut Node, chain: &ChainSlots, pid: &PersonaId) -> OrgId {
    let mut data = svc.store_of(pid).clone();
    let persona = &data.persona;
    let mut id = [0u8; 32];
    OsRng.fill_bytes(&mut id);
    let member_id = MemberId::new(id);
    let founder = MemberLeaf::new(
        member_id,
        persona.handle.clone().expect("a founder's handle"),
        persona.member_seed_for_test().x25519_keypair().member_key().unwrap(),
        persona.name.clone(),
        persona.surname.clone(),
        vec![persona.device_key],
    )
    .unwrap();
    let trie = Trie::genesis(vec![founder.clone()]).unwrap();
    let root = trie.root_hash().unwrap();
    let org_key = X25519Keypair::generate(&mut OsRng);
    let org_pub_key = org_key.org_public_key().unwrap();
    let org_id = chain.apply_genesis(root, org_pub_key);
    data.record = Some(OrgRecord::from(OrgRecordParts {
        org_id,
        root_hash: root,
        org_pub_key,
        epoch: Epoch::new(1),
        last_seq: SequenceNumber::new(1),
        trie_members: vec![snapshot_of(&founder)],
        proxy_account: Some(test_proxy()),
        org_private_key: org_key.org_private_key(),
        kept_change_set: None,
        kept_base_snapshot: None,
    }));
    data.org_name = "Acme".into();
    data.persona.org_id = Some(org_id);
    data.persona.member_id = Some(member_id);
    data.persona.status = PersonaStatus::Active;
    svc.put(data);
    org_id
}

/// Story 2, the joining node's half: its first unbound Persona's store
/// expects the admission to `org_id`, built directly (T5: no operation
/// declares one until T10's `propose_member`).
pub fn prepare_to_join(svc_b: &mut Node, org_id: OrgId) {
    let pid = svc_b
        .list_personas()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|persona| persona.org_id.is_none())
        .map(|persona| persona.persona_id.clone())
        .expect("an unbound Persona");
    let mut data = svc_b.store_of(&pid).clone();
    data.persona.org_id = Some(org_id);
    data.expected_admissions.push(ExpectedAdmission { org_id });
    svc_b.put(data);
}

/// The first Device of the Member with `handle` in `record`.
pub fn device_by_handle(record: &OrgRecord, handle: &str) -> DevicePublicKey {
    record.trie_members.iter().find(|m| m.handle.as_str() == handle).and_then(|m| m.device_keys.first().copied()).unwrap()
}

/// `msg`, of the same kind, with its Envelope replaced.
pub fn with_envelope(msg: &WireMessage, envelope: org_node::Envelope) -> WireMessage {
    match msg {
        WireMessage::OrgInformation { record_snapshot, org_private_key, .. } => WireMessage::OrgInformation {
            envelope,
            record_snapshot: record_snapshot.clone(),
            org_private_key: org_private_key.clone(),
        },
        other => panic!("only Organisation information carries an Envelope, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

/// Organisation information carrying `envelope`, an empty snapshot and a
/// key no chain holds: for tests of the chain-free checks, which refuse the
/// Envelope before the snapshot or the key is looked at.
pub fn carrying(envelope: org_node::Envelope) -> WireMessage {
    WireMessage::OrgInformation { envelope, record_snapshot: Vec::new(), org_private_key: OrgPrivateKey::from([0u8; 32]) }
}

/// The Envelope of the Organisation information `msg`; only that kind holds
/// one.
pub fn envelope_of(msg: &WireMessage) -> &org_node::Envelope {
    match msg {
        WireMessage::OrgInformation { envelope, .. } => envelope,
        other => panic!("Organisation information, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

/// The Organisation information `msg`, with its record snapshot replaced.
pub fn with_snapshot(msg: &WireMessage, record_snapshot: Vec<u8>) -> WireMessage {
    match msg {
        WireMessage::OrgInformation { envelope, org_private_key, .. } => WireMessage::OrgInformation {
            envelope: envelope.clone(),
            record_snapshot,
            org_private_key: org_private_key.clone(),
        },
        other => panic!("only Organisation information carries a snapshot, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

/// The Organisation information `msg`, with its Organisation private key
/// replaced.
pub fn with_key(msg: &WireMessage, org_private_key: OrgPrivateKey) -> WireMessage {
    match msg {
        WireMessage::OrgInformation { envelope, record_snapshot, .. } => WireMessage::OrgInformation {
            envelope: envelope.clone(),
            record_snapshot: record_snapshot.clone(),
            org_private_key,
        },
        other => panic!("only Organisation information carries a key, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

/// Stories 1–2: A creates a persona and founds the Organisation (epoch 1);
/// B creates a persona and, unless the test says not to, expects the
/// admission.
pub struct Setup {
    pub chain: ChainSlots,
    pub svc_a: Node,
    pub svc_b: Node,
    pub org_id: OrgId,
    pub pid_a: PersonaId,
    pub pid_b: PersonaId,
    pub b_device_kp: SigningKeypair,
}

pub fn setup(tag: &str) -> Setup {
    setup_with(tag, true)
}

pub fn setup_with(tag: &str, prepare: bool) -> Setup {
    setup_over_both(tag, prepare, CountingChain::over, CountingChain::over)
}

/// `setup_with`, with A's org-io reading the chain through `a_chain(chain)`
/// and B's through `b_chain(chain)`.
pub fn setup_over_both(
    tag: &str,
    prepare: bool,
    a_chain: impl FnOnce(ChainSlots) -> CountingChain,
    b_chain: impl FnOnce(ChainSlots) -> CountingChain,
) -> Setup {
    let chain = ChainSlots::new();
    let mut svc_a = Node::new(open_store(tag, "a"), a_chain(chain.clone()));
    let mut svc_b = Node::new(open_store(tag, "b"), b_chain(chain.clone()));

    let pid_a = svc_a.create_persona(&mut OsRng, h("admin"), nm("Admin"), sn("User")).unwrap();
    let org_id = found(&mut svc_a, &chain, &pid_a);
    assert_eq!(chain.get(&org_id).unwrap().epoch, Epoch::new(1));

    let pid_b = svc_b.create_persona(&mut OsRng, h("bob"), nm("Bob"), sn("Builder")).unwrap();
    if prepare {
        prepare_to_join(&mut svc_b, org_id);
    }
    let b_device_kp = device_kp(&svc_b, &pid_b);
    Setup { chain, svc_a, svc_b, org_id, pid_a, pid_b, b_device_kp }
}

/// Send `msg` to `addr` from a relay device that is neither A nor B.
pub fn deliver(to: Inbox, msg: &WireMessage) {
    deliver_from([0x5bu8; 32], to, msg);
}

/// Send `msg` to `to` from the Device of `sender_seed`.
pub fn deliver_from(sender_seed: [u8; 32], to: Inbox, msg: &WireMessage) {
    Relay::from_seed(sender_seed).send(to, msg).expect("an encodable message");
}

/// Send `body` to `to` from a relay device: bytes no `WireMessage` encodes
/// to.
pub fn deliver_raw(to: Inbox, body: &[u8]) {
    to.post(Relay::from_seed([0x5cu8; 32]).device_key(), body.to_vec());
}

/// The encoded member snapshots of `trie`, as a first admission carries them.
pub fn snapshot_bytes(trie: &Trie) -> Vec<u8> {
    let members: Vec<MemberSnapshot> = trie.members().iter().map(snapshot_of).collect();
    postcard::to_allocvec(&members).unwrap()
}

/// The state source a test's org-io reads through, over shared `ChainSlots`:
/// it counts reads, can hide an Organisation (answer `None` for it) and can
/// fail every read.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct CountingChain {
    slots: ChainSlots,
    reads: Arc<AtomicUsize>,
    hidden: Arc<Mutex<Vec<OrgId>>>,
    failing: Arc<AtomicBool>,
}

impl From<ChainSlots> for CountingChain {
    fn from(slots: ChainSlots) -> Self {
        Self::over(slots)
    }
}

impl CountingChain {
    pub fn over(slots: ChainSlots) -> Self {
        Self { slots, reads: Default::default(), hidden: Default::default(), failing: Default::default() }
    }

    /// One read of `org`'s state: counted, then the failing, hidden or slot
    /// answer.
    pub fn read(&self, org: OrgId) -> Result<Option<OrgState>, OrgNodeError> {
        self.reads.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
        if self.failing.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
            return Err(OrgNodeError::Chain("chain unreachable".into()));
        }
        if self.hidden.lock().unwrap().contains(&org) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        Ok(self.slots.get(&org))
    }
    pub fn reads(&self) -> usize {
        self.reads.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
    }
    pub fn hide(&self, org: OrgId) {
        self.hidden.lock().unwrap().push(org);
    }
    pub fn fail_reads(&self) {
        self.failing.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
    }
}

/// `setup`, with B's org-io reading the chain through its own
/// `CountingChain`, returned (B's view).
pub fn setup_counted(tag: &str) -> (Setup, CountingChain) {
    let s = setup(tag);
    let counting = s.svc_b.view.clone();
    (s, counting)
}

/// `svc`'s `receive_from` for `msg`, encoded, from the Device of
/// `sender_seed`.
pub fn receive_message_from(svc: &Node, sender_seed: [u8; 32], msg: &WireMessage) -> Result<Checked, OrgNodeError> {
    let sender = Relay::from_seed(sender_seed).device_key();
    svc.receive_from(sender, &encode_message(msg).unwrap())
}

/// The device seed of `persona_id` in `node`'s keychain, as bytes.
pub fn device_seed_of(node: &Node, persona_id: &PersonaId) -> [u8; 32] {
    node.keychain.seed(&persona_of(node, persona_id).device_key)
}

/// A calculated trie of one Member that lists neither `member` nor `device`:
/// an absence proof from it verifies under its root, not under any chain's.
pub fn trie_without(member: MemberId, device: DevicePublicKey) -> Trie {
    use org_node::test_fixtures::{device_key, member_key};
    let other = MemberId::new([0x5e; 32]);
    assert_ne!(other, member);
    assert_ne!(device_key(0x5f), device);
    let leaf = MemberLeaf::new(other, h("elsewhere"), member_key(0x5e), nm("Else"), sn("Where"), vec![device_key(0x5f)])
        .unwrap();
    Trie::genesis(vec![leaf]).unwrap()
}

/// The calculated trie of `record`'s members.
pub fn trie_of(record: &OrgRecord) -> Trie {
    trie_of_members(&record.trie_members)
}

/// The calculated trie of `members`.
pub fn trie_of_members(members: &[MemberSnapshot]) -> Trie {
    let leaves = members
        .iter()
        .map(|m| MemberLeaf::new(m.id, m.handle.clone(), m.member_key, m.name.clone(), m.surname.clone(), m.device_keys.clone()))
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
        .unwrap();
    Trie::genesis(leaves).unwrap()
}

/// `members` as the next record of `previous`: one epoch on, with their root
/// and a fresh Organisation key pair, the slot written through `chain` at
/// that epoch, and no kept Change set.
fn next_record(chain: &ChainSlots, previous: &OrgRecord, members: Vec<MemberSnapshot>) -> OrgRecord {
    let trie = trie_of_members(&members);
    let root = trie.root_hash().unwrap();
    let org_key = X25519Keypair::generate(&mut OsRng);
    let org_pub_key = org_key.org_public_key().unwrap();
    chain.apply_update(previous.org_id, root, org_pub_key, previous.epoch).unwrap();
    let epoch = previous.epoch.get() + 1;
    OrgRecord::from(OrgRecordParts {
        org_id: previous.org_id,
        root_hash: root,
        org_pub_key,
        epoch: Epoch::new(epoch),
        last_seq: SequenceNumber::new(epoch),
        trie_members: members,
        proxy_account: previous.proxy_account,
        org_private_key: org_key.org_private_key(),
        kept_change_set: None,
        kept_base_snapshot: None,
    })
}

/// Stories 3–4 as the state they leave (T5: no operation admits until the
/// verification tasks): B listed under a drawn MemberId beside A, at the
/// next epoch with a fresh key pair, in A's record and in B's own; B's
/// Persona bound, Active and given its MemberId, its expectation gone; the
/// slot at that epoch.
pub fn admit_b_directly(mut s: Setup) -> Setup {
    let previous = rec_of(&s.svc_a, s.org_id);
    let bob = persona_of(&s.svc_b, &s.pid_b);
    let mut id = [0u8; 32];
    OsRng.fill_bytes(&mut id);
    let b_member = MemberSnapshot {
        id: MemberId::new(id),
        handle: bob.handle.clone().expect("B's handle"),
        name: bob.name.clone(),
        surname: bob.surname.clone(),
        member_key: bob.member_seed_for_test().x25519_keypair().member_key().unwrap(),
        device_keys: vec![bob.device_key],
    };
    let mut members = previous.trie_members.clone();
    members.push(b_member);
    let record = next_record(&s.chain, &previous, members);

    let mut a_data = s.svc_a.store_of(&s.pid_a).clone();
    a_data.record = Some(record.clone());
    s.svc_a.put(a_data);

    let mut b_data = s.svc_b.store_of(&s.pid_b).clone();
    let mut b_record = record;
    b_record.proxy_account = None;
    b_data.record = Some(b_record);
    b_data.persona.org_id = Some(s.org_id);
    b_data.persona.member_id = Some(MemberId::new(id));
    b_data.persona.status = PersonaStatus::Active;
    b_data.expected_admissions.clear();
    s.svc_b.put(b_data);
    s
}

/// Story 5 on A's side as the state it leaves (T5): A's record without B, at
/// the next epoch with a fresh key pair, the slot at that epoch; B's store
/// is left as it was. Returns the setup and B's MemberId.
pub fn remove_b_directly(mut s: Setup) -> (Setup, MemberId) {
    let previous = rec_of(&s.svc_a, s.org_id);
    let b_device = persona_of(&s.svc_b, &s.pid_b).device_key;
    let b_id = previous.trie_members.iter().find(|m| m.device_keys.contains(&b_device)).expect("B is listed").id;
    let members = previous.trie_members.iter().filter(|m| m.id != b_id).cloned().collect();
    let record = next_record(&s.chain, &previous, members);
    let mut a_data = s.svc_a.store_of(&s.pid_a).clone();
    a_data.record = Some(record);
    s.svc_a.put(a_data);
    (s, b_id)
}
```

#![cfg(all(feature = "app", feature = "test-support"))]
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]
//! Integration tests: who delivers a message to a node's receive
//! (`check_received`), over the service API, each body delivered by value
//! with its sending Device's key, and a shared `ChainSlots`. Offline — no
//! live chain, no relay.
//!
//! *Stripped 2026-10-21 (T5 of docs/plans/2026-10-21-org-io-domain-api.md):*
//! the commit path these tests drove (`admit_member`, `revoke_member`,
//! `commit_update`, `commit_checked`, `commit_genesis`) is removed. What
//! remains is decided in the check: a revocation from a Device B's record
//! does not list is refused before anything is used, and a Persona's two
//! public keys. The admission and adoption cases come back with
//! verification (T14–T19) and the G2 ports of T60.
//!
//! The gate:
//! `cargo test -p org-node --features app,test-support --test admission_sender`

mod support;
use support::*;

use org_node::error::OrgNodeError;
use org_node::revocation::RevocationNotice;
use org_node::test_fixtures::device_keypair;
use org_node::wire::WireMessage;
use org_node::PersonaId;

// R stands between A and B: B's revocation notice, relayed by R, a Device
// B's record does not list, is refused with `SenderNotListed` before it is
// used, with no chain read; B keeps its record and its Persona.
// *Rewritten 2026-10-07 (S3 T12a)*: was
// `a_revocation_relayed_by_a_non_member_is_still_acted_on`.
// *Cut to its refusal 2026-10-21 (T5):* the notice is the one A's removal of
// B would send (B's identity and a proof of its absence from A's record
// without B), built directly; acting on it from A's own Device was
// `commit_checked`'s, removed (a kept notice is T13's, acted on by T24's
// verification).
// verifies: LLR-kzgjz8
#[test]
fn a_revocation_relayed_by_a_non_member_is_refused() {
    let s = admit_b_directly(setup("revoke-relay"));
    let b_member_id = s.svc_b.list_personas()[0].member_id.expect("B has a member id");
    let b_device = s.b_device_kp.device_key().unwrap();
    let (s, _) = remove_b_directly(s);
    let without_b = trie_of(&rec_of(&s.svc_a, s.org_id));
    let notice = RevocationNotice {
        org_id: s.org_id,
        member_id: b_member_id,
        device: b_device,
        proof: without_b.prove_absent(&b_member_id, &b_device).unwrap(),
    };
    let before = store_bytes("revoke-relay", "b");
    let reads_before = s.svc_b.view.reads();
    let refused = receive_message_from(&s.svc_b, ROGUE_SEED, &WireMessage::Revocation(notice)).map(|_| ());
    assert_eq!(refused, Err(OrgNodeError::SenderNotListed { org_id: s.org_id }));
    assert_eq!(s.svc_b.view.reads(), reads_before, "the refusal reads no chain");
    assert_eq!(s.svc_b.list_orgs().len(), 1, "B keeps its record");
    assert_eq!(s.svc_b.list_personas().len(), 1, "B keeps its Persona");
    assert_eq!(store_bytes("revoke-relay", "b"), before, "nothing written");
}

// LLR-437fvx: org-node hands the app a Persona's two public keys, each from
// its own seed, and no dialling address; an unknown Persona is refused and
// nothing is written. The absence half (no Invite, no Join request, no
// address) is `org_node_holds_no_invitation_exchange` in tests/absences.rs.
// verifies: LLR-437fvx, LLR-ctzkv7
#[test]
fn persona_public_keys_returns_the_personas_two_keys() {
    let s = setup("persona-keys");
    let persona_b = persona_of(&s.svc_b, &s.pid_b);

    let (member_key, device_key) = s.svc_b.persona_public_keys(&s.pid_b).expect("B's own Persona");
    assert_eq!(
        (member_key, device_key),
        (
            persona_b.member_seed_for_test().x25519_keypair().member_key().unwrap(),
            device_keypair(s.svc_b.keychain.seed(&persona_b.device_key)).device_key().unwrap()
        ),
        "each key from the Persona's own seed"
    );
    assert_ne!(member_key.as_bytes(), device_key.as_bytes(), "the two keys must be distinct");

    // Abnormal: a Persona this node does not hold is refused, and nothing is
    // written.
    let before = store_bytes("persona-keys", "b");
    assert!(s.svc_b.persona_public_keys(&PersonaId::new("nobody".into())).is_err());
    assert_eq!(store_bytes("persona-keys", "b"), before, "the refusal writes nothing");
}

```rust
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]
//! The one receive path, by values (SDD-busuj3): `check_received(sender,
//! body)` decodes the body and runs every check that needs no chain state.
//! No endpoint: each body is one built here with `encode_message`, and the
//! sender is a Device key the test names.
//!
//! *Stripped 2026-10-21 (T5 of docs/plans/2026-10-21-org-io-domain-api.md):*
//! `commit_checked` and `CheckedMessage` are removed with the commit path;
//! until T11 gives `check_received` its arms, the check keeps its decode,
//! notice and sender refusals and its acknowledgement decision, which the
//! tests below exercise. The stores are built directly (`support`).

mod support;
use support::*;

use org_members::DevicePublicKey;
use org_node::error::OrgNodeError;
use org_node::revocation::{sign_acknowledgements, RevocationNotice};
use org_node::service::{Checked, OrgService};
use org_node::test_fixtures::{bob_absence_notice, device_keypair};
use org_node::wire::{encode_message, WireMessage};
use org_node::{Envelope, PersonaId, SequenceNumber};

/// The Device of the rogue relay: listed in no record.
fn rogue() -> DevicePublicKey {
    device_keypair(ROGUE_SEED).device_key().unwrap()
}

/// The Device key of `persona_id` on `node`.
fn device_of(node: &Node, persona_id: &PersonaId) -> DevicePublicKey {
    node.persona_public_keys(persona_id).unwrap().1
}

/// The plaintext of every store `svc` holds, as the store encodes it.
fn plaintext(svc: &OrgService) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
    svc.list_personas()
        .iter()
        .map(|persona| postcard::to_allocvec(svc.store_data(&persona.device_key).unwrap()).unwrap())
        .collect()
}

/// B admitted (epoch 2), then A's removal of B (epoch 3, A's record only):
/// the setup and the notice A's removal would send B's Device.
fn removal(tag: &str) -> (Setup, RevocationNotice) {
    let s = admit_b_directly(setup(tag));
    let b_device = s.b_device_kp.device_key().unwrap();
    let (s, b_id) = remove_b_directly(s);
    let proof = trie_of(&rec_of(&s.svc_a, s.org_id)).prove_absent(&b_id, &b_device).unwrap();
    let notice = RevocationNotice { org_id: s.org_id, member_id: b_id, device: b_device, proof };
    (s, notice)
}

// ---- check_received ------------------------------------------------------------

// verifies: LLR-zetn7a
#[test]
fn a_body_that_does_not_decode_is_malformed_and_changes_nothing() {
    let s = setup("rp-malformed");
    let before = (plaintext(&s.svc_b), store_bytes("rp-malformed", "b"));
    for body in [&[][..], &[0xff, 0x00, 0x01][..], &[0x07; 64][..]] {
        assert!(matches!(s.svc_b.check_received(rogue(), body), Err(OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage)));
    }
    assert_eq!((plaintext(&s.svc_b), store_bytes("rp-malformed", "b")), before);
    assert!(s.svc_b.expected_admissions().len() == 1, "the expectation stays");
}

// *Cut to its refusal 2026-10-21 (T5):* the half that showed the same body
// from A's Device passing the check named `Checked::ReadChain`, removed; the
// Organisation-information arm that keeps it is T12's.
// verifies: LLR-2r2fha
#[test]
fn an_update_for_a_held_organisation_from_an_unlisted_sender_is_refused_in_the_check() {
    let s = admit_b_directly(setup("rp-update-unlisted"));
    let update = carrying(Envelope { org_id: s.org_id, parent_seq: SequenceNumber::new(3), delta_bytes: vec![0x01] });
    let body = encode_message(&update).unwrap();
    let before = plaintext(&s.svc_b);
    let reads = s.svc_b.view.reads();
    let refused = s.svc_b.check_received(rogue(), &body).map(|_| ());
    assert_eq!(refused, Err(OrgNodeError::SenderNotListed { org_id: s.org_id }));
    assert_eq!(s.svc_b.view.reads(), reads, "no chain read");
    assert_eq!(plaintext(&s.svc_b), before, "nothing changed");
}

// *Cut to its refusal 2026-10-21 (T5):* as above, the passing half is gone
// until a notice is kept (T13).
// verifies: LLR-kzgjz8, LLR-r7zm39
#[test]
fn a_revocation_from_an_unlisted_sender_is_refused_in_the_check() {
    let (s, notice) = removal("rp-notice-unlisted");
    let body = encode_message(&WireMessage::Revocation(notice)).unwrap();
    let refused = s.svc_b.check_received(rogue(), &body).map(|_| ());
    assert_eq!(refused, Err(OrgNodeError::SenderNotListed { org_id: s.org_id }));
}

// B's acknowledgement of its removal: decided in the check, from the Device
// it names only, and only when the record no longer lists that Device.
// *Adapted 2026-10-21 (T5):* B's acknowledgement is signed with
// `revocation::sign_acknowledgements` over the state of A's removal (built
// directly), as the removed commit path signed it.
// verifies: LLR-3aysup, LLR-5azhry
#[test]
fn an_acknowledgement_is_decided_in_the_check_from_its_named_device_only() {
    let tag = "rp-ack";
    let s = admit_b_directly(setup(tag));
    let members_listing_b = rec_of(&s.svc_a, s.org_id).trie_members;
    let (s, _) = remove_b_directly(s);
    let b_device = s.b_device_kp.device_key().unwrap();
    let state = s.chain.get(&s.org_id).unwrap();
    let b_store = s.svc_b.store_of(&s.pid_b).clone();
    let secret = s.svc_b.keychain.secret(&b_device).unwrap();
    let acknowledgement = sign_acknowledgements(&b_store, s.org_id, &state, vec![secret]).unwrap().remove(0);
    let ack_body = encode_message(&WireMessage::Acknowledgement(acknowledgement.clone())).unwrap();

    let before = plaintext(&s.svc_a);
    match s.svc_a.check_received(b_device, &ack_body) {
        Ok(Checked::Acknowledged(verified)) => assert_eq!(verified.into_inner(), acknowledgement),
        Err(error) => panic!("not decided as an acknowledgement: {error:?}"),
    }
    assert_eq!(plaintext(&s.svc_a), before, "no store change");

    let relayed = s.svc_a.check_received(rogue(), &ack_body).map(|_| ());
    assert_eq!(relayed, Err(OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementNotFromItsDevice { org_id: s.org_id }));

    // A record that still lists B's Device (a store this software never
    // writes, sealed back as org-io would hold it).
    tamper(tag, "a", &s.pid_a, |data| {
        if let Some(record) = data.record.as_mut() {
            record.trie_members = members_listing_b;
        }
    });
    let listing = reopened_service(tag, "a");
    let listed = listing.check_received(b_device, &ack_body).map(|_| ());
    assert_eq!(listed, Err(OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementForListedDevice { org_id: s.org_id }));
}

// PR-q8r32t stays resolved: the `RevocationNotHeld` refusal is reached
// through `check_received`, so it is no unreachable branch.
// *Changed 2026-10-15 (S4 TEST review round 1, finding-10; Seams 1):* the
// second half asserted that revocation.rs constructs the error, which pinned
// the file it is built in; it now drives `check_received` with a notice
// about an Organisation no store holds and observes the refusal.
// *Changed 2026-10-15 (S4 TEST review round 2, finding-5; Seams 1):* the
// first half, a scan of service.rs's source for `RevocationNotHeld {`, is
// dropped; the behaviour is what is asserted.
// *Renamed 2026-10-15 (S4 TEST review round 3, notes):* was
// `no_receive_branch_is_unreachable`.
// verifies: LLR-zetn7a
#[test]
fn an_unheld_organisations_notice_is_refused_as_not_held() {
    let s = setup("rp-no-unreachable");
    let body = encode_message(&WireMessage::Revocation(bob_absence_notice(s.org_id))).unwrap();
    let refused = s.svc_b.check_received(device_of(&s.svc_a, &s.pid_a), &body).map(|_| ());
    assert_eq!(refused, Err(OrgNodeError::RevocationNotHeld { org_id: s.org_id }), "check_received reaches the refusal");
}

#![cfg(all(feature = "app", feature = "test-support"))]
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]
//! The receive path takes no chain state: what it refuses or decides it
//! does without a chain read, observed through a chain that counts its
//! reads.
//!
//! *Stripped 2026-10-21 (T5 of docs/plans/2026-10-21-org-io-domain-api.md):*
//! the commit path whose chain read these tests counted is removed;
//! `check_received` reads no chain at all. What remains: an acknowledgement
//! is decided in the check, and an update from an unlisted Device is
//! refused there. T12 brings the Organisation-information arm, and T60 the
//! revocation refusals (LLR-95av3e), back here.

mod support;

use org_node::error::OrgNodeError;
use org_node::revocation::sign_acknowledgements;
use org_node::service::Checked;
use org_node::wire::{encode_message, WireMessage};
use org_node::{Envelope, SequenceNumber};
use support::*;

/// verifies: LLR-pt32fx, LLR-5azhry, LLR-3aysup
///
/// A's receive path reports B's acknowledgement, sent from B's own Device —
/// `Acknowledged`, decided in the check — with no chain read and no write;
/// an acknowledgement with a forged signature from B's Device is refused,
/// and B's genuine acknowledgement from a random relay is refused with
/// `AcknowledgementNotFromItsDevice`; nothing written. *Adapted 2026-10-21
/// (T5):* B's removal and its acknowledgement are built directly
/// (`support::remove_b_directly`, `revocation::sign_acknowledgements`).
#[test]
fn an_acknowledgement_is_checked_and_reported() {
    let (s, counting) = setup_counted("ack-report");
    let s = admit_b_directly(s);
    let (s, _) = remove_b_directly(s);
    let b_device = s.b_device_kp.device_key().unwrap();
    let state = s.chain.get(&s.org_id).unwrap();
    let secret = s.svc_b.keychain.secret(&b_device).unwrap();
    let acknowledgement =
        sign_acknowledgements(s.svc_b.store_of(&s.pid_b), s.org_id, &state, vec![secret]).unwrap().remove(0);
    let before = store_bytes("ack-report", "a");
    let reads_before = counting.reads();
    let b_seed = s.svc_b.keychain.seed(&b_device);

    let Checked::Acknowledged(verified) =
        receive_message_from(&s.svc_a, b_seed, &WireMessage::Acknowledgement(acknowledgement.clone())).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(verified.into_inner(), acknowledgement);

    let not_from_its_device = Err(OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementNotFromItsDevice { org_id: s.org_id });
    let relayed = receive_message_from(&s.svc_a, rand::random(), &WireMessage::Acknowledgement(acknowledgement.clone()));
    assert_eq!(relayed.map(|_| ()), not_from_its_device);

    let mut forged = acknowledgement;
    forged.signature.0[0] ^= 1;
    let refused = receive_message_from(&s.svc_a, b_seed, &WireMessage::Acknowledgement(forged));
    assert!(matches!(refused, Err(OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementSignatureInvalid { .. })), "{refused:?}");

    assert_eq!((counting.reads() - reads_before, store_bytes("ack-report", "a")), (0, before));
}

// REQ-uk9rw7 (supersedes REQ-ztdza4), at the value boundary: an update about
// a held Organisation from a Device the current record does not list is
// refused by the check itself, which takes no chain state; nothing is
// written. *Cut to its refusal 2026-10-21 (T5):* the half that showed the
// same update from A's Device naming the Organisation to read went with
// `Checked::ReadChain`; T12 keeps it as a provisional organisation.
// verifies: REQ-uk9rw7, REQ-ztdza4, LLR-2r2fha
#[test]
fn an_update_from_an_unlisted_device_is_refused_before_any_chain_state_is_asked_for() {
    let (s, counting) = setup_counted("unlisted-value");
    let s = admit_b_directly(s);
    let update = carrying(Envelope { org_id: s.org_id, parent_seq: SequenceNumber::new(3), delta_bytes: vec![0x01] });
    let body = encode_message(&update).unwrap();
    let on_disk = store_bytes("unlisted-value", "b");
    let held = rec_of(&s.svc_b, s.org_id);
    let reads_before = counting.reads();

    let stranger = org_node::test_fixtures::device_key(0x6d);
    assert!(!held.trie_members.iter().any(|member| member.device_keys.contains(&stranger)));
    let not_listed = Err(OrgNodeError::SenderNotListed { org_id: s.org_id });
    assert_eq!(s.svc_b.check_received(stranger, &body).map(|_| ()), not_listed);

    assert_eq!(counting.reads(), reads_before, "the check reads no chain");
    let after = rec_of(&s.svc_b, s.org_id);
    assert_eq!((after.epoch, after.root_hash, after.last_seq), (held.epoch, held.root_hash, held.last_seq));
    assert_eq!(store_bytes("unlisted-value", "b"), on_disk, "nothing written");
}

Replace `fn each_save_draws_a_fresh_nonce` with:

```rust
// Nonce freshness. The falsifiability sweep of 2026-10-03 replaced
// `rng.fill_bytes(&mut nonce)` with nothing — a fixed all-zero nonce on every
// save — and the whole suite stayed green: nothing here was asserting that the
// nonce ever changed. XChaCha20-Poly1305 does not survive nonce reuse under
// the same key, and the key is derived from the Persona's device secret, so
// it IS the same key across seals of one store. This case is what makes that
// mutation red.
// *Moved 2026-10-15 (S4 TEST review round 1, finding-5):* the seals are the
// writes four calls of one operation return on one open store, not
// `seal_for_test`'s. *2026-10-21 (T5):* the operation is `build_invite`.
// verifies: REQ-hzm4kt, LLR-8mfjey
#[test]
fn each_save_draws_a_fresh_nonce() {
    let mut data = empty_store(persona([1u8; 32], [2u8; 32]));
    data.persona.org_id = Some(OrgId::new(UNNAMED_ORG));
    let mut service = OrgService::new(vec![store_for_test(&device_secret([2u8; 32]), data)]).unwrap();

    let mut nonces = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..4 {
        let (_, write) = service.build_invite(&mut OsRng, OrgId::new(UNNAMED_ORG), "Acme", "Carol").unwrap();
        nonces.push(write.sealed.as_bytes()[..24].to_vec());
    }

    for (i, a) in nonces.iter().enumerate() {
        for (j, b) in nonces.iter().enumerate() {
            if i != j {
                assert_ne!(a, b, "saves {i} and {j} reused a nonce");
            }
        }
    }
    // And none of them is the all-zero nonce a dropped draw would leave.
    assert!(nonces.iter().all(|n| n.iter().any(|b| *b != 0)));
}
```

/// the scan of the retired removal item. *Narrowed 2026-10-21 (T5 of
/// docs/plans/2026-10-21-org-io-domain-api.md):* `forget_organisation`,
/// `OrgService::adopt` and the `orgs` list are removed, so `drop_store` is
/// the one exemption and `stores` the one collection; T27 rewrites this over
/// `into_removed` and `acknowledgement_accepted` (LLR-9jn3z8).
/// verifies: LLR-jd82t6
#[test]
fn only_the_removal_step_adopt_and_drop_store_remove_records_or_stores() {
    let removing_methods =
        ["retain(", "retain_mut(", "remove(", "swap_remove(", "clear()", "drain(", "truncate(", "pop()", "split_off(", "dedup"];
    let service = code_of(&std::fs::read_to_string(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src/service.rs")).unwrap());
    let removes_from = |body: &str, collection: &str| {
        let body = squeezed(body);
        removing_methods.iter().any(|method| !identifier_occurrences(&body, &format!("{collection}.{method}")).is_empty())
    };
    let drop_store = &service[service.find("fn drop_store(").expect("OrgService::drop_store")..];
    let drop_store = &drop_store[..drop_store.find("\n    }\n").expect("the end of drop_store")];
    assert!(removes_from(drop_store, "stores"), "drop_store removes a store");
    for (path, text) in sources() {
        let mut code = code_of(&text);
        if path.ends_with("service.rs") {
            code = without_function(&code, "drop_store");
        }
        let squeezed_code = squeezed(&code);
        let file = path.display();
        for collection in ["stores"] {
            for method in removing_methods {
                let call = format!("{collection}.{method}");
                assert!(identifier_occurrences(&squeezed_code, &call).is_empty(), "{file} calls `{call}` (LLR-jd82t6)");
            }
            for binding in [format!("{collection}:"), format!("{collection}=")] {
                for offset in identifier_occurrences(&squeezed_code, &binding) {
                    let value = expression_from(&squeezed_code, offset + binding.len());
                    if binding.ends_with('=') && value.starts_with('=') {
                        continue; // a comparison, `==`
                    }
                    assert!(
                        !value.contains(".filter(") && !value.contains(".retain"),
                        "{file} rebuilds `{collection}` through a filter: `{binding}{value}` (LLR-jd82t6)"
                    );
                    if binding.ends_with('=') {
                        for empty in ["Vec::new()", "vec![]", "Default::default()"] {
                            assert!(!value.contains(empty), "{file} empties `{collection}`: `{binding}{value}` (LLR-jd82t6)");
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            for swap in ["mem::take(", "mem::replace("] {
                for offset in squeezed_code.match_indices(swap).map(|(offset, _)| offset) {
                    let argument = expression_from(&squeezed_code, offset + swap.len());
                    assert!(!argument.ends_with(collection), "{file} takes `{collection}` out with `{swap}{argument}` (LLR-jd82t6)");
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

#[test]
fn two_services_over_one_set_of_chain_slots_see_the_same_state() {
    let chain = ChainSlots::new();
    let other_view = chain.clone();
    let mut svc = Node::new(open_store("lifecycle-two", "a"), chain.clone());
    let other = Node::new(open_store("lifecycle-two", "b"), other_view.clone());
    let pid = svc.create_persona(&mut OsRng, h("s"), nm("S"), sn("T")).unwrap();
    let org = found(&mut svc, &chain, &pid);
    let record = rec_of(&svc, org);
    assert!(other.list_orgs().is_empty(), "the other service holds no record");
    let seen = other_view.get(&org).expect("the other view sees the slot");
    assert_eq!((seen.root_hash, seen.epoch), (record.root_hash, record.epoch));
}

    assert_eq!((invite.org_name.as_str(), invite.org_id, invite.invitee_name.as_str()), ("Acme Co-op", org, "Bob Builder"));

/// names the Organisation (in `OrgId`'s `Debug` form, as the existing
/// variants do; `OrgId` has no `Display`).
#[test]
fn the_ten_new_variants_are_distinct_and_name_the_organisation() {
    let org_id = OrgId::new([7; 20]);
    let organisation_name = format!("{org_id:?}");
    let errors = all_new(org_id);
    for (index, first) in errors.iter().enumerate() {
        for second in errors.iter().skip(index + 1) {
            assert_ne!(first.to_string(), second.to_string());
        }
        assert!(first.to_string().contains(&organisation_name), "{first} names the Organisation");
    }
}

///
/// Abnormal: the stale-state refusal names both epochs; the proof refusal

#[test]
fn stale_state_names_both_epochs_and_the_proof_refusal_names_its_cause() {
    let org_id = OrgId::new([7; 20]);

}

Replace `fn check_text` with:

```rust
/// A round trip: whatever parses encodes back to text that parses to it.
fn check_text(text: &str) {
    match Invite::parse(text) {
        Ok(invite) => {
            let again = Invite::parse(&invite.encode().unwrap_or_default());
            assert!(again.as_ref().is_ok_and(|parsed| parsed == &invite), "an Invite that parses round-trips");
        }
        Err(error) => names_a_field(error, &INVITE_FIELDS),
    }
}
```

fn records_and_wire_messages_never_render_secret_bytes() {
    let (member, device, private) = (sentinel(0xd0), sentinel(0x10), org_private());
    let p = persona(member, device);
    let o = org(private);
    let data = StoreData { record: Some(o.clone()), ..StoreData::new(p.clone()) };
    let w = wire(private);
    for rendered in [format!("{p:?}"), format!("{p:#?}"), format!("{data:?}"), format!("{data:#?}")] {
        assert_not_rendered(&rendered, &member, "member seed");
        assert_not_rendered(&rendered, &device, "device seed");
        // *Adapted 2026-10-08 (S4, task T3):* no device seed is held, so none
        // is rendered, redacted or not; the Member seed's marker stays.
        assert!(rendered.contains("MemberSeed([REDACTED])"));
    }
    for rendered in [format!("{o:?}"), format!("{o:#?}"), format!("{data:?}"), format!("{data:#?}"), format!("{w:?}"), format!("{w:#?}")] {
        assert_not_rendered(&rendered, &private, "Organisation private key");
        assert!(rendered.contains("OrgPrivateKey([REDACTED])"), "{rendered}");
    }
    for rendered in [format!("{o:?}"), format!("{o:#?}"), format!("{data:?}"), format!("{data:#?}")] {

### T6 — org-node: the Person store

**Files touched:** org-node/src/person_store.rs (new), org-node/src/lib.rs, org-node/tests/person_store.rs
**Parallel:** yes (with T2–T4, T7–T10; after T5)
**Implements:** LLR-wqu26s, LLR-73sgz2, LLR-5uf4u2
**Tests (verifies: annotations):**
- `org-node/tests/person_store.rs::create_parses_the_name_and_surname_and_holds_no_handle` — `verifies: LLR-wqu26s`
- `org-node/tests/person_store.rs::create_refuses_an_invalid_name_or_surname_naming_the_field_and_creates_nothing` — `verifies: LLR-wqu26s`
- `org-node/tests/person_store.rs::a_sealed_person_store_unseals_to_the_same_person` — `verifies: LLR-73sgz2`

**Out-of-force tests handled:** none
**Intent:** `PersonStore` and `PersonData { person, device_key, person_key }` in the new `person_store.rs`, created from a name and surname with keys drawn from the caller's `rng`, sealed with the Persona store's AEAD and nonce layout under the info string `b"ods/person-store/v1"`, and re-exported with `Name`, `Surname`, `Handle`, `DevicePublicKey` and `PersonPublicKey` from `org_node::` so that org-io names no `person::` path.
*Settled at assembly:* the Person key pair's secret half is kept (fix item 19, ledger `84a31b1a`: LLR-wqu26s, LLR-73sgz2, SDD-27p679 amended): `PersonData` holds `person_seed: MemberSeed`, crate-private and redacted under `Debug` as a Persona record's `member_seed` is, sealed with the rest of the Person file and read back unchanged; `person_key` is the seed's X25519 public key.

**Steps:**

1. **Write the failing tests.** `org-node/tests/person_store.rs` (T1's stub, whole file): creation parses the name and surname (NFC), draws from the source given, holds the Person with its one Device and its Person key and no Handle; a refused name or surname names its field and draws nothing; a sealed Person store reopens to the same data with a fresh nonce per seal and refuses another Device's secret, a short file and a flipped bit as a Persona store does; a Persona store's bytes and a Person store's never open as each other under one secret; every Person and Member type is named under `org_node::` and is `person`'s or `org-members`' own type.

```rust
#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]
//! The Person store (SDD-27p679): the user's own Person, created from a name
//! and a surname with keys drawn from the caller's random source
//! (LLR-wqu26s), sealed and opened under its own key label (LLR-73sgz2), and
//! named under `org_node::` paths (LLR-5uf4u2). T6 of
//! docs/plans/2026-10-21-org-io-domain-api.md.

use org_node::store::{PersonaStore, SealedStore, StoreData, StoreRefusal};
use org_node::test_fixtures::{device_secret, persona_record, seal_for_test, store_for_test};
use org_node::{DevicePublicKey, Handle, Name, OrgNodeError, Person, PersonData, PersonPublicKey, PersonStore, Surname};
use rand::rngs::OsRng;

/// A random source that counts the bytes drawn from it, so a test can show a
/// refusal drew nothing.
struct CountingRng {
    drawn: usize,
}

impl rand::RngCore for CountingRng {
    fn next_u32(&mut self) -> u32 {
        self.drawn += 4;
        rand::RngCore::next_u32(&mut OsRng)
    }
    fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64 {
        self.drawn += 8;
        rand::RngCore::next_u64(&mut OsRng)
    }
    fn fill_bytes(&mut self, dest: &mut [u8]) {
        self.drawn += dest.len();
        rand::RngCore::fill_bytes(&mut OsRng, dest)
    }
    fn try_fill_bytes(&mut self, dest: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), rand::Error> {
        self.fill_bytes(dest);
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl rand::CryptoRng for CountingRng {}

/// The seed bytes of `secret`, read back as org-io's keychain would.
fn reopened_secret(secret: &org_node::DeviceSecret) -> org_node::DeviceSecret {
    let mut bytes = vec![];
    secret
        .lend_to_keychain(|seed| {
            bytes.extend_from_slice(seed);
            Ok::<(), std::convert::Infallible>(())
        })
        .unwrap();
    org_node::DeviceSecret::from_keychain_bytes(zeroize::Zeroizing::new(bytes)).unwrap()
}

// Normal: the name and surname are parsed (NFC, as stored), the Person holds
// them, its one Device and its Person key, and no Handle; the secret
// returned is the Person's Device's; the keys come from the source given.
// verifies: LLR-wqu26s
#[test]
fn create_parses_the_name_and_surname_and_holds_no_handle() {
    let mut rng = CountingRng { drawn: 0 };
    let (store, secret, _) = PersonStore::create(&mut rng, "Jose\u{0301}", "Nun\u{0303}ez").unwrap();
    assert!(rng.drawn >= 64, "a Device seed and a Person key pair are drawn from the source given");
    let data: &PersonData = store.data();
    assert_eq!((data.person.name().as_str(), data.person.surname().as_str()), ("Jos\u{e9}", "Nu\u{f1}ez"));
    assert_eq!(data.device_key, secret.device_key());
    assert_eq!(store.device_key(), secret.device_key());
    assert_eq!(data.person.person_key(), Some(&data.person_key));
    assert_eq!(data.person.devices().devices(), [data.device_key].as_slice());
    assert_ne!(data.person_key.as_bytes(), data.device_key.as_bytes());
    assert_eq!(
        data.person_seed_for_test().x25519_keypair().member_key().unwrap(),
        data.person_key,
        "the Person key is the kept Person seed's public half"
    );
    let rendered = format!("{data:?}");
    assert!(!rendered.contains("Handle") && !rendered.contains("handle"), "no Handle: {rendered}");
    let seed_bytes = format!("{:?}", data.person_seed_for_test().expose_secret());
    assert!(!rendered.contains(&seed_bytes), "the Person seed is redacted: {rendered}");
    let (other, other_secret, _) = PersonStore::create(&mut OsRng, "Ann", "Lee").unwrap();
    assert_ne!(other.data().person_key, data.person_key, "drawn, not derived");
    assert_ne!(other_secret.device_key(), secret.device_key());
}

// Abnormal: a name or a surname its type refuses is refused naming the
// field, before any draw from the source; no store is created.
// verifies: LLR-wqu26s
#[test]
fn create_refuses_an_invalid_name_or_surname_naming_the_field_and_creates_nothing() {
    let over = "a".repeat(129);
    for (name, surname, field) in [(over.as_str(), "Lee", "person.name"), ("Ann", over.as_str(), "person.surname")] {
        let mut rng = CountingRng { drawn: 0 };
        let refused = PersonStore::create(&mut rng, name, surname).err().expect("must be refused");
        assert!(matches!(&refused, OrgNodeError::InvalidField { field: f, .. } if *f == field), "{refused:?}");
        assert_eq!(rng.drawn, 0, "{field}: nothing drawn, nothing created");
    }
    let refused = PersonStore::create(&mut OsRng, &over, &over).err().expect("must be refused");
    assert!(matches!(&refused, OrgNodeError::InvalidField { field: "person.name", .. }), "the first in order: {refused:?}");
}

// Normal: a sealed Person store unseals, with its secret, to the same Person
// and keys; each seal draws a fresh nonce. Abnormal: another Device's
// secret, too few bytes and a flipped bit are refused as a Persona store's
// are.
// verifies: LLR-73sgz2
#[test]
fn a_sealed_person_store_unseals_to_the_same_person() {
    let (store, secret, sealed) = PersonStore::create(&mut OsRng, "Ann", "Lee").unwrap();
    let reopened = PersonStore::unseal(&sealed, store.device_key(), reopened_secret(&secret)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(reopened.data(), store.data());
    assert_eq!(
        reopened.data().person_seed_for_test(),
        store.data().person_seed_for_test(),
        "the Person seed is sealed with the rest and read back unchanged"
    );
    let again = store.seal(&mut OsRng).unwrap();
    assert_ne!(again.as_bytes()[..24], sealed.as_bytes()[..24], "a fresh nonce");
    assert_eq!(PersonStore::unseal(&again, store.device_key(), reopened_secret(&secret)).unwrap().data(), store.data());

    let other = device_secret([0x51; 32]);
    assert_eq!(
        PersonStore::unseal(&sealed, store.device_key(), other).err(),
        Some(OrgNodeError::DeviceSecretMismatch)
    );
    let short = SealedStore::from_bytes(vec![0; 39]);
    assert_eq!(
        PersonStore::unseal(&short, store.device_key(), reopened_secret(&secret)).err(),
        Some(OrgNodeError::StoreRefused(StoreRefusal::TooShort))
    );
    let mut flipped = sealed.as_bytes().to_vec();
    flipped[30] ^= 1;
    assert_eq!(
        PersonStore::unseal(&SealedStore::from_bytes(flipped), store.device_key(), reopened_secret(&secret)).err(),
        Some(OrgNodeError::StoreRefused(StoreRefusal::NotAuthentic))
    );
}

// Abnormal: under one Device secret, a Persona store's sealed bytes do not
// open as a Person store, nor a Person store's as a Persona store: the two
// keys are derived under different labels.
// verifies: LLR-73sgz2
#[test]
fn a_persona_store_never_opens_as_a_person_store_or_the_reverse() {
    let (person, secret, person_sealed) = PersonStore::create(&mut OsRng, "Ann", "Lee").unwrap();
    let device_key: DevicePublicKey = person.device_key();
    let mut persona = persona_record("p1", 0x11, 0);
    persona.device_key = device_key;
    let persona_store = store_for_test(&reopened_secret(&secret), StoreData::new(persona));
    let persona_sealed = seal_for_test(&persona_store, &mut OsRng).sealed;
    assert_eq!(
        PersonStore::unseal(&persona_sealed, device_key, reopened_secret(&secret)).err(),
        Some(OrgNodeError::StoreRefused(StoreRefusal::NotAuthentic)),
        "a Persona store is not a Person store"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        PersonaStore::unseal(&person_sealed, device_key, reopened_secret(&secret)).err(),
        Some(OrgNodeError::StoreRefused(StoreRefusal::NotAuthentic)),
        "a Person store is not a Persona store"
    );
    assert!(PersonaStore::unseal(&persona_sealed, device_key, reopened_secret(&secret)).is_ok());
}

It reuses `store::seal_bytes` and `store::parse_field`; the derivation is its own, so `store.rs` is untouched.

```rust
//! The Person store (SDD-27p679): the user's own Person, kept apart from
//! every Persona — a `person::Person` and the Person's own DevicePublicKey
//! and PersonPublicKey — sealed with the Person's own Device seed exactly as
//! a Persona store is (LLR-bg538c's AEAD and nonce layout), under its own
//! HKDF label, so a Persona store's bytes never open as a Person store or
//! the reverse (LLR-73sgz2). org-node names no path and touches no file.
use chacha20poly1305::aead::{Aead, KeyInit};
use chacha20poly1305::{XChaCha20Poly1305, XNonce};
use hkdf::Hkdf;
use person::{DeviceSlots, Person};
use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use sha2::Sha256;
use zeroize::Zeroizing;

use org_members::{DevicePublicKey, Name, PersonPublicKey, Surname};

use crate::error::{OrgNodeError, StoreRefusal};
use crate::keys::DeviceSecret;
use crate::store::{parse_field, seal_bytes, SealedStore};
use crate::types::MemberSeed;

/// The HKDF info string of the Person store key (LLR-73sgz2): not the
/// Persona store's `ods/persona-store/v1`.
const PERSON_STORE_KEY_INFO: &[u8] = b"ods/person-store/v1";

/// The nonce, then the authentication tag: the shortest sealed store.
const NONCE_LENGTH: usize = 24;
const TAG_LENGTH: usize = 16;

/// The Person, its two public keys and the Person key pair's secret seed
/// (LLR-wqu26s): no Handle. The seed is crate-private and redacted under
/// `Debug`, as a Persona record's member seed is.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PersonData {
    pub person: Person,
    pub device_key: DevicePublicKey,
    pub person_key: PersonPublicKey,
    pub(crate) person_seed: MemberSeed,
}

#[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
impl PersonData {
    /// The kept Person seed (test builds only).
    pub fn person_seed_for_test(&self) -> &MemberSeed {
        &self.person_seed
    }
}

/// `PersonData` as the store encodes it: the Person's name and surname, its
/// two keys, then the Person seed. The Person value is rebuilt on unseal.
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct PersonDataEncoding<'a> {
    name: &'a Name,
    surname: &'a Surname,
    device_key: &'a DevicePublicKey,
    person_key: &'a PersonPublicKey,
    person_seed: &'a MemberSeed,
}

/// `PersonData` as decoded, before parsing (`person.*`, LLR-73sgz2).
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct RawPersonData {
    name: String,
    surname: String,
    device_key: [u8; 32],
    person_key: [u8; 32],
    person_seed: MemberSeed,
}

/// The Person built from parsed values: one device, its key, and the
/// Person key (`person`'s group-key rules).
fn person_of(name: Name, surname: Surname, device_key: DevicePublicKey, person_key: PersonPublicKey) -> Result<Person, OrgNodeError> {
    let devices = parse_field("person", DeviceSlots::parse(vec![device_key]))?;
    parse_field("person", Person::new(name, surname, Some(person_key), devices))
}

impl TryFrom<RawPersonData> for PersonData {
    type Error = OrgNodeError;

    fn try_from(raw: RawPersonData) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
        let name = parse_field("person.name", Name::parse(&raw.name))?;
        let surname = parse_field("person.surname", Surname::parse(&raw.surname))?;
        let device_key = parse_field("person.device_key", DevicePublicKey::parse(&raw.device_key))?;
        let person_key = parse_field("person.person_key", PersonPublicKey::parse(&raw.person_key))?;
        Ok(Self { person: person_of(name, surname, device_key, person_key)?, device_key, person_key, person_seed: raw.person_seed })
    }
}

/// The user's open Person store: the store key, held only as the cipher,
/// and the data. No path: org-node touches no file.
pub struct PersonStore {
    key: XChaCha20Poly1305,
    data: PersonData,
}

/// HKDF-SHA-256 of the device seed, salted with the Device public key, under
/// `PERSON_STORE_KEY_INFO`: LLR-2qqqx6's derivation with the Person store's
/// label (LLR-73sgz2).
fn cipher(secret: &DeviceSecret, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> Result<XChaCha20Poly1305, OrgNodeError> {
    let mut key = Zeroizing::new([0u8; 32]);
    Hkdf::<Sha256>::new(Some(device_key.as_bytes()), secret.seed())
        .expand(PERSON_STORE_KEY_INFO, key.as_mut())
        .map_err(|_| OrgNodeError::Chain("person store key derivation failed".into()))?;
    XChaCha20Poly1305::new_from_slice(key.as_ref()).map_err(|error| OrgNodeError::Chain(format!("bad key length: {error}")))
}

impl PersonStore {
    /// A new Person store (LLR-wqu26s): the name and surname parsed
    /// (`InvalidField` `person.name` / `person.surname`, before any draw,
    /// creating nothing), then a fresh Device seed and a Person key pair drawn
    /// from `rng`; returns the store, the Device secret by value for org-io's
    /// keychain (org-node keeps no copy) and the store sealed.
    pub fn create<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
        rng: &mut R,
        name: &str,
        surname: &str,
    ) -> Result<(PersonStore, DeviceSecret, SealedStore), OrgNodeError> {
        let name = parse_field("person.name", Name::parse(name))?;
        let surname = parse_field("person.surname", Surname::parse(surname))?;
        let secret = DeviceSecret::generate(rng);
        let mut seed = Zeroizing::new([0u8; 32]);
        rng.fill_bytes(seed.as_mut());
        let person_seed = MemberSeed::from(*seed);
        let person_key = person_seed.x25519_keypair().member_key()?;
        let device_key = secret.device_key();
        let data =
            PersonData { person: person_of(name, surname, device_key, person_key)?, device_key, person_key, person_seed };
        let store = PersonStore { key: cipher(&secret, &device_key)?, data };
        let sealed = store.seal(rng)?;
        Ok((store, secret, sealed))
    }

    /// This store, sealed with a fresh 24-byte nonce (LLR-73sgz2).
    pub fn seal<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(&self, rng: &mut R) -> Result<SealedStore, OrgNodeError> {
        let plaintext = Zeroizing::new(
            postcard::to_allocvec(&PersonDataEncoding {
                name: self.data.person.name(),
                surname: self.data.person.surname(),
                device_key: &self.data.device_key,
                person_key: &self.data.person_key,
                person_seed: &self.data.person_seed,
            })
            .map_err(|error| OrgNodeError::Chain(format!("person store encode: {error}")))?,
        );
        seal_bytes(&self.key, &plaintext, rng)
    }

    /// Open the sealed Person store of `device_key` with its secret, which is
    /// consumed, refusing as `PersonaStore::unseal` refuses (LLR-73sgz2): a
    /// secret of another Device (`DeviceSecretMismatch`), too few bytes
    /// (`TooShort`), a ciphertext that does not authenticate under the Person
    /// store key (`NotAuthentic`: a Persona store's bytes among them), a
    /// plaintext that does not decode (`Undecodable`) or holds a value its
    /// type refuses (`InvalidField`, `person.*`), and a store naming another
    /// Device (`DeviceSecretMismatch`).
    pub fn unseal(sealed: &SealedStore, device_key: DevicePublicKey, secret: DeviceSecret) -> Result<Self, OrgNodeError> {
        if secret.device_key() != device_key {
            return Err(OrgNodeError::DeviceSecretMismatch);
        }
        let bytes = sealed.as_bytes();
        if bytes.len() < NONCE_LENGTH + TAG_LENGTH {
            return Err(OrgNodeError::StoreRefused(StoreRefusal::TooShort));
        }
        let key = cipher(&secret, &device_key)?;
        drop(secret);
        let (nonce, ciphertext) = bytes.split_at(NONCE_LENGTH);
        let plaintext = Zeroizing::new(
            key.decrypt(XNonce::from_slice(nonce), ciphertext)
                .map_err(|_| OrgNodeError::StoreRefused(StoreRefusal::NotAuthentic))?,
        );
        let raw: RawPersonData =
            postcard::from_bytes(&plaintext).map_err(|_| OrgNodeError::StoreRefused(StoreRefusal::Undecodable))?;
        let data = PersonData::try_from(raw)?;
        if data.device_key != device_key {
            return Err(OrgNodeError::DeviceSecretMismatch);
        }
        Ok(Self { key, data })
    }

    /// The Person's DevicePublicKey.
    pub fn device_key(&self) -> DevicePublicKey {
        self.data.device_key
    }

    pub fn data(&self) -> &PersonData {
        &self.data
    }
}
```

**Intent:** `WireMessage` gains `AdmissionRequest { org_id, invite_id, name, surname, preferred_handles, member_key, device_key, addresses }` (3), `OrganisationRequest { org_id, addresses }` (4) and `Organisation { org_id, epoch, record_snapshot, org_private_key }` (5) beside the three existing kinds; `decode_message` refuses unknown indices, short bodies and leftovers; `peek_admission_request` reads the first 1+20+32 bytes only. `check_received` refuses the three new kinds as `MalformedMessage` until T11/T22 give them arms; only `AdmissionRequest` carries an invite identifier.
Field type chosen (later tasks must match): the two requests carry their addresses as the strings the sender gave (`addresses: Vec<String>`), not as `EndpointAddresses`, so that a list the parse refuses reaches `check_received` and is refused there as `InvalidField { field: "request.addresses" }` (LLR-h4gwns), not as `MalformedMessage` at decode; every other field is its parsed type (`Name`, `Surname`, `Handle`, `PersonPublicKey`, `DevicePublicKey`, `OrgPrivateKey`), whose own decoding refuses a bad value as `MalformedMessage`. `InviteId` is `ids::InviteId` (moved there in T5 so this ungated module can name it).

```rust
/// verifies: LLR-xr88a8
///
/// Normal: each of the six kinds round-trips with its variant index and its
/// payload, as the same kind. Abnormal: a body of any kind with a leftover
/// byte, or the body of any kind under an unknown variant index (every first
/// byte from 6 to 0xFF), is `Malformed`, without a panic.
/// *Rewritten 2026-10-21 (T7):* was
/// `exactly_three_kinds_round_trip_and_an_unknown_kind_or_leftover_bytes_are_refused`.
#[test]
fn exactly_six_kinds_round_trip_and_an_unknown_kind_or_leftover_bytes_are_refused() {
    for (message, index) in &the_six_kinds() {
        let body = body_of(message);
        assert_eq!(body[0], *index);
        let decoded = decode_message(&body).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(&decoded, message, "kind {index} decodes to the message it was encoded from");
        assert_eq!(std::mem::discriminant(&decoded), std::mem::discriminant(message), "kind {index} as the same kind");

        let mut leftover = body.clone();
        leftover.push(0);
        assert!(
            matches!(decode_message(&leftover), Err(OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage)),
            "kind {index} with a leftover byte"
        );

        for unknown_index in 6u8..=0xFF {
            let mut unknown_kind = body.clone();
            unknown_kind[0] = unknown_index;
            assert!(
                matches!(decode_message(&unknown_kind), Err(OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage)),
                "kind {index}'s payload under index {unknown_index}"
            );
        }
    }
}

/// verifies: LLR-xr88a8, REQ-zxgd46
///
/// Abnormal: in every kind that carries one, a key field that is not 32
/// bytes — the Organisation private key of Organisation information and of
/// an organisation answer, an admission request's Member-as-a-group key and
/// DevicePublicKey — makes the body not decode, without a panic.
#[test]
fn a_key_field_that_is_not_32_bytes_does_not_decode() {
    // Organisation information and an answer: the key is last; 31 bytes of
    // it, or 33.
    for message in [sample_msg(), sample_organisation()] {
        let body = body_of(&message);
        let short = &body[..body.len() - 1];
        assert!(matches!(decode_message(short), Err(OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage)), "31 key bytes");
        let mut long = body.clone();
        long.push(0x77);
        assert!(matches!(decode_message(&long), Err(OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage)), "33 key bytes");
    }
    // An admission request whose Member-as-a-group key or DevicePublicKey is
    // 31 bytes: the tuple after the Handles is re-encoded with one byte less.
    let WireMessage::AdmissionRequest { org_id, invite_id, name, surname, preferred_handles, member_key, device_key, addresses } =
        sample_admission_request()
    else {
        unreachable!()
    };
    let head = postcard::to_allocvec(&(3u8, org_id, invite_id, name, surname, preferred_handles)).unwrap();
    for (member, device) in [
        (member_key.as_bytes()[..31].to_vec(), device_key.as_bytes().to_vec()),
        (member_key.as_bytes().to_vec(), device_key.as_bytes()[..31].to_vec()),
    ] {
        let mut body = head.clone();
        body.extend(member);
        body.extend(device);
        body.extend(postcard::to_allocvec(&addresses).unwrap());
        assert!(matches!(decode_message(&body), Err(OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage)), "a 31-byte key");
    }
}
