   - New `org-node/src/removal.rs`. It defines the removed form, its decode mirror with each key and address
     list re-parsed under a `removed.*` field, and `StoreData::into_removed`.
     ```rust
     //! SDD-z4m57w: the node's own removal and what it keeps. A store whose Persona verified its own
     //! removal holds only the signed acknowledgements, their recipients' keys and addresses and the time of
     //! the verification (LLR-2d5a7m, LLR-6zaeb6). Values only: no file, no keychain, no clock.
     use org_members::{DevicePublicKey, MemberId, RootHash};
     use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

     use crate::error::OrgNodeError;
     use crate::ids::OrgId;
     use crate::invitation::EndpointAddresses;
     use crate::revocation::{Acknowledgement, Signature64};
     use crate::store::{parse_field, StoreData};
     use crate::types::Epoch;
     use crate::verify_org::VerificationTime;

     /// A Persona store's plaintext (LLR-6zaeb6): postcard writes the variant index, then the fields.
     /// `Serialize` in test builds only, as `StoreData`'s; `Deserialize` through T5's `StoreData` and
     /// `RemovedStore`'s raw mirrors (used by T26's pins; `unseal` decodes each form itself).
     #[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
     #[cfg_attr(feature = "test-support", derive(Serialize))]
     pub enum StoreContent {
         /// Index 0: the Persona's view of its Organisation.
         Active(StoreData),
         /// Index 1: what is left after the Persona's own removal.
         Removed(RemovedStore),
     }

     #[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
     impl PartialEq for StoreContent {
         /// Compared by encoding (test builds only): `StoreData` holds secret types and has no `PartialEq`.
         fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
             postcard::to_allocvec(self).ok() == postcard::to_allocvec(other).ok()
         }
     }

     /// The removed store (LLR-6zaeb6): in this order the Organisation, the time of the verification that
     /// found the removal, and the acknowledgements still to deliver.
     #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
     #[serde(try_from = "RawRemovedStore")]
     pub struct RemovedStore {
         pub org_id: OrgId,
         pub verified_at: VerificationTime,
         pub acknowledgements: Vec<KeptAcknowledgement>,
     }

     /// One acknowledgement kept for one recipient, with that recipient's addresses when the store kept any
     /// (LLR-6zaeb6, LLR-vq5d5n).
     #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
     pub struct KeptAcknowledgement {
         pub ack: Acknowledgement,
         pub recipient: DevicePublicKey,
         pub recipient_addresses: Option<EndpointAddresses>,
     }

     /// The removed store as decoded, before parsing (LLR-6zaeb6; the `Raw…` rule of LLR-8bum44).
     #[derive(Deserialize)]
     pub(crate) struct RawRemovedStore {
         org_id: OrgId,
         verified_at: VerificationTime,
         acknowledgements: Vec<RawKeptAcknowledgement>,
     }

     #[derive(Deserialize)]
     pub(crate) struct RawKeptAcknowledgement {
         ack: RawAcknowledgement,
         recipient: [u8; 32],
         recipient_addresses: Option<Vec<String>>,
     }

     #[derive(Deserialize)]
     pub(crate) struct RawAcknowledgement {
         org_id: OrgId,
         member_id: MemberId,
         device: [u8; 32],
         epoch: Epoch,
         root: RootHash,
         signature: Signature64,
     }

     impl TryFrom<RawRemovedStore> for RemovedStore {
         type Error = OrgNodeError;

         fn try_from(raw: RawRemovedStore) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
             let acknowledgements = raw
                 .acknowledgements
                 .into_iter()
                 .map(|kept| {
                     Ok(KeptAcknowledgement {
                         ack: Acknowledgement {
                             org_id: kept.ack.org_id,
                             member_id: kept.ack.member_id,
                             device: parse_field("removed.ack.device", DevicePublicKey::parse(&kept.ack.device))?,
                             epoch: kept.ack.epoch,
                             root: kept.ack.root,
                             signature: kept.ack.signature,
                         },
                         recipient: parse_field("removed.recipient", DevicePublicKey::parse(&kept.recipient))?,
                         recipient_addresses: kept
                             .recipient_addresses
                             .map(|addresses| parse_field("removed.recipient_addresses", EndpointAddresses::parse(addresses)))
                             .transpose()?,
                     })
                 })
                 .collect::<Result<_, OrgNodeError>>()?;
             Ok(Self { org_id: raw.org_id, verified_at: raw.verified_at, acknowledgements })
         }
     }

     impl StoreData {
         /// Consume the store, keeping only the Organisation, the verification time and `acknowledgements`
         /// (LLR-2d5a7m). Everything else — the record and its key pair, the Organisation name, every
         /// provisional change and organisation, the founding, the provisional Member, every expectation,
         /// invite, kept request and notice, the revoked Devices, the address book and the Persona with its
         /// member seed — is dropped with `self`. Called from one place, `OrgService::seal_removal`
         /// (LLR-9jn3z8).
         pub fn into_removed(
             self,
             acknowledgements: Vec<KeptAcknowledgement>,
             verified_at: VerificationTime,
         ) -> Result<RemovedStore, OrgNodeError> {
             let org_id = match (&self.record, self.persona.org_id) {
                 (Some(record), _) => record.org_id,
                 (None, Some(org_id)) => return Err(OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { org_id }),
                 (None, None) => return Err(OrgNodeError::OrgNotOnChain),
             };
             Ok(RemovedStore { org_id, verified_at, acknowledgements })
         }
     }
     ```

       ```rust
           pub(crate) fn seal_data<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(&self, data: &StoreData, rng: &mut R) -> Result<StoreWrite, OrgNodeError> {
       ```

   ```rust
   /// A chain state at `epoch` with `members`' root and the key whose private half is `seed`.
   fn chain(members: &[MemberSnapshot], epoch: u64, seed: u8) -> OrgState {
       OrgState::from_chain(*root_of(members).as_bytes(), *org_key(seed).1.as_bytes(), epoch).unwrap()
   }

   /// `data` holding one received provisional organisation for epoch 4 whose members are `next`.
   fn with_received(mut data: StoreData, next: Vec<MemberSnapshot>, seed: u8) -> StoreData {
       let (private, public) = org_key(seed);
       data.provisional_organisations.push(ProvisionalOrganisation::from(ProvisionalOrganisationParts {
           epoch: Epoch::new(4),
           base_root: data.record.as_ref().unwrap().root_hash,
           root: root_of(&next),
           members: next,
           org_pub_key: public,
           org_private_key: private,
           change_set: Some(vec![1]),
           base_snapshot: Some(vec![2]),
           origin: Origin::Received { from: device_key(0x21) },
           applied: Vec::new(),
       }));
       data
   }

   /// A recording `device_secrets`: each call's keys, answered with `answer`.
   fn recording(asked: &mut Vec<Vec<DevicePublicKey>>, answer: Vec<DeviceSecret>) -> impl FnOnce(&[DevicePublicKey]) -> Vec<DeviceSecret> + '_ {
       move |keys: &[DevicePublicKey]| {
           asked.push(keys.to_vec());
           answer
       }
   }

   fn removed_of(change: Option<StoreChange>) -> RemovedStore {
       let StoreChange::Sealed(write) = change.expect("a removal seals the removed store");
       assert_eq!(write.device_key, own());
       match content_of(&write) {
           StoreContent::Removed(removed) => removed,
           StoreContent::Active(_) => panic!("the removed form"),
       }
   }

   fn verify_signature(ack: &Acknowledgement) {
       let signature = ed25519_dalek::Signature::from_bytes(&ack.signature.0);
       ack.device.verifying_key().verify_strict(&ack.signed_bytes(), &signature).unwrap();
   }

       let mut svc = service(with_received(member_data(others), next.clone(), 0x63));
       let mut asked = vec![];

           .verify(&mut OsRng, &own(), Some(chain(&next, 4, 0x63)), VerificationTime(100), recording(&mut asked, vec![own_secret()]))
           .unwrap();

       let removed = removed_of(change);

       assert_eq!(removed.acknowledgements.len(), 1);

   #[test]
   fn the_acknowledgement_is_signed_once_with_the_personas_secret_and_kept_per_recipient() {

           (0..5).map(|i| snapshot(10 + i, &format!("m{i}"), 0x30 + i, 0x31 + i)).collect();

       let mut both = still.clone();
   ```

     ```rust
     /// `k` for `n` candidates (LLR-vq5d5n): 3 for five or more, 2 for three or four, 1 for one or two, 0 for none.
     pub fn recipient_count(n: usize) -> usize {
         match n {
             0 => 0,
             1 | 2 => 1,
             3 | 4 => 2,
             _ => 3,
         }
     }

     /// The recipients of a removal (LLR-vq5d5n). The candidates are the distinct DevicePublicKeys that
     /// `previous` lists other than `own`. For a removal by a match (`matched` is `Some`), the ones the
     /// match still lists come first, then the others; for a removal by a notice, all of them. Each group
     /// is in ascending order of the key's bytes, and the first `recipient_count(n)` are taken.
     pub fn recipients(
         previous: &[crate::store::MemberSnapshot],
         own: &DevicePublicKey,
         matched: Option<&[crate::store::MemberSnapshot]>,
     ) -> Vec<DevicePublicKey> {
         let mut candidates: Vec<DevicePublicKey> = Vec::new();
         for device in previous.iter().flat_map(|member| member.device_keys.iter()) {
             if device != own && !candidates.contains(device) {
                 candidates.push(*device);
             }
         }
         let k = recipient_count(candidates.len());
         candidates.sort_by(|a, b| a.as_bytes().cmp(b.as_bytes()));
         let still_listed =
             |device: &DevicePublicKey| matched.is_some_and(|members| members.iter().any(|m| m.device_keys.contains(device)));
         let (mut first, rest): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) = candidates.into_iter().partition(|device| still_listed(device));
         first.extend(rest);
         first.truncate(k);
         first
     }
     ```
   - `org-node/src/revocation.rs`: `accept` decides only, and one acknowledgement is signed by a new function.
     Replace the bodies T13 left for `accept` and `sign_acknowledgements` with these two functions. Delete
     `Accepted` and `bound_devices` if they are still there.
     ```rust
     /// Decides a kept notice against the chain state the caller read (LLR-rhsfw9's refusals, in order;
     /// LLR-jhy6t6). `check_notice`; no state (`OrgNotOnChain`); a state older than the record
     /// (`StaleChainState`); at the record's epoch with another root (`ChainStateConflict`); a proof that
     /// does not hold under the chain's root (`RevocationProofRefused`). Asks for no secret and changes nothing.
     #[cfg(feature = "app")]
     pub fn accept(store: &StoreData, notice: &RevocationNotice, chain: Option<OrgState>) -> Result<(), OrgNodeError> {
         check_notice(store, notice)?;
         let org_id = notice.org_id;
         let chain = chain.ok_or(OrgNodeError::OrgNotOnChain)?;
         let record = store.record.as_ref().ok_or(OrgNodeError::RevocationNotHeld { org_id })?;
         if chain.epoch < record.epoch {
             return Err(OrgNodeError::StaleChainState { org_id, chain_epoch: chain.epoch, record_epoch: record.epoch });
         }
         if chain.epoch == record.epoch && chain.root_hash != record.root_hash {
             return Err(OrgNodeError::ChainStateConflict { org_id });
         }
         notice
             .proof
             .verify::<Blake3Hasher>(&chain.root_hash, &notice.member_id, &notice.device)
             .map_err(|cause| OrgNodeError::RevocationProofRefused { org_id, cause })
     }

     /// This Persona's one acknowledgement of its own removal from `org_id`, naming `chain`'s epoch and root,
     /// signed with `secret` (LLR-5tvn7g, LLR-bs6yxf; Ed25519, deterministic). `secret` must be the Persona's
     /// (`DeviceSecretNotSupplied`).
     #[cfg(feature = "app")]
     pub fn sign_acknowledgement(
         persona: &PersonaRecord,
         org_id: OrgId,
         chain: &OrgState,
         secret: &DeviceSecret,
     ) -> Result<Acknowledgement, OrgNodeError> {
         let member_id = persona.member_id.ok_or(OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { org_id })?;
         if secret.device_key() != persona.device_key {
             return Err(OrgNodeError::DeviceSecretNotSupplied { org_id });
         }
         let mut acknowledgement = Acknowledgement {
             org_id,
             member_id,
             device: persona.device_key,
             epoch: chain.epoch,
             root: chain.root_hash,
             signature: Signature64([0; 64]),
         };
         acknowledgement.signature = Signature64(secret.signing_keypair().sign(&acknowledgement.signed_bytes()).to_bytes());
         Ok(acknowledgement)
     }
     ```

     ```rust
     /// A refused notice stays kept and is skipped (LLR-f9mcsq).
     pub fn accepted_notice(store: &StoreData, chain: &OrgState) -> bool {
     ```

     (a) Add the removal itself, which is the only caller of `seal_removal`. Remove the
     `#[cfg_attr(…, allow(dead_code))]` T23 put on `seal_removal`.
     ```rust
         /// This Persona's own removal (LLR-jhy6t6, LLR-5tvn7g, LLR-vq5d5n): choose the recipients among
         /// the record's other Devices and, when there is at least one, call `device_secrets` once for the
         /// Persona's key, sign one acknowledgement and keep it for each recipient with its address-book
         /// entry. Then seal the removed store. With no secret it refuses `DeviceSecretNotSupplied`, changing
         /// nothing. Every secret is dropped before return.
         fn remove_own<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
             &mut self,
             index: usize,
             rng: &mut R,
             chain: &OrgState,
             matched: Option<Vec<MemberSnapshot>>,
             verified_at: VerificationTime,
             device_secrets: impl FnOnce(&[DevicePublicKey]) -> Vec<DeviceSecret>,
         ) -> Result<(Verified, Option<StoreChange>), OrgNodeError> {
             let data = self.stores[index].data()?;
             let record = data.record.as_ref().ok_or(OrgNodeError::OrgNotOnChain)?;
             let org_id = record.org_id;
             let own = data.persona.device_key;
             let recipients = crate::removal::recipients(&record.trie_members, &own, matched.as_deref());
             let mut acknowledgements = Vec::with_capacity(recipients.len());
             if !recipients.is_empty() {
                 let secrets = device_secrets(&[own]);
                 let secret = secrets
                     .iter()
                     .find(|secret| secret.device_key() == own)
                     .ok_or(OrgNodeError::DeviceSecretNotSupplied { org_id })?;
                 let ack = crate::revocation::sign_acknowledgement(&data.persona, org_id, chain, secret)?;
                 drop(secrets);
                 for recipient in recipients {
                     let recipient_addresses =
                         data.address_book.iter().find(|(key, _)| *key == recipient).map(|(_, addresses)| addresses.clone());
                     acknowledgements.push(KeptAcknowledgement { ack: ack.clone(), recipient, recipient_addresses });
                 }
             }
             let kept = acknowledgements.len();
             let change = self.seal_removal(index, rng, acknowledgements, verified_at)?;
             Ok((Verified::Removed { org_id, acknowledgements_kept: kept }, Some(change)))
         }
     ```

     ```rust
     impl RemovedStore {
         /// Remove the kept acknowledgement whose recipient is `recipient`, with its key and addresses;
         /// true when one was kept (LLR-85kves). Called only from `OrgService::acknowledgement_accepted`.
         pub(crate) fn remove_acknowledgement(&mut self, recipient: &DevicePublicKey) -> bool {
             match self.acknowledgements.iter().position(|kept| &kept.recipient == recipient) {
                 Some(position) => {
                     self.acknowledgements.remove(position);
                     true
                 }
                 None => false,
             }
         }
     }
     ```
   - `org-node/src/service.rs`: add the view type beside `OutgoingMessage`, and the two operations.
     ```rust
     /// What a removed store keeps for org-io's delivery (LLR-75sn9g): the Organisation, the verification time
     /// for the 7-day deadline, and each acknowledgement as a message to its recipient with that recipient's
     /// kept addresses, in kept order. Not `Clone`.
     #[derive(Debug)]
     pub struct KeptAcknowledgements {
         pub org_id: OrgId,
         pub verified_at: VerificationTime,
         pub acknowledgements: Vec<(OutgoingMessage, Option<EndpointAddresses>)>,
     }
     ```
     ```rust
         /// The recipient `recipient` accepted its acknowledgement: remove it, with that key and its addresses,
         /// and return how many are still kept and the store sealed (LLR-85kves). An Active store, or a
         /// recipient no kept acknowledgement names, is refused with `AcknowledgementNotKept`. The answer
         /// itself is not judged here; org-io received it.
         pub fn acknowledgement_accepted<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
             &mut self,
             rng: &mut R,
             device_key: &DevicePublicKey,
             recipient: DevicePublicKey,
         ) -> Result<(usize, StoreChange), OrgNodeError> {
             let index = self.store_index(device_key)?;
             let StoreContent::Removed(removed) = self.stores[index].content() else {
                 return Err(OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementNotKept { recipient: Box::new(recipient) });
             };
             let mut next = removed.clone();
             if !next.remove_acknowledgement(&recipient) {
                 return Err(OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementNotKept { recipient: Box::new(recipient) });
             }
             let left = next.acknowledgements.len();
             let content = StoreContent::Removed(next);
             let write = self.stores[index].seal_content(&content, rng)?;
             self.stores[index].replace_content(content);
             Ok((left, StoreChange::Sealed(write)))
         }

         /// The acknowledgements a removed store keeps, as messages to their recipients with the recipients'
         /// addresses; `None` for an Active store (LLR-75sn9g). Changes nothing.
         pub fn kept_acknowledgements(&self, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> Result<Option<KeptAcknowledgements>, OrgNodeError> {
             let index = self.store_index(device_key)?;
             let StoreContent::Removed(removed) = self.stores[index].content() else {
                 return Ok(None);
             };
             let acknowledgements = removed
                 .acknowledgements
                 .iter()
                 .map(|kept| {
                     let body = encode_message(&WireMessage::Acknowledgement(kept.ack.clone()))?;
                     Ok((OutgoingMessage { recipient: kept.recipient, body }, kept.recipient_addresses.clone()))
                 })
                 .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, OrgNodeError>>()?;
             Ok(Some(KeptAcknowledgements { org_id: removed.org_id, verified_at: removed.verified_at, acknowledgements }))
         }
     ```

   ```rust
   // Re-pinned 2026-10-22 (change worktree-org-io-domain-api, T26; LLR-mkvx2k, LLR-d925uu, LLR-6zaeb6). The
   // store plaintext is a `StoreContent`: its variant index, then its fields. No migration (LLR-78jfrd:
   // stores written before this change are not read). Both values are derived by the format rule from the
   // fields below, never captured from the code: varint lengths, counts, epochs and variant indices; `00`/`01`
   // option tags; strings as length ‖ UTF-8; keys, identifiers and roots as their raw bytes; a Signature64 as

   //              "Jones", MB, [DB])], proxy Some(55×32), org_private_key 44×32,

   //   org_name "Acme";

   //              Some([9,8,7,6]), Some([5,4,3,2,1]), Own, applied [Revoke { 02×32 }]);
   //              Received (epoch 4, base 33×32, [alice, bob], root 77×32, K, 88×32, Some([1,2]),
   //              Some([3]), Received { DB }, []); Answer (epoch 5, base 33×32, [alice], root 22×32, K,
   ```

     ```rust
                         .rev()

                 takers,
     ```

     ```rust
     /// The callers, as `file::function`, of every call of `name(` in `src/` other than its definition.
     fn callers_of(name: &str) -> (Vec<String>, Vec<String>) {
         let mut definitions = vec![];
         let mut callers = vec![];
         for (path, text) in sources() {
             let code = code_of(&text);
             let file = path.file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy().to_string();
             for offset in identifier_occurrences(&code, name) {
                 let after = &code[offset + name.len()..];
                 if !(after.starts_with('(') || after.starts_with("::<")) {
                     continue;
                 }
                 if code[..offset].trim_end().ends_with("fn") {
                     definitions.push(file.clone());
                     continue;
                 }
                 callers.push(format!("{file}::{}", enclosing_function(&code, offset).unwrap_or_default()));
             }
         }
         callers.sort();
         (definitions, callers)
     }

     /// `into_removed` is defined once, in removal.rs. It is called from `seal_removal` alone, and
     /// `seal_removal` from `verify`'s removal (`remove_own`) and the test-support wrapper.
     /// Mutation check, 2026-10-22: a second `into_removed` call added to `cancel_invite` failed this test,
     /// and was removed.
     // verifies: LLR-9jn3z8
     #[test]
     fn into_removed_is_called_only_from_verify() {
         let (definitions, callers) = callers_of("into_removed");
         assert_eq!(definitions, ["removal.rs"]);
         assert_eq!(callers, ["service.rs::seal_removal"]);
         let (_, callers) = callers_of("seal_removal");
         assert_eq!(callers, ["service.rs::remove_own", "service.rs::seal_removal_for_test"]);
         let (_, callers) = callers_of("remove_own");
         assert_eq!(callers, ["service.rs::verify", "service.rs::verify"], "the two removal cases of verify");
         let service = std::fs::read_to_string(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src/service.rs")).unwrap();
         let wrapper = service.find("pub fn seal_removal_for_test").unwrap();
         assert!(service[..wrapper].lines().rev().take(4).any(|line| line.contains("feature = \"test-support\"")), "the wrapper is test-only");
     }

     #[test]
     fn into_removed_is_called_only_from_verify_and_an_acknowledgement_removed_only_on_acceptance() {
         let (_, callers) = callers_of("into_removed");
         assert_eq!(callers, ["service.rs::seal_removal"]);
         let (definitions, callers) = callers_of("remove_acknowledgement");
         assert_eq!(definitions, ["removal.rs"]);
         assert_eq!(callers, ["service.rs::acknowledgement_accepted"]);
         // No other code removes from a removed store's acknowledgements.
         let removing = ["retain(", "retain_mut(", "remove(", "swap_remove(", "clear()", "drain(", "truncate(", "pop()", "split_off("];
         for (path, text) in sources() {
             let mut code = code_of(&text);
             if path.ends_with("removal.rs") {
                 code = without_function(&code, "remove_acknowledgement");
             }
             let squeezed_code = squeezed(&code);
             for method in removing {
                 let call = format!("acknowledgements.{method}");
                 assert!(identifier_occurrences(&squeezed_code, &call).is_empty(), "{} calls `{call}` (LLR-9jn3z8)", path.display());

     /// Nothing in org-node removes a store except `drop_store`. Nothing empties the current record:
     /// `record` is never set to `None`, taken, or swapped out. The Persona is never reset. A removed form
     /// is built only by `seal_removal`.
     // verifies: LLR-9jn3z8
     #[test]
     fn only_the_removal_and_the_accepted_acknowledgement_delete() {
         let removing = ["retain(", "retain_mut(", "remove(", "swap_remove(", "clear()", "drain(", "truncate(", "pop()", "split_off(", "dedup"];
         for (path, text) in sources() {
             let mut code = code_of(&text);
             if path.ends_with("service.rs") {
                 code = without_function(&code, "drop_store");
             }
             let squeezed_code = squeezed(&code);
             let file = path.display();
             for method in removing {
                 assert!(identifier_occurrences(&squeezed_code, &format!("stores.{method}")).is_empty(), "{file} removes a store");
             }
             for emptying in ["record=None", "record.take()", "mem::take(&mutdata.record)", "mem::replace(&mutdata.record"] {
                 assert!(!squeezed_code.contains(emptying), "{file}: `{emptying}` removes the current record (LLR-9jn3z8)");
             }
             for reset in ["persona=", "member_seed="] {
                 for offset in identifier_occurrences(&squeezed_code, reset) {
                     assert!(squeezed_code[offset + reset.len()..].starts_with('='), "{file} rewrites `{reset}` (LLR-9jn3z8)");
                 }
             }
         }
         // A removed form is built by the removal and rebuilt only on an acceptance; `StoreContent::Removed(removed)`
         // is a pattern, not a construction.
         let service = code_of(&std::fs::read_to_string(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src/service.rs")).unwrap());
         let mut builders: Vec<String> = identifier_occurrences(&service, "StoreContent::Removed(")
             .into_iter()
             .filter(|&offset| !service[offset..].starts_with("StoreContent::Removed(removed)"))
             .map(|offset| enclosing_function(&service, offset).unwrap_or_default())
             .collect();
         builders.sort();
         builders.dedup();
         assert_eq!(builders, ["acknowledgement_accepted", "seal_removal"]);
     }

     /// `verify` and the functions it calls in revocation.rs, verify_org.rs and removal.rs are values in,
     /// values out: no `async`, no chain, transport, endpoint or file system, and no clock (LLR-g2jeqd).
     /// Replaces `revocation_and_reconcile_do_no_io` (LLR-xgefn8), whose reconcile.rs is gone.
     // verifies: LLR-g2jeqd
     #[test]
     fn verification_revocation_and_removal_do_no_io_and_read_no_clock() {
         let forbidden = [
             "async ", ".await", "impl Future", "ChainOps", "ChainReader", "read_state", "OrgEndpoint", "crate::transport",
             "iroh", "tokio", "std::fs", "std::io", "std::net", "File::", ".save(", "SystemTime", "Instant", "std::time",
         ];
         for file in ["revocation.rs", "verify_org.rs", "removal.rs"] {
             let code = code_of(&std::fs::read_to_string(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src").join(file)).unwrap());
             for name in forbidden {
                 assert!(!code.contains(name), "{file} names `{name}` (LLR-g2jeqd)");
             }
             let squeezed_code = squeezed(&code);
             for borrow in ["&mutStoreData", "&mutself"] {
                 if file == "removal.rs" && borrow == "&mutself" {
                     continue; // RemovedStore::remove_acknowledgement mutates the removed store's own list
                 }
                 assert!(!squeezed_code.contains(borrow), "{file} takes `{borrow}` (LLR-g2jeqd: the store is taken as a value)");
             }
         }
         let service = code_of(&std::fs::read_to_string(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src/service.rs")).unwrap());
         let verify = &service[service.find("pub fn verify<").expect("OrgService::verify")..];
         let verify = &verify[..verify.find("\n    }\n").expect("the end of verify")];
         for name in forbidden {
             assert!(!verify.contains(name), "verify names `{name}` (LLR-g2jeqd)");
         }
         assert!(verify.contains("chain: Option<OrgState>"), "verify takes the chain state as a value");
         assert!(!service.contains("SystemTime") && !service.contains("Instant::now"), "service.rs reads no clock: the time is the caller's");
     }
     ```
   - `org-node/tests/own_removal.rs`: the LLR-f9mcsq test. It drives T23's `rich_data` store through each
     operation's refusal and each non-removal outcome, and compares every field by name. The serde model of
     `StoreData` gives one entry per field.
     ```rust
     /// Every field of the store's data, by name, as serde's data model renders it.
     fn fields(svc: &OrgService) -> serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> {
         serde_json::to_value(svc.store_data(&own()).unwrap()).unwrap().as_object().unwrap().clone()
     }

     /// `after` equals `before` in every field but `named`.
     fn only_changed(before: &serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>, after: &serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>, named: &[&str], what: &str) {
         for (field, value) in before {
             if !named.contains(&field.as_str()) {
                 assert_eq!(after.get(field), Some(value), "{what} changed `{field}`");
             }
         }
     }

     // verifies: LLR-f9mcsq
     #[test]
     fn on_an_active_store_nothing_but_the_removal_deletes_and_each_operation_removes_only_what_it_names() {
         let data = rich_data();
         let record = data.record.clone().unwrap();
         let invite_id = data.kept_admission_requests[0].invite_id;
         let mut svc = service(data.clone());
         let start = fields(&svc);

         // Every refusal leaves the store as it was.
         let refusals: Vec<Result<(), OrgNodeError>> = vec![
             svc.record_revocation(&mut OsRng, &own(), MemberId::new([0x77; 32])).map(|_| ()),
             svc.record_revocation(&mut OsRng, &own(), MemberId::new([2; 32])).map(|_| ()),
             svc.record_admission(&mut OsRng, &own(), InviteId::new([0x39; 32]), None).map(|_| ()),
             svc.cancel_invite(&mut OsRng, &own(), InviteId::new([0x39; 32])).map(|_| ()),
             svc.build_invite(&mut OsRng, &own(), "x".into(), vec!["a".repeat(257)]).map(|_| ()),
             svc.record_founding_proxy(&mut OsRng, &own(), org(), org_node::ChainAccount::new([1; 32])).map(|_| ()),
             svc.verify(&mut OsRng, &own(), None, VerificationTime(1), never_asked).map(|_| ()),
             svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &own(), device_key(0x2f), &encode_message(&WireMessage::OrganisationRequest { org_id: org(), addresses: vec![] }).unwrap()).map(|_| ()),
             svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &own(), own(), &[0xff, 0xff]).map(|_| ()),
         ];
         assert!(refusals.iter().all(Result::is_err), "each case is a refusal: {refusals:?}");
         assert_eq!(fields(&svc), start, "every refusal leaves every field as it was");

         // InStep, Behind and Inconsistent remove nothing.
         let root = *record.root_hash.as_bytes();
         let key = *record.org_pub_key.as_bytes();
         for (epoch, root) in [(3, root), (2, root), (3, [0x12; 32]), (9, [0x13; 32])] {
             let (verified, change) =
                 svc.verify(&mut OsRng, &own(), Some(OrgState::from_chain(root, key, epoch).unwrap()), VerificationTime(2), never_asked).unwrap();
             assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::InStep | Verified::Behind { .. } | Verified::Inconsistent { .. }), "{verified:?}");
             assert!(change.is_none());
             assert_eq!(fields(&svc), start, "{verified:?} removes nothing");
         }

         // check_received removes nothing on any outcome: a kept request only adds its entry.
         let mut check = service(data.clone());
         let body = encode_message(&WireMessage::OrganisationRequest { org_id: org(), addresses: vec!["192.0.2.22:1".into()] }).unwrap();
         check.check_received(&mut OsRng, &own(), device_key(0x22), &body).unwrap();
         only_changed(&start, &fields(&check), &["address_book"], "an answered organisation request");

         // cancel_invite removes only its request, pair and Admit (here none).
         let mut cancel = service(data.clone());
         cancel.cancel_invite(&mut OsRng, &own(), invite_id).unwrap();
         let after = fields(&cancel);
         only_changed(&start, &after, &["kept_admission_requests", "outstanding_invites", "provisional_changes"], "cancel_invite");
         assert_eq!(after["provisional_changes"], start["provisional_changes"], "no Admit named it: the Revoke stays");
         assert_eq!(after["kept_admission_requests"], serde_json::json!([]));

         // An adoption whose record lists this Device removes only LLR-d9x6xf's, LLR-x8drb8's and LLR-rzqs2u's.
         let proposal = &data.provisional_organisations[0];
         let state = OrgState::from_chain(*proposal.root.as_bytes(), *proposal.org_pub_key.as_bytes(), 4).unwrap();
         let (verified, _) = svc.verify(&mut OsRng, &own(), Some(state), VerificationTime(3), never_asked).unwrap();
         assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Adopted { .. }));
         let after = fields(&svc);
         only_changed(
             &start,
             &after,
             &["persona", "record", "provisional_changes", "provisional_organisations", "kept_revocation_notices", "revoked_devices", "address_book", "kept_admission_requests", "outstanding_invites"],
             "an adoption",
         );
         assert_eq!(after["persona"]["member_seed"], start["persona"]["member_seed"], "the Persona's keys stay");
         assert_eq!(after["persona"]["device_key"], start["persona"]["device_key"]);
         assert!(after["record"].is_object(), "the record is replaced, never removed");
         assert_eq!(after["kept_admission_requests"], start["kept_admission_requests"], "Dave is not in the adopted record: his request stays");
         assert_eq!(after["outstanding_invites"], start["outstanding_invites"]);
         assert_eq!(after["address_book"][0], start["address_book"][0], "existing entries are kept");
     }
     ```
     An adoption marks the Persona Active, and its `persona` field is named in the list above for that
     reason. The two key asserts then pin that the Persona's keys survive. Before the adoption the store
     holds Bob in the record and the Revoke for Bob, so the Revoke is included and removed (LLR-d9x6xf).
     Bob's Device goes to `revoked_devices`, and the received notice goes (LLR-x8drb8). The test names those
     fields and checks nothing else moves.

     ```rust
     mod organisation_key_custody {
         use org_members::{DevicePublicKey, Handle, MemberId, MemberLeaf, Name, Surname};
         use org_node::ids::OrgId;
         use org_node::service::{Checked, OrgService};
         use org_node::store::{
             MemberSnapshot, OrgRecord, OrgRecordParts, Origin, PersonaStatus, ProvisionalOrganisation, ProvisionalOrganisationParts,
         };
         use org_node::test_fixtures::{device_key, device_secret, empty_store, member_key, persona_record, store_for_test, Trie};
         use org_node::wire::{decode_message, encode_message, WireMessage};
         use org_node::{Epoch, OrgNodeError, OrgPrivateKey, SequenceNumber};
         use rand::rngs::OsRng;

         const OWN: u8 = 4;
         const PROVISIONAL: [u8; 32] = [0x6d; 32];
         const CURRENT: [u8; 32] = [0x60; 32];

         fn snapshot(id: u8, handle: &str, member: u8, device: u8) -> MemberSnapshot {
             MemberSnapshot {
                 id: MemberId::new([id; 32]),
                 handle: Handle::parse(handle).unwrap(),
                 name: Name::parse("Test").unwrap(),
                 surname: Surname::parse("User").unwrap(),
                 member_key: member_key(member),
                 device_keys: vec![device_key(device)],
             }
         }

         fn service() -> OrgService {
             let members = vec![snapshot(1, "alice", 1, OWN), snapshot(3, "carol", 0x12, 0x22)];
             let leaves = members.iter().map(|s| MemberLeaf::new(s.id, s.handle.clone(), s.member_key, s.name.clone(), s.surname.clone(), s.device_keys.clone()).unwrap()).collect();
             let root = Trie::genesis(leaves).unwrap().root_hash().unwrap();
             let current = OrgPrivateKey::from(CURRENT);
             let org_id = OrgId::new([0xaa; 20]);
             let mut persona = persona_record("p-alice", 1, OWN);
             persona.org_id = Some(org_id);
             persona.member_id = Some(MemberId::new([1; 32]));
             persona.status = PersonaStatus::Active;
             let mut data = empty_store(persona);
             data.record = Some(OrgRecord::from(OrgRecordParts {
                 org_id,
                 root_hash: root,
                 org_pub_key: current.x25519_keypair().org_public_key().unwrap(),
                 epoch: Epoch::new(3),
                 last_seq: SequenceNumber::new(3),
                 trie_members: members.clone(),
                 proxy_account: None,
                 org_private_key: current,
                 kept_change_set: None,
                 kept_base_snapshot: None,
             }));
             let provisional = OrgPrivateKey::from(PROVISIONAL);
             data.provisional_organisations = vec![ProvisionalOrganisation::from(ProvisionalOrganisationParts {
                 epoch: Epoch::new(4),
                 base_root: root,
                 members,
                 root,
                 org_pub_key: provisional.x25519_keypair().org_public_key().unwrap(),
                 org_private_key: provisional,
                 change_set: Some(vec![1]),
                 base_snapshot: Some(vec![2]),
                 origin: Origin::Own,
                 applied: vec![],
             })];
             OrgService::new(vec![store_for_test(&device_secret([OWN; 32]), data)]).unwrap()
         }

         /// The text of each production `pub fn` signature in `file` (not gated on `test-support`).
         fn public_signatures(file: &str) -> Vec<String> {
             let text = std::fs::read_to_string(std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src").join(file)).unwrap();
             let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();
             let mut signatures = vec![];
             for (index, line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
                 if !line.trim_start().starts_with("pub fn ") {
                     continue;
                 }
                 if lines[..index].iter().rev().take_while(|l| l.trim_start().starts_with("#[") || l.trim_start().starts_with("///")).any(|l| l.contains("test-support")) {
                     continue;
                 }
                 let mut signature = String::new();
                 for continuation in &lines[index..] {
                     let end = continuation.find('{');
                     signature.push_str(continuation[..end.unwrap_or(continuation.len())].trim());
                     if end.is_some() {
                         break;
                     }
                 }
                 signatures.push(signature);
             }
             signatures
         }

         // verifies: LLR-qw8tyu
         #[test]
         fn a_provisional_private_key_leaves_the_store_only_inside_a_message_to_a_listed_device() {
             // No operation returns an OrgPrivateKey: none names it after its `->`.
             for file in ["service.rs", "store.rs", "removal.rs", "verify_org.rs"] {
                 for signature in public_signatures(file) {
                     if let Some(returns) = signature.split("->").nth(1) {
                         assert!(!returns.contains("OrgPrivateKey"), "{file}: `{signature}` returns an Organisation private key");
                     }
                 }
             }
             let mut svc = service();
             let own = device_key(OWN);
             // The views clone no key: their Debug holds no byte of either.
             let views = format!("{:?}", svc.provisional_organisations(&own).unwrap());
             for key in [PROVISIONAL, CURRENT] {
                 assert!(!views.contains(&format!("{:02x}{:02x}", key[0], key[1])) && !views.contains(&key[0].to_string()));
             }
             // A never-listed requester gets nothing; a listed one gets the current key, inside the encoded body.
             let request = encode_message(&WireMessage::OrganisationRequest { org_id: OrgId::new([0xaa; 20]), addresses: vec![] }).unwrap();
             assert!(matches!(svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &own, device_key(0x2f), &request), Err(OrgNodeError::SenderNotListed { .. })));
             let (Checked::OrganisationRequest { answer }, _) = svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &own, device_key(0x22), &request).unwrap() else {
                 panic!("an answer")
             };
             assert_eq!(answer.recipient, device_key(0x22));
             let WireMessage::Organisation { org_private_key, .. } = decode_message(&answer.body).unwrap() else { panic!("the Organisation kind") };
             assert_eq!(org_private_key.expose_secret(), &CURRENT, "the current key, never the provisional one");
             assert!(!answer.body.windows(32).any(|window| window == PROVISIONAL), "no provisional key leaves on an answer");
             // messages_for_current_epoch carries keys only to listed Devices.
             let listed: Vec<DevicePublicKey> = vec![device_key(0x22)];
             for message in svc.messages_for_current_epoch(&own).unwrap() {
                 if let WireMessage::OrgInformation { .. } = decode_message(&message.body).unwrap() {
                     assert!(listed.contains(&message.recipient), "an Organisation key goes only to a listed Device");
                 }
             }
         }
     }
     ```

**Intent:** `HandleRng` (rand_core 0.6.4 `OsRng`, behind a `std::sync::Mutex`) built by `OrgIo::open`, passed to every org-node call that draws and to `write_store`'s 16-hex suffix (`try_fill_bytes`, refusing `StoreFileError { step: CreateTemporary }` on failure); `with_rng_for_test` under `test-support` only. Every `OrgIo` method that took `rng`, and `create_persona`, `found_organisation`, `admit_member`, `revoke_member`, `expect_admission`, `produce_reply`, `import_reply`, `admit_reply`, `submit_commit_send`, `settle_unknown`, `reconcile`, `reconcile_held` and `peer_addr` (with `PeerAddr`, SDD-wr8m5n's parse) are removed, `submit.rs`'s sequence and `publish.rs` with them (`ChainWriter`, `WRITE_TIMEOUT`, `bounded` and `PublishState` move to `write.rs`); org-io compiles on P2's org-node again. Deleted test files' targets leave `Cargo.toml` and the verify line.
*Settled at assembly (PLAN DELTA accepted, fix item 17):* also touches `org-io/src/write.rs` (new; see the range-wide delta), `org-io/src/endpoints.rs` (the
receiving Device key on each inbound body, because org-node's `check_received` now names the receiving store;
`#[allow(dead_code)]` on the three functions that lose their production caller), `org-io/src/transport/endpoint.rs`
(`send_body_at` and its `PeerAddr` import go with `peer_addr.rs`; `#[allow(dead_code)]` on the send functions until
T38), `org-io/src/keychain.rs` (the two signing helpers that only removed sequences called go; `#[allow(dead_code)]` on
`keep` and `for_signing_noting_refusal` until T29/T35), `org-io/src/signatory.rs` (`crate::submit::NOT_CONFIGURED` →
`crate::write::NOT_CONFIGURED`, two lines). `org-io/tests/app_boundary.rs`, `org-io/tests/keychain.rs` and
`org-io/tests/signatory_rule.rs` need no edit (checked: they call no removed operation and their scans still hold).
*Settled at assembly:* the test seam takes `Box<dyn rand_core::CryptoRngCore + Send>` (LLR-5acgfg amended in the
design draft; fix item 17, ledger 84a31b1a).

**Steps:**

1. **Write the failing tests.** Three new tests in `org-io/tests/rng_source.rs` (the T1 stub), two in
   `org-io/tests/absences.rs`. The rng tests drive the only store write a T28 handle can make without an operation
   later tasks add — `OrgIo::store_for_test`, which writes an org-node store change through `LocalStore::store`, the
   path every operation uses — and pin the org-node call sites by a source scan; LLR-94nn6q's own draw (the suffix)
   is driven with a failing source.

   `org-io/tests/rng_source.rs` (replaces the stub whole):
   ```rust
   #![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]
   #![allow(
       clippy::await_holding_lock,
       reason = "`fresh_keychain`'s lock serialises the tests over keyring's process-global credential builder for their whole run; each test has its own runtime"
   )]
   //! The handle's random source (SDD-3qwjs2; plan 2026-10-21-org-io-domain-api, T28): one
   //! cryptographic generator `OrgIo` owns, behind its own lock; every org-node draw an `OrgIo`
   //! method makes and the store file's temporary suffix come from it (LLR-4qd5fx), a test build
   //! may replace it (LLR-5acgfg), and a failing entropy source refuses org-io's own draw
   //! (LLR-94nn6q).

   use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
   use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

   use org_node::service::OrgService;
   use org_node::{ChainAccount, OrgId};
   use org_io::store_file::StoreFileStep;
   use org_io::test_support::FakeChain;
   use org_io::{OrgIo, StoreFailure};
   use rand::rngs::{OsRng, StdRng};
   use rand::{CryptoRng, RngCore, SeedableRng};

   mod common;
   use common::handles::{create, file_of, fresh_keychain, handle, store_dir};

   /// A source that hands out what `inner` draws and records the length of every request.
   struct Recording {
       inner: StdRng,
       requests: Arc<Mutex<Vec<usize>>>,
   }

   impl RngCore for Recording {
       fn next_u32(&mut self) -> u32 {
           self.requests.lock().unwrap().push(4);
           self.inner.next_u32()
       }
       fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64 {
           self.requests.lock().unwrap().push(8);
           self.inner.next_u64()
       }
       fn fill_bytes(&mut self, dest: &mut [u8]) {
           self.requests.lock().unwrap().push(dest.len());
           self.inner.fill_bytes(dest);
       }
       fn try_fill_bytes(&mut self, dest: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), rand::Error> {
           self.fill_bytes(dest);
           Ok(())
       }
   }

   impl CryptoRng for Recording {}

   /// A source whose every draw fails, as an operating system's entropy source that is gone.
   struct Failing;

   impl RngCore for Failing {
       fn next_u32(&mut self) -> u32 {
           panic!("an infallible draw from a failed source")
       }
       fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64 {
           panic!("an infallible draw from a failed source")
       }
       fn fill_bytes(&mut self, _dest: &mut [u8]) {
           panic!("an infallible draw from a failed source")
       }
       fn try_fill_bytes(&mut self, _dest: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), rand::Error> {
           Err(rand::Error::new("entropy source unavailable"))
       }
   }

   impl CryptoRng for Failing {}

   fn sources() -> Vec<(PathBuf, String)> {
       fn walk(dir: &Path, out: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) {
           for entry in std::fs::read_dir(dir).unwrap() {
               let path = entry.unwrap().path();
               if path.is_dir() {
                   walk(&path, out);
               } else if path.extension().is_some_and(|extension| extension == "rs") {
                   out.push(path);
               }
           }
       }
       let mut paths = vec![];
       walk(&Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src"), &mut paths);
       paths.into_iter().map(|path| {
           let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap();
           (path, text)
       }).collect()
   }

   /// A source's lines with `//` comments (doc comments included) removed.
   fn code_lines(text: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
       text.lines().map(|line| line.split("//").next().unwrap_or("")).collect()
   }

   /// The names in `dir`, sorted.
   fn names_in(dir: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
       let mut names: Vec<String> =
           std::fs::read_dir(dir).unwrap().map(|entry| entry.unwrap().file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string()).collect();
       names.sort();
       names
   }

   /// Observed: a store write through the handle draws one 8-byte suffix from the handle's source
   /// and nothing else from it. Read: every call `org-io/src` makes of an org-node operation that
   /// takes a random source passes `&mut *rng`, and every `rng` bound in `org-io/src` is the
   /// handle's (`.rng.lock()`), so no other source reaches org-node.
   // verifies: LLR-4qd5fx
   #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
   async fn every_org_node_draw_and_the_temporary_suffix_come_from_the_handles_source() {
       let (_guard, _keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let requests = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
       let recording = Recording { inner: StdRng::seed_from_u64(1), requests: requests.clone() };
       let io = handle("rng-source", "a", &FakeChain::new()).with_rng_for_test(Box::new(recording));
       // The helper's org-node proposal draws from the test's own `OsRng`; the file write is the handle's.
       create(&io, "alice").await;
       assert_eq!(*requests.lock().unwrap(), vec![8], "one draw from the handle's source: the 8-byte temporary suffix");

       let drawing = [
           "check_received(", "propose_founding(", "record_founding_proxy(", "propose_member(", "record_admission(",
           "record_revocation(", "propose_updated_organisation(", ".verify(", "build_invite(", "cancel_invite(",
           "acknowledgement_accepted(", "PersonStore::create(", "write_store(", "write_person_store(",
       ];
       let mut calls = 0;
       let mut other_sources = vec![];
       for (path, text) in sources() {
           if path.ends_with("test_support.rs") {
               continue;
           }
           let lines = code_lines(&text);
           for (index, line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
               if line.contains("let mut rng") && !line.contains(".rng.lock()") {
                   other_sources.push(format!("{}:{}: {}", path.display(), index + 1, line.trim()));
               }
               for operation in drawing.iter().filter(|operation| line.contains(**operation)) {
                   if line.contains("fn ") {
                       continue;
                   }
                   calls += 1;
                   let rest = &line[line.find(operation).unwrap() + operation.len()..];
                   let arguments = if rest.trim().is_empty() { lines.get(index + 1).copied().unwrap_or("") } else { rest };
                   let passes_the_handles = arguments.trim_start().starts_with("&mut *rng")
                       || arguments.contains("&self.rng")
                       || arguments.contains("&self.local.rng")
                       || arguments.contains("&local.rng");
                   if !passes_the_handles {
                       other_sources.push(format!("{}:{}: `{operation}` without the handle's source: {}", path.display(), index + 1, line.trim()));
                   }
               }
           }
       }
       assert!(calls >= 2, "the scan found org-io's drawing calls ({calls})");
       assert!(other_sources.is_empty(), "a draw from another source:\n{}", other_sources.join("\n"));
   }

   /// A test build replaces the source with a seeded one, so a draw reproduces; no production
   /// file replaces or seeds it, and `open` and `connect` take none.
   // verifies: LLR-5acgfg
   #[tokio::test]
   async fn a_seeded_source_reproduces_a_draw_under_test_support() {
       let seeded = |seed: u64| {
           OrgIo::not_configured(OrgService::new(Vec::new()).unwrap()).with_rng_for_test(Box::new(StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed)))
       };
       let (first, again, other) = (seeded(7), seeded(7), seeded(8));
       let os = OrgIo::not_configured(OrgService::new(Vec::new()).unwrap());
       let drawn = first.draw_for_test(32);
       assert_eq!(drawn, again.draw_for_test(32), "the same seed, the same draw");
       assert_ne!(drawn, other.draw_for_test(32), "another seed, another draw");
       assert_ne!(drawn, os.draw_for_test(32), "the operating system's source is not the seeded one");

       let lib = std::fs::read_to_string(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src/lib.rs")).unwrap();
       assert!(lib.contains("#[cfg(feature = \"test-support\")]\npub mod test_support;"), "test_support is compiled only with test-support");
       for (path, text) in sources() {
           if path.ends_with("test_support.rs") {
               continue;
           }
           for line in code_lines(&text) {
               for replacing in ["fn with_rng_for_test", "seed_from_u64", "from_seed", "fn replaced_by"] {
                   let declared_for_test = replacing == "fn replaced_by" && path.ends_with("rng.rs");
                   assert!(declared_for_test || !line.contains(replacing), "{} replaces or seeds the source: {}", path.display(), line.trim());
               }
           }
       }
       let rng = std::fs::read_to_string(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src/rng.rs")).unwrap();
       let replaced_by = rng.find("fn replaced_by").unwrap();
       assert!(rng[..replaced_by].lines().rev().nth(1).unwrap().contains("#[cfg(feature = \"test-support\")]"), "replaced_by is test-only");
       for entry in ["pub fn open(", "pub async fn connect("] {
           for declared in lib.match_indices(entry) {
               let signature = &lib[declared.0..declared.0 + lib[declared.0..].find('{').unwrap()];

   /// A failing entropy source refuses org-io's own draw as `CreateTemporary` naming the random
   /// source, writes nothing, leaves no temporary file and falls back to no other source; the
   /// Persona is reloaded from its file. No code in `org-io/src` catches a panic.
   // verifies: LLR-94nn6q
   #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
   async fn a_failing_entropy_source_refuses_the_store_write_and_writes_nothing() {
       let (_guard, _keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let io = handle("rng-failing", "a", &FakeChain::new());
       let alice = create(&io, "alice").await;
       let device = io.persona_public_keys(&alice).await.unwrap().1;
       let dir = store_dir("rng-failing", "a");
       let file = file_of(&dir, &device);
       let (bytes, names) = (std::fs::read(&file).unwrap(), names_in(&dir));
       let change = io.node_for_test().record_founding_proxy(&mut OsRng, &device, OrgId::new([0x0a; 20]), ChainAccount::new([0x0b; 32])).unwrap();

       let io = io.with_rng_for_test(Box::new(Failing));
       let StoreFailure::Reloaded { failed } = io.store_for_test(change).unwrap_err() else {
           panic!("not reported as a failed write, reloaded")
       };
       assert_eq!(failed.step, StoreFileStep::CreateTemporary, "{failed}");
       assert!(failed.reason.contains("random source"), "the refusal names the random source: {failed}");
       assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&file).unwrap(), bytes, "nothing written");
       assert_eq!(names_in(&dir), names, "no temporary file");
       let held = io.node_for_test().store_data(&device).unwrap().founding.as_ref().unwrap().proxy;
       assert!(held.is_none(), "the Persona was reloaded from its file: no proxy recorded");
       for (path, text) in sources() {
           assert!(!text.contains("catch_unwind"), "{} catches a panic", path.display());
       }
   }
   ```

   **b. `org-io/src/rng.rs` (new):** the handle's source, a boxed `CryptoRngCore` behind a `std::sync::Mutex` (never
   held across an `.await`: every caller takes it for one synchronous org-node call or one suffix draw).
   ```rust
   //! The handle's random source (SDD-3qwjs2): one cryptographic generator `OrgIo` owns, through its
   //! `LocalStore`, and draws every random value of its operations from — the keys org-node draws for a
   //! Person, a Persona, a provisional organisation and an Organisation key pair, the invite identifier,
   //! the store nonces, and the store file's temporary suffix — so that no caller supplies or sees one
   //! (LLR-4qd5fx, LLR-ctm86b). Production builds hold `rand_core::OsRng` (rand_core 0.6.4 over
   //! `getrandom`); a test build may replace it (LLR-5acgfg). A draw org-node makes through
   //! `fill_bytes` panics on an entropy failure, inside the org-node call and before any store change
   //! is returned (LLR-94nn6q); org-io's own draw uses `try_fill_bytes` and refuses.

   use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard, PoisonError};

   use rand_core::{CryptoRngCore, OsRng};

   /// The source, behind its own lock. Not `Clone`, no `Debug`, and no public path reaches it.
   pub(crate) struct HandleRng {
       source: Mutex<Box<dyn CryptoRngCore + Send>>,
   }

   impl HandleRng {
       /// The operating system's source: the only one a production build holds.
       pub(crate) fn os() -> Self {
           Self { source: Mutex::new(Box::new(OsRng)) }
       }

       /// The source replaced by `source` (test builds only; `OrgIo::with_rng_for_test`).
       #[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
       pub(crate) fn replaced_by(source: Box<dyn CryptoRngCore + Send>) -> Self {
           Self { source: Mutex::new(source) }
       }

       /// The source, for one synchronous draw. A lock poisoned by a draw that panicked (a failed
       /// entropy source, LLR-94nn6q) is taken as it is: the panic already refused that call.
       pub(crate) fn lock(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, Box<dyn CryptoRngCore + Send>> {
           self.source.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
       }
   }

   impl Default for HandleRng {
       fn default() -> Self {
           Self::os()
       }
   }
   ```
   Call sites pass `&mut *rng` with `let mut rng = self.local.rng.lock();`: `Box<dyn CryptoRngCore + Send>` is
   `RngCore + CryptoRng` (rand_core's `Box` impls; its `alloc` feature is on in org-io's normal graph, `cargo tree -e
   features -i rand_core@0.6.4 -p org-io`).

   ```rust
   /// Where org-io keeps what org-node hands out: each store change in its
   /// Persona's store file (`store_file`), each new Persona's device secret in
   /// the OS keychain (`keychain`), the node's endpoints (`endpoints`) and the
   /// handle's random source (`rng`, LLR-4qd5fx). A handle built without a data
   /// directory keeps its stores in memory only.
   #[derive(Default)]
   pub(crate) struct LocalStore {
       data_dir: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
       keychain: Keychain,
       endpoints: Endpoints,
       rng: HandleRng,
   }

   impl LocalStore {
       /// Write `change`, the sealed store org-node returned, to its file
       /// (LLR-b9bm36), drawing the temporary suffix from the handle's source.
       /// When that fails, the Persona is reloaded into `service` from its file,
       /// which reads its keychain item once more, so the service never runs
       /// ahead of the file; when the reload fails too, its store is dropped
       /// from the service (LLR-murjr6).
       pub(crate) fn store(&self, service: &mut OrgService, change: StoreChange) -> Result<(), StoreFailure> {
           let StoreChange::Sealed(write) = change;
           let Some(data_dir) = &self.data_dir else { return Ok(()) };
           let device_key = write.device_key;
           let Err(failed) = store_file::write_store(data_dir, &write, &self.rng) else { return Ok(()) };
           match open_store(data_dir, &self.keychain, device_key) {
               Ok(store) => {
                   service.restore_store(store);
                   Err(StoreFailure::Reloaded { failed })
               }
               Err(reload) => {
                   service.drop_store(&device_key);
                   Err(StoreFailure::Dropped { failed, reload: Box::new(reload) })
               }
           }
       }
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   /// Replace `write`'s Persona's store file with exactly `write.sealed`'s
   /// bytes (LLR-b9bm36): a new temporary file `persona-<hex>.store.tmp-<16
   /// hex>` in the same directory, its suffix drawn from the handle's source

   /// can and names the step. Crate-visible: the app writes a store only
   /// through the handle's operations.
   pub(crate) fn write_store(data_dir: &Path, write: &StoreWrite, rng: &HandleRng) -> Result<(), StoreFileError> {
       let path = store_path(data_dir, &write.device_key);
       let mut suffix = [0u8; 8];
       rng.lock().try_fill_bytes(&mut suffix).map_err(|error| {
           StoreFileError::new(StoreFileStep::CreateTemporary, &path, format!("the random source failed: {error}"))
       })?;
       let mut temporary_name = path.as_os_str().to_owned();
       temporary_name.push(format!(".tmp-{}", hex::encode(suffix)));
       let temporary = PathBuf::from(temporary_name);
   ```

   ```rust
   pub enum ExchangeError {
   ```

   **j. `org-io/src/receiver.rs`:** the receive step over the new check, with the handle's source and no chain read;
   its reports are transitional until T40 (LLR-x36szv), and an answer org-node builds for an organisation request is not
   sent until T41.
   ```rust
   //! The receive step (SDD-2fc2cq): `OrgIo::start_receiving` and `OrgIo::next_received`. The step
   //! waits for the next body on the receive channel holding no lock on the node; it takes the node
   //! only around org-node's chain-free check and the store write that follows, and reads no chain.
   //! The end of the receive loop is a typed terminal condition, and nothing else is (LLR-szhe7j).
   //! *Plan T28:* the commit after a chain read is gone with org-node's `commit_checked`; T40 gives
   //! each kind its report, T41 sends an organisation request's answer.

   use org_node::{AdmissionVerdict, Checked, DevicePublicKey, OrgNodeError};

   use crate::endpoints::Inbound;
   use crate::transport::{TransportError, Verdict};
   use crate::{OrgIo, StoreFailure};

   /// What `OrgIo::next_received` received, public data only: the receiving and the sending Device.
   #[derive(Debug)]
   pub enum Received {
       /// org-node's check accepted the body, or found it already held; its store change, if any, is
       /// written. Answered `Verdict::Accepted`.
       Accepted { receiver: DevicePublicKey, sender: DevicePublicKey },
       /// An admission request org-node's check did not keep (already received, or the invite used by
       /// another Device): nothing written. Answered `Verdict::Refused` until T40's verdict bytes.
       NotKept { receiver: DevicePublicKey, sender: DevicePublicKey },
   }

   /// Why the receive loop ends (LLR-szhe7j).
   #[derive(Debug)]
   pub enum TerminalCause {
       /// Every accept task has ended, or none was started: nothing more can arrive.
       EndpointClosed,
       /// An endpoint could not be bound.
       BindFailed(TransportError),
   }

   /// Why the receive step returned no message (LLR-szhe7j). Public data only.
   #[derive(Debug)]
   pub enum ReceiveError {
       /// The receive loop ends.
       Terminal(TerminalCause),
       /// One inbound connection failed before it carried a body.
       Connection(TransportError),
       /// org-node refused the body.
       Refused(OrgNodeError),
       /// org-node's store change was not written; the Persona was reloaded or dropped (LLR-murjr6).
       Store(StoreFailure),
   }

   impl std::fmt::Display for ReceiveError {
       fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
           match self {
               Self::Terminal(TerminalCause::EndpointClosed) => write!(formatter, "the receive loop ended: every endpoint closed"),
               Self::Terminal(TerminalCause::BindFailed(error)) => write!(formatter, "the receive loop ended: {error}"),
               Self::Connection(error) => write!(formatter, "an inbound connection failed: {error}"),
               Self::Refused(error) => write!(formatter, "{error}"),
               Self::Store(failure) => write!(formatter, "the message was kept, but {failure}"),
           }
       }
   }

   impl std::error::Error for ReceiveError {}
   ```
   followed by today's `impl OrgIo { start_receiving, with_connection_time_limit_for_test }` unchanged, and:
   ```rust
   impl OrgIo {
       /// Receive one message: wait, with no lock on the node, for one body, the Device it reached and
       /// its authenticated sender; hand them to org-node's `check_received` with the handle's source;
       /// write the store change it returns; answer the sender with one verdict byte.
       pub async fn next_received(&self) -> Result<Received, ReceiveError> {
           let Inbound { receiver, sender, body, verdict } = self.local.endpoints.next_inbound().await.map_err(|error| match error {
               TransportError::EndpointClosed => ReceiveError::Terminal(TerminalCause::EndpointClosed),
               other => ReceiveError::Connection(other),
           })?;
           let received = self.check(receiver, sender, &body).await;
           let answer = if matches!(received, Ok(Received::Accepted { .. })) { Verdict::Accepted } else { Verdict::Refused };
           // A sender gone already reads silence as a refusal: nothing to do.
           let _ = verdict.send(answer);
           received
       }

       /// org-node's check of `body` in `receiver`'s store, and its store change written.
       async fn check(&self, receiver: DevicePublicKey, sender: DevicePublicKey, body: &[u8]) -> Result<Received, ReceiveError> {
           let mut service = self.service.lock().await;
           let checked = {
               let mut rng = self.local.rng.lock();
               service.check_received(&mut *rng, &receiver, sender, body)
           };
           let (checked, change) = checked.map_err(ReceiveError::Refused)?;
           if let Some(change) = change {
               self.local.store(&mut service, change).map_err(ReceiveError::Store)?;
           }
           Ok(match checked {
               Checked::AdmissionRequest { verdict: AdmissionVerdict::AlreadyReceived | AdmissionVerdict::InviteUsedByAnotherDevice } => {
                   Received::NotKept { receiver, sender }
               }
               // An organisation request's answer (`Checked::OrganisationRequest { answer }`) is dropped
               // here, unsent, until T41's send.
               _ => Received::Accepted { receiver, sender },
           })
       }
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   //! Handles, Personas and transport helpers for the tests that drive `OrgIo`. The relay and sink
   //! helpers are copied from org-node's `tests/support/mod.rs`. Endpoints are org-io's, each bound
   //! from a keychain item of the installed in-memory keychain (`keep_device_seed`, `bind_seed`). A
   //! device key pair in a test file is allowed: org-io's absence of device private keys
   //! (LLR-3zdw8v) is a scan of `org-io/src`.
   //!
   //! *Plan T28, 2026-10-21:* org-io's `create_persona`, `found_organisation`, `admit_member`,
   //! `revoke_member`, `submit_commit_send` and the reply operations are gone. A Persona is made
   //! here as org-node now makes one — a provisional founding (`propose_founding`) — its Device seed
   //! put in the keychain and its store written through the handle (`store_for_test`), so a test
   //! that needs only a Persona and its endpoint reads as before. `founded`, `held`, `timed_out`,
   //! `hung`, `committed`, `joiner`, `joiner_of` and `at` are gone with the operations they drove.
   #![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

   use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard};
   use std::time::Duration;

   use org_node::service::OrgService;
   use org_node::store::{PersonaStore, SealedStore};
   use org_node::test_fixtures::device_keypair;
   use org_node::wire::WireMessage;
   use org_node::{DevicePublicKey, DeviceSecret, OrgNodeError, PersonaId};
   use org_io::test_support::{FakeChain, MemoryKeychain};
   use org_io::transport::{BindPlan, OrgEndpoint};
   use org_io::{OrgIo, ReceiveError, Received};
   use rand::rngs::OsRng;
   use tokio::sync::mpsc;
   use zeroize::Zeroizing;

   /// How long a network step may take before the test gives up.
   pub const NET: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);

   /// The data directory of `party`'s handle in test `tag`.
   pub fn store_dir(tag: &str, party: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {
       std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("org-io-{tag}-{party}-{}", std::process::id()))
   }

   /// `party`'s stores in test `tag`, opened again from its data directory with the device secrets
   /// the keychain holds: what the handle persisted.
   pub fn reopened_service(tag: &str, party: &str, io: &OrgIo) -> OrgService {
       let mut stores = vec![];
       for entry in std::fs::read_dir(store_dir(tag, party)).unwrap() {
           let path = entry.unwrap().path();
           let name = path.file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy().to_string();
           let Some(hex_key) = name.strip_prefix("persona-").and_then(|rest| rest.strip_suffix(".store")) else { continue };
           let key_bytes: [u8; 32] = hex::decode(hex_key).unwrap().try_into().unwrap();
           let device = DevicePublicKey::parse(&key_bytes).unwrap();
           let sealed = SealedStore::from_bytes(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap());
           let secret = io.device_secret_for_test(&device).expect("the keychain holds the Persona's secret");
           stores.push(PersonaStore::unseal(&sealed, device, secret).unwrap());
       }
       OrgService::new(stores).unwrap()
   }

   /// A fresh handle for `party` in test `tag`, over `chain`, writing its stores to a fresh directory.
   pub fn handle(tag: &str, party: &str, chain: &FakeChain) -> OrgIo {
       let dir = store_dir(tag, party);
       let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
       std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
       OrgIo::for_test(OrgService::new(Vec::new()).unwrap(), chain).with_data_dir_for_test(dir)
   }

   /// The bytes of `party`'s store files in test `tag`, in file-name order.
   pub fn store_bytes(tag: &str, party: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
       let mut paths: Vec<_> = std::fs::read_dir(store_dir(tag, party)).unwrap().map(|entry| entry.unwrap().path()).collect();
       paths.sort();
       paths.into_iter().flat_map(|path| std::fs::read(path).unwrap()).collect()
   }

   /// A Persona on the handle's node, its secret in the shared in-memory keychain.
   pub async fn persona(io: &OrgIo, handle_text: &str) -> PersonaId {
       persona_named(io, handle_text, "Test", "User").await
   }

   /// `persona` with the name and surname given.
   pub async fn persona_named(io: &OrgIo, handle_text: &str, name: &str, surname: &str) -> PersonaId {
       MemoryKeychain::shared().install();
       create_named(io, handle_text, name, surname).await
   }

   /// A Persona named Test User; its secret goes to whichever in-memory keychain the test installed.
   pub async fn create(io: &OrgIo, handle_text: &str) -> PersonaId {
       create_named(io, handle_text, "Test", "User").await
   }

   /// A Persona as org-node makes one: a provisional founding of "Test Organisation", proposed with
   /// the test's own source, its Device seed written to the keychain item first, then its store
   /// written through the handle. Binds no endpoint.
   pub async fn create_named(io: &OrgIo, handle_text: &str, name: &str, surname: &str) -> PersonaId {
       let (device_key, secret, change) =
           io.node_for_test().propose_founding(&mut OsRng, name, surname, handle_text, "Test Organisation".to_string()).unwrap();
       org_io::test_support::keychain::write_device_secret(&device_key, &secret).unwrap();
       drop(secret);
       io.store_for_test(change).unwrap();
       persona_of(io, &device_key)
   }

   /// The Persona whose Device key is `device_key`.
   pub fn persona_of(io: &OrgIo, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> PersonaId {
       io.node_for_test()
           .list_personas()
           .into_iter()
           .find(|persona| &persona.device_key == device_key)
           .map(|persona| persona.persona_id.clone())
           .unwrap()
   }

   /// Serialises the tests of one binary that install a keychain of their own.
   static KEYCHAIN_LOCK: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());

   /// The lock, and a fresh in-memory keychain installed for as long as it is held.
   pub fn fresh_keychain() -> (MutexGuard<'static, ()>, MemoryKeychain) {
       let guard = KEYCHAIN_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());
       let keychain = MemoryKeychain::default();
       keychain.install();
       (guard, keychain)
   }

   /// org-node's refusal of a receive; anything else fails the test.
   pub fn refusal(received: Result<Received, ReceiveError>) -> OrgNodeError {
       match received {
           Err(ReceiveError::Refused(refused)) => refused,
           other => panic!("not refused by org-node: {other:?}"),
       }
   }

   /// The store file of `device_key` in `dir`, by the naming rule spelled out here.
   pub fn file_of(dir: &std::path::Path, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> std::path::PathBuf {
       dir.join(format!("persona-{}.store", hex::encode(device_key.as_bytes())))
   }

   /// The store `io` holds for `persona_id`, as its `Debug` shows it.
   pub fn held_store(io: &OrgIo, persona_id: &PersonaId) -> String {
       let service = io.node_for_test();
       let device_key = service
           .list_personas()
           .into_iter()
           .find(|persona| &persona.persona_id == persona_id)
           .map(|persona| persona.device_key)
           .expect("the handle holds the Persona");
       format!("{:?}", service.store_data(&device_key).expect("the handle holds the Persona's store"))
   }
   ```

     ```rust
     /// One handle receiving on one Persona's endpoint: the address a stranger sends to.
     async fn receiving(tag: &str) -> (OrgIo, iroh::EndpointAddr) {
         let io = handle(tag, "b", &FakeChain::new());
         create(&io, "bob").await;
         let addr = receiving_addr(&io).await;

     /// What `io` receives while `send` runs.
     async fn received_while<F: std::future::Future<Output = ()>>(io: &OrgIo, send: F) -> Result<Received, ReceiveError> {
         let (received, ()) = tokio::join!(async { tokio::time::timeout(NET, io.next_received()).await.unwrap() }, send);
         received
     }

     // Abnormal: bytes that do not decode are org-node's refusal, and the receive step goes on to
     // the next body, refused the same way.

     #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
     async fn a_malformed_body_is_not_terminal() {
         let (_guard, _keychain) = fresh_keychain();
         let (io, addr) = receiving("step-malformed").await;
         let stranger = bind_seed([0x5c; 32]).await;
         let refused = received_while(&io, send_raw(&stranger, addr.clone(), b"not a wire message")).await;
         assert!(matches!(refused, Err(ReceiveError::Refused(OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage))), "{refused:?}");
         let again = received_while(&io, send_raw(&stranger, addr, b"still not one")).await;
         assert!(matches!(again, Err(ReceiveError::Refused(OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage))), "the next body is received: {again:?}");
     }

     // Abnormal: a connection that fails before it carries a body is `ReceiveError::Connection`,
     // not terminal, and the receive step goes on to the next body.
     // verifies: LLR-szhe7j
     #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
     async fn a_connection_failing_before_a_body_is_not_terminal() {
         let (_guard, _keychain) = fresh_keychain();
         let (io, addr) = receiving("step-connection-failed").await;
         let stranger = bind_seed([0x5d; 32]).await;
         let dial = addr.clone();
         let failed = received_while(&io, async {
             let connection = tokio::time::timeout(NET, stranger.inner().connect(dial, org_io::transport::ALPN)).await.unwrap().unwrap();
             connection.close(1u32.into(), b"no body");
         })
         .await;
         assert!(matches!(failed, Err(ReceiveError::Connection(_))), "{failed:?}");
         let next = received_while(&io, send_raw(&stranger, addr, b"not a wire message")).await;
         assert!(matches!(next, Err(ReceiveError::Refused(OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage))), "the next body is received: {next:?}");
     }
     ```

   ```rust
   #![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]
   ```
