   ```rust
   //! The Person (SDD-j7k844; plan T29): `propose_person` writes the Person's Device seed to its
   //! keychain item, then its sealed `person-<hex>.store` file (LLR-3cysjk); every summary is
   //! provisional (LLR-mas8vc); `open` lists Person files apart from Persona files (LLR-z7kbf9); no
   //! endpoint is bound for the Person's key (LLR-g6kaa8).

   use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

   use org_node::OrgNodeError;
   use org_io::test_support::{FakeChain, Refusal};
   use org_io::transport::TransportMode;
   use org_io::view::PersonStatus;
   use org_io::{CreateError, OpenError, OrgIo, StoreFailure};

   mod common;
   use common::handles::{create, fresh_keychain, handle};

   const SERVICE: &str = "ods-device-seed";

   fn dir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
       let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("org-io-person-{tag}-{}", std::process::id()));
       if dir.exists() {
           make_writable(&dir);
       }
       let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
       dir
   }

   fn names_in(dir: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
       let mut names: Vec<String> =
           std::fs::read_dir(dir).unwrap().map(|entry| entry.unwrap().file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string()).collect();
       names.sort();
       names
   }

   fn person_file(dir: &Path, device_key: &org_node::DevicePublicKey) -> PathBuf {
       dir.join(format!("person-{}.store", hex::encode(device_key.as_bytes())))
   }

   #[cfg(unix)]
   fn make_read_only(dir: &Path) {
       let mut permissions = std::fs::metadata(dir).unwrap().permissions();
       permissions.set_readonly(true);
       std::fs::set_permissions(dir, permissions).unwrap();
   }

   #[allow(clippy::permissions_set_readonly_false)]
   fn make_writable(dir: &Path) {
       let mut permissions = std::fs::metadata(dir).unwrap().permissions();
       permissions.set_readonly(false);
       std::fs::set_permissions(dir, permissions).unwrap();
   }

   // verifies: LLR-3cysjk
   #[tokio::test]
   async fn propose_person_writes_the_keychain_item_then_the_person_file() {
       let (_guard, keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let dir = dir("writes");
       let io = OrgIo::open(&dir, TransportMode::Loopback).unwrap();
       let person = io.propose_person("Ada", "Lovelace").await.unwrap();
       assert_eq!(keychain.items(), vec![(SERVICE.to_string(), hex::encode(person.device_key.as_bytes()))], "one item, named for the Person's key");
       assert_eq!(names_in(&dir), vec![format!("person-{}.store", hex::encode(person.device_key.as_bytes()))], "one Person file, no Persona file");
       assert!(io.personas().await.is_empty(), "the Person is no Persona");
       drop(io);
       let reopened = OrgIo::open(&dir, TransportMode::Loopback).unwrap();
       assert_eq!(reopened.person().await, Some(person), "the file reopens as the Person proposed");
   }

   // Abnormal: org-node refuses the name; the keychain refuses the item; the file write fails
   // after the item was written, which shows the item came first.
   // verifies: LLR-3cysjk
   #[tokio::test]
   async fn a_refused_name_writes_nothing_and_a_failed_file_write_leaves_the_item() {
       let (_guard, keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let dir = dir("refused");
       let io = OrgIo::open(&dir, TransportMode::Loopback).unwrap();
       match io.propose_person("", "Lovelace").await {
           Err(CreateError::Node(OrgNodeError::InvalidField { field, .. })) => assert_eq!(field, "person.name"),
           other => panic!("not org-node's refusal of the name: {other:?}"),
       }
       assert!(keychain.items().is_empty() && names_in(&dir).is_empty(), "nothing written");

       keychain.refuse_as(Some(Refusal::Unavailable));
       let refused = io.propose_person("Ada", "Lovelace").await;
       keychain.refuse_as(None);
       assert!(matches!(refused, Err(CreateError::Keychain(_))), "{refused:?}");
       assert!(keychain.items().is_empty() && names_in(&dir).is_empty(), "no item and no file");
       assert_eq!(io.person().await, None, "no Person held");

       #[cfg(unix)]
       {
           make_read_only(&dir);
           let refused = io.propose_person("Ada", "Lovelace").await;
           make_writable(&dir);
           assert!(matches!(refused, Err(CreateError::Store(StoreFailure::NotKept { .. }))), "{refused:?}");
           assert_eq!(keychain.items().len(), 1, "the item was written before the file was tried, and stays");
           assert!(names_in(&dir).is_empty(), "no file");
           assert_eq!(io.person().await, None, "the Person is dropped");
       }
   }

   // Abnormal: one Person per device (owner ruling 2026-10-22). A second proposal is refused
   // naming the Person held, before any draw or write: no keychain item and no file is added,
   // and `person()` still returns the first.
   // verifies: LLR-3cysjk
   #[tokio::test]
   async fn a_second_person_is_refused_naming_the_one_held_and_writes_nothing() {
       let (_guard, keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let dir = dir("second");
       let io = OrgIo::open(&dir, TransportMode::Loopback).unwrap();
       let first = io.propose_person("Ada", "Lovelace").await.unwrap();
       let (items, names) = (keychain.items(), names_in(&dir));
       match io.propose_person("Grace", "Hopper").await {
           Err(CreateError::PersonAlreadyHeld { device_key }) => assert_eq!(device_key, first.device_key, "names the Person held"),
           other => panic!("a second Person was not refused: {other:?}"),
       }
       assert_eq!(keychain.items(), items, "no keychain item added");
       assert_eq!(names_in(&dir), names, "no file added");
       assert_eq!(io.person().await, Some(first), "the one Person is still the first");
   }

   // Abnormal: a data directory holding two Person files (a corruption: `propose_person` refuses a
   // second) is refused by `open` naming both Device keys; no file is unsealed, changed or removed.
   // verifies: LLR-z7kbf9
   #[tokio::test]
   async fn open_refuses_two_person_files_naming_both_and_touches_nothing() {
       let (_guard, keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let (dir_a, dir_b) = (dir("two-a"), dir("two-b"));
       let a = OrgIo::open(&dir_a, TransportMode::Loopback).unwrap().propose_person("Ada", "Lovelace").await.unwrap();
       let b = OrgIo::open(&dir_b, TransportMode::Loopback).unwrap().propose_person("Grace", "Hopper").await.unwrap();
       std::fs::copy(person_file(&dir_b, &b.device_key), person_file(&dir_a, &b.device_key)).unwrap();
       let before: Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)> =
           names_in(&dir_a).into_iter().map(|name| (name.clone(), std::fs::read(dir_a.join(&name)).unwrap())).collect();
       let items = keychain.items();
       let mut expected = vec![a.device_key, b.device_key];
       expected.sort_by(|left, right| left.as_bytes().cmp(right.as_bytes()));
       match OrgIo::open(&dir_a, TransportMode::Loopback) {
           Err(OpenError::MoreThanOnePerson { device_keys }) => assert_eq!(device_keys, expected, "both Person files named"),
           Err(other) => panic!("not refused as more than one Person: {other:?}"),
           Ok(_) => panic!("opened a directory holding two Persons"),
       }
       let after: Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)> =
           names_in(&dir_a).into_iter().map(|name| (name.clone(), std::fs::read(dir_a.join(&name)).unwrap())).collect();
       assert_eq!(after, before, "no file changed, added or removed");
       assert_eq!(keychain.items(), items, "no keychain item changed");
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   const PERSON_PREFIX: &str = "person-";

   /// The Person file of the Person whose Device key is `device_key` (LLR-3cysjk, LLR-z7kbf9).
   pub fn person_path(data_dir: &Path, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> PathBuf {
       data_dir.join(format!("{PERSON_PREFIX}{}{SUFFIX}", hex::encode(device_key.as_bytes())))
   }

   /// The Device key a file name with `prefix` carries, or `None` for any other name.
   fn key_named(name: &str, prefix: &str) -> Option<DevicePublicKey> {
       let hex_key = name.strip_prefix(prefix)?.strip_suffix(SUFFIX)?;
       let lower_case_hex = |character: char| character.is_ascii_digit() || ('a'..='f').contains(&character);
       if hex_key.len() != 64 || !hex_key.chars().all(lower_case_hex) {
           return None;
       }
       let bytes: [u8; 32] = hex::decode(hex_key).ok()?.try_into().ok()?;
       DevicePublicKey::parse(&bytes).ok()
   }

   /// The Device keys of the files in `data_dir` named `<prefix><hex>.store`, in byte order.
   fn list_named(data_dir: &Path, prefix: &str) -> Result<Vec<DevicePublicKey>, StoreFileError> {
       let entries = std::fs::read_dir(data_dir).map_err(|error| StoreFileError::new(StoreFileStep::List, data_dir, error))?;
       let mut keys = vec![];
       for entry in entries {
           let entry = entry.map_err(|error| StoreFileError::new(StoreFileStep::List, data_dir, error))?;
           if let Some(device_key) = entry.file_name().to_str().and_then(|name| key_named(name, prefix)) {
               keys.push(device_key);
           }
       }
       keys.sort_by(|left, right| left.as_bytes().cmp(right.as_bytes()));
       Ok(keys)
   }

   /// The Device keys of the Persona store files in `data_dir`, in byte order; every other name,
   /// Person files included, is ignored (LLR-nt8dja, LLR-z7kbf9).
   pub fn list_stores(data_dir: &Path) -> Result<Vec<DevicePublicKey>, StoreFileError> {
       list_named(data_dir, PREFIX)
   }

   /// The Device keys of the Person files in `data_dir`, in byte order (LLR-z7kbf9).
   pub fn list_person_stores(data_dir: &Path) -> Result<Vec<DevicePublicKey>, StoreFileError> {
       list_named(data_dir, PERSON_PREFIX)
   }

   /// The sealed bytes of `device_key`'s Person file.
   pub(crate) fn read_person_store(data_dir: &Path, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> Result<SealedStore, StoreFileError> {
       let path = person_path(data_dir, device_key);
       std::fs::read(&path).map(SealedStore::from_bytes).map_err(|error| StoreFileError::new(StoreFileStep::Read, &path, error))
   }

   /// `write_store`'s steps (LLR-b9bm36) for the Person file of `device_key` (LLR-3cysjk).
   pub(crate) fn write_person_store(
       data_dir: &Path,
       device_key: &DevicePublicKey,
       sealed: &SealedStore,
       rng: &HandleRng,
   ) -> Result<(), StoreFileError> {
       replace_file(data_dir, &person_path(data_dir, device_key), sealed.as_bytes(), rng)
   }
   ```

   `org-io/src/person.rs` (new):
   ```rust
   //! The Person (SDD-j7k844): the user's Person, proposed apart from any Organisation, kept as a
   //! small sealed Person file and its own keychain item, reported provisional. Its types are
   //! org-node's (`PersonStore`); org-io names no `person` crate (LLR-b97usg).

   use crate::view::PersonSummary;
   use crate::{store_file, CreateError, OrgIo, StoreFailure};

   impl OrgIo {
       /// Propose the Person (LLR-3cysjk): org-node builds the Person store from `name`, `surname`
       /// and keys drawn from the handle's source; its Device seed is written to its keychain item
       /// first, then the sealed bytes to `person-<hex>.store`; only then is it held and returned.
       /// One Person per device: while one is held a proposal is refused with `PersonAlreadyHeld`
       /// naming it, before any draw or write (owner ruling 2026-10-22). The Persons' lock is held
       /// for the whole (synchronous) body, so two calls cannot both pass the check.
       pub async fn propose_person(&self, name: &str, surname: &str) -> Result<PersonSummary, CreateError> {
           let mut persons = self.local.persons.lock().unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
           if let Some(held) = persons.first() {
               return Err(CreateError::PersonAlreadyHeld { device_key: held.data().device_key });
           }
           let created = {
               let mut rng = self.local.rng.lock();
               org_node::PersonStore::create(&mut *rng, name, surname)
           };
           let (person, secret, sealed) = created.map_err(CreateError::Node)?;
           let summary = PersonSummary::of(person.data());
           self.local.keychain.keep(secret).map_err(CreateError::Keychain)?;
           if let Some(data_dir) = &self.local.data_dir {
               store_file::write_person_store(data_dir, &summary.device_key, &sealed, &self.local.rng)
                   .map_err(|failed| CreateError::Store(StoreFailure::NotKept { failed }))?;
           }
           persons.push(person);
           Ok(summary)
       }

       /// The one Person this node holds, or `None` (LLR-mas8vc, LLR-z7kbf9).
       pub async fn person(&self) -> Option<PersonSummary> {
           self.local.persons.lock().unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner).first().map(|person| PersonSummary::of(person.data()))
       }
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   /// The Person file of `device_key`, unsealed with its keychain item (LLR-z7kbf9): refused as a
   /// Persona's is, naming the file.
   #[allow(clippy::result_large_err, reason = "as open_store's")]
   fn open_person(data_dir: &std::path::Path, keychain: &Keychain, device_key: DevicePublicKey) -> Result<org_node::PersonStore, OpenError> {
       let path = store_file::person_path(data_dir, &device_key);
       let sealed = store_file::read_person_store(data_dir, &device_key).map_err(OpenError::ReadStore)?;
       keychain.unseal_person(&sealed, device_key).map_err(|failure| match failure {
           UnsealFailure::Keychain(KeychainError::ItemMissing { device_key }) => OpenError::KeychainItemMissing { device_key, path },
           UnsealFailure::Keychain(error) => OpenError::Keychain { path, error },
           UnsealFailure::Store(error) => OpenError::Unseal { device_key, path, error },
       })
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   //! A new Persona per proposal (SDD-bzu2jg; plan T30): `propose_founding_organisation` and

   use std::path::Path;

   use org_node::invitation::{Invite, InviteId};
   use org_node::invitation::EndpointAddresses;
   use org_node::test_fixtures::device_key;
   use org_node::{ChainAccount, DevicePublicKey, Epoch, OrgId, OrgNodeError, OrgState, VerificationTime};
   use org_io::test_support::{FakeChain, Refusal};
   use org_io::{CreateError, OrgIo, StoreFailure};
   use rand::rngs::OsRng;

   mod common;

   const SERVICE: &str = "ods-device-seed";

   /// An Invite of "Acme" from Device `device_key(0x31)`, with no address.
   fn invite_blob(org: u8) -> String {
       Invite {
           org_name: "Acme".to_string(),
           org_id: OrgId::new([org; 20]),
           invitee_name: "Bob".to_string(),
           issuer: device_key(0x31),
           issuer_addresses: EndpointAddresses::parse(vec![]).unwrap(),
           invite_id: InviteId::new([0x33; 32]),
       }
       .encode()
       .unwrap()
   }

   fn names_in(dir: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
       let mut names: Vec<String> =
           std::fs::read_dir(dir).unwrap().map(|entry| entry.unwrap().file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string()).collect();
       names.sort();
       names
   }

   /// Make `founder`'s founding the current record, as a verification would: the proxy recorded,
   /// then org-node's verification against the chain state the founding names.
   fn adopt_founding(io: &OrgIo, founder: DevicePublicKey, root: org_node::RootHash, key: org_node::OrgPublicKey) -> OrgId {
       let org_id = OrgId::new([0x0f; 20]);
       let change = io.node_for_test().record_founding_proxy(&mut OsRng, &founder, org_id, ChainAccount::new([0x0f; 32])).unwrap();
       io.store_for_test(change).unwrap();
       let state = OrgState { root_hash: root, org_pub_key: key, epoch: Epoch::new(1) };
       let (_, change) = io.node_for_test().verify(&mut OsRng, &founder, Some(state), VerificationTime(1), |_| Vec::new()).unwrap();
       io.store_for_test(change.unwrap()).unwrap();
       org_id
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   // REQ-2xgsbn (the outstanding invites are kept in the store files and settled by an adoption):
   // the issuing Persona's file keeps the invite across a reopen, and the adoption that admits the
   // invitee removes it, as the file then shows. The issuer's invite, the joiner's request and the
   // admitting epoch are org-node's operations, through the handles' nodes.
   // verifies: REQ-2xgsbn
   #[tokio::test]
   async fn outstanding_invites_are_kept_in_the_store_files_and_settled_by_adoption() {
       let (_guard, _keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       let dir_a = fresh_dir("invites-settled", "a");
       let a = open(&dir_a, &chain);
       let founder = a.propose_founding_organisation("Alice", "Doe", "alice", "Acme").await.unwrap();
       let org_id = OrgId::new([0x0f; 20]);
       let change = a.node_for_test().record_founding_proxy(&mut OsRng, &founder.founder, org_id, org_node::ChainAccount::new([0x0f; 32])).unwrap();
       a.store_for_test(change).unwrap();
       let founded = OrgState { root_hash: founder.root, org_pub_key: founder.org_public_key, epoch: Epoch::new(1) };
       let (_, change) = a.node_for_test().verify(&mut OsRng, &founder.founder, Some(founded), org_node::VerificationTime(1), |_| Vec::new()).unwrap();
       a.store_for_test(change.unwrap()).unwrap();
       let (invite, change) = a.node_for_test().build_invite(&mut OsRng, &founder.founder, "Bob".into(), vec![]).unwrap();
       a.store_for_test(change).unwrap();
       let kept = |io: &OrgIo| io.node_for_test().store_data(&founder.founder).unwrap().outstanding_invites.len();
       assert_eq!(kept(&open(&dir_a, &chain)), 1, "the invite is kept in the file across a reopen");

       let b = open(&fresh_dir("invites-settled", "b"), &chain);
       let joiner = b.propose_member(&invite.encode().unwrap(), "Bob", "Builder", &["bob"]).await.unwrap();
       let request = b.node_for_test().build_admission_request(&joiner.member_device, vec![]).unwrap();
       let (_, change) = a.node_for_test().check_received(&mut OsRng, &founder.founder, joiner.member_device, &request.body).unwrap();
       a.store_for_test(change.unwrap()).unwrap();
       a.store_for_test(a.node_for_test().record_admission(&mut OsRng, &founder.founder, invite.invite_id, None).unwrap()).unwrap();
       a.store_for_test(a.node_for_test().propose_updated_organisation(&mut OsRng, &founder.founder).unwrap()).unwrap();
       let next = a.node_for_test().provisional_organisations(&founder.founder).unwrap().last().map(|view| (view.root, view.org_pub_key)).unwrap();
       let admitting = OrgState { root_hash: next.0, org_pub_key: next.1, epoch: Epoch::new(2) };
       let (_, change) = a.node_for_test().verify(&mut OsRng, &founder.founder, Some(admitting), org_node::VerificationTime(2), |_| Vec::new()).unwrap();
       a.store_for_test(change.unwrap()).unwrap();
       assert_eq!(kept(&open(&dir_a, &chain)), 0, "the adoption that admits the invitee settles the invite, in the file");
   }
   ```

   `org-io/src/persona.rs` (new):
   ```rust
   //! A new Persona per proposal (SDD-bzu2jg): each provisional founding and each provisional
   //! Member is a new Persona, created by the operation that proposes it — keychain item, then
   //! store file, then its endpoint when the node receives — and never a held one reused
   //! (LLR-kna4zj, LLR-jvx6j9). Replaces `OrgIo::create_persona`.

   use org_node::invitation::{Invite, InviteId};
   use org_node::{DevicePublicKey, Epoch, OrgId, OrgPublicKey, RootHash};

   use crate::transport::TransportError;
   use crate::{CreateError, OrgIo};

   /// What `propose_founding_organisation` built (LLR-4yte89): public data only.
   #[derive(Debug)]
   pub struct ProposedFounding {
       pub founder: DevicePublicKey,
       pub epoch: Epoch,
       pub root: RootHash,
       pub org_public_key: OrgPublicKey,
       /// The bind that failed after the creation, when the node receives (LLR-jvx6j9).
       pub bind: Option<TransportError>,
   }

   /// What `propose_member` built (LLR-6d6wfw): public data only.
   #[derive(Debug)]
   pub struct ProposedMember {
       pub member_device: DevicePublicKey,
       pub org_id: OrgId,
       pub invite_id: InviteId,
       pub org_name: String,
       pub bind: Option<TransportError>,
   }

   impl OrgIo {
       /// Propose a founding (LLR-4yte89, LLR-kna4zj): org-node builds a new Persona holding the
       /// provisional founding of `org_name`, from keys drawn from the handle's source; its Device seed
       /// goes to its keychain item, then its store file; no chain is touched.
       pub async fn propose_founding_organisation(
           &self,
           name: &str,
           surname: &str,
           handle: &str,
           org_name: &str,
       ) -> Result<ProposedFounding, CreateError> {
           let mut service = self.service.lock().await;
           let proposed = {
               let mut rng = self.local.rng.lock();
               service.propose_founding(&mut *rng, name, surname, handle, org_name.to_string())
           };
           let (founder, secret, change) = proposed.map_err(CreateError::Node)?;
           if let Err(refused) = self.local.keychain.keep(secret) {
               service.drop_store(&founder);
               return Err(CreateError::Keychain(refused));
           }
           self.local.store(&mut service, change).map_err(CreateError::Store)?;
           // Read through org-node's key-free Persona view (LLR-8ru6mv), not the test-support `store_data`.
           let founding = service
               .persona_view(&founder)
               .ok()
               .and_then(|view| view.founding)
               .map(|founding| (founding.epoch, founding.root, founding.org_pub_key));
           drop(service);
           let Some((epoch, root, org_public_key)) = founding else {
               return Err(CreateError::Node(org_node::OrgNodeError::NoProvisionalFounding));
           };
           let bind = self.local.endpoints.accept_if_receiving(&founder).await.err();
           Ok(ProposedFounding { founder, epoch, root, org_public_key, bind })
       }

       /// Propose this node as a Member of the Invite's Organisation (LLR-6d6wfw, LLR-kna4zj): the
       /// Invite parsed through org-node, a new Persona holding the provisional Member and its
       /// expected first admission, written as `propose_founding_organisation`'s; it sends nothing.
       pub async fn propose_member(
           &self,
           invite_blob: &str,
           name: &str,
           surname: &str,
           handles: &[&str],
       ) -> Result<ProposedMember, CreateError> {
           let invite = Invite::parse(invite_blob).map_err(CreateError::Node)?;
           let mut service = self.service.lock().await;
           let proposed = {
               let mut rng = self.local.rng.lock();
               service.propose_member(&mut *rng, &invite, name, surname, handles)
           };
           let (member_device, secret, change) = proposed.map_err(CreateError::Node)?;
           if let Err(refused) = self.local.keychain.keep(secret) {
               service.drop_store(&member_device);
               return Err(CreateError::Keychain(refused));
           }
           self.local.store(&mut service, change).map_err(CreateError::Store)?;
           drop(service);
           let bind = self.local.endpoints.accept_if_receiving(&member_device).await.err();
           Ok(ProposedMember { member_device, org_id: invite.org_id, invite_id: invite.invite_id, org_name: invite.org_name, bind })
       }
   }
   ```
   (`NoProvisionalFounding` there guards a state org-node's `propose_founding` cannot leave — a store with no founding
   after it succeeded; no test reaches it.)

   `org-io/src/lib.rs` — `mod persona;`, `pub use crate::persona::{ProposedFounding, ProposedMember};`, and the
   lookup the later tasks share (stores are named by Device key, N2, so no Persona-id lookup is needed):
   ```rust
   /// The Device key of the Persona holding `org_id` as its current record.
   pub(crate) fn holder_of(service: &OrgService, org_id: OrgId) -> Option<DevicePublicKey> {
       service.list_personas().into_iter().find_map(|persona| {
           let holds = persona.org_id == Some(org_id)
               && service.persona_view(&persona.device_key).is_ok_and(|view| view.record.is_some());
           holds.then_some(persona.device_key)
       })
   }
   ```
   `organisations` and `organisation` read each record with its stored name:
   ```rust
       pub async fn organisations(&self) -> Vec<OrgSummary> {
           let service = self.service.lock().await;
           service
               .list_personas()
               .into_iter()
               .filter_map(|persona| service.persona_view(&persona.device_key).ok())
               .filter_map(|view| view.record.as_ref().map(|record| OrgSummary::of(record, &view.org_name)))
               .collect()
       }

       pub async fn organisation(&self, org_id: OrgId) -> Option<OrgSummary> {
           self.organisations().await.into_iter().find(|summary| summary.org_id == org_id)
       }
   ```

   ```rust
   //! The invitation operations (SDD-6gb59p; plan T31): `issue_invite` builds the Invite in the
   //! holding Persona's store with that endpoint's addresses and writes before it returns
   //! (LLR-95e3jx, LLR-v9dkrv); `read_invite` reads its public fields (LLR-npw5zg); `cancel_invite`
   //! removes a kept admission request and its invite (LLR-8ze6cc); `admission_requests` lists the
   //! kept requests (LLR-dm2h8u).

   use std::path::Path;

   use org_node::invitation::{Invite, InviteId};
   use org_node::{ChainAccount, DevicePublicKey, Epoch, OrgId, OrgNodeError, OrgState, VerificationTime};
   use org_io::test_support::{FakeChain, Refusal};
   use org_io::transport::TransportMode;
   use org_io::{ExchangeError, OrgIo};
   use rand::rngs::OsRng;

   mod common;
   use common::handles::{fresh_keychain, handle, persona_of, reopened_service, store_bytes, store_dir};

   /// A's handle over `chain`, holding "Acme" as a current record: a founding proposed through the
   /// handle, then adopted by org-node as a verification would.
   async fn founded(tag: &str, chain: &FakeChain) -> (OrgIo, OrgId, DevicePublicKey) {
       let a = handle(tag, "a", chain);
       let founding = a.propose_founding_organisation("Alice", "Doe", "alice", "Acme").await.unwrap();
       let org_id = OrgId::new([0x0e; 20]);
       let change = a.node_for_test().record_founding_proxy(&mut OsRng, &founding.founder, org_id, ChainAccount::new([0x0e; 32])).unwrap();
       a.store_for_test(change).unwrap();
       let state = OrgState { root_hash: founding.root, org_pub_key: founding.org_public_key, epoch: Epoch::new(1) };
       let (_, change) = a.node_for_test().verify(&mut OsRng, &founding.founder, Some(state), VerificationTime(1), |_| Vec::new()).unwrap();
       a.store_for_test(change.unwrap()).unwrap();
       (a, org_id, founding.founder)
   }

   /// The (Organisation, invite id) pairs `device`'s store keeps.
   fn outstanding(io: &OrgIo, device: &DevicePublicKey) -> Vec<(OrgId, InviteId)> {
       io.node_for_test().store_data(device).unwrap().outstanding_invites.iter().map(|invite| (invite.org_id, invite.invite_id)).collect()
   }

   /// B proposes itself as a Member from `blob` and A keeps its admission request.
   async fn requested(a: &OrgIo, founder: DevicePublicKey, tag: &str, chain: &FakeChain, blob: &str) -> DevicePublicKey {
       let b = handle(tag, "b", chain);
       let member = b.propose_member(blob, "Bob", "Builder", &["bob", "bobby"]).await.unwrap();
       let request = b.node_for_test().build_admission_request(&member.member_device, vec![]).unwrap();
       let (_, change) = a.node_for_test().check_received(&mut OsRng, &founder, member.member_device, &request.body).unwrap();
       a.store_for_test(change.unwrap()).unwrap();
       member.member_device
   }

   #[tokio::test]
   async fn issue_invite_builds_in_the_holding_persona_and_writes_before_it_returns() {
       let (_guard, _keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       let (a, org, founder) = founded("issue-holding", &chain).await;
       let blob = a.issue_invite(org, "Bob Builder").await.unwrap();
       let invite = Invite::parse(&blob).unwrap();
       assert_eq!((invite.org_name.as_str(), invite.org_id, invite.invitee_name.as_str(), invite.issuer), ("Acme", org, "Bob Builder", founder));
       assert_eq!(outstanding(&a, &founder), vec![(org, invite.invite_id)]);
       let on_disk = reopened_service("issue-holding", "a", &a);
       assert_eq!(on_disk.store_data(&founder).unwrap().outstanding_invites.len(), 1, "written before the Blob was returned");
       assert!(matches!(a.issue_invite(OrgId::new([9; 20]), "Y").await, Err(ExchangeError::Node(OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { .. }))));
   }

   // verifies: LLR-v9dkrv
   #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
   async fn the_invite_carries_the_issuing_endpoints_addresses_in_the_current_mode() {
       let (_guard, _keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       let (a, org, founder) = founded("issue-addresses", &chain).await;
       assert_eq!(a.transport_mode_for_test(), TransportMode::Loopback);
       let invite = Invite::parse(&a.issue_invite(org, "Bob").await.unwrap()).unwrap();
       let endpoint = a.bound_endpoint_for_test(&persona_of(&a, &founder)).await.expect("bound by the issue");
       let id = hex::encode(founder.as_bytes());
       let bound: Vec<String> = endpoint.bound_sockets().iter().map(|socket| format!("{id}@{socket}")).collect();
       assert_eq!(invite.issuer_addresses.as_slice(), bound.as_slice(), "the bound loopback sockets, as kept address text");
       assert!(!bound.is_empty(), "at least one bound socket");
       for address in &bound {
           let (endpoint_id, socket) = address.split_once('@').expect("<endpoint id>@<socket>");
           assert_eq!(endpoint_id, id, "the endpoint id is the issuing Device key, 64 lower-case hex");
           assert!(socket.starts_with("127.0.0.1:") || socket.starts_with("[::1]:"), "{address}");
       }
   }

   #[tokio::test]
   async fn read_invite_returns_the_public_fields_and_writes_nothing() {
       let (_guard, keychain) = fresh_keychain();

       let (a, org, founder) = founded("read-invite", &chain).await;
   ```

   `org-io/src/transport/endpoint.rs` (PLAN DELTA) — in `impl OrgEndpoint`:
   ```rust
       /// The addresses this endpoint holds in `mode`, as the kept address text
       /// `"<64 lower-case hex endpoint id>@<socket>"` (LLR-v9dkrv, LLR-4k43dm, LLR-34tfm8; fix item
       /// 18): its bound loopback sockets in Loopback mode; in Networked mode the direct addresses
       /// iroh currently knows for it, possibly none. The endpoint id is the Device key. No relay URL
       /// and no iroh type leaves the transport.
       pub fn addresses(&self, mode: TransportMode) -> Vec<String> {
           let id = hex::encode(self.device_key().as_bytes());
           let sockets: Vec<std::net::SocketAddr> = match mode {
               TransportMode::Loopback => self.bound_sockets(),
               TransportMode::Networked => self
                   .inner
                   .addr()
                   .addrs
                   .iter()
                   .filter_map(|address| match address {
                       iroh::TransportAddr::Ip(socket) => Some(*socket),
                       _ => None,
                   })
                   .collect(),
           };
           sockets.into_iter().map(|socket| format!("{id}@{socket}")).collect()
       }
   ```

   `org-io/src/exchange.rs` — after T28's error type:
   ```rust
   use org_node::invitation::{Invite, InviteId};
   use org_node::OrgId;

   use crate::view::{InviteSummary, KeptAdmissionRequestSummary};
   use crate::OrgIo;

   impl OrgIo {
       /// An Invite for `org_id` from the Persona holding it (LLR-95e3jx, LLR-v9dkrv): that Persona's
       /// endpoint bound first and its addresses in the current mode taken, then org-node builds the
       /// Invite with an identifier drawn from the handle's source and keeps it outstanding; the store
       /// is written before the Blob is returned.
       pub async fn issue_invite(&self, org_id: OrgId, invitee_name: &str) -> Result<String, ExchangeError> {
           let device_key = crate::holder_of(&*self.service.lock().await, org_id).ok_or(OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { org_id })?;
           let addresses = self.local.endpoints.addresses(&device_key).await.map_err(ExchangeError::Bind)?;
           let mut service = self.service.lock().await;
           let built = {
               let mut rng = self.local.rng.lock();
               service.build_invite(&mut *rng, &device_key, invitee_name.to_string(), addresses)
           };
           let (invite, change) = built?;
           self.local.store(&mut service, change).map_err(ExchangeError::Store)?;
           Ok(invite.encode()?)
       }

       /// The public fields of `invite_blob` (LLR-npw5zg); writes and creates nothing.
       pub async fn read_invite(&self, invite_blob: &str) -> Result<InviteSummary, ExchangeError> {
           let invite = Invite::parse(invite_blob)?;
           Ok(InviteSummary {
               issuer_addresses: invite.issuer_addresses.as_slice().to_vec(),
               org_name: invite.org_name,
               org_id: invite.org_id,
               invitee_name: invite.invitee_name,
               issuer: invite.issuer,
               invite_id: invite.invite_id,
           })
       }

       /// Cancel `invite_id` of `org_id` (LLR-8ze6cc): org-node removes its kept admission request and
       /// the outstanding invite, and the store is written before `Ok`.
       pub async fn cancel_invite(&self, org_id: OrgId, invite_id: InviteId) -> Result<(), ExchangeError> {
           let mut service = self.service.lock().await;
           let device_key = crate::holder_of(&service, org_id).ok_or(OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { org_id })?;
           let cancelled = {
               let mut rng = self.local.rng.lock();
               service.cancel_invite(&mut *rng, &device_key, invite_id)
           };
           self.local.store(&mut service, cancelled?).map_err(ExchangeError::Store)
       }

       /// Every admission request the held Organisations keep (LLR-dm2h8u), in store-file order and,
       /// within a store, in org-node's; changes nothing.
       pub async fn admission_requests(&self) -> Vec<KeptAdmissionRequestSummary> {
           let service = self.service.lock().await;
           let mut holders: Vec<_> = service
               .list_personas()
               .into_iter()
               .filter(|persona| service.persona_view(&persona.device_key).is_ok_and(|view| view.record.is_some()))
               .map(|persona| persona.device_key)
               .collect();
           holders.sort_by(|left, right| left.as_bytes().cmp(right.as_bytes()));
           let mut listed = vec![];
           for device_key in holders {
               let Ok(requests) = service.admission_requests(&device_key) else { continue };
               listed.extend(requests.into_iter().map(|(request, invitee_name)| KeptAdmissionRequestSummary {
                   org_id: request.org_id,
                   invite_id: request.invite_id,
                   name: request.name.clone(),
                   surname: request.surname.clone(),
                   preferred_handles: request.preferred_handles.clone(),
                   device_key: request.device_key,
                   invitee_name: invitee_name.to_string(),
               }));
           }
           listed
       }
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   /// `[seed; 32]` and Organisation `[seed; 20]` recorded, its slot set on `chain` at epoch 1, then
   /// org-node's verification against that slot. A held Organisation before org-io writes or
   /// verifies a founding itself (T34–T36). Returns the Organisation and the founder's Device key.
   pub async fn founded(io: &OrgIo, chain: &FakeChain, seed: u8) -> (OrgId, DevicePublicKey) {
       let founding = io.propose_founding_organisation("Alice", "Doe", &format!("alice{seed}"), "Acme").await.unwrap();
       let org_id = OrgId::new([seed; 20]);
       let change = io.node_for_test().record_founding_proxy(&mut OsRng, &founding.founder, org_id, ChainAccount::new([seed; 32])).unwrap();
       io.store_for_test(change).unwrap();
       chain.slots().set(org_id, org_node::OrgState { root_hash: founding.root, org_pub_key: founding.org_public_key, epoch: Epoch::new(1) });
       let state = chain.slots().get(&org_id);
   ```

   ```rust
   //! The Admin's provisional changes and the proposed Organisation (SDD-frsa73): recording an
   //! admission or a revocation, and having org-node calculate the provisional organisation from all
   //! of them; each writes the store org-node returns and touches no chain or transport. No
   //! operation discards (LLR-vvd8dn).

   use org_node::invitation::InviteId;
   use org_node::store::{Origin, ProvisionalChange};
   use org_node::{Epoch, Handle, MemberId, OrgId, OrgNodeError, OrgPublicKey, RootHash};

   use crate::{OperationError, OrgIo};

   /// A provisional change as recorded (LLR-un47j8, LLR-6kb33y): public data only.
   #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum ProvisionalChangeSummary {
       Admission { org_id: OrgId, invite_id: InviteId, handle: Handle },
       Revocation { org_id: OrgId, member_id: MemberId },
   }

   /// The provisional organisation `propose_updated_organisation` kept (LLR-5fchwt).
   #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub struct ProposedOrganisation {
       pub org_id: OrgId,
       pub epoch: Epoch,
       pub root: RootHash,
       pub org_public_key: OrgPublicKey,
   }

   impl OrgIo {
       /// Record the admission of the request kept for `invite_id` (LLR-un47j8), with `chosen_handle`
       /// when one is given; the store is written before the change is returned with its Handle.
       pub async fn propose_admission(
           &self,
           org_id: OrgId,
           invite_id: InviteId,
           chosen_handle: Option<&str>,
       ) -> Result<ProvisionalChangeSummary, OperationError> {
           let mut service = self.service.lock().await;
           let device_key = crate::holder_of(&service, org_id).ok_or(OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { org_id })?;
           let recorded = {
               let mut rng = self.local.rng.lock();
               service.record_admission(&mut *rng, &device_key, invite_id, chosen_handle)
           };
           self.local.store(&mut service, recorded?).map_err(OperationError::Store)?;
           let handle = service.provisional_changes(&device_key)?.iter().rev().find_map(|change| match change {
               ProvisionalChange::Admit { invite_id: admitted, handle } if *admitted == invite_id => Some(handle.clone()),
               _ => None,
           });
           let handle = handle.ok_or(OrgNodeError::NoAdmissionRequestKept)?;
           Ok(ProvisionalChangeSummary::Admission { org_id, invite_id, handle })
       }

       /// Record the revocation of `member_id` (LLR-6kb33y); the store is written before it returns.
       pub async fn propose_revocation(&self, org_id: OrgId, member_id: MemberId) -> Result<ProvisionalChangeSummary, OperationError> {
           let mut service = self.service.lock().await;
           let device_key = crate::holder_of(&service, org_id).ok_or(OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { org_id })?;
           let recorded = {
               let mut rng = self.local.rng.lock();
               service.record_revocation(&mut *rng, &device_key, member_id)
           };
           self.local.store(&mut service, recorded?).map_err(OperationError::Store)?;
           Ok(ProvisionalChangeSummary::Revocation { org_id, member_id })
       }

       /// Have org-node apply every held provisional change to the current record with one fresh
       /// Organisation key pair (LLR-5fchwt); the store is written before the proposal is returned.
       pub async fn propose_updated_organisation(&self, org_id: OrgId) -> Result<ProposedOrganisation, OperationError> {
           let mut service = self.service.lock().await;
           let device_key = crate::holder_of(&service, org_id).ok_or(OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { org_id })?;
           let proposed = {
               let mut rng = self.local.rng.lock();
               service.propose_updated_organisation(&mut *rng, &device_key)
           };
           self.local.store(&mut service, proposed?).map_err(OperationError::Store)?;
           let view = service
               .provisional_organisations(&device_key)?
               .into_iter()
               .rev()
               .find(|view| matches!(view.origin, Origin::Own) && view.current_proposal)
               .ok_or(OrgNodeError::NoProvisionalChange)?;
           Ok(ProposedOrganisation { org_id, epoch: view.epoch, root: view.root, org_public_key: view.org_pub_key })
       }
   }
   ```
   (The two `ok_or` after a successful org-node call guard a store org-node just changed and are unreachable; no test

   ProvisionalChangeSummary};`. `org-io/src/view.rs`: module doc gains "the proposal summaries are `propose.rs`'s";
   no type moves.

**Intent:** `write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Organisation(org_id)) -> Result<WriteReport, WriteRefused>` writes the latest own provisional organisation through `ChainWriter::write_window` and `update` under `WRITE_TIMEOUT`, refusing `NotHeld`, `NoProxyAccount`, `Stale` (org-node's `current_proposal` false) and `OutcomeUnknown` first; a timeout records the unknown write in `PublishState`. No state read, no adoption, no store write.
*Settled at assembly (PLAN DELTA accepted, fix item 17):* `org-io/src/write.rs` is edited, not new (T28 created it); also touches `org-io/tests/absences.rs`
(`WriteReport`, `WriteRefused` and the path segment `write` join the allowlist).

**Steps:**

1. **Write the failing tests.** `org-io/tests/chain_write.rs` (replaces the T1 stub): fourteen tests — six new, eight
   re-created from `publish_path.rs`/`submit_flow.rs` (deleted by T28) under their new names. The update writes go to
   `FakeChain`, whose writer must know the founding's proxy (`register_proxy`, added below); the 90-second bound is
   crossed on a paused clock in a current-thread runtime, as `submit_flow`'s tests did.
   ```rust
   #![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]
   #![allow(
       clippy::await_holding_lock,
       reason = "`fresh_keychain`'s lock serialises the tests over keyring's process-global credential builder for their whole run; each test has its own runtime"
   )]
   //! Writing a provisional organisation to the chain (SDD-mk39e5; plan T33 for an update, T34 for
   //! a founding): `write_organisation_to_chain` writes the latest own provisional organisation
   //! through `ChainWriter` and reports included, refused or unknown (LLR-s7rq5x), refusing first
   //! what it must not write (LLR-48me7m, LLR-mhn4n5); every call is bounded (LLR-d3farr); the window
   //! is read once (LLR-a66ufr); an unknown write is recorded (LLR-7y46be).

   use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;

   use org_node::service::OrgService;
   use org_node::{ChainAccount, Epoch, OrgId, VerificationTime};
   use org_io::test_support::FakeChain;
   use org_io::write::{HeldTarget, WriteRefused, WRITE_TIMEOUT};
   use org_io::{OrgIo, ProposedOrganisation, WriteReport};
   use rand::rngs::OsRng;

   mod common;
   use common::handles::{founded, fresh_keychain, handle, proposed, store_bytes};

   /// A's handle over `chain` holding Organisation `[seed; 20]` (proxy `[seed; 32]`, known to the
   /// chain's writer) with its next epoch proposed.
   async fn ready(tag: &str, chain: &FakeChain, seed: u8) -> (OrgIo, OrgId, ProposedOrganisation) {
       let a = handle(tag, "a", chain);
       let (org, founder) = founded(&a, chain, seed).await;
       chain.register_proxy(ChainAccount::new([seed; 32]), org);
       let next = proposed(&a, org, founder, &handle(tag, &format!("b{seed}"), chain)).await;
       (a, org, next)
   }

   /// `write_organisation_to_chain(Organisation(org))` with the clock paused, so the 90-second bound
   /// passes at once when the write never finishes.
   async fn written_paused(a: &OrgIo, org: OrgId) -> Result<WriteReport, WriteRefused> {
       tokio::time::pause();
       let written = a.write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Organisation(org)).await;
       tokio::time::resume();
       written
   }

   fn still_held(a: &OrgIo, org: OrgId, next: &ProposedOrganisation) -> bool {
       let founder = a.node_for_test().list_personas().into_iter().find(|persona| persona.org_id == Some(org)).unwrap().device_key;
       a.node_for_test().provisional_organisations(&founder).unwrap().iter().any(|view| view.root == next.root && view.org_pub_key == next.org_public_key)
   }

   // verifies: LLR-s7rq5x
   #[tokio::test]
   async fn an_update_is_written_and_reported_included_with_no_state_read_and_no_adoption() {
       let (_guard, _keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       let (a, org, next) = ready("write-included", &chain, 0x31).await;
       let before = store_bytes("write-included", "a");
       assert_eq!(
           a.write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Organisation(org)).await.unwrap(),
           WriteReport::Included { epoch: Epoch::new(2) },
           "included, naming the epoch it wrote"
       );
       let slot = chain.slots().get(&org).unwrap();
       assert_eq!((slot.epoch, slot.root_hash, slot.org_pub_key), (Epoch::new(2), next.root, next.org_public_key), "the chain holds the next epoch");
       assert_eq!((chain.reads(), chain.finalised_reads()), (0, 0), "no state read");
       assert_eq!(a.organisation(org).await.unwrap().epoch.get(), 1, "no adoption");
       assert!(still_held(&a, org, &next), "the provisional organisation stays held until verification");
       assert_eq!(store_bytes("write-included", "a"), before, "no store change");
   }

   // verifies: LLR-48me7m
   #[tokio::test]
   async fn not_held_no_proxy_and_stale_are_refused_before_any_chain_call() {
       let (_guard, _keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       let tag = "write-refused-first";
       let a = handle(tag, "a", &chain);
       let b = handle(tag, "b", &chain);
       let (org, founder) = founded(&a, &chain, 0x32).await;
       chain.register_proxy(ChainAccount::new([0x32; 32]), org);
       assert!(matches!(a.write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Organisation(OrgId::new([0x77; 20]))).await, Err(WriteRefused::NotHeld)));
       assert!(matches!(a.write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Organisation(org)).await, Err(WriteRefused::NotHeld)), "no own provisional organisation");

       // Epoch 2 admits B and is written and adopted by both: B's record is created by a first
       // admission and holds no proxy account.
       proposed(&a, org, founder, &b).await;
       let joiner = b.node_for_test().list_personas()[0].device_key;
       assert!(matches!(a.write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Organisation(org)).await.unwrap(), WriteReport::Included { .. }));
       let state = chain.slots().get(&org);
       let (_, change) = a.node_for_test().verify(&mut OsRng, &founder, state, VerificationTime(2), |_| Vec::new()).unwrap();
       a.store_for_test(change.unwrap()).unwrap();
       let to_b = a.node_for_test().messages_for_current_epoch(&founder).unwrap().into_iter().find(|message| message.recipient == joiner).unwrap();
       let (_, change) = b.node_for_test().check_received(&mut OsRng, &joiner, founder, &to_b.body).unwrap();
       b.store_for_test(change.unwrap()).unwrap();
       let (_, change) = b.node_for_test().verify(&mut OsRng, &joiner, chain.slots().get(&org), VerificationTime(3), |_| Vec::new()).unwrap();
       b.store_for_test(change.unwrap()).unwrap();
       let writes = (chain.update_writes(), chain.write_windows());

       let bob = b.organisation(org).await.unwrap().members.iter().find(|member| member.device_keys.contains(&joiner)).unwrap().id;
       b.propose_revocation(org, bob).await.unwrap();
       b.propose_updated_organisation(org).await.unwrap();
       assert!(matches!(b.write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Organisation(org)).await, Err(WriteRefused::NoProxyAccount)));

       // A proposes epoch 3, then records another change: the proposal is no longer current.
       a.propose_revocation(org, bob).await.unwrap();
       a.propose_updated_organisation(org).await.unwrap();
       let own = a.organisation(org).await.unwrap().members.iter().find(|member| member.device_keys.contains(&founder)).unwrap().id;
       a.propose_revocation(org, own).await.unwrap();
       assert!(matches!(a.write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Organisation(org)).await, Err(WriteRefused::Stale)), "a change recorded after the proposal");
       assert_eq!((chain.update_writes(), chain.write_windows()), writes, "no chain call for any refusal");
   }
   ```

3. **Write the minimal implementation.** `org-io/src/write.rs` — after T28's contents:
   ```rust
   use std::collections::HashMap;
   use std::future::Future;

   use org_node::store::Origin;
   use org_node::{DevicePublicKey, OrgNodeError};

   use crate::{OrgIo, StoreFailure};

   /// What a write or a verification is for (LLR-s7rq5x): a held Organisation's next epoch, or a
   /// provisional founding, by its founder's Device key.
   #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
   pub enum HeldTarget {
       Organisation(OrgId),
       Founding(DevicePublicKey),
   }

   /// A write's outcome (LLR-s7rq5x): public data only.
   #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum WriteReport {
       /// The write executed; `epoch` is the epoch it wrote (LLR-s7rq5x; the app's LLR-rhc555
       /// reports it).
       Included { epoch: Epoch },
       /// It did not; the provisional organisation stays held.
       Refused { reason: String },
       /// The bound elapsed: it may yet execute (LLR-d3farr).
       Unknown { reason: String },
   }

   /// Why nothing was written (LLR-48me7m, LLR-mhn4n5): public data only.
   #[derive(Debug)]
   pub enum WriteRefused {
       NotHeld,
       NoProxyAccount,
       Stale,
       OutcomeUnknown,
       /// org-node refused a query or a record the write needs.
       Node(OrgNodeError),
       /// A founding's proxy exists but its store write failed (LLR-5tpdxw; T34).
       Store { proxy: ChainAccount, failure: StoreFailure },
   }

   /// The write whose outcome is unknown (LLR-7y46be): what it wrote, the epoch it expected, and
   /// for an update the window's last valid block.
   #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub(crate) struct UnknownWrite {
       pub(crate) root: RootHash,
       pub(crate) key: OrgPublicKey,
       pub(crate) expected_epoch: Epoch,
       pub(crate) last_valid_block: Option<u64>,
   }

   /// What org-io keeps between calls, in the handle's memory (SDD-mk39e5, SDD-t4z8sz): one unknown
   /// write per target, cleared only by verification (LLR-zey4mg; T37).
   #[derive(Default)]
   pub(crate) struct PublishState {
       pub(crate) unknown_writes: HashMap<HeldTarget, UnknownWrite>,
   }

   /// Why a bounded call did not succeed.
   enum WriteNotDone {
       Failed(String),
       TimedOut,
   }

   /// One writer call, bounded by `WRITE_TIMEOUT` (LLR-d3farr).
   async fn bounded<T>(write: impl Future<Output = Result<T, String>>) -> Result<T, WriteNotDone> {
       match tokio::time::timeout(WRITE_TIMEOUT, write).await {
           Ok(written) => written.map_err(WriteNotDone::Failed),
           Err(_) => Err(WriteNotDone::TimedOut),
       }
   }

   fn timed_out() -> WriteReport {
       WriteReport::Unknown {
           reason: format!("the write timed out after {} s and may yet execute on chain", WRITE_TIMEOUT.as_secs()),
       }
   }

   impl OrgIo {
       /// Write `target`'s latest own provisional organisation to the chain (LLR-s7rq5x): no state
       /// read, no adoption, no store change but a founding's proxy (T34).
       pub async fn write_organisation_to_chain(&self, target: HeldTarget) -> Result<WriteReport, WriteRefused> {
           match target {
               HeldTarget::Organisation(org_id) => self.write_update(org_id).await,
               HeldTarget::Founding(_) => Err(WriteRefused::NotHeld),
           }
       }

       /// The next epoch of `org_id`: the refusals first (LLR-48me7m, LLR-mhn4n5), then one window
       /// read and one bounded update (LLR-a66ufr, LLR-d3farr), an elapsed bound recorded (LLR-7y46be).
       async fn write_update(&self, org_id: OrgId) -> Result<WriteReport, WriteRefused> {
           let target = HeldTarget::Organisation(org_id);
           let (proxy, root, key, expected_epoch, written_epoch) = {
               let service = self.service.lock().await;
               let device_key = crate::holder_of(&service, org_id).ok_or(WriteRefused::NotHeld)?;
               let record_epoch =
                   service.list_orgs().into_iter().find(|record| record.org_id == org_id).map(|record| record.epoch).ok_or(WriteRefused::NotHeld)?;
               let own = service
                   .provisional_organisations(&device_key)
                   .map_err(WriteRefused::Node)?
                   .into_iter()
                   .rev()
                   .find(|view| matches!(view.origin, Origin::Own))
                   .ok_or(WriteRefused::NotHeld)?;
               let proxy = service.proxy_account(org_id).map_err(WriteRefused::Node)?.ok_or(WriteRefused::NoProxyAccount)?;
               if !own.current_proposal {
                   return Err(WriteRefused::Stale);
               }
               (proxy, own.root, own.org_pub_key, record_epoch, own.epoch)
           };
           let mut publish = self.publish.lock().await;
           if publish.unknown_writes.contains_key(&target) {
               return Err(WriteRefused::OutcomeUnknown);
           }
           let window = match bounded(self.writer.write_window()).await {
               Ok(window) => window,
               Err(WriteNotDone::Failed(error)) => {
                   return Ok(WriteReport::Refused { reason: format!("reading the chain's write window failed, so no write was made: {error}") })
               }
               Err(WriteNotDone::TimedOut) => {
                   return Ok(WriteReport::Refused { reason: "reading the chain's write window timed out, so no write was made".into() })
               }
           };
           match bounded(self.writer.update(proxy, root, key, expected_epoch, window)).await {
               Ok(()) => Ok(WriteReport::Included { epoch: written_epoch }),
               Err(WriteNotDone::Failed(error)) => Ok(WriteReport::Refused { reason: format!("the chain write did not execute: {error}") }),
               Err(WriteNotDone::TimedOut) => {
                   let unknown = UnknownWrite { root, key, expected_epoch, last_valid_block: Some(window.last_valid_block()) };
                   publish.unknown_writes.insert(target, unknown);
                   Ok(timed_out())
               }
           }
       }
   }
   ```
   (The service lock is released before the publish lock is taken and before any chain call: no lock on the node is held
   across a write, so `next_received` and every other command run meanwhile; the publish lock, held across the write,
   keeps a second write of any target from racing the record of an unknown one.)
   `org-io/src/lib.rs`: `OrgIo` regains `publish: tokio::sync::Mutex<write::PublishState>` (every constructor builds
   `publish: Default::default()`); the `#[allow(dead_code)]` on `writer` goes; `pub use crate::write::{HeldTarget,
   WriteRefused, WriteReport};`.
   `org-io/src/test_support.rs`: `FakeChain` gains `write_windows: Arc<AtomicUsize>`, `last_window:
   Arc<Mutex<Option<WriteWindow>>>`; `write_window` counts itself first (`self.write_windows.fetch_add(1, …)`), `update`
   records its window (`*self.last_window.lock()… = Some(window)`, the parameter renamed from `_window`); and:

   ```rust
       }

       pub fn last_update_window(&self) -> Option<WriteWindow> {
           *self.last_window.lock().unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner())
   ```

   ```rust
       /// A founding in two steps (LLR-5tpdxw, LLR-sq5pbq): the proxy created unless one is stored,
       /// recorded by org-node and written before `found_at`; a retry founds at the stored proxy.
       async fn write_founding(&self, founder: DevicePublicKey) -> Result<WriteReport, WriteRefused> {
           let target = HeldTarget::Founding(founder);
           let mut publish = self.publish.lock().await;
           if publish.unknown_writes.contains_key(&target) {
               return Err(WriteRefused::OutcomeUnknown);
           }
           let (stored, root, key, written_epoch) = {
               let service = self.service.lock().await;
               // Read through org-node's key-free Persona view (LLR-8ru6mv).
               let founding = service
                   .persona_view(&founder)
                   .ok()
                   .and_then(|view| view.founding)
                   .ok_or(WriteRefused::NotHeld)?;
               (founding.proxy, founding.root, founding.org_pub_key, founding.epoch)
           };
           let proxy = match stored {
               Some(proxy) => proxy,
               None => {
                   let (org_id, proxy) = match bounded(self.writer.create_proxy()).await {
                       Ok(created) => created,
                       Err(WriteNotDone::Failed(error)) => {
                           return Ok(WriteReport::Refused { reason: format!("creating the pure proxy failed; nothing stored: {error}") })
                       }
                       Err(WriteNotDone::TimedOut) => {
                           publish.unknown_writes.insert(target, UnknownWrite { root, key, expected_epoch: Epoch::new(0), last_valid_block: None });
                           return Ok(timed_out());
                       }
                   };
                   let mut service = self.service.lock().await;
                   let recorded = {
                       let mut rng = self.local.rng.lock();
                       service.record_founding_proxy(&mut *rng, &founder, org_id, proxy)
                   };
                   let change = recorded.map_err(WriteRefused::Node)?;
                   self.local.store(&mut service, change).map_err(|failure| WriteRefused::Store { proxy, failure })?;
                   proxy
               }
           };
           match bounded(self.writer.found_at(proxy, root, key)).await {
               Ok(()) => Ok(WriteReport::Included { epoch: written_epoch }),
               Err(WriteNotDone::Failed(error)) => Ok(WriteReport::Refused {
                   reason: format!("the founding at proxy {} did not complete: {error}", hex::encode(proxy.as_bytes())),
               }),
               Err(WriteNotDone::TimedOut) => {
                   publish.unknown_writes.insert(target, UnknownWrite { root, key, expected_epoch: Epoch::new(0), last_valid_block: None });
                   Ok(timed_out())
               }
           }
       }
   ```

   ```rust
   #![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]
   #![allow(
       clippy::await_holding_lock,
       reason = "`fresh_keychain`'s lock serialises the tests over keyring's process-global credential builder for their whole run; each test has its own runtime"
   )]
   //! Verification (SDD-t4z8sz; plan T35–T37): `verify_organisation` reads the finalised block,
   //! then the state, once each, takes one reading of the handle's clock and hands both to org-node's
   //! verification, mapping its outcome (LLR-t2pve7); a failed read is unverified (LLR-ce42ce); the
   //! clock is replaceable under test-support only (LLR-fzf2n3, LLR-6vtbn6).

   use std::path::Path;
   use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
   use std::sync::Arc;

   use org_node::{ChainAccount, DevicePublicKey, Epoch, OrgId, OrgState, VerificationTime};
   use org_io::test_support::{FakeChain, TestClock};
   use org_io::transport::TransportMode;
   use org_io::verify::{Inconsistency, UnverifiedReason, Verified};
   use org_io::write::HeldTarget;
   use org_io::{OrgIo, WriteReport};
   use rand::rngs::OsRng;

   mod common;
   use common::handles::{founded, fresh_keychain, handle, proposed, store_bytes, store_dir};

   /// `io`'s Organisation `[seed; 20]`, founded, its proxy known to `chain`'s writer.
   async fn held(io: &OrgIo, chain: &FakeChain, seed: u8) -> (OrgId, DevicePublicKey) {
       let (org, founder) = founded(io, chain, seed).await;
       chain.register_proxy(ChainAccount::new([seed; 32]), org);
       (org, founder)
   }

   /// What `founder`'s store holds for the current epoch, delivered to `joiner`'s store as the
   /// receive path would keep it.
   fn deliver_epoch(a: &OrgIo, founder: DevicePublicKey, b: &OrgIo, joiner: DevicePublicKey) {
       let to_b = a.node_for_test().messages_for_current_epoch(&founder).unwrap().into_iter().find(|message| message.recipient == joiner).unwrap();
       let (_, change) = b.node_for_test().check_received(&mut OsRng, &joiner, founder, &to_b.body).unwrap();
       if let Some(change) = change {
           b.store_for_test(change).unwrap();
       }
   }

   /// A holds `[seed; 20]` with B admitted at epoch 2: A wrote and verified it; B kept A's epoch and
   /// adopted it through org-node. Returns A, B, the Organisation, A's and B's Device keys.
   async fn two_members(tag: &str, chain: &FakeChain, seed: u8) -> (OrgIo, OrgIo, OrgId, DevicePublicKey, DevicePublicKey) {
       let (a, b) = (handle(tag, "a", chain), handle(tag, "b", chain));
       let (org, founder) = held(&a, chain, seed).await;
       proposed(&a, org, founder, &b).await;
       assert!(matches!(a.write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Organisation(org)).await.unwrap(), WriteReport::Included { .. }));
       assert!(matches!(a.verify_organisation(HeldTarget::Organisation(org)).await, Verified::Adopted { .. }));
       let joiner = b.node_for_test().list_personas()[0].device_key;
       deliver_epoch(&a, founder, &b, joiner);
       let (_, change) = b.node_for_test().verify(&mut OsRng, &joiner, chain.slots().get(&org), VerificationTime(3), |_| Vec::new()).unwrap();
       b.store_for_test(change.unwrap()).unwrap();
       (a, b, org, founder, joiner)
   }

   /// A removes B in epoch 3, written, verified by A, and B's notice delivered to B.
   async fn remove_b(a: &OrgIo, b: &OrgIo, org: OrgId, founder: DevicePublicKey, joiner: DevicePublicKey) {
       let bob = a.organisation(org).await.unwrap().members.iter().find(|member| member.device_keys.contains(&joiner)).unwrap().id;
       a.propose_revocation(org, bob).await.unwrap();
       a.propose_updated_organisation(org).await.unwrap();
       assert!(matches!(a.write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Organisation(org)).await.unwrap(), WriteReport::Included { .. }));
       assert!(matches!(a.verify_organisation(HeldTarget::Organisation(org)).await, Verified::Adopted { .. }));
       deliver_epoch(a, founder, b, joiner);
   }

   // verifies: LLR-t2pve7
   #[tokio::test]
   async fn verify_organisation_reads_the_block_then_the_state_once_and_maps_each_outcome() {
       let (_guard, _keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       let (a, b, org, founder, joiner) = two_members("verify-outcomes", &chain, 0x51).await;
       let target = HeldTarget::Organisation(org);
       let (reads, finalised) = (chain.reads(), chain.finalised_reads());
       assert_eq!(a.verify_organisation(target).await, Verified::InStep { epoch: Epoch::new(2) });
       assert_eq!((chain.reads() - reads, chain.finalised_reads() - finalised), (1, 1), "one block read, one state read");

       chain.epoch_ahead.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
       assert_eq!(a.verify_organisation(target).await, Verified::Behind { chain_epoch: Epoch::new(3) });
       chain.epoch_ahead.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);

       let slot = chain.slots().get(&org).unwrap();
       chain.slots().set(org, OrgState { epoch: Epoch::new(1), ..slot });
       assert_eq!(
           a.verify_organisation(target).await,
           Verified::Inconsistent { reason: Inconsistency::ChainBehindRecord { chain_epoch: Epoch::new(1), record_epoch: Epoch::new(2) } }
       );
       chain.slots().set(org, slot);

       remove_b(&a, &b, org, founder, joiner).await;
       assert_eq!(b.verify_organisation(target).await, Verified::Removed { org_id: org }, "B's kept notice, accepted against the chain");
       assert!(b.organisations().await.is_empty());
   }

   // verifies: LLR-ce42ce
   #[tokio::test]
   async fn a_failed_read_or_parse_is_unverified_calls_no_org_node_and_writes_nothing() {
       let (_guard, _keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       let a = handle("verify-failed-read", "a", &chain);
       let (org, _founder) = held(&a, &chain, 0x52).await;
       let target = HeldTarget::Organisation(org);
       let before = store_bytes("verify-failed-read", "a");
       chain.read_failing.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
       assert!(matches!(a.verify_organisation(target).await, Verified::Unverified { reason: UnverifiedReason::Read(_), .. }));
       chain.read_failing.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
       chain.parse_refusing.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
       assert!(matches!(a.verify_organisation(target).await, Verified::Unverified { reason: UnverifiedReason::Read(_), .. }));
       chain.parse_refusing.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
       assert_eq!(store_bytes("verify-failed-read", "a"), before, "nothing written");
       chain.state_hidden.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
       assert!(matches!(a.verify_organisation(target).await, Verified::Unverified { reason: UnverifiedReason::OrgNotOnChain, .. }), "no state: org-node's refusal, unverified");
       chain.state_hidden.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
       assert_eq!(store_bytes("verify-failed-read", "a"), before, "nothing written");
       assert_eq!(a.verify_organisation(target).await, Verified::InStep { epoch: Epoch::new(1) }, "nothing judged by the failed reads");

   // verifies: LLR-fzf2n3
   #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
   async fn the_time_given_is_one_clock_reading_after_the_read() {
       let (_guard, _keychain) = fresh_keychain();
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       let (a, b, org, founder, joiner) = two_members("verify-clock", &chain, 0x55).await;
       remove_b(&a, &b, org, founder, joiner).await;
       let clock = TestClock::at(1_000_000);
       let b = Arc::new(b.with_clock_for_test(clock.clone()));
       let held = chain.hold_next_read();
       let verifying = {
           let b = b.clone();
           tokio::spawn(async move { b.verify_organisation(HeldTarget::Organisation(org)).await })
       };
       held.arrived().await;
       assert_eq!(clock.readings(), 0, "no reading before the state read returns");
       held.release();
       assert!(matches!(verifying.await.unwrap(), Verified::Removed { .. }));
       assert_eq!(clock.readings(), 1, "one reading per verification");
       let kept = b.node_for_test().kept_acknowledgements(&joiner).unwrap().unwrap();
       assert_eq!(kept.verified_at, VerificationTime(1_000_000), "the time org-node kept is the clock's reading");
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   //! The handle's clock (SDD-83un8g, LLR-fzf2n3): one reading per verification, whole seconds since
   //! the Unix epoch; org-io keeps no time of its own. Replaced under test-support only (LLR-6vtbn6).

   /// A clock: `None` for a reading before the Unix epoch.
   pub trait Clock: Send + Sync {
       fn now(&self) -> Option<u64>;
   }

   /// The production clock: `std::time::SystemTime::now()`.
   pub struct SystemClock;

   impl Clock for SystemClock {
       fn now(&self) -> Option<u64> {
           std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).ok().map(|elapsed| elapsed.as_secs())
       }
   }
   ```

   ```rust
               rng: HandleRng::os(),
               persons: std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
               clock: std::sync::Arc::new(clock::SystemClock),
   ```

   ```rust
   //! Verification (SDD-t4z8sz): read an Organisation's state at a finalised block, hand it to
   //! org-node's verification with one reading of the handle's clock, write the store change it
   //! returns, and report one outcome. The only caller of org-node's `verify` (LLR-3ame3g) and,
   //! with `preflight.rs`, of `StateReader` (LLR-k3zmqb). Replaces `publish.rs`'s reconcile.

   use org_node::invitation::InviteId;
   use org_node::verify_org::{Inconsistency as NodeInconsistency, Verified as NodeVerified};
   use org_node::{DevicePublicKey, Epoch, Handle, MemberId, Name, OrgId, OrgNodeError, Surname, VerificationTime};

   use crate::keychain::KeychainError;
   use crate::write::HeldTarget;
   use crate::OrgIo;

   /// Why a target was not verified (LLR-ce42ce, LLR-fzf2n3, LLR-4qyeut).
   #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum UnverifiedReason {
       /// No verification of the target has run on this handle.
       NotYetVerified,
       /// No Persona here holds the target.
       NotHeld,
       /// The block or state read failed, or the parse refused the state.
       Read(String),
       /// The chain holds no state for the Organisation.
       OrgNotOnChain,
       /// A founding whose write is not recorded.
       FoundingNotWritten,
       /// A founding with no proxy stored: nothing to read (LLR-4qyeut).
       NoProxyYet,
       /// The handle's clock read before the Unix epoch.
       ClockBeforeEpoch,
   }

   /// Why a state is inconsistent with the record (org-node's judgement, mirrored).
   #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum Inconsistency {
       ChainBehindRecord { chain_epoch: Epoch, record_epoch: Epoch },
       OtherRoot { epoch: Epoch },
   }

   impl std::fmt::Display for UnverifiedReason {
       fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
           match self {
               Self::NotYetVerified => write!(formatter, "not yet verified on this handle"),
               Self::NotHeld => write!(formatter, "no Persona here holds the target"),
               Self::Read(error) => write!(formatter, "the chain read failed: {error}"),
               Self::OrgNotOnChain => write!(formatter, "the chain holds no state for the Organisation"),
               Self::FoundingNotWritten => write!(formatter, "the founding is not written to the chain"),
               Self::NoProxyYet => write!(formatter, "the founding has no proxy stored yet"),
               Self::ClockBeforeEpoch => write!(formatter, "the clock reads before the Unix epoch"),
           }
       }
   }

   impl std::fmt::Display for Inconsistency {
       fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
           match self {
               Self::ChainBehindRecord { chain_epoch, record_epoch } => write!(
                   formatter,
                   "the chain is at epoch {} below the record's epoch {}",
                   chain_epoch.get(),
                   record_epoch.get()
               ),
               Self::OtherRoot { epoch } => write!(formatter, "the chain holds another root at epoch {}", epoch.get()),
           }
       }
   }

   /// A provisional change an adoption left out (LLR-gaanm2; filled in T36).
   #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum DiscardedChangeSummary {
       Admission { invite_id: InviteId, name: Option<Name>, surname: Option<Surname>, handle: Handle },
       Revocation { member_id: MemberId, handle: Option<Handle> },
   }

   /// One verification's outcome (LLR-t2pve7): public data only.
   #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum Verified {
       InStep { epoch: Epoch },
       Adopted { epoch: Epoch, discarded: Vec<DiscardedChangeSummary>, own: bool },
       Removed { org_id: OrgId },
       Behind { chain_epoch: Epoch },
       Inconsistent { reason: Inconsistency },
       Unverified { reason: UnverifiedReason },
       /// org-node refused for another reason; nothing written.
       Refused { reason: String },
       /// The keychain refused the Device secret the removal signs with (LLR-8w2z64).
       Keychain { error: KeychainError },
       /// org-node's store change was not written; the Persona was reloaded or dropped (LLR-zcw3xv).
       Store { reason: String },
   }

   impl OrgIo {
       /// Verify `target` against the chain (LLR-t2pve7) and keep the outcome for `verification`.
       pub async fn verify_organisation(&self, target: HeldTarget) -> Verified {
           let verified = self.verify_target(target).await;
           self.publish.lock().await.verifications.insert(target, verified.clone());
           verified
       }

       /// The last outcome of `target`; `Unverified` before any (LLR-ce42ce).
       pub async fn verification(&self, target: HeldTarget) -> Verified {
           let kept = self.publish.lock().await.verifications.get(&target).cloned();
           kept.unwrap_or(Verified::Unverified { reason: UnverifiedReason::NotYetVerified })
       }

       /// The store and Organisation `target` is read for: a held Organisation's record (T36 adds the
       /// founding and the provisional Member).
       async fn read_target(&self, target: HeldTarget) -> Result<(DevicePublicKey, OrgId), UnverifiedReason> {
           let service = self.service.lock().await;
           match target {
               HeldTarget::Organisation(org_id) => crate::holder_of(&service, org_id).map(|device_key| (device_key, org_id)).ok_or(UnverifiedReason::NotHeld),
               HeldTarget::Founding(_) => Err(UnverifiedReason::NotHeld),
           }
       }

       async fn verify_target(&self, target: HeldTarget) -> Verified {
           let unverified = |reason| Verified::Unverified { reason };
           let (device_key, org_id) = match self.read_target(target).await {
               Ok(read) => read,
               Err(reason) => return unverified(reason),
           };
           let _finalised = match self.reader.finalised_block().await {
               Ok(number) => number,
               Err(error) => return unverified(UnverifiedReason::Read(error.to_string())),
           };
           let state = match self.reader.read_state(org_id).await {
               Ok(state) => state,
               Err(error) => return unverified(UnverifiedReason::Read(error.to_string())),
           };
           let Some(now) = self.local.clock.now() else { return unverified(UnverifiedReason::ClockBeforeEpoch) };
           let mut service = self.service.lock().await;
           let mut refused: Option<KeychainError> = None;
           let keychain = &self.local.keychain;
           let judged = {
               let mut rng = self.local.rng.lock();
               service.verify(&mut *rng, &device_key, state, VerificationTime(now), |device_keys| {
                   keychain.for_signing_noting_refusal(device_keys, &mut refused)
               })
           };
           let (outcome, change) = match judged {
               Ok(judged) => judged,
               Err(OrgNodeError::OrgNotOnChain) => return unverified(UnverifiedReason::OrgNotOnChain),
               Err(OrgNodeError::FoundingNotWritten) => return unverified(UnverifiedReason::FoundingNotWritten),
               Err(error @ OrgNodeError::DeviceSecretNotSupplied { .. }) => {
                   return match refused {
                       Some(error) => Verified::Keychain { error },
                       None => Verified::Refused { reason: error.to_string() },
                   }
               }
               Err(error) => return Verified::Refused { reason: error.to_string() },
           };
           if let Some(change) = change {
               if let Err(failure) = self.local.store(&mut service, change) {
                   return Verified::Store { reason: failure.to_string() };
               }
           }
           let record_epoch = service.list_orgs().into_iter().find(|record| record.org_id == org_id).map(|record| record.epoch);
           drop(service);
           match outcome {
               NodeVerified::InStep => Verified::InStep { epoch: record_epoch.unwrap_or(Epoch::new(0)) },
               NodeVerified::Adopted { epoch, own, .. } => {
                   self.clear_adopted_unknown_write(target, org_id).await;
                   Verified::Adopted { epoch, discarded: Vec::new(), own }
               }
               NodeVerified::Removed { org_id, .. } => Verified::Removed { org_id },
               NodeVerified::Behind { chain_epoch } => Verified::Behind { chain_epoch },
               NodeVerified::Inconsistent { reason } => Verified::Inconsistent {
                   reason: match reason {
                       NodeInconsistency::ChainBehindRecord { chain_epoch, record_epoch } => Inconsistency::ChainBehindRecord { chain_epoch, record_epoch },
                       NodeInconsistency::OtherRoot { epoch } => Inconsistency::OtherRoot { epoch },
                   },
               },
           }
       }

       /// The unknown write of `target` an adoption shows executed — the adopted record holds its
       /// root and key — is cleared (LLR-zey4mg's `Adopted`; T37 reports it and settles the rest).
       async fn clear_adopted_unknown_write(&self, target: HeldTarget, org_id: OrgId) {
           let adopted = self.service.lock().await.list_orgs().into_iter().find(|record| record.org_id == org_id).map(|record| (record.root_hash, record.org_pub_key));
           let mut publish = self.publish.lock().await;
           if publish.unknown_writes.get(&target).is_some_and(|unknown| Some((unknown.root, unknown.key)) == adopted) {
               publish.unknown_writes.remove(&target);
           }
       }
   }
   ```
   (`InStep`'s `Epoch::new(0)` fallback is for a record org-node just judged in step and cannot be missing; no test
   reaches it.) `org-io/src/test_support.rs` — append:
   ```rust
   /// A settable clock (LLR-6vtbn6): every reading counted; `set_before_epoch` makes it read before
   /// the Unix epoch.
   #[derive(Default)]
   pub struct TestClock {
       seconds: AtomicU64,
       before_epoch: AtomicBool,
       readings: AtomicUsize,
   }

   impl TestClock {
       /// A clock reading `seconds`.
       pub fn at(seconds: u64) -> Arc<Self> {
           Arc::new(Self { seconds: AtomicU64::new(seconds), ..Self::default() })
       }

       pub fn set(&self, seconds: u64) {
           self.seconds.store(seconds, Ordering::SeqCst);
       }

       pub fn advance(&self, seconds: u64) {
           self.seconds.fetch_add(seconds, Ordering::SeqCst);
       }

       pub fn set_before_epoch(&self, before: bool) {
           self.before_epoch.store(before, Ordering::SeqCst);
       }

       /// How many times the clock was read.
       pub fn readings(&self) -> usize {
           self.readings.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
       }
   }

   impl crate::clock::Clock for TestClock {
       fn now(&self) -> Option<u64> {
           self.readings.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
           (!self.before_epoch.load(Ordering::SeqCst)).then(|| self.seconds.load(Ordering::SeqCst))
       }
   }
   ```

   ```rust
                           (None, Some(_), _) => HeldTarget::Founding(persona.device_key),
                           (None, None, Some(member_of)) => HeldTarget::Organisation(member_of),
                           (None, None, None) => return None,
   ```
