   `org-io/src/receiver.rs`: replaced whole.
   ```rust
   //! The receive step (SDD-2fc2cq): `OrgIo::start_receiving` and
   //! `OrgIo::next_received`. The step waits for the next body on the
   //! receive channel holding no lock on the node (LLR-eeh4pq); it takes the
   //! node only around org-node's `check_received` and the store write that
   //! follows (LLR-kz9hj4), writes exactly one verdict byte (LLR-hhgdk7), and
   //! reads no chain and adopts nothing. The end of the receive loop is a
   //! typed terminal condition, and nothing else is (LLR-szhe7j).

   use org_node::revocation::VerifiedAcknowledgement;
   use org_node::wire::peek_admission_request;
   use org_node::{AdmissionVerdict, Checked, DevicePublicKey, Epoch, Handle, InviteId, Name, OrgId, OrgNodeError, RootHash, Surname};

   use crate::endpoints::Inbound;
   use crate::send::Delivery;
   use crate::transport::{TransportError, Verdict};
   use crate::{OrgIo, StoreFailure};

   /// What `OrgIo::next_received` kept or decided (LLR-x36szv): public data
   /// only. The field types of `AdmissionRequestKept` are those of
   /// `KeptAdmissionRequestSummary` (T31).
   #[derive(Debug)]
   pub enum Received {
       /// Organisation information, or an answer to this node's organisation
       /// request, kept as a provisional organisation for verification.
       ProvisionalOrganisationReceived { org_id: OrgId, epoch: Epoch, root: RootHash, from: DevicePublicKey },
       /// A first admission request, kept for the Admin.
       AdmissionRequestKept {
           org_id: OrgId,
           invite_id: InviteId,
           name: Name,
           surname: Surname,
           preferred_handles: Vec<Handle>,
           from: DevicePublicKey,
           invitee_name: String,
       },
       /// An organisation request answered (T41).
       OrganisationRequestAnswered { org_id: OrgId, requester: DevicePublicKey, delivery: Delivery },
       /// A revocation notice kept for this node; only a verification acts on it.
       RevocationNoticeKept { org_id: OrgId, from: DevicePublicKey },
       /// A revoked Device's acknowledgement, decided against the store alone.
       Acknowledged(VerifiedAcknowledgement),
   }

   /// Why the receive loop ends (LLR-szhe7j).
   #[derive(Debug)]
   pub enum TerminalCause {
       /// Every accept task has ended, or none was started.
       EndpointClosed,
       /// An endpoint could not be bound.
       BindFailed(TransportError),
   }

   /// Why the receive step returned no message: the terminal condition, or
   /// one of the failures after which the loop goes on. Public data only.
   #[derive(Debug)]
   pub enum ReceiveError {
       Terminal(TerminalCause),
       /// One inbound connection failed before it carried a body.
       Connection(TransportError),
       /// org-node's check refused the body; nothing was written.
       Refused(OrgNodeError),
       /// The check's store change was not written (LLR-murjr6).
       Store(StoreFailure),
       /// An organisation request this step does not answer yet; nothing
       /// written, `0x01` written (removed by T41, which answers it).
       AnswerNotSent,
   }

   impl std::fmt::Display for ReceiveError {
       fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
           match self {
               Self::Terminal(TerminalCause::EndpointClosed) => write!(formatter, "the receive loop ended: every endpoint closed"),
               Self::Terminal(TerminalCause::BindFailed(error)) => write!(formatter, "the receive loop ended: {error}"),
               Self::Connection(error) => write!(formatter, "an inbound connection failed: {error}"),
               Self::Refused(error) => write!(formatter, "{error}"),
               Self::Store(failure) => write!(formatter, "the message was kept, but {failure}"),
               Self::AnswerNotSent => write!(formatter, "an organisation request was refused: no answer is sent"),
           }
       }
   }

   impl std::error::Error for ReceiveError {}

   /// What one body came to: a report for the app, nothing to report (an
   /// already-held provisional organisation, a repeated admission request), or
   /// a failure.
   enum Step {
       Report(Received),
       Silent,
       Failed(ReceiveError),
   }

   impl OrgIo {
       /// Start receiving (LLR-z35vbh, LLR-g6kaa8): bind and accept on the
       /// endpoint of every Persona store; the Person's key has none.
       pub async fn start_receiving(&self) -> Result<(), ReceiveError> {
           self.local.endpoints.mark_receiving().await;
           let device_keys: Vec<_> = self.service.lock().await.list_personas().into_iter().map(|persona| persona.device_key).collect();
           self.local
               .endpoints
               .start_accepting(&device_keys)
               .await
               .map_err(|error| ReceiveError::Terminal(TerminalCause::BindFailed(error)))
       }

       /// This handle, dropping each inbound connection that has given no body
       /// within `limit` (LLR-8uf9a5; test builds only).
       #[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
       pub fn with_connection_time_limit_for_test(mut self, limit: std::time::Duration) -> Self {
           self.local.endpoints.set_connection_time_limit(limit);
           self
       }

       /// Receive (LLR-kz9hj4, LLR-eeh4pq): wait, with no lock, for a body,
       /// its receiving Persona and its authenticated sender; hand them to
       /// org-node's check; write the store change it returns; write one
       /// verdict byte; and report what was kept. A body that keeps nothing new
       /// is answered and not reported, and the step waits for the next.
       pub async fn next_received(&self) -> Result<Received, ReceiveError> {
           loop {
               let Inbound { receiver, sender, body, verdict } = self.local.endpoints.next_inbound().await.map_err(|error| match error {
                   TransportError::EndpointClosed => ReceiveError::Terminal(TerminalCause::EndpointClosed),
                   other => ReceiveError::Connection(other),
               })?;
               let (answer, step) = self.check_and_keep(receiver, sender, &body).await;
               // A sender gone already reads silence as a refusal.
               let _ = verdict.send(answer);
               match step {
                   Step::Report(received) => return Ok(received),
                   Step::Silent => continue,
                   Step::Failed(error) => return Err(error),
               }
           }
       }

       /// org-node's check of `body` in `receiver`'s store and the store write
       /// after it, under the lock (LLR-kz9hj4, LLR-zkybw7); the verdict to
       /// write and the step's result.
       async fn check_and_keep(&self, receiver: DevicePublicKey, sender: DevicePublicKey, body: &[u8]) -> (Verdict, Step) {
           let mut service = self.service.lock().await;
           let checked = {
               let mut rng = self.local.rng.lock();
               service.check_received(&mut *rng, &receiver, sender, body)
           };
           let (checked, change) = match checked {
               Ok(checked) => checked,
               Err(refused) => return (Verdict::Refused, Step::Failed(ReceiveError::Refused(refused))),
           };
           if matches!(checked, Checked::OrganisationRequest { .. }) {
               return (Verdict::Refused, Step::Failed(ReceiveError::AnswerNotSent));
           }
           if let Some(change) = change {
               if let Err(failure) = self.local.store(&mut service, change) {
                   return (Verdict::Refused, Step::Failed(ReceiveError::Store(failure)));
               }
           }
           let Some(org_id) = service.list_personas().into_iter().find(|persona| persona.device_key == receiver).and_then(|persona| persona.org_id) else {
               return (Verdict::Refused, Step::Failed(ReceiveError::Refused(OrgNodeError::PersonaNotHeld)));
           };
           match checked {
               Checked::ProvisionalOrganisationKept { epoch } | Checked::OrganisationAnswerKept { epoch } => {
                   let root = service.provisional_organisations(&receiver).ok().and_then(|held| {
                       held.into_iter().find(|provisional| provisional.epoch == epoch).map(|provisional| provisional.root)
                   });
                   match root {
                       Some(root) => (Verdict::Accepted, Step::Report(Received::ProvisionalOrganisationReceived { org_id, epoch, root, from: sender })),
                       None => (Verdict::Accepted, Step::Silent),
                   }
               }
               Checked::AlreadyHeld => (Verdict::Accepted, Step::Silent),
               Checked::RevocationNoticeKept => (Verdict::Accepted, Step::Report(Received::RevocationNoticeKept { org_id, from: sender })),
               Checked::AdmissionRequest { verdict: AdmissionVerdict::AlreadyReceived } => (Verdict::AlreadyReceived, Step::Silent),
               Checked::AdmissionRequest { verdict: AdmissionVerdict::InviteUsedByAnotherDevice } => {
                   (Verdict::InviteUsedByAnotherDevice, Step::Silent)
               }
               Checked::AdmissionRequest { verdict: AdmissionVerdict::Accepted } => {
                   drop(service);
                   (Verdict::Accepted, self.admission_kept(org_id, body).await)
               }
               Checked::Acknowledged(verified) => (Verdict::Accepted, Step::Report(Received::Acknowledged(verified))),
               Checked::OrganisationRequest { .. } => (Verdict::Refused, Step::Failed(ReceiveError::AnswerNotSent)),
           }
       }

       /// The report of a first admission request, filled after its write from
       /// the kept request `admission_requests` lists for its invite
       /// (LLR-zkybw7, LLR-dm2h8u).
       async fn admission_kept(&self, org_id: OrgId, body: &[u8]) -> Step {
           let Some((_, invite_id)) = peek_admission_request(body) else { return Step::Silent };
           let kept = self.admission_requests().await.into_iter().find(|kept| kept.org_id == org_id && kept.invite_id == invite_id);
           match kept {
               Some(kept) => Step::Report(Received::AdmissionRequestKept {
                   org_id,
                   invite_id,
                   name: kept.name,
                   surname: kept.surname,
                   preferred_handles: kept.preferred_handles,
                   from: kept.device_key,
                   invitee_name: kept.invitee_name,
               }),
               None => Step::Silent,
           }
       }
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   enum Step {
       Report(Received),
       Silent,
       Failed(ReceiveError),
       /// An organisation request answered by org-node: its store change is
       /// written; the answer goes out after the verdict, with no lock held.
       Answer { org_id: OrgId, outgoing: crate::send::Outgoing },
   ```

   ```rust
               Checked::OrganisationRequest { answer } => {
                   let addresses = crate::send::kept_for(&service, &receiver, answer.recipient);
                   let outgoing = crate::send::Outgoing { recipient: answer.recipient, body: answer.body, addresses };

               }
   ```
   - `next_received`'s loop sends the answer after the verdict:
   ```rust
       pub async fn next_received(&self) -> Result<Received, ReceiveError> {
           loop {
               let Inbound { receiver, sender, body, verdict } = self.local.endpoints.next_inbound().await.map_err(|error| match error {
                   TransportError::EndpointClosed => ReceiveError::Terminal(TerminalCause::EndpointClosed),
                   other => ReceiveError::Connection(other),
               })?;
               let (answer, step) = self.check_and_keep(receiver, sender, &body).await;
               // A sender gone already reads silence as a refusal.
               let _ = verdict.send(answer);
               match step {
                   Step::Report(received) => return Ok(received),
                   Step::Silent => continue,
                   Step::Failed(error) => return Err(error),
                   Step::Answer { org_id, outgoing } => {
                       // From the Persona the request reached, on a new
                       // connection, at the addresses kept for the requester
                       // (LLR-898z24, LLR-34tfm8); never on the inbound one.
                       let requester = outgoing.recipient;
                       let mut report = crate::send::send_all(&self.local.endpoints, receiver, vec![outgoing]).await;
                       let delivery = report.per_device.pop().map(|(_, delivery)| delivery).unwrap_or(Delivery::NotDelivered {
                           reason: crate::send::SendError::NoAddress,
                       });
                       return Ok(Received::OrganisationRequestAnswered { org_id, requester, delivery });
                   }
               }
           }
       }
   ```
   (`Outgoing` and `kept_for` are `pub(crate)` in `send.rs` since T38.)

   ```rust
   /// An endpoint of `device` that takes one body and answers it `Accepted`
   /// only once `release` is notified; its addresses and arrivals.
   async fn ack_holding(device: org_node::DevicePublicKey, release: Arc<tokio::sync::Notify>) -> (Vec<String>, journey::Arrivals, Arc<OrgEndpoint>) {
       let endpoint = Arc::new(OrgEndpoint::bind_from_keychain(&device, BindPlan::Loopback).await.unwrap());
       let addresses = journey::kept_addresses(&endpoint);
       let (forward, arrivals) = tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel();
       let serving = endpoint.clone();
       tokio::spawn(async move {
           if let Ok((sender, body, reply)) = serving.recv_answerable().await {
               let _ = forward.send((sender, body));
               release.notified().await;
               reply.answer(Verdict::Accepted).await;
           }
       });
       (addresses, arrivals, endpoint)
   }
   ```

   `org-io/src/acknowledge.rs` (new):
   ```rust
   //! The removal acknowledgements (SDD-83un8g): after verification reports
   //! this node removed, one task per removed Persona sends each
   //! acknowledgement org-node keeps to its recipient, from the Persona's own
   //! identity over a direct-only bind (LLR-zzsqj4, LLR-cqr26z, LLR-3w22wc).
   //! org-io learns them only from org-node's list (LLR-sn5ded). The task
   //! holds the node's lock only to read the list, never across a dial.

   use std::collections::HashMap;
   use std::net::SocketAddr;
   use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

   use org_node::service::OrgService;
   use org_node::DevicePublicKey;

   use crate::clock::Clock;
   use crate::rng::HandleRng;
   use crate::send::{send_one, Delivery, SendError};
   use crate::transport::{parse_kept_address, BindPlan, OrgEndpoint, TransportMode};

   /// The delivery tasks running, one at most per removed Persona.
   #[derive(Default)]
   pub(crate) struct Deliveries {
       running: Mutex<HashMap<DevicePublicKey, tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>>,
   }

   impl Deliveries {
       fn running(&self) -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, HashMap<DevicePublicKey, tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>> {
           self.running.lock().unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner())
       }

       /// How many tasks are still running.
       pub(crate) fn running_count(&self) -> usize {
           self.running().values().filter(|task| !task.is_finished()).count()
       }
   }

   /// What a delivery task shares with the handle.
   #[derive(Clone)]
   pub(crate) struct Context {
       pub(crate) service: Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<OrgService>>,
       pub(crate) rng: Arc<HandleRng>,
       pub(crate) clock: Arc<dyn Clock + Send + Sync>,
       pub(crate) data_dir: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
       pub(crate) mode: TransportMode,
       pub(crate) deliveries: Arc<Deliveries>,
   }

   /// The direct-only plan for `mode` (LLR-cqr26z).
   fn direct_plan(mode: TransportMode) -> BindPlan {
       match mode {
           TransportMode::Loopback => BindPlan::Loopback,
           TransportMode::Networked => BindPlan::Direct,
       }
   }

   /// Start `device_key`'s delivery, unless one runs (LLR-zzsqj4): called
   /// once the removed store is written. A store holding no kept removal
   /// starts none.
   pub(crate) async fn start(context: Context, device_key: DevicePublicKey) {
       let kept = context.service.lock().await.kept_acknowledgements(&device_key);
       if !matches!(kept, Ok(Some(_))) {
           return;
       }
       let mut running = context.deliveries.running();
       if running.get(&device_key).is_some_and(|task| !task.is_finished()) {
           return;
       }
       let task = tokio::spawn(deliver(context.clone(), device_key));
       running.insert(device_key, task);
   }

   /// The delivery task: bind the Persona's endpoint direct-only, then run
   /// one round.
   async fn deliver(context: Context, device_key: DevicePublicKey) {
       let endpoint = OrgEndpoint::bind_from_keychain(&device_key, direct_plan(context.mode)).await.ok();
       round(&context, &device_key, endpoint.as_ref()).await;
   }

   /// One round (LLR-3w22wc): every kept acknowledgement, in org-node's
   /// order, each recipient tried at its kept addresses in order until one
   /// accepts; one recipient's outcome never stops the others. The node's
   /// lock is held only while the list is read.
   pub(crate) async fn round(context: &Context, device_key: &DevicePublicKey, endpoint: Option<&OrgEndpoint>) -> Vec<(DevicePublicKey, Delivery)> {
       let kept = context.service.lock().await.kept_acknowledgements(device_key);
       let Ok(Some(kept)) = kept else { return Vec::new() };
       let mut outcomes = Vec::with_capacity(kept.acknowledgements.len());
       for (message, addresses) in kept.acknowledgements {
           let recipient = message.recipient;
           let outcome = match endpoint {
               None => Delivery::NotDelivered { reason: SendError::SenderEndpoint("the direct bind failed".into()) },
               Some(endpoint) => {
                   let addresses = addresses.map(|addresses| addresses.as_slice().to_vec()).unwrap_or_default();
                   try_addresses(endpoint, context.mode, &recipient, &addresses, &message.body).await
               }
           };
           outcomes.push((recipient, outcome));
       }
       outcomes
   }

   /// `recipient`'s kept addresses that may be dialled, in order: in Loopback
   /// mode only those whose identity is the recipient's key.
   fn dialable(mode: TransportMode, recipient: &DevicePublicKey, addresses: &[String]) -> Vec<SocketAddr> {
       addresses
           .iter()
           .filter_map(|text| parse_kept_address(text))
           .filter(|(id, _)| mode == TransportMode::Networked || id == recipient.as_bytes())
           .map(|(_, socket)| socket)
           .collect()
   }

   /// Dial each address alone, in order, stopping at the first `Delivered`;
   /// the last address's outcome otherwise, `NoAddress` when none may be
   /// dialled.
   async fn try_addresses(endpoint: &OrgEndpoint, mode: TransportMode, recipient: &DevicePublicKey, addresses: &[String], body: &[u8]) -> Delivery {
       let mut last = Delivery::NotDelivered { reason: SendError::NoAddress };
       for socket in dialable(mode, recipient, addresses) {
           last = send_one(endpoint, recipient, &[socket], body).await;
           if matches!(last, Delivery::Delivered) {
               break;
           }
       }
       last
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   /// A kept recipient's last outcome in the removal's delivery (LLR-rav7dr).
   #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum AcknowledgementOutcome {
       /// No round has sent to it yet.
       NotYetSent,
   ```

   ```rust
   /// The removal's deletion deadline after its verification time: 7 days.
   pub(crate) const DEADLINE_SECONDS: u64 = 604_800;

   /// The first rounds' offsets from the verification time; then hourly
   /// after the last.
   const FIRST_ROUNDS: [u64; 4] = [0, 60, 300, 1_800];

   /// The first due time after `now` (LLR-bv6wkz): T, T+1 min, T+5 min,
   /// T+30 min, then T+30 min+k hours; `None` once it would be at or past
   /// T+7 days. Pure; due times already passed are skipped, not caught up.
   pub fn next_round_after(verified_at: u64, now: u64) -> Option<u64> {
       let after_first = verified_at + FIRST_ROUNDS[3];
       let due = FIRST_ROUNDS.iter().map(|offset| verified_at + offset).find(|due| *due > now).unwrap_or_else(|| {
           let hours = now.saturating_sub(after_first) / 3_600 + 1;
           after_first + hours * 3_600
       });
       (due < verified_at + DEADLINE_SECONDS).then_some(due)
   }

   /// What the report reads of one removal's delivery.
   #[derive(Clone, Default)]
   pub(crate) struct Progress {
       pub(crate) device_key: Option<DevicePublicKey>,
       pub(crate) outcomes: HashMap<DevicePublicKey, crate::view::AcknowledgementOutcome>,
       pub(crate) next_round: Option<u64>,
       pub(crate) deletion_failure: Option<String>,
   }
   ```

   `Deliveries` gains two fields and their accessors:
   ```rust
   #[derive(Default)]
   pub(crate) struct Deliveries {
       running: Mutex<HashMap<DevicePublicKey, tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>>,
       progress: Mutex<HashMap<org_node::OrgId, Progress>>,
       /// Wakes a waiting task to read the clock again (a settable clock in
       /// tests; never notified in production).
       pub(crate) wake: tokio::sync::Notify,
   }

   impl Deliveries {
       pub(crate) fn progress_of(&self, org_id: org_node::OrgId) -> Option<Progress> {
           self.progress.lock().unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner()).get(&org_id).cloned()
       }

       fn update(&self, org_id: org_node::OrgId, change: impl FnOnce(&mut Progress)) {
           change(self.progress.lock().unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner()).entry(org_id).or_default());
       }

       /// Stop every task (the handle is dropped: a restart resumes them).
       pub(crate) fn abort_all(&self) {
           for task in self.running().values() {
               task.abort();
           }
       }
   }

   /// The handle's share of the deliveries: dropping the handle stops its tasks.
   pub(crate) struct Tasks(pub(crate) Arc<Deliveries>);

   impl Drop for Tasks {
       fn drop(&mut self) {
           self.0.abort_all();
       }
   }
   ```

   ```rust
       let Ok(Some(kept)) = kept else { return };
       let (org_id, verified_at) = (kept.org_id, kept.verified_at.0);
       context.deliveries.update(org_id, |progress| progress.device_key = Some(device_key));
       let mut endpoint = None;
       loop {
           if endpoint.is_none() {
               endpoint = OrgEndpoint::bind_from_keychain(&device_key, direct_plan(context.mode)).await.ok();
           }
           let left = round(&context, &device_key, org_id, endpoint.as_ref()).await;
           let now = context.clock.now().unwrap_or(0);
           let next = next_round_after(verified_at, now);
           context.deliveries.update(org_id, |progress| progress.next_round = next);
           let (true, Some(next)) = (left > 0, next) else { return };
           wait_until(&context, next).await;
       }
   }

   /// Wait until the handle's clock reads `due` (LLR-bv6wkz): sleep for the
   /// difference, or until woken, and read the clock again.
   async fn wait_until(context: &Context, due: u64) {
       loop {
           let now = context.clock.now().unwrap_or(0);
           if now >= due {
               return;
           }
           tokio::select! {
               () = tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(due - now)) => {}
               () = context.deliveries.wake.notified() => {}
           }
       }
   }
   ```
   `round` takes `org_id`, records each outcome, has org-node delete an accepted acknowledgement and writes the
   store before the next recipient (LLR-6ux6yw), does nothing on any other answer (LLR-xwz3nu), and returns how many
   are still kept:
   ```rust
   pub(crate) async fn round(context: &Context, device_key: &DevicePublicKey, org_id: org_node::OrgId, endpoint: Option<&OrgEndpoint>) -> usize {
       let kept = context.service.lock().await.kept_acknowledgements(device_key);
       let Ok(Some(kept)) = kept else { return 0 };
       let mut left = kept.acknowledgements.len();
       for (message, addresses) in kept.acknowledgements {
           let recipient = message.recipient;
           let delivery = match endpoint {
               None => Delivery::NotDelivered { reason: SendError::SenderEndpoint("the direct bind failed".into()) },
               Some(endpoint) => {
                   let addresses = addresses.map(|addresses| addresses.as_slice().to_vec()).unwrap_or_default();
                   try_addresses(endpoint, context.mode, &recipient, &addresses, &message.body).await
               }
           };
           let outcome = match delivery {
               Delivery::Delivered => {
                   if let Some(still) = accepted(context, device_key, recipient).await {
                       left = still;
                   }
                   continue;
               }
               Delivery::NotDelivered { reason } => crate::view::AcknowledgementOutcome::NotDelivered { reason: reason.to_string() },
               Delivery::Refused | Delivery::AlreadyReceived | Delivery::InviteUsedByAnotherDevice => crate::view::AcknowledgementOutcome::Refused,
           };
           context.deliveries.update(org_id, |progress| {
               progress.outcomes.insert(recipient, outcome);
           });
       }
       left
   }

   /// `recipient` accepted (LLR-6ux6yw): under the lock, org-node deletes its
   /// acknowledgement and the sealed store is written; how many are left. A
   /// failed write reloads the Persona (the acknowledgement stays kept); a
   /// refusal writes nothing.
   async fn accepted(context: &Context, device_key: &DevicePublicKey, recipient: DevicePublicKey) -> Option<usize> {
       let mut service = context.service.lock().await;
       let accepted = {
           let mut rng = context.rng.lock();
           service.acknowledgement_accepted(&mut *rng, device_key, recipient)
       };
       let (left, change) = accepted.ok()?;
       crate::store_change(context.data_dir.as_deref(), &context.rng, &mut service, change).ok()?;
       Some(left)
   }
   ```

   - `OrgIo.acks` becomes `acks: acknowledge::Tasks` (`acknowledge::Tasks(Default::default())` where T42 had
     `Default::default()`; `ack_context` clones `self.acks.0`, `delivery_tasks_for_test` reads `self.acks.0`).
   - The store write without a `LocalStore`, which `LocalStore::store` now calls (its body becomes
     `store_change(self.data_dir.as_deref(), &self.rng, service, change)`):
   ```rust
   /// Write `change` to its Persona's store file in `data_dir` (none: kept in
   /// memory only); on a failure the Persona is reloaded from its file, or
   /// dropped when that fails too (LLR-b9bm36, LLR-murjr6).
   pub(crate) fn store_change(
       data_dir: Option<&std::path::Path>,
       rng: &rng::HandleRng,
       service: &mut OrgService,
       change: StoreChange,
   ) -> Result<(), StoreFailure> {
       let Some(data_dir) = data_dir else { return Ok(()) };
       let StoreChange::Sealed(write) = change;
       let device_key = write.device_key;
       let Err(failed) = store_file::write_store(data_dir, &write, rng) else { return Ok(()) };
       match open_store(data_dir, &Keychain, device_key) {
           Ok(store) => {
               service.restore_store(store);
               Err(StoreFailure::Reloaded { failed })
           }
           Err(reload) => {
               service.drop_store(&device_key);
               Err(StoreFailure::Dropped { failed, reload: Box::new(reload) })
           }
       }
   }
   ```
   (T28's `write_store(data_dir, write, rng)` draws the temporary suffix from the handle's source, so `store_change`
   takes it: `LocalStore::store` passes `&self.rng`, the delivery task `&context.rng`.)

   ```rust
   impl OrgIo {
       /// The removal of `org_id` as its delivery stands (LLR-rav7dr); `None`
       /// for an Organisation no removed Persona holds. Writes and sends
       /// nothing.
       pub async fn acknowledgement_report(&self, org_id: OrgId) -> Option<AcknowledgementReport> {
           let progress = self.acks.0.progress_of(org_id).unwrap_or_default();
           let service = self.service.lock().await;
           let candidates: Vec<DevicePublicKey> = match (&progress.device_key, &self.local.data_dir) {
               (Some(device_key), _) => vec![*device_key],
               (None, Some(data_dir)) => store_file::list_stores(data_dir).unwrap_or_default(),
               (None, None) => Vec::new(),
           };
           let kept = candidates
               .iter()
               .find_map(|device_key| service.kept_acknowledgements(device_key).ok().flatten().filter(|kept| kept.org_id == org_id));
           let Some(kept) = kept else {
               return progress.deletion_failure.map(|failure| AcknowledgementReport {
                   org_id,
                   recipients: Vec::new(),
                   next_round: None,
                   deadline: 0,
                   last_deletion_failure: Some(failure),
               });
           };
           let recipients = kept
               .acknowledgements
               .iter()
               .map(|(message, _)| {
                   let outcome = progress.outcomes.get(&message.recipient).cloned().unwrap_or(AcknowledgementOutcome::NotYetSent);
                   (message.recipient, outcome)
               })
               .collect();
           Some(AcknowledgementReport {
               org_id,
               recipients,
               next_round: progress.next_round,
               deadline: kept.verified_at.0 + acknowledge::DEADLINE_SECONDS,
               last_deletion_failure: progress.deletion_failure,
           })
       }

       /// Wake the delivery tasks to read the handle's clock again (test
       /// builds only: a settable clock moves without a sleep ending).
       #[cfg(feature = "test-support")]
       pub fn wake_deliveries_for_test(&self) {
           self.acks.0.wake.notify_one();
       }
   }
   ```

   ```rust
       pub async fn start_receiving(&self) -> Result<(), ReceiveError> {
           self.local.endpoints.mark_receiving().await;
           let device_keys: Vec<_> = self.service.lock().await.list_personas().into_iter().map(|persona| persona.device_key).collect();
           self.local
               .endpoints
               .start_accepting(&device_keys)
               .await
               .map_err(|error| ReceiveError::Terminal(TerminalCause::BindFailed(error)))?;
           let stores = match &self.local.data_dir {
               Some(data_dir) => crate::store_file::list_stores(data_dir).unwrap_or_default(),
               None => Vec::new(),
           };
           let now = self.local.clock.now().unwrap_or(0);
           for device_key in stores {
               let kept = self.service.lock().await.kept_acknowledgements(&device_key);
               if let Ok(Some(kept)) = kept {
                   if now < kept.verified_at.0 + crate::acknowledge::DEADLINE_SECONDS {
                       crate::acknowledge::start(self.ack_context(), device_key).await;
                   }
               }
           }
           Ok(())
       }
   ```

   ```rust
   const REMOVED_PREFIX: &str = "removed-";

   /// The name a Persona's store file has once its deletion began (LLR-vj2nkb).
   pub(crate) fn removed_path(data_dir: &Path, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> PathBuf {
       data_dir.join(format!("{REMOVED_PREFIX}{}{SUFFIX}", hex::encode(device_key.as_bytes())))
   }

   /// The Device key a file name with `prefix` carries (LLR-nt8dja's parse).
   fn device_key_named_with(name: &str, prefix: &str) -> Option<DevicePublicKey> {
       let hex_key = name.strip_prefix(prefix)?.strip_suffix(SUFFIX)?;
       let lower_case_hex = |character: char| character.is_ascii_digit() || ('a'..='f').contains(&character);
       if hex_key.len() != 64 || !hex_key.chars().all(lower_case_hex) {
           return None;
       }
       let bytes: [u8; 32] = hex::decode(hex_key).ok()?.try_into().ok()?;
       DevicePublicKey::parse(&bytes).ok()
   }

   /// The Device keys of the `removed-<hex>.store` files in `data_dir`, in
   /// byte order (LLR-upqj5g).
   pub(crate) fn list_removed(data_dir: &Path) -> Result<Vec<DevicePublicKey>, StoreFileError> {
       let entries = std::fs::read_dir(data_dir).map_err(|error| StoreFileError::new(StoreFileStep::List, data_dir, error))?;
       let mut keys = vec![];
       for entry in entries {
           let entry = entry.map_err(|error| StoreFileError::new(StoreFileStep::List, data_dir, error))?;
           if let Some(device_key) = entry.file_name().to_str().and_then(|name| device_key_named_with(name, REMOVED_PREFIX)) {
               keys.push(device_key);
           }
       }
       keys.sort_by(|left, right| left.as_bytes().cmp(right.as_bytes()));
       Ok(keys)
   }

   /// Rename `device_key`'s store file to its removed name, and on Unix sync
   /// the directory (LLR-vj2nkb): the first step of the Persona's deletion,
   /// called only from `acknowledge.rs`.
   pub(crate) fn mark_removed(data_dir: &Path, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> Result<(), StoreFileError> {
       let (from, to) = (store_path(data_dir, device_key), removed_path(data_dir, device_key));
       std::fs::rename(&from, &to).map_err(|error| StoreFileError::new(StoreFileStep::Rename, &from, error))?;
       sync_directory(data_dir)
   }

   /// Remove `device_key`'s removed file, and on Unix sync the directory
   /// (LLR-vj2nkb): the last file step of the deletion, called only from
   /// `acknowledge.rs`. A file already gone counts as removed.
   pub(crate) fn remove_store(data_dir: &Path, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> Result<(), StoreFileError> {
       let path = removed_path(data_dir, device_key);
       match std::fs::remove_file(&path) {
           Ok(()) => sync_directory(data_dir),
           Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(()),
           Err(error) => Err(StoreFileError::new(StoreFileStep::Remove, &path, error)),
       }
   }
   ```

   `org-io/src/acknowledge.rs`: the deletion, at the deadline, at once with none left, at open, and its retry.
   ```rust
   use crate::{keychain, store_file};

   /// One hour, the retry period of a failed deletion (LLR-3fxxpp).
   const RETRY_SECONDS: u64 = 3_600;

   /// The keychain item, then the renamed file (LLR-vj2nkb's last two steps).
   pub(crate) fn finish_removed(data_dir: &std::path::Path, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> Result<(), String> {
       keychain::delete_device_secret(device_key).map_err(|error| format!("keychain item: {error}"))?;
       store_file::remove_store(data_dir, device_key).map_err(|error| format!("store file: {error}"))
   }

   /// Delete the Persona of `device_key` (LLR-vj2nkb, LLR-3fxxpp), under the
   /// caller's lock: rename its file — on failure nothing else, the Persona
   /// stays — then the item, then the file, then drop its store (dropped too
   /// when a later step fails, which the retry finishes).
   pub(crate) fn delete_now(data_dir: Option<&std::path::Path>, service: &mut OrgService, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> Result<(), String> {
       let Some(data_dir) = data_dir else {
           service.drop_store(device_key);
           return Ok(());
       };
       store_file::mark_removed(data_dir, device_key).map_err(|error| format!("store file: {error}"))?;
       let finished = finish_removed(data_dir, device_key);
       service.drop_store(device_key);
       finished
   }

   /// `OrgIo::open`'s first step (LLR-upqj5g): finish every deletion a
   /// `removed-<hex>.store` records, unsealing nothing; a failure is left for
   /// the hourly retry and the next open (LLR-3fxxpp).
   pub(crate) fn finish_leftovers_at_open(data_dir: &std::path::Path) {
       for device_key in store_file::list_removed(data_dir).unwrap_or_default() {
           let _ = finish_removed(data_dir, &device_key);
       }
   }

   /// `OrgIo::open`'s step after unsealing (LLR-upqj5g): delete each Persona
   /// whose removal is past its deadline by `now`, or keeps no
   /// acknowledgement; the failures, by Organisation.
   pub(crate) fn delete_expired_at_open(data_dir: &std::path::Path, service: &mut OrgService, now: u64) -> Vec<(org_node::OrgId, String)> {
       let mut failures = vec![];
       for device_key in store_file::list_stores(data_dir).unwrap_or_default() {
           let Ok(Some(kept)) = service.kept_acknowledgements(&device_key) else { continue };
           if kept.acknowledgements.is_empty() || now >= kept.verified_at.0 + DEADLINE_SECONDS {
               if let Err(failure) = delete_now(Some(data_dir), service, &device_key) {
                   failures.push((kept.org_id, failure));
               }
           }
       }
       failures
   }

   /// Delete the Persona from its task: close the endpoint, then retry hourly
   /// until done, reporting each failure (LLR-vj2nkb, LLR-3fxxpp).
   async fn delete_from_task(context: &Context, org_id: org_node::OrgId, device_key: &DevicePublicKey, endpoint: Option<OrgEndpoint>) {
       if let Some(endpoint) = endpoint {
           endpoint.close().await;
       }
       loop {
           let attempt = {
               let mut service = context.service.lock().await;
               let still_held = matches!(service.kept_acknowledgements(device_key), Ok(Some(_)));
               match (still_held, context.data_dir.as_deref()) {
                   (true, data_dir) => delete_now(data_dir, &mut service, device_key),
                   (false, Some(data_dir)) => finish_removed(data_dir, device_key),
                   (false, None) => Ok(()),
               }
           };
           match attempt {
               Ok(()) => {
                   context.deliveries.forget(org_id);
                   return;
               }
               Err(failure) => {
                   context.deliveries.update(org_id, |progress| {
                       progress.deletion_failure = Some(failure);
                       progress.next_round = None;
                   });
                   let now = context.clock.now().unwrap_or(0);
                   wait_until(context, now + RETRY_SECONDS).await;
               }
           }
       }
   }

   /// Retry, hourly, every leftover `removed-` file in `data_dir` until none
   /// is left (LLR-3fxxpp; started by `start_receiving` when one is found).
   pub(crate) async fn retry_leftovers(context: Context) {
       let Some(data_dir) = context.data_dir.clone() else { return };
       while !store_file::list_removed(&data_dir).unwrap_or_default().is_empty() {
           let now = context.clock.now().unwrap_or(0);
           wait_until(&context, now + RETRY_SECONDS).await;
           finish_leftovers_at_open(&data_dir);
       }
   }
   ```
   `Deliveries` gains:
   ```rust
       /// Drop `org_id`'s progress: its Persona is deleted (the report is `None`).
       fn forget(&self, org_id: org_node::OrgId) {
           self.progress.lock().unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner()).remove(&org_id);
       }

       /// Record failures found at open, so the report names them.
       pub(crate) fn record_failures(&self, failures: Vec<(org_node::OrgId, String)>) {
           for (org_id, failure) in failures {
               self.update(org_id, |progress| progress.deletion_failure = Some(failure));
           }
       }
   ```
   `deliver` deletes when none is kept (at its start, too) or at the deadline (its loop's body, complete):
   ```rust
   async fn deliver(context: Context, device_key: DevicePublicKey) {
       let kept = context.service.lock().await.kept_acknowledgements(&device_key);
       let Ok(Some(kept)) = kept else { return };
       let (org_id, verified_at) = (kept.org_id, kept.verified_at.0);
       let deadline = verified_at + DEADLINE_SECONDS;
       context.deliveries.update(org_id, |progress| progress.device_key = Some(device_key));
       let mut endpoint = None;
       let mut left = kept.acknowledgements.len();
       loop {
           let now = context.clock.now().unwrap_or(0);
           if left == 0 || now >= deadline {
               delete_from_task(&context, org_id, &device_key, endpoint).await;
               return;
           }
           if endpoint.is_none() {
               endpoint = OrgEndpoint::bind_from_keychain(&device_key, direct_plan(context.mode)).await.ok();
           }
           left = round(&context, &device_key, org_id, endpoint.as_ref()).await;
           if left == 0 {
               continue;
           }
           let now = context.clock.now().unwrap_or(0);
           let next = next_round_after(verified_at, now).unwrap_or(deadline);
           context.deliveries.update(org_id, |progress| progress.next_round = Some(next));
           wait_until(&context, next).await;
       }
   }
   ```
   (the next due time is the deadline once no round is left before it, so the task wakes for the deletion).

   ```rust
   /// The body of the org-io type `name` (`pub struct`, `pub enum` or `pub
   /// type`), comments dropped, from its declaration to its closing brace (or
   /// its `;`), with its file; `None` when org-io defines no such type.
   fn type_body(name: &str) -> Option<(String, String)> {
       for (path, text) in sources() {
           let code = code_lines(&text);
           for (index, line) in code.iter().enumerate() {
               let declares = [format!("pub struct {name} "), format!("pub struct {name}{{"), format!("pub enum {name} "), format!("pub type {name} ")];
               if !declares.iter().any(|declared| line.trim_start().starts_with(declared.as_str())) {
                   continue;
               }
               let mut body = vec![];
               for continuation in &code[index..] {
                   body.push(*continuation);
                   if continuation.trim_end().ends_with(';') && body.len() == 1 {
                       break;
                   }
                   if continuation.starts_with('}') || (body.len() == 1 && continuation.trim_end().ends_with("{}")) {
                       break;
                   }
               }
               return Some((path.display().to_string(), body.join("\n")));
           }
       }
       None
   }

   /// The production public methods of `OrgIo` (wherever its `impl` is), by
   /// name, de-duplicated, with their signatures.
   fn org_io_methods() -> Vec<(String, String)> {
       let mut methods = vec![];
       for (_, text) in sources() {
           let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();
           for signature in public_signatures(&text) {
               let item = (0..signature.line - 1).rev().find(|&earlier| lines[earlier].starts_with("impl")).map(|earlier| lines[earlier]);
               if !item.is_some_and(|line| line.starts_with("impl OrgIo") || line.starts_with("impl crate::OrgIo")) {
                   continue;
               }
               if signature.only_in_test_builds() || enclosing_item_only_in_test_builds(&lines, signature.line - 1) {
                   continue;
               }
               let after = &signature.signature[signature.signature.find("fn ").unwrap() + 3..];
               let name = after[..after.find(['(', '<']).unwrap()].to_string();
               methods.push((name, signature.signature.clone()));
           }
       }
       methods.sort();
       methods.dedup_by(|later, earlier| later.0 == earlier.0);
       methods
   }

   // The handle's production surface is exactly the domain's (LLR-4usfu2):
   // the methods and queries the design names, `open`, `connect`,
   // `not_configured` and `is_own_admin`; none of the removed ones; no
   // parameter is a `PeerAddr`; no method sends, deletes or resends an
   // acknowledgement.
   // verifies: LLR-4usfu2
   #[test]
   fn the_handles_production_methods_are_exactly_the_domain_surface() {
       let expected = [
           "acknowledgement_report", "admission_requests", "cancel_invite", "connect", "is_own_admin", "issue_invite",
           "next_received", "not_configured", "open", "organisation", "organisations", "person", "personas",
           "propose_admission", "propose_founding_organisation", "propose_member", "propose_person", "propose_revocation",
           "propose_updated_organisation", "read_invite", "request_admission", "request_organisation", "send_organisation",
           "start_receiving", "verification", "verify_all", "verify_organisation", "write_organisation_to_chain",
       ];
       let methods = org_io_methods();
       let names: Vec<&str> = methods.iter().map(|(name, _)| name.as_str()).collect();
       assert_eq!(names, expected, "the handle's production methods");
       for (name, signature) in &methods {
           assert!(!signature.contains("PeerAddr"), "{name} takes a peer address: {signature}");
           assert!(name == "acknowledgement_report" || !name.contains("acknowledg"), "{name}: no acknowledgement command");
       }
   }

   // Every type the domain methods return is in the allowlist, every handle
   // method's return type names allowlisted types only, and no allowlisted
   // type org-io defines holds a secret — read through every org-io type its
   // body names, to a fixed point (LLR-gh4rw3).
   // verifies: LLR-gh4rw3
   #[test]
   fn every_returned_type_is_in_the_handle_return_allowlist_and_holds_no_secret() {
       let mut found = vec![];
       for name in DOMAIN_RETURN_TYPES {
           if !HANDLE_RETURN_ALLOWLIST.contains(name) {
               found.push(format!("{name}: not allowlisted"));
           }
       }
       for (file, signature) in handle_methods() {
           for named in named_types(signature.returns()) {
               if !HANDLE_RETURN_ALLOWLIST.contains(&named.as_str()) {
                   found.push(format!("{file}:{}: returns {named}, not allowlisted", signature.line));
               }
           }
       }
       // The handle itself, and the refusal that hands it back, hold org-node's
       // service by design; their way out is the method surface scanned above.
       let handle_types = ["OrgIo", "ConnectFailed"];
       let mut to_read: Vec<String> =
           HANDLE_RETURN_ALLOWLIST.iter().filter(|name| !handle_types.contains(name)).map(|name| name.to_string()).collect();
       let mut read: Vec<String> = handle_types.iter().map(|name| name.to_string()).collect();
       let mut defined = 0;
       while let Some(name) = to_read.pop() {
           if read.contains(&name) {
               continue;
           }
           read.push(name.clone());
           let Some((file, body)) = type_body(&name) else { continue };
           defined += 1;
           for named in named_types(&body) {
               if SECRET_HOLDERS.contains(&named.as_str()) {
                   found.push(format!("{file}: {name} holds {named}"));
               } else if !read.contains(&named) {
                   to_read.push(named);
               }
           }
       }
       assert!(defined >= DOMAIN_RETURN_TYPES.len(), "the scan read org-io's returned types ({defined})");
       assert!(found.is_empty(), "returned types beyond the allowlist, or holding a secret:\n{}", found.join("\n"));
   }

   // Rewritten from absences.rs:1148 (LLR-cc59ys): org-io removes, renames or
   // deletes nothing itself but in the Persona deletion. File removals and
   // renames are only in `store_file::write_store` (its temporary file),
   // `mark_removed` and `remove_store`; those two and the keychain's
   // `delete_device_secret` are called only from acknowledge.rs; no store
   // record is retained, removed or cleared, and nothing is discarded.
   // verifies: LLR-vvd8dn
   #[test]
   fn org_io_removes_nothing_itself_but_in_the_persona_deletion() {
       let mut found = vec![];
       for (path, text) in sources() {
           let file = path.file_name().unwrap().to_string_lossy().to_string();
           let code = code_lines(&text);
           for (index, line) in code.iter().enumerate() {
               let line = without_strings(line);
               let in_function = enclosing_function(&code, index);
               let file_step = file == "store_file.rs" && matches!(in_function.as_deref(), Some("write_store" | "mark_removed" | "remove_store"));
               let removes = ["remove_file", "remove_dir", "fs::rename"].iter().any(|call| line.contains(call));
               if removes && !file_step {
                   found.push(format!("{file}:{}: removes or renames: {}", index + 1, line.trim()));
               }
               let deletion_call = ["mark_removed(", "remove_store(", "delete_device_secret("].iter().any(|call| line.contains(call));
               let declares = line.contains("fn mark_removed") || line.contains("fn remove_store") || line.contains("fn delete_device_secret");
               let defining_file = file == "keychain.rs" && line.contains("delete_device_secret(");
               if deletion_call && !declares && !defining_file && file != "acknowledge.rs" {
                   found.push(format!("{file}:{}: deletes outside acknowledge.rs: {}", index + 1, line.trim()));
               }
               let drops_records = [".retain(", ".remove(", ".clear("].iter().any(|call| line.contains(call))
                   && ["record", "provisional", "members"].iter().any(|field| line.contains(field));
               if drops_records || line.contains("discard_") {
                   found.push(format!("{file}:{}: drops records itself: {}", index + 1, line.trim()));
               }
           }
       }
       assert!(found.is_empty(), "org-io deletes outside the Persona deletion:\n{}", found.join("\n"));
   }

   // Rewritten from absences.rs:1179 (LLR-cc59ys): no public function of a
   // production build writes, renames or removes a file, or calls the store
   // file or keychain functions that do.
   // verifies: LLR-vvd8dn
   #[test]
   fn no_public_function_writes_renames_or_removes_a_file() {
       let file_calls = [
           "remove_file", "remove_dir", "fs::write", "rename(", "OpenOptions", "File::create", "write_store(", "mark_removed(",
           "remove_store(", "delete_device_secret(",
       ];
       let mut found = vec![];
       let mut scanned = 0;
       for (path, text) in sources() {
           if path.ends_with("test_support.rs") {
               continue;
           }
           let lines: Vec<&str> = text.lines().collect();
           for (name, body) in functions(&text) {
               let (declared_at, declaration) = &body[0];
               let trimmed = declaration.trim_start();
               if !(trimmed.starts_with("pub fn ") || trimmed.starts_with("pub async fn ")) {
                   continue;
               }
               if gated_to_test_builds(&lines, declared_at - 1) || enclosing_item_only_in_test_builds(&lines, declared_at - 1) {
                   continue;
               }
               scanned += 1;
               for (line_number, line) in &body {
                   let code = without_strings(line);
                   if let Some(call) = file_calls.iter().find(|call| code.contains(*call)) {
                       found.push(format!("{}:{line_number}: public `{name}` calls `{call}`", path.display()));
                   }
               }
           }
       }
       assert!(scanned >= 20, "the scan found org-io's public functions ({scanned})");
       assert!(found.is_empty(), "a public function writes, renames or removes a file:\n{}", found.join("\n"));
   }

   // Rewritten from absences.rs:1215 (LLR-cc59ys): no public function of
   // org-io discards or forgets a provisional change or organisation.
   // verifies: LLR-vvd8dn
   #[test]
   fn no_public_method_discards_a_provisional_change_or_organisation() {
       let mut found = vec![];
       for (path, text) in sources() {
           for (index, line) in code_lines(&text).iter().enumerate() {
               let trimmed = line.trim_start();
               let Some(after) = trimmed.strip_prefix("pub fn ").or_else(|| trimmed.strip_prefix("pub async fn ")) else { continue };
               let name = &after[..after.find(['(', '<']).unwrap_or(after.len())];
               if ["discard", "forget", "drop_provisional", "cancel_provisional", "drop_change"].iter().any(|word| name.contains(word)) {
                   found.push(format!("{}:{}: a public discard: {}", path.display(), index + 1, line.trim()));
               }
           }
       }
       assert!(found.is_empty(), "org-io offers a public discard:\n{}", found.join("\n"));
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   // verifies: LLR-7qdjqn
   #[tokio::test]
   async fn is_own_admin_makes_one_pinned_signatory_set_read() {
       let chain = FakeChain::new();

       assert_eq!(io.is_own_admin(org()).await, Ok(AdminStatus::Admin));
       assert_eq!(chain.signatory_reads(), 3, "mapped: the account and its definitions, in the one read");
   }
   ```

**Steps:**

The org-io surface this task calls is the design's (org-io's LLR-4usfu2, LLR-3cysjk, LLR-mas8vc, LLR-4yte89, LLR-95e3jx, LLR-npw5zg, LLR-s7rq5x, LLR-t2pve7, LLR-kz9hj4, LLR-x36szv). Where the design names a value but not its field, this task uses the names listed at the end of the T52 section ("Names the app relies on"); org-io's T29–T45 must use them, or this task's code follows whatever org-io chose.

1. **Write the failing tests.** `app/src-tauri/tests/ipc.rs`: rewrite the whole file. The rewrite keeps the in-force tests (the connection-status ones, `unknown_command_is_rejected`, the two LLR-pguhw5 tests over a founding Persona instead of `create_persona`, and the two inherited LLR-4wcyqy tests with the count set to the eight commands that exist after this task). It cuts every test that calls a removed command; the later task named in each test's out-of-force line re-creates it. It adds this task's six tests and the two `propose_person_*` rewrites. The harness gains `harness_over(&FakeChain)`, `org_io_of`, `block_on`, `propose_founding`, `device_key_of` and `founded_org`. `founded_org` founds an Organisation through the handle over the substitute chain, because the app's write and verify commands come only in T50 and T51. Later tasks extend these helpers.
   ```rust
   #![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]
   //! The commands driven across the REAL Tauri IPC boundary.
   //!
   //! Carries: REQ-645jq9 (the transport mode crosses the boundary and is named
   //! `transport_mode` on the wire), REQ-sjkp8z (the org-id boundary check is
   //! reached by the real handler under the real argument name), REQ-vb5pag
   //! (the Person, founding and Invite commands, change
   //! worktree-org-io-domain-api). Each test is annotated with the low-level
   //! requirement of `app/docs/architecture/` it verifies.
   //!
   //! Everything here uses `tauri::test::mock_builder`, the same
   //! `generate_handler!` list as `lib.rs`, and the same camelCase argument names
   //! the frontend sends. What it catches that an extracted-logic test cannot is a
   //! handler that is correct inside and unreachable, misnamed or mis-typed at its
   //! boundary.
   //!
   //! `mock_context` installs an empty ACL (`Resolved::default()`). In Tauri 2 the
   //! capability system gates PLUGIN commands, not app commands registered through
   //! `generate_handler!`, so this suite reaches every handler without a
   //! fixture `tauri.conf.json`.
   //!
   //! No test here sets an environment variable: `AppState::for_test` takes every
   //! input as a parameter, exactly so that these tests cannot race each other.
   //!
   //! *2026-10-22 (worktree-org-io-domain-api, T46):* the old commands
   //! (`create_persona`, `create_organisation`, `export_invite`,
   //! `import_invite`, `produce_invite_reply`, `import_invite_reply`,
   //! `admit_member`, `revoke_member`, `reconcile_organisations`) left with
   //! their tests; the tests whose out-of-force line names a later task are
   //! re-created there over the new commands.

   use std::path::PathBuf;
   use std::sync::Arc;

   use ods_poc_lib::commands;
   use ods_poc_lib::policy::{ChainEndpoint, TransportModeName};
   use ods_poc_lib::state::AppState;
   use org_io::node::DevicePublicKey;
   use org_io::test_support::FakeChain;
   use org_io::{HeldTarget, OrgIo, Verified, WriteReport};

   use tauri::test::{get_ipc_response, mock_builder, mock_context, noop_assets, INVOKE_KEY};
   use tauri::test::MockRuntime;
   use tauri::webview::InvokeRequest;
   use tauri::{Manager, WebviewWindow};

   /// A live mock application with a real `AppState` over a fresh store.
   ///
   /// The `TempDir` is held so the store outlives the test; the `App` is held
   /// because dropping it would tear down the webview the requests go to.
   struct Harness {
       _dir: tempfile::TempDir,
       _app: tauri::App<MockRuntime>,
       webview: WebviewWindow<MockRuntime>,
   }

   fn harness_with(transport: TransportModeName, chain: Option<ChainEndpoint>) -> Harness {
       let dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("tempdir");
       let data_dir = dir.path().to_path_buf();
       harness_at(dir, data_dir, transport, chain)
   }

   /// A harness whose store is opened in `data_dir`, which may lie inside `dir`
   /// and need not exist yet.
   fn harness_at(
       dir: tempfile::TempDir,
       data_dir: PathBuf,
       transport: TransportModeName,
       chain: Option<ChainEndpoint>,
   ) -> Harness {
       let state = AppState::for_test(data_dir, chain, transport).expect("AppState::for_test");
       harness_of(dir, state)
   }

   /// A harness over org-io's substitute chain `chain`, in Loopback mode,
   /// where Organisations can be founded, written and verified.
   fn harness_over(chain: &FakeChain) -> Harness {
       let dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("tempdir");
       let state = AppState::for_test_over(dir.path().to_path_buf(), chain, TransportModeName::Loopback)
           .expect("AppState::for_test_over");
       harness_of(dir, state)
   }

   /// `harness_over` a fresh substitute chain.
   fn harness_over_chain() -> Harness {
       harness_over(&FakeChain::new())
   }

   /// A live mock application managing `state`, whose store lies in `dir`.
   fn harness_of(dir: tempfile::TempDir, state: AppState) -> Harness {
       // The SAME handler list as lib.rs, spelled out here because the macro needs
       // the paths at compile time. `product_registers_the_same_commands_as_the_harness`
       // fails if the two lists drift apart.
       let app = mock_builder()
           .manage(state)
           .invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![
               commands::propose_person,
               commands::propose_founding_organisation,
               commands::issue_invite,
               commands::read_invite,
               commands::list_personas,
               commands::list_orgs,
               commands::connection_status,
               commands::start_receiver,
           ])
           .build(mock_context(noop_assets()))
           .expect("build mock app");

       let webview = tauri::WebviewWindowBuilder::new(&app, "main", Default::default())
           .build()
           .expect("build webview");

       Harness {
           _dir: dir,
           _app: app,
           webview,
       }
   }

   fn harness() -> Harness {
       harness_with(TransportModeName::Networked, None)
   }

   fn request(cmd: &str, body: tauri::ipc::InvokeBody) -> InvokeRequest {
       InvokeRequest {
           cmd: cmd.into(),
           callback: tauri::ipc::CallbackFn(0),
           error: tauri::ipc::CallbackFn(1),
           // The ORIGIN matters, not just the spelling. `Webview::is_local_url`
           // compares against the platform's tauri protocol URL, and a request
           // that is not local is gated by the ACL — which `mock_context` leaves
           // empty — so the wrong literal here makes every command in this suite
           // fail with "not allowed. Plugin not found" rather than run.
           url: if cfg!(any(windows, target_os = "android")) {
               "http://tauri.localhost"
           } else {
               "tauri://localhost"
           }
           .parse()
           .unwrap(),
           body,
           headers: Default::default(),
           invoke_key: INVOKE_KEY.to_string(),
       }
   }

   /// Invoke `cmd` with a JSON argument object and return the raw result.
   fn invoke(
       h: &Harness,
       cmd: &str,
       args: serde_json::Value,
   ) -> Result<serde_json::Value, serde_json::Value> {
       get_ipc_response(&h.webview, request(cmd, tauri::ipc::InvokeBody::Json(args)))
           .map(|b| b.deserialize::<serde_json::Value>().expect("response is JSON"))
   }

   /// Invoke `cmd` and require it to have failed, returning the error message.
   fn invoke_err(h: &Harness, cmd: &str, args: serde_json::Value) -> String {
       match invoke(h, cmd, args) {
           Ok(v) => panic!("{cmd} unexpectedly succeeded: {v}"),
           Err(e) => e.as_str().map(str::to_string).unwrap_or_else(|| e.to_string()),
       }
   }

   /// The harness's shared org-io handle, for what the IPC surface does not
   /// reach (the write and the verification until T50/T51, the Person).
   fn org_io_of(h: &Harness) -> Arc<OrgIo> {
       Arc::clone(&h._app.state::<AppState>().org_io)
   }

   /// Run one of the handle's futures to completion from a test thread.
   fn block_on<F: std::future::Future>(future: F) -> F::Output {
       tauri::async_runtime::block_on(future)
   }

   /// `propose_founding_organisation` over IPC for "Alice Smith" with
   /// `handle` and `org_name`; the new Persona's id.
   fn propose_founding(h: &Harness, handle: &str, org_name: &str) -> String {
       let proposed = invoke(
           h,
           "propose_founding_organisation",
           serde_json::json!({ "name": "Alice", "surname": "Smith", "handle": handle, "orgName": org_name }),
       )
       .expect("propose_founding_organisation");
       proposed["persona_id"].as_str().expect("a Persona id").to_string()
   }

   /// The Device key org-io lists for the Persona `persona_id`.
   fn device_key_of(h: &Harness, persona_id: &str) -> DevicePublicKey {
       block_on(org_io_of(h).personas())
           .into_iter()
           .find(|persona| persona.persona_id.as_str() == persona_id)
           .map(|persona| persona.device_key)
           .expect("org-io lists the Persona")
   }

   /// An Organisation "Acme" founded by the Persona `alice`: proposed over
   /// IPC, then written and verified through the handle over the harness's
   /// substitute chain. Its id as hex, and the founder's Device key.
   fn founded_org(h: &Harness) -> (String, DevicePublicKey) {
       let persona_id = propose_founding(h, "alice", "Acme");
       let founder = device_key_of(h, &persona_id);
       let io = org_io_of(h);
       let written = block_on(io.write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Founding(founder)));
       assert!(matches!(written, Ok(WriteReport::Included { .. })), "the founding is written: {written:?}");
       let verified = block_on(io.verify_organisation(HeldTarget::Founding(founder)));
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Adopted { .. }), "the founding is adopted: {verified:?}");
       let org_id = block_on(io.personas())
           .into_iter()
           .find(|persona| persona.device_key == founder)
           .and_then(|persona| persona.org_id)
           .expect("an adopted founding's Persona holds its org id");
       (hex::encode(org_id.as_bytes()), founder)
   }

   // verifies: LLR-8tzbzn, LLR-4wcyqy
   // It holds the precondition every REQ above depends on: that the handler list
   // is CLOSED, so a command renamed in lib.rs but not in api.ts is an error the
   // frontend can see rather than a silent undefined.
   #[test]
   fn unknown_command_is_rejected() {
       let h = harness();
       let res = invoke(&h, "connectionStatus", serde_json::json!({}));

       );
   }

   /// The command paths in the first `generate_handler![...]` list of `source`.
   fn handler_list(source: &str) -> std::collections::BTreeSet<String> {
       let start = source.find("generate_handler![").expect("a generate_handler! list") + "generate_handler![".len();
       let end = start + source[start..].find(']').expect("the list is closed");
       source[start..end]
           .split(',')
           .map(str::trim)
           .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
           .map(String::from)
           .collect()
   }

   /// `source` with every `//` comment cut off its line. It does not parse block
   /// comments or string literals; the files it reads have neither around what
   /// they check.
   fn without_line_comments(source: &str) -> String {
       source
           .lines()
           .map(|line| line.split("//").next().unwrap_or(""))
           .collect::<Vec<_>>()
           .join("\n")
   }

   // verifies: LLR-4wcyqy
   // The harness registers its own copy of the handler list; this test gates the
   // product's copy against it. It reads both files as text and edits neither.
   #[test]
   fn product_registers_the_same_commands_as_the_harness() {
       let read = |rel: &str| {
           std::fs::read_to_string(format!("{}/{rel}", env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")))
               .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("read {rel}: {e}"))
       };
       let lib = read("src/lib.rs");
       // `Builder::invoke_handler` replaces any earlier handler, so a second call
       // would silently narrow what the product registers. Exactly one list, in
       // exactly one call, keeps the comparison below about the list that wins.
       let code = without_line_comments(&lib);
       assert_eq!(code.matches("generate_handler!").count(), 1, "lib.rs must have exactly one generate_handler!");
       assert_eq!(code.matches(".invoke_handler(").count(), 1, "lib.rs must call invoke_handler exactly once");
       let product = handler_list(&lib);
       let harness = handler_list(&read("tests/ipc.rs"));
       // *Amended 2026-10-22 (T46):* the eight commands that exist once the old
       // ones left; T48–T52 add the rest of LLR-kk8gc7's seventeen.
       assert_eq!(harness.len(), 8, "the harness registers eight commands: {harness:?}");
       assert_eq!(product, harness, "lib.rs and the ipc harness register different commands");
   }

   /// The crate names of every dependency table of `manifest`: `[dependencies]`,
   /// `[dev-dependencies]`, `[build-dependencies]`, their `target.*` forms and
   /// their dotted one-crate tables (`[dependencies.rand]`).
   fn dependency_names(manifest: &str) -> Vec<String> {
       const TABLES: [&str; 3] = ["dependencies", "dev-dependencies", "build-dependencies"];
       let mut names = vec![];
       let mut in_table = false;
       for line in manifest.lines().map(str::trim) {
           if line.starts_with('[') {
               let header = line.trim_matches(|c| c == '[' || c == ']');
               in_table = false;
               for table in TABLES {
                   if header == table || header.ends_with(&format!(".{table}")) {
                       in_table = true;
                   }
                   if let Some(name) = header.strip_prefix(&format!("{table}.")) {
                       names.push(name.to_string());
                   }
               }
               continue;
           }
           if !in_table || line.is_empty() || line.starts_with('#') {
               continue;
           }
           if let Some((name, _)) = line.split_once('=') {
               names.push(name.trim().trim_matches('"').to_string());
           }
       }
       names
   }

   // verifies: LLR-vj5s28
   #[test]
   fn the_app_manifest_names_no_rand_rand_core_or_getrandom() {
       let manifest = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("{}/Cargo.toml", env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))).expect("read Cargo.toml");
       let names = dependency_names(&manifest);
       assert!(names.iter().any(|name| name == "org-io"), "the [dependencies] table was read: {names:?}");
       assert!(names.iter().any(|name| name == "tempfile"), "the [dev-dependencies] table was read: {names:?}");
       let named: Vec<&String> =
           names.iter().filter(|name| ["rand", "rand_core", "getrandom"].contains(&name.as_str())).collect();
       assert!(named.is_empty(), "the app's manifest names {named:?}; org-io holds the one random source");
   }

   /// The unit's sources under `src-tauri/src`, as (path, text).
   fn app_sources() -> Vec<(PathBuf, String)> {
       let mut pending = vec![PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src")];
       let mut sources = Vec::new();
       while let Some(dir) = pending.pop() {
           for entry in std::fs::read_dir(&dir).expect("read src dir") {
               let path = entry.expect("dir entry").path();
               if path.is_dir() {
                   pending.push(path);
               } else if path.extension().is_some_and(|ext| ext == "rs") {
                   let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).expect("read source");
                   sources.push((path, text));
               }
           }
       }
       sources
   }

   // verifies: LLR-vj5s28
   #[test]
   fn no_app_source_names_a_generator_or_passes_an_rng() {
       let sources = app_sources();
       assert!(sources.iter().any(|(path, _)| path.ends_with("commands.rs")), "the sources were read");
       let mut found = vec![];
       for (path, text) in &sources {
           let code = without_line_comments(text);
           for name in ["OsRng", "RngCore", "CryptoRng", "rand::", "rand_core", "getrandom"] {
               if code.contains(name) {
                   found.push(format!("{} names {name}", path.display()));
               }
           }
       }
       assert!(found.is_empty(), "the app names a generator: {found:#?}");
   }
   ```

     ```rust
     #[test]
     fn locally_reachable_variants_are_classified_as_receiver_errors() {
         // `OrgNotOnChain` and `Trie(_)` sound like verdicts and are not always:
         // each is also reachable from a LOCAL condition (no record held, a local
         // members snapshot that fails to reconstruct), so neither may be
         // rendered as a ✗ MISMATCH row — the defect RC-3rddh7 exists to remove.
         // An unexpected first admission, one that lists none of this node's
         // Personas, and the provisional limit are refusals about this node.
         // A message that does not decode and a revocation about an Organisation
         // not held are refused before anything is verified, and a revocation
         // that leaves this node listed after it, on a rule about this node.
         // *2026-10-22 (T46):* `NoProvisionalUpdate`, `PersonaAlreadyBound` and
         // `OrgKeyMismatch` left org-node with their raisers (T5).
         for e in [
             OrgNodeError::OrgNotOnChain,
             OrgNodeError::Trie(OrgMembersError::IdNotFound),
             OrgNodeError::AdmissionNotExpected { org_id: org_io::node::OrgId::new([1; 20]) },
             OrgNodeError::AdmissionNotOurs { org_id: org_io::node::OrgId::new([1; 20]) },
             OrgNodeError::ProvisionalLimit { limit: 1 },
             OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage,
             OrgNodeError::RevocationNotHeld { org_id: org_io::node::OrgId::new([1; 20]) },
             OrgNodeError::RevocationNotForThisDevice { org_id: org_io::node::OrgId::new([1; 20]) },
         ] {
             let outcome = events::classify_receive_error(&e);
             assert_eq!(
                 outcome,
                 ReceiverOutcome::ReceiveError {
                     message: e.to_string()
                 },
                 "{e:?} is reachable from a local condition and must not be a verdict"
             );
             let out = events::emissions_for(&outcome);
             assert_eq!(names(&out), vec!["receiver-error"], "{e:?}");
             assert!(
                 !has_key_anywhere(&out[0].payload, "org_id"),
                 "{e:?}: a receiver error carries no organisation: {}",
                 out[0].payload
             );
         }
     }
     ```

   ```rust
   //! Tauri command handlers for the ODS PoC app.
   //!
   //! Each command calls the org-io method of its name on the shared handle
   //! (`AppState.org_io`, an `Arc<OrgIo>` taking no app-side lock, LLR-5wb4vd)
   //! with values parsed at the IPC edge, passes no randomness (org-io holds
   //! the one random source, LLR-vj5s28), and maps org-io's outcome to a DTO
   //! carrying no secret, its refusal to text for the Tauri `Result<T, String>`
   //! convention (SDD-6pjvhc).
   //!
   //! ## `start_receiver` and its events
   //!
   //! Each iteration produces `crate::events::ReceiverOutcome`s, and
   //! `crate::events::emissions_for` maps each to the events it produces. The
   //! mapping is total, it is gated by `tests/receiver_events.rs`, and it is the
   //! only place the event names and payload shapes are written down.

   use std::sync::Arc;

   use serde::Serialize;
   use tauri::{AppHandle, Emitter, Runtime, State};

   use org_io::node::{DevicePublicKey, OrgNodeError};
   use org_io::view::PersonStatus;
   use org_io::{CreateError, OrgIo, OrgSummary, PersonSummary, PersonaSummary, Received};

   use crate::parsing::parse_org_id;
   use crate::state::{AppState, ConnectionStatus};
   use crate::{events, policy};

   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   // Serialisable DTOs
   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   /// A serialisable view of a Persona (org-io's `PersonaSummary`: no key
   /// material). `handle` is null for a provisional Member (LLR-pguhw5's six
   /// fields, unchanged).
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   pub struct PersonaDto {
       pub persona_id: String,
       pub org_id: Option<String>,
       pub handle: Option<String>,
       pub name: String,
       pub surname: String,
       pub status: String,
   }

   impl From<&PersonaSummary> for PersonaDto {
       fn from(p: &PersonaSummary) -> Self {
           Self {
               persona_id: p.persona_id.as_str().to_string(),
               org_id: p.org_id.map(|id| hex::encode(id.as_bytes())),
               handle: p.handle.as_ref().map(ToString::to_string),
               name: p.name.to_string(),
               surname: p.surname.to_string(),
               status: format!("{:?}", p.status),
           }
       }
   }

   /// A serialisable view of an Organisation (org-io's `OrgSummary`).
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   pub struct OrgDto {
       pub org_id: String,
       pub epoch: u64,
       pub root_hash: String,
       pub member_count: usize,
       pub verification: VerificationDto,
   }

   impl OrgDto {
       /// `summary`. *2026-10-22 (T46):* `verification` is `not_checked` until
       /// T51 reads org-io's last verification per Organisation (LLR-g8wfy9).
       pub fn new(summary: &OrgSummary) -> Self {
           Self {
               org_id: hex::encode(summary.org_id.as_bytes()),
               epoch: summary.epoch.get(),
               root_hash: hex::encode(summary.root_hash.as_bytes()),
               member_count: summary.members.len(),
               verification: VerificationDto::NotChecked,
           }
       }
   }

   /// An Organisation's last verification as `list_orgs` reports it. T51
   /// gives it LLR-g8wfy9's statuses.
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   #[serde(tag = "status", rename_all = "snake_case")]
   pub enum VerificationDto {
       NotChecked,
   }

   /// The Person as `propose_person` returns it (LLR-k57uqv): its Device key
   /// as 64 hex characters, the names org-io stored, and its status.
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   pub struct PersonDto {
       pub device_public_key: String,
       pub name: String,
       pub surname: String,
       pub status: &'static str,
   }

   impl From<&PersonSummary> for PersonDto {
       fn from(person: &PersonSummary) -> Self {
           Self {
               device_public_key: hex::encode(person.device_key.as_bytes()),
               name: person.name.to_string(),
               surname: person.surname.to_string(),
               status: match person.status {
                   PersonStatus::Provisional => "provisional",
               },
           }
       }
   }

   /// A Persona a Member proposal created: its id and its status
   /// (`provisional_member`, LLR-rg9vc7). A founding's is `ProposedFoundingDto`.
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   pub struct ProposedPersonaDto {
       pub persona_id: String,
       pub status: &'static str,
   }

   /// A founding a proposal created (LLR-6ff735, amended 2026-10-22): its
   ```
