   ```rust
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   pub struct ProposedFoundingDto {
       pub persona_id: String,
       pub status: &'static str,
       pub founder: String,
   }

   /// An Invite as the invitee is shown it (LLR-b7ywy4). Nothing in it is
   /// verified (RC-wzb48r).
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   pub struct InviteDto {
       pub org_name: String,
       pub org_id: String,
       pub invitee_name: String,
       pub issuer_device_key: String,
   }

   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   // Helpers
   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   /// org-io's refusal of a creation as text, a refused field named first
   /// (`name: <reason>`, `surname: <reason>`, `handle: <reason>`) without org-node's record prefix.
   fn field_refusal(error: &CreateError) -> String {
       match error {
           CreateError::Node(OrgNodeError::InvalidField { field, reason }) => {
               let field = field.strip_prefix("person.").or_else(|| field.strip_prefix("persona.")).unwrap_or(field);
               format!("{field}: {reason}")
           }
           other => other.to_string(),
       }
   }

   /// The id of the Persona org-io lists with `device_key`: a proposal names
   /// its new Persona by Device key (LLR-6ff735's and LLR-rg9vc7's notes).
   async fn persona_id_for(org_io: &OrgIo, device_key: &DevicePublicKey) -> Result<String, String> {
       org_io
           .personas()
           .await
           .iter()
           .find(|persona| &persona.device_key == device_key)
           .map(|persona| persona.persona_id.as_str().to_string())
           .ok_or_else(|| format!("org-io lists no Persona with Device key {}", hex::encode(device_key.as_bytes())))
   }

   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   // Commands
   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   /// LLR-k57uqv: propose the user's Person from a name and a surname (no
   /// Handle); a refusal names the field and creates nothing.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn propose_person(state: State<'_, AppState>, name: String, surname: String) -> Result<PersonDto, String> {
       let person = state.org_io.propose_person(&name, &surname).await.map_err(|error| field_refusal(&error))?;
       Ok(PersonDto::from(&person))
   }

   /// LLR-6ff735: propose a founding, which creates a new Persona; returns
   /// that Persona's id and its founder's Device key. A refusal names the
   /// field and leaves no new Persona.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn propose_founding_organisation(
       state: State<'_, AppState>,
       name: String,
       surname: String,
       handle: String,
       org_name: String,
   ) -> Result<ProposedFoundingDto, String> {
       let founding = state
           .org_io
           .propose_founding_organisation(&name, &surname, &handle, &org_name)
           .await
           .map_err(|error| field_refusal(&error))?;
       let persona_id = persona_id_for(&state.org_io, &founding.founder).await?;
       Ok(ProposedFoundingDto {
           persona_id,
           status: "provisional_founding",
           founder: hex::encode(founding.founder.as_bytes()),
       })
   }

   /// LLR-y3zykm: issue an Invite to `org_id` for `invitee_name`; org-io's
   /// Blob, unchanged. No Organisation name (the stored one) and no address
   /// (the issuing Device's) is taken.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn issue_invite(state: State<'_, AppState>, org_id: String, invitee_name: String) -> Result<String, String> {
       let org_id = parse_org_id(&org_id)?;
       state.org_io.issue_invite(org_id, &invitee_name).await.map_err(|error| error.to_string())
   }

   /// LLR-b7ywy4: read an Invite Blob; stores nothing.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn read_invite(state: State<'_, AppState>, blob: String) -> Result<InviteDto, String> {
       let invite = state.org_io.read_invite(&blob).await.map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
       Ok(InviteDto {
           org_name: invite.org_name.to_string(),
           org_id: hex::encode(invite.org_id.as_bytes()),
           invitee_name: invite.invitee_name.to_string(),
           issuer_device_key: hex::encode(invite.issuer.as_bytes()),
       })
   }

   /// List all local personas (no key material returned).
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn list_personas(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> Result<Vec<PersonaDto>, String> {
       Ok(state.org_io.personas().await.iter().map(PersonaDto::from).collect())
   }

   /// List all local org records.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn list_orgs(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> Result<Vec<OrgDto>, String> {
       Ok(state.org_io.organisations().await.iter().map(OrgDto::new).collect())
   }

   /// Return the current connection status: what the running configuration was
   /// actually built from, not what the environment currently says.
   ///
   /// REQ-e4ah9h / REQ-bvx4nh / REQ-645jq9. Nothing here reads the environment.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn connection_status<R: Runtime>(
       state: State<'_, AppState>,
       app_handle: AppHandle<R>,
   ) -> Result<ConnectionStatus, String> {
       // The handle stays in the signature because it is what makes this
       // command generic over the runtime, and a command that is not generic
       // over the runtime cannot be driven by `MockRuntime`.
       let _ = &app_handle;
       Ok(policy::connection_status_from_state(
           &state.data_dir,
           state.chain_endpoint.as_ref(),
           state.transport_mode,
       ))
   }

   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   // start_receiver: spawns a background task looping org-io's `next_received`
   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   /// One iteration of the receiver loop, as outcomes: none, one, or (for a
   /// terminal error) the failure and the stop (REQ-affyf5, REQ-jfxah3).
   ///
   /// `org_io` is the shared handle (LLR-5wb4vd); no app-side lock is taken, so
   /// the wait in `next_received` blocks no command.
   async fn next_outcomes(org_io: &OrgIo) -> Vec<events::ReceiverOutcome> {
       match org_io.next_received().await {
           // A revoked Device's acknowledgement verified; the UI is told nothing.
           Ok(Received::Acknowledged(acknowledged)) => vec![events::outcome_for_arrival(
               events::Arrival::Acknowledged,
               hex::encode(acknowledged.into_inner().org_id.as_bytes()),
           )],
           // *2026-10-22 (T46):* announced by nothing until T53 maps them
           // (LLR-4bvdn7, LLR-dp45mm, LLR-t9rdf8, LLR-ygr6gd) and T54 follows
           // them up (LLR-w7m3d4). Nothing is misannounced meanwhile.
           Ok(
               Received::ProvisionalOrganisationReceived { .. }
               | Received::AdmissionRequestKept { .. }
               | Received::OrganisationRequestAnswered { .. }
               | Received::RevocationNoticeKept { .. },
           ) => Vec::new(),
           // RC-3rddh7 / REQ-kn5rtx / REQ-jfxah3: classified by the error's
           // variant, the loop's exit included (LLR-zw6jqy).
           Err(error) => events::outcomes_for_receive_error(&error),
       }
   }

   /// Spawn a background tokio task that loops org-io's `next_received` and
   /// emits Tauri events. The task runs until the app is closed or the
   /// endpoint returns a permanent error (endpoint closed).
   ///
   /// REQ-6hgm8r: only one loop runs at a time. REQ-3hfggn: when the loop ends —
   /// by break, by return, or by panic — the slot is released and a later call may
   /// start a new one (HAZ-cfp4jb).
   ///
   /// Returns immediately; the task runs in the background.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn start_receiver<R: Runtime>(
       state: State<'_, AppState>,
       app_handle: AppHandle<R>,
   ) -> Result<(), String> {
       let Some(guard) = events::StartGuard::try_claim(&state.receiver_started) else {
           return Ok(()); // REQ-6hgm8r: a loop is already running.
       };

       let app_handle_clone = app_handle.clone();
       // LLR-5wb4vd: the loop holds its own clone of the shared handle.
       let org_io = Arc::clone(&state.org_io);
       tokio::spawn(async move {
           // REQ-3hfggn: the guard is moved in, so the slot is released when this
           // task ends — by break, by return, or by panic.
           let _guard = guard;
           // A bind that fails (`ReceiveError::Terminal`) ends the loop before
           // it begins.
           if let Err(error) = org_io.start_receiving().await {
               for outcome in &events::outcomes_for_receive_error(&error) {
                   for emission in events::emissions_for(outcome) {
                       // Events are the only channel to the webview, so a
                       // failed emit has nowhere to be reported.
                       let _ = app_handle_clone.emit(emission.name, emission.payload);
                   }
               }
               return;
           }
           loop {
               let outcomes = next_outcomes(&org_io).await;
               let stopping = outcomes
                   .iter()
                   .any(|o| matches!(o, events::ReceiverOutcome::Stopped { .. }));
               for outcome in &outcomes {
                   for e in events::emissions_for(outcome) {
                       let _ = app_handle_clone.emit(e.name, e.payload);
                   }
               }
               if stopping {
                   break;
               }
           }
       });

       Ok(())
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   /// A startup value that is missing and is not permitted to be defaulted,
   /// or one that is not of its form. No passphrase is among them: org-io
   /// opens each store with its keychain item.
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum StartupError {
       UnresolvableDataDir,
       /// LLR-rvrc25: `ODS_VERIFICATION_INTERVAL_SECS` as given, refused.
       InvalidVerificationInterval { value: String },
   }

   impl core::fmt::Display for StartupError {
       fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
           // REQ-bmk2z2: the message names BOTH the variable that would supply the
           // value AND the variable that would waive the requirement, and names the
           // supplying variable FIRST — a refusal an operator reads as "set the
           // waiver" is a refusal that recreates the hazard it was added for.
           match self {
               StartupError::UnresolvableDataDir => write!(
                   f,
                   "The application data directory could not be resolved and \
                    ODS_DATA_DIR is not set. Set ODS_DATA_DIR to the directory \
                    this installation should keep its persona store in. To fall \
                    back to a temporary directory instead, set \
                    ODS_ALLOW_DEV_DEFAULTS=1 — that directory is world-readable \
                    and is cleared by the operating system."
               ),
               // LLR-rvrc25: the variable, the form, and the value quoted.
               StartupError::InvalidVerificationInterval { value } => write!(
                   f,
                   "ODS_VERIFICATION_INTERVAL_SECS must be a whole number of seconds of at least 1 \
                    (at most 4294967295), got {value:?}"
               ),
           }
       }
   }

   /// LLR-2dpn52: the verification interval when none is configured.
   pub const DEFAULT_VERIFICATION_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(600);

   /// REQ-ergn9z. `raw` is `ODS_VERIFICATION_INTERVAL_SECS`. Absent or empty
   /// is the 10-minute default (LLR-2dpn52); a decimal integer from 1 to
   /// 4294967295, with no sign, space or other character, is that many
   /// seconds; anything else is refused quoting the value (LLR-rvrc25). What
   /// leaves here is never zero.
   pub fn resolve_verification_interval(raw: Option<&str>) -> Result<Duration, StartupError> {
       let value = match raw {
           None | Some("") => return Ok(DEFAULT_VERIFICATION_INTERVAL),
           Some(value) => value,
       };
       let refused = || StartupError::InvalidVerificationInterval { value: value.to_string() };
       if !value.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()) {
           return Err(refused());
       }
       let seconds: u32 = value.parse().map_err(|_| refused())?;
       if seconds == 0 {
           return Err(refused());
       }
       Ok(Duration::from_secs(u64::from(seconds)))
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   // The Member's commands (T48: LLR-rg9vc7, LLR-q2k9z8, LLR-8cz828)
   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   /// An inviter that founded "Acme" over the substitute chain and is
   /// receiving, an Invite it issued to "Bob Builder", and an invitee (Loopback,
   /// no chain) holding a provisional Member proposed from that Invite with
   /// `handles`. `proposed` is `propose_member`'s answer.
   struct Exchange {
       inviter: Harness,
       org_id: String,
       blob: String,
       invitee: Harness,
       proposed: serde_json::Value,
   }

   fn exchange(handles: &[&str]) -> Exchange {
       let inviter = harness_over_chain();
       let (org_id, _) = founded_org(&inviter);
       invoke(&inviter, "start_receiver", serde_json::json!({})).expect("start_receiver");
       let blob = invoke(&inviter, "issue_invite", serde_json::json!({ "orgId": org_id, "inviteeName": "Bob Builder" }))
           .expect("issue_invite");
       let blob = blob.as_str().expect("the Blob as text").to_string();
       let invitee = harness_with(TransportModeName::Loopback, None);
       let proposed = invoke(
           &invitee,
           "propose_member",
           serde_json::json!({ "inviteBlob": blob, "name": "Bob", "surname": "Builder", "preferredHandles": handles }),
       )
       .expect("propose_member");
       Exchange { inviter, org_id, blob, invitee, proposed }
   }

   /// The inviter's kept admission requests once there are `n` of them, or
   /// whatever is kept after five seconds.
   fn kept_requests(inviter: &Harness, n: usize) -> Vec<org_io::KeptAdmissionRequestSummary> {
       let io = org_io_of(inviter);
       let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);
       loop {
           let kept = block_on(io.admission_requests());
           if kept.len() >= n || std::time::Instant::now() >= deadline {
               return kept;
           }
           std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50));
       }
   }

       assert_eq!(personas[0]["org_id"], serde_json::json!(ex.org_id), "the Invite's Organisation");
   ```

   ```rust
   /// The text `request_admission` refuses an unconfirmed request with
   /// (LLR-q2k9z8).
   pub const NOT_CONFIRMED_ADMISSION_REQUEST: &str = "the user has not confirmed the admission request";

   /// org-io's outcome of an admission request as it crosses IPC (LLR-8cz828),
   /// tagged by `result`, each reason org-io's text unchanged.
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   #[serde(tag = "result", rename_all = "snake_case")]
   pub enum AdmissionDto {
       Delivered,
       AlreadyReceived,
       InviteUsedByAnotherDevice,
       Refused,
       NotDelivered { reason: String },
   }

   impl From<&AdmissionOutcome> for AdmissionDto {
       fn from(outcome: &AdmissionOutcome) -> Self {
           match outcome {
               AdmissionOutcome::Delivered => Self::Delivered,
               AdmissionOutcome::AlreadyReceived => Self::AlreadyReceived,
               AdmissionOutcome::InviteUsedByAnotherDevice => Self::InviteUsedByAnotherDevice,
               AdmissionOutcome::Refused => Self::Refused,
               AdmissionOutcome::NotDelivered { reason } => Self::NotDelivered { reason: reason.to_string() },
           }
       }
   }

   /// LLR-rg9vc7: propose a provisional Member from an Invite Blob, its
   /// preferred Handles handed to org-io in the order given; returns the new
   /// Persona's id. Sends nothing.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn propose_member(
       state: State<'_, AppState>,
       invite_blob: String,
       name: String,
       surname: String,
       preferred_handles: Vec<String>,
   ) -> Result<ProposedPersonaDto, String> {
       let handles: Vec<&str> = preferred_handles.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
       let member = state
           .org_io
           .propose_member(&invite_blob, &name, &surname, &handles)
           .await
           .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
       let persona_id = persona_id_for(&state.org_io, &member.member_device).await?;
       Ok(ProposedPersonaDto { persona_id, status: "provisional_member" })
   }

   /// LLR-q2k9z8, LLR-8cz828: send the provisional Member's admission request,
   /// only once the user confirmed, for the Organisation org-io lists for that
   /// Persona; org-io's outcome, tagged.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn request_admission(
       state: State<'_, AppState>,
       persona_id: String,
       confirmed: bool,
   ) -> Result<AdmissionDto, String> {
       if !confirmed {
           return Err(NOT_CONFIRMED_ADMISSION_REQUEST.to_string());
       }
       let persona = state
           .org_io
           .personas()
           .await
           .into_iter()
   ```

   ```rust
   /// `exchange(handles)` whose provisional Member sent its admission request
   /// and the inviter kept it; the kept request's invite id as hex.
   fn requested(handles: &[&str]) -> (Exchange, String) {
       let ex = exchange(handles);
       let outcome = invoke(
           &ex.invitee,
           "request_admission",
           serde_json::json!({ "personaId": ex.proposed["persona_id"], "confirmed": true }),
       )
       .expect("request_admission");
       assert_eq!(outcome, serde_json::json!({ "result": "delivered" }));
       let kept = kept_requests(&ex.inviter, 1);
       assert_eq!(kept.len(), 1, "the inviter keeps the request");
       let invite_id = hex::encode(kept[0].invite_id.as_bytes());
       (ex, invite_id)
   }

   /// The inviter's next epoch, proposed from its provisional changes, written
   /// and verified through the handle over its substitute chain; the record
   /// adopted.
   fn adopt_next_epoch(h: &Harness, org_id: &str) -> org_io::OrgSummary {
       let io = org_io_of(h);
       let org = ods_poc_lib::parsing::parse_org_id(org_id).expect("an org id");
       block_on(io.propose_updated_organisation(org)).expect("the next epoch is proposed");
       let written = block_on(io.write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Organisation(org)));
       assert!(matches!(written, Ok(WriteReport::Included { .. })), "{written:?}");
       let verified = block_on(io.verify_organisation(HeldTarget::Organisation(org)));
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Adopted { .. }), "{verified:?}");
       block_on(io.organisation(org)).expect("the Organisation is held")
   }

   /// `propose_admission`'s arguments.
   fn admission_args(org_id: &str, invite_id: &str, handle: serde_json::Value, confirmed: bool) -> serde_json::Value {
       serde_json::json!({ "orgId": org_id, "inviteId": invite_id, "handle": handle, "confirmed": confirmed })
   }
   ```

   `app/src-tauri/src/parsing.rs`: add the two 32-byte parses. Each strips one `0x`, decodes the hex (refused as `<field> hex: …`) and then checks the width (refused as `<field> must be 32 bytes (64 hex chars)`). This keeps `revoke_member`'s old order: a doubled prefix is refused by the decode.
   ```rust
   use org_io::node::{InviteId, MemberId, OrgId};

   /// Thirty-two bytes from hex, with at most one leading `0x`: a remainder
   /// that is not hex is refused with `<field> hex: <reason>`, one that is not 32
   /// bytes with `<field> must be 32 bytes (64 hex chars)`.
   fn parse_32_bytes(field: &str, s: &str) -> Result<[u8; 32], String> {
       let s = s.strip_prefix("0x").unwrap_or(s);
       let bytes = hex::decode(s).map_err(|e| format!("{field} hex: {e}"))?;
       <[u8; 32]>::try_from(bytes.as_slice()).map_err(|_| format!("{field} must be 32 bytes (64 hex chars)"))
   }

   /// LLR-7n4hgr: a Member identifier (64 hex chars, one optional `0x`).
   pub fn parse_member_id(s: &str) -> Result<MemberId, String> {
       parse_32_bytes("member_id", s).map(MemberId::new)
   }

   /// LLR-r8jeu8: an invite identifier (64 hex chars, one optional `0x`).
   pub fn parse_invite_id(s: &str) -> Result<InviteId, String> {
       parse_32_bytes("invite_id", s).map(InviteId::new)
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   /// The text `propose_admission` refuses an unconfirmed admission with
   /// (LLR-cr9nmw).
   pub const NOT_CONFIRMED_ADMISSION: &str = "the Admin has not confirmed the admission";

   /// LLR-gmb4p8: a Handle that is absent, empty or only whitespace is none
   /// (org-io chooses the first preferred one free); any other is the Admin's
   /// choice, unchanged.
   pub fn chosen_handle(handle: Option<&str>) -> Option<&str> {
       handle.filter(|handle| !handle.trim().is_empty())
   }

   /// LLR-cr9nmw, LLR-gmb4p8: record the admission of the request kept for
   /// `invite_id`, once the Admin confirmed. It takes these four values alone.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn propose_admission(
       state: State<'_, AppState>,
       org_id: String,
       invite_id: String,
       handle: Option<String>,
       confirmed: bool,
   ) -> Result<(), String> {
       let org_id = parse_org_id(&org_id)?;
       let invite_id = parse_invite_id(&invite_id)?;
       if !confirmed {
           return Err(NOT_CONFIRMED_ADMISSION.to_string());
       }
       state
           .org_io
           .propose_admission(org_id, invite_id, chosen_handle(handle.as_deref()))
           .await
           .map(|_| ())
           .map_err(|error| error.to_string())
   }

   /// LLR-7n4hgr: record the revocation of `member_id`; no peer address, and
   /// nothing is sent.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn propose_revocation(state: State<'_, AppState>, org_id: String, member_id: String) -> Result<(), String> {
       let org_id = parse_org_id(&org_id)?;
       let member_id = parse_member_id(&member_id)?;
       state.org_io.propose_revocation(org_id, member_id).await.map(|_| ()).map_err(|error| error.to_string())
   }

   }
   ```

   ```ts
    */
   export function proposeAdmission(
   	orgId: string,
   	inviteId: string,
   	handle: string | null,
   	confirmed: boolean
   ```

   ```rust
   #![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]
   //! The write and the verification it asks (LLR-rhc555, LLR-k4rhbs), and
   //! from T51 the verification's entries, sends and requests, over org-io's
   //! substitute chain (`test_support::FakeChain`). The commands over IPC are
   //! `ipc.rs`'s.

   use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
   use std::sync::Arc;
   use std::time::Duration;

   use ods_poc_lib::commands;
   use org_io::node::{DevicePublicKey, OrgId};
   use org_io::test_support::{FakeChain, MemoryKeychain};
   use org_io::transport::TransportMode;
   use org_io::{AdmissionOutcome, HeldTarget, OrgIo, WriteReport};

   /// A handle over `chain` in Loopback mode, its store in a fresh directory.
   fn handle(chain: &FakeChain) -> (tempfile::TempDir, OrgIo) {
       let dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("tempdir");
       MemoryKeychain::shared().install();
       let io = OrgIo::open_for_test(dir.path(), TransportMode::Loopback, chain).expect("open");
       (dir, io)
   }

   /// A provisional founding "Acme" by "Alice Smith"; the founder's Device key.
   async fn founding(io: &OrgIo) -> DevicePublicKey {
       io.propose_founding_organisation("Alice", "Smith", "alice", "Acme").await.expect("proposed").founder
   }

   /// The Organisation the founder's Persona now holds.
   async fn org_of(io: &OrgIo, founder: DevicePublicKey) -> OrgId {
       io.personas()
           .await
           .into_iter()
           .find(|persona| persona.device_key == founder)
           .and_then(|persona| persona.org_id)
           .expect("the founding's Persona holds its org id")
   }

   fn wire(dto: &impl serde::Serialize) -> serde_json::Value {
       serde_json::to_value(dto).expect("serialises")
   }

   /// An Organisation founded and adopted over `chain`, with one admission
   /// recorded and the next epoch proposed: Bob's Device asked over Loopback,
   /// the inviter receiving. The invitee's handle and the directories are
   /// held so its endpoint stays up.
   struct Admitted {
       inviter: Arc<OrgIo>,
       org: OrgId,
       member_device: DevicePublicKey,
       _invitee: OrgIo,
       _dirs: [tempfile::TempDir; 2],
   }

   async fn admitted(chain: &FakeChain) -> Admitted {
       let (inviter_dir, inviter) = handle(chain);
       let founder = founding(&inviter).await;
       let founded = commands::write_then_verify(&inviter, HeldTarget::Founding(founder)).await.expect("written");
       assert_eq!(wire(&founded)["verification"]["result"], "adopted", "{}", wire(&founded));
       let org = org_of(&inviter, founder).await;
       let inviter = Arc::new(inviter);
       inviter.start_receiving().await.expect("receiving");
       let receiving = Arc::clone(&inviter);
       tokio::spawn(async move {
           loop {
               if let Err(org_io::ReceiveError::Terminal(_)) = receiving.next_received().await {
                   break;
               }
           }
       });
       let blob = inviter.issue_invite(org, "Bob Builder").await.expect("issued");
       let (invitee_dir, invitee) = handle(&FakeChain::new());
       let member = invitee.propose_member(&blob, "Bob", "Builder", &["bob"]).await.expect("proposed");
       let outcome = invitee.request_admission(org).await.expect("requested");
       assert!(matches!(outcome, AdmissionOutcome::Delivered), "{outcome:?}");
       let mut kept = inviter.admission_requests().await;
       for _ in 0..100 {
           if !kept.is_empty() {
               break;
           }
           tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
           kept = inviter.admission_requests().await;
       }
       assert_eq!(kept.len(), 1, "the inviter keeps Bob's request");
       inviter.propose_admission(org, kept[0].invite_id.clone(), None).await.expect("recorded");
       inviter.propose_updated_organisation(org).await.expect("proposed");
       Admitted { inviter, org, member_device: member.member_device, _invitee: invitee, _dirs: [inviter_dir, invitee_dir] }
   }

   // verifies: LLR-rhc555
   #[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]
   async fn write_organisation_to_chain_tags_included_refused_and_unknown() {
       // Included, with the epoch written.
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       let (_included_dir, io) = handle(&chain);
       let founder = founding(&io).await;
       let included = wire(&commands::write_then_verify(&io, HeldTarget::Founding(founder)).await.expect("a report"));
       assert_eq!(included["result"], "included", "{included}");
       assert_eq!(included["epoch"], 1, "{included}");

       // Refused, with org-io's reason unchanged.
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       chain.write_failing.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
       let (_refused_dir, io) = handle(&chain);
       let founder = founding(&io).await;
       let refused = wire(&commands::write_then_verify(&io, HeldTarget::Founding(founder)).await.expect("a report"));
       assert_eq!(refused["result"], "refused", "{refused}");
       let mut keys: Vec<&str> = refused.as_object().expect("an object").keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
       keys.sort_unstable();
       assert_eq!(keys, ["reason", "result"]);
       match io.write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Founding(founder)).await {
           Ok(WriteReport::Refused { reason }) => assert_eq!(refused["reason"], serde_json::json!(reason.to_string())),
           other => panic!("org-io refuses the same write again: {other:?}"),
       }

       // Unknown: the write does not return within the 90-second bound.
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       chain.write_hanging.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
       let (_unknown_dir, io) = handle(&chain);
       let founder = founding(&io).await;
       let unknown = wire(&commands::write_then_verify(&io, HeldTarget::Founding(founder)).await.expect("a report"));
       assert_eq!(unknown["result"], "unknown", "{unknown}");
       let reason = unknown["reason"].as_str().expect("a reason");
       assert!(reason.contains("90"), "org-io's reason names the bound: {reason}");
   }

   // verifies: LLR-k4rhbs
   #[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]
   async fn an_included_write_is_verified_once_and_a_refused_or_unknown_one_is_not() {
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       let (_included_dir, io) = handle(&chain);
       let founder = founding(&io).await;
       let included = wire(&commands::write_then_verify(&io, HeldTarget::Founding(founder)).await.expect("a report"));
       assert_eq!(included["verification"]["result"], "adopted", "{included}");
       assert_eq!(chain.reads(), 1, "one state read: the verification's");
       assert_eq!(chain.finalised_reads(), 1, "one finalised-block read: the verification's");

       for flag in ["write_failing", "write_hanging"] {
           let chain = FakeChain::new();
           match flag {
               "write_failing" => chain.write_failing.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst),
               _ => chain.write_hanging.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst),
           }
           let (_dir, io) = handle(&chain);
           let founder = founding(&io).await;
           let report = wire(&commands::write_then_verify(&io, HeldTarget::Founding(founder)).await.expect("a report"));
           assert!(report.get("verification").is_none(), "{flag}: no verification is asked: {report}");
           assert_eq!(chain.reads(), 0, "{flag}: no state read");
       }
   }

   async fn an_included_founding_write_is_verified_by_its_founder_and_an_update_by_its_org_id() {

       );
       assert_eq!(updated["result"], "included", "{updated}");
       assert_eq!(updated["verification"]["result"], "adopted", "{updated}");
       assert_eq!(updated["verification"]["org_id"], serde_json::json!(hex::encode(admitted.org.as_bytes())));
       assert_eq!(updated["verification"]["epoch"], 2);
       let _ = admitted.member_device;
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   /// What `propose_updated_organisation` returns (LLR-2u3cga): org-io's
   /// `ProposedOrganisation`, each root and key as 64 hex characters.
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   pub struct ProposedOrganisationDto {
       pub epoch: u64,
       pub root: String,
       pub org_public_key: String,
   }

   /// LLR-2u3cga: have org-io propose the next epoch from the held provisional
   /// changes; writes nothing to the chain.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn propose_updated_organisation(
       state: State<'_, AppState>,
       org_id: String,
   ) -> Result<ProposedOrganisationDto, String> {
       let org_id = parse_org_id(&org_id)?;
       let proposed = state.org_io.propose_updated_organisation(org_id).await.map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
       Ok(ProposedOrganisationDto {
           epoch: proposed.epoch.get(),
           root: hex::encode(proposed.root.as_bytes()),
           org_public_key: hex::encode(proposed.org_public_key.as_bytes()),
       })
   }

   /// One provisional change an adoption left out (LLR-n64wvr), tagged by
   /// `kind`, ids as 64 hex characters. Every field is always present: a
   /// name, surname or Handle org-io does not report is `null`, never absent
   /// (LLR-n64wvr as amended 2026-10-22, dispatcher decision O2).
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   #[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
   pub enum DiscardedDto {
       Admission { invite_id: String, name: Option<String>, surname: Option<String>, handle: String },
       Revocation { member_id: String, handle: Option<String> },
   }

   impl From<&DiscardedChangeSummary> for DiscardedDto {
       fn from(change: &DiscardedChangeSummary) -> Self {
           match change {
               DiscardedChangeSummary::Admission { invite_id, name, surname, handle } => Self::Admission {
                   invite_id: hex::encode(invite_id.as_bytes()),
                   name: name.as_ref().map(ToString::to_string),
                   surname: surname.as_ref().map(ToString::to_string),
                   handle: handle.to_string(),
               },
               DiscardedChangeSummary::Revocation { member_id, handle } => Self::Revocation {
                   member_id: hex::encode(member_id.as_bytes()),
                   handle: handle.as_ref().map(ToString::to_string),
               },
           }
       }
   }

   /// What an entry names its target by (LLR-jf63e4, amended 2026-10-22): a
   /// held Organisation by its identifier; a provisional founding by its
   /// founder's Device key, always, with the identifier its proxy gave once
   /// the proxy is recorded (LLR-qqqg4b) and none before.
   #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum EntryOrg {
       Id(OrgId),
       Founding { founder: DevicePublicKey, org_id: Option<OrgId> },
   }

   /// One verification's result, tagged by `result` (LLR-jf63e4); flattened
   /// into `VerificationEntryDto`.
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   #[serde(tag = "result", rename_all = "snake_case")]
   pub enum EntryResultDto {
       InStep { epoch: u64 },
       Adopted { epoch: u64, own: bool, discarded: Vec<DiscardedDto> },
       Removed,
       Behind { chain_epoch: u64 },
       Inconsistent { reason: String },
       Unverified { reason: String },
   }

   /// What a verification settled of the target's unknown write (org-io's
   /// `WriteOutcome`, LLR-jf63e4 as amended 2026-10-22).
   #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
   #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
   pub enum WriteLabelDto {
       Adopted,
       NotExecuted,
       Deprecated,
       StillUnknown,
   }

   impl From<WriteOutcome> for WriteLabelDto {
       fn from(write: WriteOutcome) -> Self {
           match write {
               WriteOutcome::Adopted => Self::Adopted,
               WriteOutcome::NotExecuted => Self::NotExecuted,
               WriteOutcome::Deprecated => Self::Deprecated,
               WriteOutcome::StillUnknown => Self::StillUnknown,
           }
       }
   }

   /// One verification result as it crosses IPC (LLR-jf63e4): `org_id` as 40
   /// hex characters, or `null` (never an empty string) for a provisional
   /// founding with no proxy recorded; every founding entry carries `founder`
   /// (64 hex), before its proxy is recorded and after;
   /// the result tagged by `result`, each reason org-io's text; `write` only
   /// for a verification that settled an unknown write.
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   pub struct VerificationEntryDto {
       pub org_id: Option<String>,
       #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
       pub founder: Option<String>,
       #[serde(flatten)]
       pub result: EntryResultDto,
       #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
       pub write: Option<WriteLabelDto>,
   }

   /// LLR-jf63e4: org-io's `verified` for the Organisation `named` names, as
   /// its entry. `Settled` is its inner outcome's entry with the `write`
   /// label; `Refused` (an org-node refusal no other result names), `Store`
   /// and `Keychain` (the store write or the keychain read a verification
   /// needed failed) are `unverified`, with org-io's text as the reason.
   pub fn entry_for(named: &EntryOrg, verified: &Verified) -> VerificationEntryDto {
       let (org_id, founder) = match named {
           EntryOrg::Id(org_id) => (Some(hex::encode(org_id.as_bytes())), None),
           EntryOrg::Founding { founder, org_id } => {
               (org_id.map(|org_id| hex::encode(org_id.as_bytes())), Some(hex::encode(founder.as_bytes())))
           }
       };
       let entry = |result| VerificationEntryDto { org_id: org_id.clone(), founder: founder.clone(), result, write: None };
       match verified {
           Verified::InStep { epoch } => entry(EntryResultDto::InStep { epoch: epoch.get() }),
           Verified::Adopted { epoch, discarded, own } => entry(EntryResultDto::Adopted {
               epoch: epoch.get(),
               own: *own,
               discarded: discarded.iter().map(DiscardedDto::from).collect(),
           }),
           Verified::Removed { .. } => entry(EntryResultDto::Removed),
           Verified::Behind { chain_epoch } => entry(EntryResultDto::Behind { chain_epoch: chain_epoch.get() }),
           Verified::Inconsistent { reason } => entry(EntryResultDto::Inconsistent { reason: reason.to_string() }),
           Verified::Unverified { reason } => entry(EntryResultDto::Unverified { reason: reason.to_string() }),
           Verified::Refused { reason } => entry(EntryResultDto::Unverified { reason: reason.clone() }),
           Verified::Store { reason } => entry(EntryResultDto::Unverified { reason: reason.clone() }),
           Verified::Keychain { error } => entry(EntryResultDto::Unverified { reason: error.to_string() }),
           Verified::Settled { outcome, write } => {
               let mut settled = entry_for(named, outcome);
               settled.write = Some(WriteLabelDto::from(*write));
               settled
           }
       }
   }

   /// What an entry for `target` names: an Organisation by its id; a founding
   /// by its founder, always, beside the id its founder's Persona holds once
   /// its proxy is recorded (LLR-qqqg4b) and none before (LLR-jf63e4 as
   /// amended 2026-10-22).
   async fn org_id_for(org_io: &OrgIo, target: &HeldTarget) -> EntryOrg {
       match target {
           HeldTarget::Organisation(org_id) => EntryOrg::Id(*org_id),
           HeldTarget::Founding(founder) => EntryOrg::Founding {
               founder: *founder,
               org_id: org_io
                   .personas()
                   .await
                   .into_iter()
                   .find(|persona| &persona.device_key == founder)
                   .and_then(|persona| persona.org_id),
           },
       }
   }

   /// The body every verification runs (SDD-6pjvhc): org-io's verification of
   /// `target`, as its entry. T51 adds the send of an own adoption and the
   /// request of a behind Organisation.
   pub async fn verify_and_send(org_io: &OrgIo, target: HeldTarget) -> VerificationEntryDto {
       let verified = org_io.verify_organisation(target).await;
       entry_for(&org_id_for(org_io, &target).await, &verified)
   }

   /// What `write_organisation_to_chain` returns (LLR-rhc555), tagged by
   /// `result`; an included write carries its verification (LLR-k4rhbs).
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   #[serde(tag = "result", rename_all = "snake_case")]
   pub enum WriteDto {
       Included { epoch: u64, verification: VerificationEntryDto },
       Refused { reason: String },
       Unknown { reason: String },
   }

   /// `write_organisation_to_chain`'s body: org-io's write of `target`, then,
   /// only when included, one verification of the same target (LLR-k4rhbs).
   /// org-io's refusal before any chain call is the command's error text.
   pub async fn write_then_verify(org_io: &OrgIo, target: HeldTarget) -> Result<WriteDto, String> {
       let report = org_io.write_organisation_to_chain(target).await.map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
       Ok(match report {
           WriteReport::Included { epoch } => {
               WriteDto::Included { epoch: epoch.get(), verification: verify_and_send(org_io, target).await }
           }
           WriteReport::Refused { reason } => WriteDto::Refused { reason: reason.to_string() },
           WriteReport::Unknown { reason } => WriteDto::Unknown { reason: reason.to_string() },
       })
   }

   /// The text `write_organisation_to_chain` refuses both or neither target
   /// with (LLR-rhc555).
   pub const EXACTLY_ONE_TARGET: &str = "write_organisation_to_chain takes exactly one of org_id or founder";

   /// A founding's founder: its Device key, 64 hex characters with one
   /// optional `0x`.
   fn parse_founder(founder: &str) -> Result<DevicePublicKey, String> {
       let founder = founder.strip_prefix("0x").unwrap_or(founder);
       let bytes = hex::decode(founder).map_err(|e| format!("founder hex: {e}"))?;
       let bytes = <[u8; 32]>::try_from(bytes.as_slice()).map_err(|_| "founder must be 32 bytes (64 hex chars)".to_string())?;
       DevicePublicKey::parse(&bytes).map_err(|e| format!("founder: {e}"))
   }

   /// LLR-rhc555, LLR-k4rhbs: write the latest own provisional organisation of
   /// `org_id`, or of the founding of `founder`, exactly one of them.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn write_organisation_to_chain(
       state: State<'_, AppState>,
       org_id: Option<String>,
       founder: Option<String>,
   ) -> Result<WriteDto, String> {
       // LLR-97hujy: the org id is parsed before any other argument.
       let org_id = org_id.as_deref().map(parse_org_id).transpose()?;
       let target = match (org_id, founder.as_deref()) {
           (Some(org_id), None) => HeldTarget::Organisation(org_id),
           (None, Some(founder)) => HeldTarget::Founding(parse_founder(founder)?),
           _ => return Err(EXACTLY_ONE_TARGET.to_string()),
       };
       write_then_verify(&state.org_io, target).await
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   // verifies: LLR-jf63e4
   // A founding whose proxy is recorded and which no verification has
   // adopted yet: its entry names the Organisation identifier the proxy gave
   // and still carries its founder, the key the webview writes it by
   // (LLR-rhc555), so a restarted app finds it in its first verification.
   #[tokio::test]
   async fn a_founding_with_its_proxy_recorded_is_entered_with_its_org_id_and_still_its_founder() {
       let proxied = OrgId::new([0x22; 20]);
       let constructed = wire(&entry_for(
           &EntryOrg::Founding { founder: device(), org_id: Some(proxied) },
           &Verified::Unverified { reason: UnverifiedReason::NotYetVerified },
       ));
       assert_eq!(
           constructed,
           serde_json::json!({
               "result": "unverified",
               "org_id": hex::encode(proxied.as_bytes()),
               "founder": hex::encode(device().as_bytes()),
               "reason": UnverifiedReason::NotYetVerified.to_string(),
           })
       );
       // Live: the write creates and records the proxy, then its founding
       // step is refused, so the founding is held with its proxy and not adopted.
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       let (_dir, io) = handle(&chain);
       let founder = founding(&io).await;
       chain.found_at_failing.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
       let refused = wire(&commands::write_then_verify(&io, HeldTarget::Founding(founder)).await.expect("a report"));
       assert_eq!(refused["result"], "refused", "{refused}");

       assert_eq!(entries.len(), 1, "{entries:?}");
       assert_eq!(entries[0]["org_id"], serde_json::json!(hex::encode(org.as_bytes())), "{entries:?}");
       assert_eq!(entries[0]["founder"], serde_json::json!(hex::encode(founder.as_bytes())), "{entries:?}");
       let one = wire(&commands::verify_and_send(&io, HeldTarget::Founding(founder)).await);
       assert_eq!((&one["org_id"], &one["founder"]), (&entries[0]["org_id"], &entries[0]["founder"]), "{one}");
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   // Verification over IPC (T51: LLR-jf63e4, LLR-g8wfy9)
   // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   /// Seed the store the harness will open in `data_dir` with an Organisation
   /// founded, written and verified over a substitute chain; its id as hex.
   /// The seeding handle is dropped before the harness opens the same files
   /// with the chain not configured.
   fn seed_store(data_dir: &std::path::Path) -> String {
       org_io::test_support::MemoryKeychain::shared().install();
       let chain = FakeChain::new();
       let io = OrgIo::open_for_test(data_dir, org_io::transport::TransportMode::Networked, &chain).expect("open");
       let founder = block_on(io.propose_founding_organisation("Test", "User", "alice", "Acme")).expect("proposed").founder;
       let written = block_on(io.write_organisation_to_chain(HeldTarget::Founding(founder)));
       assert!(matches!(written, Ok(WriteReport::Included { .. })), "{written:?}");
       let verified = block_on(io.verify_organisation(HeldTarget::Founding(founder)));
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Adopted { .. }), "{verified:?}");
       let org_id = block_on(io.personas())
           .into_iter()
           .find(|persona| persona.device_key == founder)
           .and_then(|persona| persona.org_id)
           .expect("the founding's org id");
       hex::encode(org_id.as_bytes())
   }

   /// A harness over a seeded store, chain not configured, and the seeded
   /// Organisation's id as hex.
   fn seeded_harness() -> (Harness, String) {
       let dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("tempdir");
       let data_dir = dir.path().to_path_buf();
       let org_id = seed_store(&data_dir);
       (harness_at(dir, data_dir, TransportModeName::Networked, None), org_id)
   }
   ```

   - `VerificationDto` takes LLR-g8wfy9's statuses, `removed` among them, and `OrgDto::new` takes the last verification.

   ```rust
   /// An Organisation's last verification as `list_orgs` reports it
   /// (LLR-g8wfy9): `not_checked` until one ran on this handle.
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   #[serde(tag = "status", rename_all = "snake_case")]
   pub enum VerificationDto {
       NotChecked,
       InStep { epoch: u64 },
       Adopted { epoch: u64 },
       Removed,
       Behind { chain_epoch: u64 },
       Inconsistent { reason: String },
       Unverified { reason: String },
   }

   impl VerificationDto {
       /// `last`, as `OrgIo::verification` returned it: org-io's
       /// `Unverified { NotYetVerified }` (no verification yet, LLR-ce42ce) is
       /// `not_checked`; a settled verification is its outcome's status; a
       /// refusal, a store failure or a keychain refusal is `unverified` with
       /// org-io's text.
       fn of(last: &Verified) -> Self {
           match last {
               Verified::Unverified { reason: UnverifiedReason::NotYetVerified } => Self::NotChecked,
               Verified::InStep { epoch } => Self::InStep { epoch: epoch.get() },
               Verified::Adopted { epoch, .. } => Self::Adopted { epoch: epoch.get() },
               Verified::Removed { .. } => Self::Removed,
               Verified::Behind { chain_epoch } => Self::Behind { chain_epoch: chain_epoch.get() },
               Verified::Inconsistent { reason } => Self::Inconsistent { reason: reason.to_string() },
               Verified::Unverified { reason } => Self::Unverified { reason: reason.to_string() },
               Verified::Refused { reason } | Verified::Store { reason } => Self::Unverified { reason: reason.clone() },
               Verified::Keychain { error } => Self::Unverified { reason: error.to_string() },
               Verified::Settled { outcome, .. } => Self::of(outcome),
           }
       }
   }

   impl OrgDto {
       /// `summary`, with `verification` as `OrgIo::verification` returned it.
       pub fn new(summary: &OrgSummary, last: &Verified) -> Self {
           Self {
               org_id: hex::encode(summary.org_id.as_bytes()),
               epoch: summary.epoch.get(),
               root_hash: hex::encode(summary.root_hash.as_bytes()),
               member_count: summary.members.len(),
               verification: VerificationDto::of(last),
           }
       }
   }

   /// List all local org records, each with its last verification.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn list_orgs(state: State<'_, AppState>) -> Result<Vec<OrgDto>, String> {
       let mut orgs = Vec::new();
       for org in state.org_io.organisations().await {
           let last = state.org_io.verification(HeldTarget::Organisation(org.org_id)).await;
           orgs.push(OrgDto::new(&org, &last));
       }
       Ok(orgs)
   }

   /// One Device's outcome of a send or a request (LLR-rywe8f, LLR-nkg8sb).
   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   pub struct DeviceReportDto {
       pub device: String,
       #[serde(flatten)]
       pub result: DeviceResultDto,
   }

   #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
   #[serde(tag = "result", rename_all = "snake_case")]
   pub enum DeviceResultDto {
       Sent,
       Failed { reason: String },
   }

   /// One recipient's delivery as the app reports it: `Delivered` is sent;
   /// every other outcome is failed, `NotDelivered` with org-io's reason, the
   /// three other verdicts with a fixed text.
   fn device_result(delivery: &Delivery) -> DeviceResultDto {
       let reason = match delivery {
           Delivery::Delivered => return DeviceResultDto::Sent,
           Delivery::NotDelivered { reason } => reason.to_string(),
           Delivery::Refused => "refused by the recipient".to_string(),
           Delivery::AlreadyReceived => "already received".to_string(),
           Delivery::InviteUsedByAnotherDevice => "invite used by another device".to_string(),
       };
       DeviceResultDto::Failed { reason }
   }

   /// org-io's per-Device report, in its order.
   pub fn device_reports(report: &SendReport) -> Vec<DeviceReportDto> {
       report
           .per_device
           .iter()
           .map(|(device, delivery)| DeviceReportDto { device: hex::encode(device.as_bytes()), result: device_result(delivery) })
           .collect()
   }
   ```
   `EntryResultDto`'s `Adopted` and `Behind` variants are replaced by:
   ```rust
       Adopted {
           epoch: u64,
           own: bool,
           discarded: Vec<DiscardedDto>,
           #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
           sends: Option<Vec<DeviceReportDto>>,
           #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
           sends_refused: Option<String>,
       },
       Behind {
           chain_epoch: u64,
           #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
           requests: Option<Vec<DeviceReportDto>>,
           #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
           requests_refused: Option<String>,
       },
   ```
   In `entry_for` the two arms become:
   ```rust
           Verified::Adopted { epoch, discarded, own } => entry(EntryResultDto::Adopted {
               epoch: epoch.get(),
               own: *own,
               discarded: discarded.iter().map(DiscardedDto::from).collect(),
               sends: None,
               sends_refused: None,
           }),
           Verified::Behind { chain_epoch } => entry(EntryResultDto::Behind {
               chain_epoch: chain_epoch.get(),
               requests: None,
               requests_refused: None,
           }),
   ```
   The old `verify_and_send` is replaced, and the following are added:
   ```rust
   /// LLR-es49wp, LLR-nkg8sb: after a verification, an own adoption is sent
   /// once, and a behind Organisation is requested once, each with the
   /// Organisation alone and no user step; no other entry asks for anything.
   /// A settled verification follows its outcome's result.
   pub async fn send_and_request(
       org_io: &OrgIo,
       org_id: Option<OrgId>,
       mut entry: VerificationEntryDto,
   ) -> VerificationEntryDto {
       match (&mut entry.result, org_id) {
           (EntryResultDto::Adopted { own: true, sends, sends_refused, .. }, Some(org_id)) => {
               match org_io.send_organisation(org_id).await {
                   Ok(report) => *sends = Some(device_reports(&report)),
                   Err(refused) => {
                       *sends = Some(Vec::new());
                       *sends_refused = Some(refused.to_string());
                   }
               }
           }
           (EntryResultDto::Behind { requests, requests_refused, .. }, Some(org_id)) => {
               match org_io.request_organisation(org_id).await {
                   Ok(report) => *requests = Some(device_reports(&report)),
                   Err(refused) => {
                       *requests = Some(Vec::new());
                       *requests_refused = Some(refused.to_string());
                   }
               }
           }
           _ => {}
       }
       entry
   }

   async fn entry_and_follow_up(org_io: &OrgIo, target: &HeldTarget, verified: &Verified) -> VerificationEntryDto {
       let named = org_id_for(org_io, target).await;
       let entry = entry_for(&named, verified);
       let org_id = match named {
           EntryOrg::Id(org_id) | EntryOrg::Founding { org_id: Some(org_id), .. } => Some(org_id),
           // A founding with no proxy names no Organisation: nothing is sent or requested.
           EntryOrg::Founding { org_id: None, .. } => None,
       };
       send_and_request(org_io, org_id, entry).await
   }

   /// The body every verification runs (SDD-6pjvhc): `verify_organisation`'s,
   /// the receiver loop's, the write's and the periodic run's.
   pub async fn verify_and_send(org_io: &OrgIo, target: HeldTarget) -> VerificationEntryDto {
       let verified = org_io.verify_organisation(target).await;
       entry_and_follow_up(org_io, &target, &verified).await
   }

   /// `verify_and_send` for every target org-io holds, in org-io's order,
   /// each outcome beside the target it verified (LLR-jf63e4 with no
   /// `org_id`; org-io's LLR-kq7z58).
   pub async fn verify_all_and_send(org_io: &OrgIo) -> Vec<VerificationEntryDto> {
       let mut entries = Vec::new();
       for (target, verified) in org_io.verify_all().await {
           entries.push(entry_and_follow_up(org_io, &target, &verified).await);
       }
       entries
   }

   /// LLR-jf63e4: verify one held Organisation (`org_id`), or every target
   /// org-io holds, sending and requesting as `verify_and_send` does.
   #[tauri::command]
   pub async fn verify_organisation(
       state: State<'_, AppState>,
       org_id: Option<String>,
   ) -> Result<Vec<VerificationEntryDto>, String> {
       match org_id {
           Some(org_id) => {
               let org_id = parse_org_id(&org_id)?;
               Ok(vec![verify_and_send(&state.org_io, HeldTarget::Organisation(org_id)).await])
           }
           None => Ok(verify_all_and_send(&state.org_io).await),
       }
   }
   ```

   ```rust
   #[test]
   fn list_admission_requests_returns_each_kept_request_with_the_events_fields_and_changes_nothing() {
       let fresh = harness();
       assert_eq!(invoke(&fresh, "list_admission_requests", serde_json::json!({})).expect("list"), serde_json::json!([]));

       let (ex, invite_id) = requested(&["bob", "builder"]);
       let member_device = device_key_of(&ex.invitee, ex.proposed["persona_id"].as_str().expect("an id"));
       let personas = invoke(&ex.inviter, "list_personas", serde_json::json!({})).expect("list_personas");
       let orgs = invoke(&ex.inviter, "list_orgs", serde_json::json!({})).expect("list_orgs");
       let listed = invoke(&ex.inviter, "list_admission_requests", serde_json::json!({})).expect("list_admission_requests");
       assert_eq!(
           listed,
           serde_json::json!([{
               "org_id": ex.org_id,
               "invite_id": invite_id,
               "invitee_name": "Bob Builder",
               "name": "Bob",
               "surname": "Builder",
               "preferred_handles": ["bob", "builder"],
               "device_public_key": hex::encode(member_device.as_bytes()),
           }])
       );

       assert_eq!(invoke(&ex.inviter, "list_personas", serde_json::json!({})).expect("list_personas"), personas);
   ```

**Intent:** `outcome_for_arrival` maps org-io's `Received` variants to `ProvisionalReceived`, `AdmissionRequested` (the `admission-requested` event), `OrganisationRequestAnswered`, `RevocationNoticeKept` and `AcknowledgementReceived`; `outcomes_for_verification` maps `removed` to `SelfDeleted` then the result; `classify_receive_error` classifies every `OrgNodeError` variant exhaustively.
*Settled at assembly:* `app/src-tauri/src/commands.rs` is in T53's files: T46 leaves `next_outcomes` matching `Received::Acknowledged` with its transitional unit `Arrival::Acknowledged` and announcing the other arrivals by nothing, so its body changes with `Arrival` here (step 3c) (fix item 10).

NAMES THIS TASK FIXES (T54, T55 and T57 use them): `events::Arrival` (`ProvisionalOrganisation`, `AdmissionRequestKept`, `OrganisationRequestAnswered`, `RevocationNoticeKept`, `Acknowledged`); `events::AdmissionRequested` (the `admission-requested` payload, which T52's `list_admission_requests` entry may reuse); the new `ReceiverOutcome` variants `ProvisionalReceived`, `AdmissionRequested`, `OrganisationRequestAnswered`, `RevocationNoticeKept` and `VerificationResult { entry }`; `events::VerifiedKind`; and `events::outcomes_for_verification(entry: serde_json::Value, record: Option<(u64, String)>)`. The verification entry reaches `events` as the JSON value of T51's entry type, read by its `result` and `org_id` fields (LLR-jf63e4 fixes both), so `events.rs` does not depend on the Rust name T51 gives that type.

- `OrgNodeError` (T5, LLR-3sddey) has the field shapes this task's table uses: `OrganisationBehind { org_id, chain_epoch: Epoch }`, `MemberNotHeld { member_id: MemberId }`, `RevocationAlreadyRecorded { member_id }`, `OrganisationNotRequested { org_id }`, `AdmissionKeyNotSender { org_id }`, `OrganisationRemoved { org_id }`, `AcknowledgementNotKept { recipient: Box<DevicePublicKey> }` (built with `Box::new`; names table N6). Every other new variant is a unit variant. Together they show four things. A received provisional organisation is `ProvisionalReceived` and is never announced with an epoch or root. A `removed` verification result is a self-delete followed by the result. A kept revocation notice, an answered organisation request and an acknowledgement announce nothing.    /// Every `OrgNodeError` variant the app can build through org-io's
   ```rust
   /// re-exports, with whether it is a verdict on a delivered update
   /// (LLR-wgr46u). `StoreRefused(_)` is the one variant left out: org-io
   /// does not re-export `StoreRefusal`, so the app cannot build it. The
   /// no-wildcard scan below covers it, because its arm must name it.
   fn every_org_node_error_variant() -> Vec<(org_io::node::OrgNodeError, bool)> {
       use org_io::node::{DevicePublicKey, Epoch, MemberId, OrgId, OrgMembersError, OrgNodeError as E};
       let org_id = OrgId::new([1; 20]);
       let member_id = MemberId::new([2; 32]);
       let recipient = DevicePublicKey::parse(&ARRIVAL_DEVICE_KEY).unwrap();
       vec![
           // The five refusals of a delivered update's own content, and the two chain verdicts.
           (E::OrgIdMismatch, true),
           (E::StaleSeq { got: 3, last_seen: 7 }, true),
           (E::MalformedDelta, true),
           (E::DeltaBaseMismatch, true),
           (E::SeqNotEpoch { seq: 9, epoch: 3 }, true),
           (E::RootMismatch, true),
           (E::StaleEpoch { got: 2, last: 9 }, true),
           // Every other variant: a receiver error.
           (E::Chain("io".to_string()), false),
           (E::OrgNotOnChain, false),
           (E::Trie(OrgMembersError::IdNotFound), false),
           (E::InvalidOrgPublicKey, false),
           (E::InvalidField { field: "member.handle", reason: "bad".to_string() }, false),
           (E::AdmissionNotExpected { org_id }, false),
           (E::AdmissionNotOurs { org_id }, false),
           (E::ProvisionalLimit { limit: 1 }, false),
           (E::MalformedMessage, false),
           (E::MessageTooLarge { length: 1 << 21 }, false),
           (E::RevocationNotHeld { org_id }, false),
           (E::RevocationNotForThisDevice { org_id }, false),
           (E::OrgNotHeld { org_id }, false),
           (E::StaleChainState { org_id, chain_epoch: Epoch::new(1), record_epoch: Epoch::new(2) }, false),
           (E::ChainStateConflict { org_id }, false),
           (E::RevocationProofRefused { org_id, cause: OrgMembersError::IdNotFound }, false),
           (E::AcknowledgementNotHeld { org_id }, false),
           (E::AcknowledgementFromFuture { org_id }, false),
           (E::AcknowledgementForListedDevice { org_id }, false),
           (E::AcknowledgementSignatureInvalid { org_id }, false),
           (E::DeviceSecretNotSupplied { org_id }, false),
           (E::SenderNotListed { org_id }, false),
           (E::AcknowledgementNotFromItsDevice { org_id }, false),
           (E::DeviceSecretMismatch, false),
           (E::DuplicatePersonaStore, false),
           (E::InviteNotOutstanding, false),
           (E::OrganisationHeldByAnotherPersona { org_id }, false),
           (E::NoProvisionalChange, false),
           (E::OrganisationBehind { org_id, chain_epoch: Epoch::new(5) }, false),
           (E::NoAdmissionRequestKept, false),
           (E::AdmissionAlreadyRecorded, false),
           (E::NoFreeHandle, false),
           (E::HandleTaken, false),
           (E::MemberNotHeld { member_id }, false),
           (E::RevocationAlreadyRecorded { member_id }, false),
           (E::NoProvisionalFounding, false),
           (E::FoundingProxyAlreadyRecorded, false),
           (E::FoundingNotWritten, false),
           (E::NoProvisionalMember, false),
           (E::OrganisationNotRequested { org_id }, false),
           (E::PersonaNotHeld, false),
           (E::AdmissionKeyNotSender { org_id }, false),
           (E::OrganisationRemoved { org_id }, false),
           (E::AcknowledgementNotKept { recipient: Box::new(recipient) }, false),
       ]
   }

   /// `classify_receive_error`'s body, as written in `src/events.rs`.
   fn classify_source() -> &'static str {
       let source = include_str!("../src/events.rs");
       let start = source.find("pub fn classify_receive_error").expect("classify_receive_error is defined");
       let end = start + source[start..].find("\n}\n").expect("its body ends at a closing brace in column one");
       &source[start..end]
   }

   // verifies: LLR-wgr46u
   #[test]
   fn every_org_node_error_variant_is_classified_with_no_wildcard() {
       for (e, verdict) in every_org_node_error_variant() {
           let expected = if verdict {
               ReceiverOutcome::VerifyFailed { org_id: None, message: e.to_string() }
           } else {
               ReceiverOutcome::ReceiveError { message: e.to_string() }
           };
           assert_eq!(events::classify_receive_error(&e), expected, "{e:?}");
       }
       let body = classify_source();
       assert!(!body.contains("_ =>"), "classify_receive_error has a wildcard arm:\n{body}");
       let all_variants = [
           "OrgIdMismatch", "StaleSeq", "MalformedDelta", "DeltaBaseMismatch", "SeqNotEpoch", "RootMismatch",
           "StaleEpoch", "Chain", "OrgNotOnChain", "Trie", "InvalidOrgPublicKey", "InvalidField",
           "AdmissionNotExpected", "AdmissionNotOurs", "ProvisionalLimit", "MalformedMessage", "MessageTooLarge",
           "RevocationNotHeld", "RevocationNotForThisDevice", "OrgNotHeld", "StaleChainState",
           "ChainStateConflict", "RevocationProofRefused", "AcknowledgementNotHeld", "AcknowledgementFromFuture",
           "AcknowledgementForListedDevice", "AcknowledgementSignatureInvalid", "DeviceSecretNotSupplied",
           "SenderNotListed", "AcknowledgementNotFromItsDevice", "StoreRefused", "DeviceSecretMismatch",
           "DuplicatePersonaStore", "InviteNotOutstanding", "OrganisationHeldByAnotherPersona",
           "NoProvisionalChange", "OrganisationBehind", "NoAdmissionRequestKept", "AdmissionAlreadyRecorded",
           "NoFreeHandle", "HandleTaken", "MemberNotHeld", "RevocationAlreadyRecorded", "NoProvisionalFounding",
           "FoundingProxyAlreadyRecorded", "FoundingNotWritten", "NoProvisionalMember",
           "OrganisationNotRequested", "PersonaNotHeld", "AdmissionKeyNotSender", "OrganisationRemoved",
           "AcknowledgementNotKept",
       ];

           assert!(body.contains(&format!("OrgNodeError::{variant}")), "classify_receive_error names no arm for {variant}");
       }
       // The removed variants are named nowhere (LLR-3sddey).
       for removed in ["NoProvisionalUpdate", "ReplyForAnotherOrganisation", "PersonaAlreadyBound", "RecordMovedSinceCheck", "OrgKeyMismatch"] {
           assert!(!body.contains(removed), "classify_receive_error still names {removed}");
   ```

   ```rust
   use org_io::node::OrgNodeError;
   use org_io::{ReceiveError, Received};
   use serde::Serialize;
   use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
   use std::sync::Arc;

   /// What one iteration of the receiver loop, or one verification it ran,
   /// concluded.
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
   pub enum ReceiverOutcome {
       /// LLR-ygr6gd: a verification found this node removed; its Persona's
       /// data is deleted. No epoch (REQ-tw4cb5).
       SelfDeleted { org_id: String },
       /// LLR-ygr6gd: a removed Device's acknowledgement was kept. Nothing is announced.
       AcknowledgementReceived { org_id: String },
       /// LLR-4bvdn7: a provisional organisation was received and kept. It is
       /// never an adoption, so it states no epoch and no root.
       ProvisionalReceived { org_id: String },
       /// LLR-dp45mm: an admission request was kept.
       AdmissionRequested(AdmissionRequested),
       /// LLR-t9rdf8: an organisation request was answered. Nothing is announced.
       OrganisationRequestAnswered { org_id: String, requester: String },
       /// LLR-ygr6gd: a revocation notice was kept; the next verification acts
       /// on it. Nothing is announced.
       RevocationNoticeKept { org_id: String },
       /// A verification adopted an epoch and its record was read back.
       Updated { org_id: String, epoch: u64, root: String },
       /// REQ-2k7ys4 / REQ-dp95pv: an epoch was adopted and the record could NOT
       /// be read back.
       RecordUnreadable { org_id: String },
       /// One verification result: the entry `verify_organisation` returns for
       /// it (LLR-jf63e4), as its JSON value.
       VerificationResult { entry: serde_json::Value },
       /// REQ-affyf5: a delivered update's content was refused.
       VerifyFailed { org_id: Option<String>, message: String },
       /// REQ-kn5rtx / RC-3rddh7: the receive path failed for a reason that is
       /// NOT a verdict on any update.
       ReceiveError { message: String },
       /// REQ-jfxah3: the loop is about to exit.
       Stopped { reason: String },
   }

   /// LLR-dp45mm: the `admission-requested` payload, field for field, in this
   /// order: `org_id` (40 hex), `invite_id` (64), the `invitee_name` typed for
   /// that Invite, the request's `name`, `surname` and `preferred_handles`,
   /// and its `device_public_key` (64).
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
   pub struct AdmissionRequested {
       pub org_id: String,
       pub invite_id: String,
       pub invitee_name: String,
       pub name: String,
       pub surname: String,
       pub preferred_handles: Vec<String>,
       pub device_public_key: String,
   }

   /// What org-io's `next_received` reported, as far as the announcement
   /// depends on it: org-io's `Received`, ids and keys as hex, values as text.
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum Arrival {
       ProvisionalOrganisation { org_id: String },
       AdmissionRequestKept(AdmissionRequested),
       OrganisationRequestAnswered { org_id: String, requester: String },
       RevocationNoticeKept { org_id: String },
       Acknowledged { org_id: String },
   }

   impl From<Received> for Arrival {
       fn from(received: Received) -> Self {
           let hex_org = |org_id: &org_io::node::OrgId| hex::encode(org_id.as_bytes());
           match received {
               // LLR-4bvdn7: the epoch, root and sender are not carried; nothing
               // announces them before a verification adopts.
               Received::ProvisionalOrganisationReceived { org_id, .. } => {
                   Arrival::ProvisionalOrganisation { org_id: hex_org(&org_id) }
               }
               Received::AdmissionRequestKept { org_id, invite_id, name, surname, preferred_handles, from, invitee_name } => {
                   Arrival::AdmissionRequestKept(AdmissionRequested {
                       org_id: hex_org(&org_id),
                       invite_id: hex::encode(invite_id.as_bytes()),
                       invitee_name: invitee_name.to_string(),
                       name: name.to_string(),
                       surname: surname.to_string(),
                       preferred_handles: preferred_handles.iter().map(ToString::to_string).collect(),
                       device_public_key: hex::encode(from.as_bytes()),
                   })
               }
               Received::OrganisationRequestAnswered { org_id, requester, .. } => Arrival::OrganisationRequestAnswered {
                   org_id: hex_org(&org_id),
                   requester: hex::encode(requester.as_bytes()),
               },
               Received::RevocationNoticeKept { org_id, .. } => Arrival::RevocationNoticeKept { org_id: hex_org(&org_id) },
               Received::Acknowledged(verified) => Arrival::Acknowledged { org_id: hex_org(&verified.into_inner().org_id) },
           }
       }
   }

   /// LLR-4bvdn7, LLR-ygr6gd, LLR-dp45mm, LLR-t9rdf8. The outcome of one
   /// arrival. No arrival is an adoption or a self-delete: those are
   /// verification results (`outcomes_for_verification`).
   pub fn outcome_for_arrival(arrival: Arrival) -> ReceiverOutcome {
       match arrival {
           Arrival::ProvisionalOrganisation { org_id } => ReceiverOutcome::ProvisionalReceived { org_id },
           Arrival::AdmissionRequestKept(request) => ReceiverOutcome::AdmissionRequested(request),
           Arrival::OrganisationRequestAnswered { org_id, requester } => {
               ReceiverOutcome::OrganisationRequestAnswered { org_id, requester }
           }
           Arrival::RevocationNoticeKept { org_id } => ReceiverOutcome::RevocationNoticeKept { org_id },
           Arrival::Acknowledged { org_id } => ReceiverOutcome::AcknowledgementReceived { org_id },
       }
   }

   /// The result a verification entry carries, read from its `result` tag
   /// (LLR-jf63e4). A tag this app does not know is `Unknown`, and it maps
   /// to the result alone, never to `Updated` or `SelfDeleted`.
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum VerifiedKind {
       InStep,
       Adopted,
       Removed,
       Behind,
       Inconsistent,
       Unverified,
       Unknown,
   }

   impl VerifiedKind {
       pub fn of(entry: &serde_json::Value) -> Self {
           match entry.get("result").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
               Some("in_step") => Self::InStep,
               Some("adopted") => Self::Adopted,
               Some("removed") => Self::Removed,
               Some("behind") => Self::Behind,
               Some("inconsistent") => Self::Inconsistent,
               Some("unverified") => Self::Unverified,
               _ => Self::Unknown,
           }
       }
   }

   /// LLR-ygr6gd (LLR-acb5g4 from T54). The outcomes of one verification
   /// result: `entry` is the JSON value of the entry `verify_organisation`
   /// returns for it, and `record` the record read back after it (epoch and
   /// root), or `None`. A `removed` result is a self-delete naming the
   /// Organisation, with no epoch, whatever the record reads, then the result.
   pub fn outcomes_for_verification(entry: serde_json::Value, _record: Option<(u64, String)>) -> Vec<ReceiverOutcome> {
       let org_id = entry.get("org_id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
       match VerifiedKind::of(&entry) {
           VerifiedKind::Removed => vec![ReceiverOutcome::SelfDeleted { org_id }, ReceiverOutcome::VerificationResult { entry }],
           VerifiedKind::InStep
           | VerifiedKind::Adopted
           | VerifiedKind::Behind
           | VerifiedKind::Inconsistent
           | VerifiedKind::Unverified
           | VerifiedKind::Unknown => vec![ReceiverOutcome::VerificationResult { entry }],
       }
   }

   /// LLR-wgr46u (REQ-kn5rtx). The class of a refusal org-io's receive step
   /// returned, from the error's TYPE. The five refusals of a delivered
   /// update's own content, with `RootMismatch` and `StaleEpoch`, are
   /// verdicts: `VerifyFailed`, with the message and no organisation. Every
   /// other variant is a receiver error. org-io's receive step reads no chain,
   /// so a chain judgement reaches the app as a verification result, never
   /// here; `RootMismatch` and `StaleEpoch` stay verdicts only because the type
   /// still has them. A misfiled verdict is the hazard (HAZ-9fmhm4); a
   /// misfiled receiver error is merely less specific.
   ///
   /// There is no wildcard arm, deliberately: a variant org-io's type gains is
   /// a compile error here until it is classified.
   pub fn classify_receive_error(e: &OrgNodeError) -> ReceiverOutcome {
       match e {
           OrgNodeError::OrgIdMismatch { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::StaleSeq { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::MalformedDelta { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::DeltaBaseMismatch { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::SeqNotEpoch { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::RootMismatch { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::StaleEpoch { .. } => ReceiverOutcome::VerifyFailed { org_id: None, message: e.to_string() },

           // Not verdicts. A chain read or a value that could not be parsed:
           // `Chain`, `OrgNotOnChain`, `Trie`, `InvalidOrgPublicKey`,
           // `InvalidField`. Refusals of a received message made before
           // anything is judged: `MalformedMessage`, `MessageTooLarge`,
           // `SenderNotListed`, `AcknowledgementNotFromItsDevice`,
           // `AdmissionKeyNotSender`, `AdmissionNotExpected`,
           // `AdmissionNotOurs`, `RevocationNotHeld`,
           // `RevocationNotForThisDevice`, `OrganisationNotRequested`,
           // `OrganisationRemoved`. Acknowledgements and proofs, which are not
           // updates: the four `Acknowledgement*`, `AcknowledgementNotKept`,
           // `RevocationProofRefused`. This node's own store and bookkeeping:
           // `StoreRefused`, `DeviceSecretMismatch`, `DuplicatePersonaStore`,
           // `InviteNotOutstanding`, `OrganisationHeldByAnotherPersona`,
           // `PersonaNotHeld`, `OrgNotHeld`, `StaleChainState`,
           // `ChainStateConflict`, `DeviceSecretNotSupplied`,
           // `ProvisionalLimit`. The proposal refusals, which no receive raises
           // but the type has: `NoProvisionalChange`, `OrganisationBehind`,
           // `NoAdmissionRequestKept`, `AdmissionAlreadyRecorded`,
           // `NoFreeHandle`, `HandleTaken`, `MemberNotHeld`,
           // `RevocationAlreadyRecorded`, `NoProvisionalFounding`,
           // `FoundingProxyAlreadyRecorded`, `FoundingNotWritten`,
           // `NoProvisionalMember`.
           OrgNodeError::Chain { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::OrgNotOnChain { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::Trie { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::InvalidOrgPublicKey { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::InvalidField { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::AdmissionNotExpected { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::AdmissionNotOurs { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::ProvisionalLimit { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::MessageTooLarge { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::RevocationNotHeld { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::RevocationNotForThisDevice { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::StaleChainState { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::ChainStateConflict { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::RevocationProofRefused { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementNotHeld { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementFromFuture { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementForListedDevice { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementSignatureInvalid { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::DeviceSecretNotSupplied { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::SenderNotListed { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementNotFromItsDevice { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::StoreRefused { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::DeviceSecretMismatch { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::DuplicatePersonaStore { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::InviteNotOutstanding { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::OrganisationHeldByAnotherPersona { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::NoProvisionalChange { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::OrganisationBehind { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::NoAdmissionRequestKept { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::AdmissionAlreadyRecorded { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::NoFreeHandle { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::HandleTaken { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::MemberNotHeld { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::RevocationAlreadyRecorded { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::NoProvisionalFounding { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::FoundingProxyAlreadyRecorded { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::FoundingNotWritten { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::NoProvisionalMember { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::OrganisationNotRequested { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::PersonaNotHeld { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::AdmissionKeyNotSender { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::OrganisationRemoved { .. }
           | OrgNodeError::AcknowledgementNotKept { .. } => ReceiverOutcome::ReceiveError { message: e.to_string() },
       }
   }
   ```
