   ```rust
   /// LLR-w7m3d4: the one follow-up a received message asks for.
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum FollowUp {
       /// Verify this Organisation, once, before the next message is read.
       Verify { org_id: String },
   }

   /// LLR-w7m3d4. "Verify this Organisation" for a received provisional
   /// organisation or a kept revocation notice, nothing for any other outcome.
   pub fn follow_up_for(outcome: &ReceiverOutcome) -> Option<FollowUp> {
       match outcome {
           ReceiverOutcome::ProvisionalReceived { org_id } | ReceiverOutcome::RevocationNoticeKept { org_id } => {
               Some(FollowUp::Verify { org_id: org_id.clone() })
           }
           ReceiverOutcome::SelfDeleted { .. }
           | ReceiverOutcome::AcknowledgementReceived { .. }
           | ReceiverOutcome::AdmissionRequested(_)
           | ReceiverOutcome::OrganisationRequestAnswered { .. }
           | ReceiverOutcome::Updated { .. }
           | ReceiverOutcome::RecordUnreadable { .. }
           | ReceiverOutcome::VerificationResult { .. }
           | ReceiverOutcome::VerifyFailed { .. }
           | ReceiverOutcome::ReceiveError { .. }
           | ReceiverOutcome::Stopped { .. } => None,
       }
   }

   /// LLR-w7m3d4. One iteration of the receiver loop: `next` once, every
   /// outcome's events in order, and, right after an outcome that asks for
   /// one, `verify` once for its Organisation with every outcome of that
   /// verification announced, all before this returns and the loop asks
   /// `next` again. Returns whether the loop stops (REQ-jfxah3).
   pub async fn receive_iteration<N, NF, V, VF, E>(next: N, mut verify: V, mut emit: E) -> bool
   where
       N: FnOnce() -> NF,
       NF: Future<Output = Vec<ReceiverOutcome>>,
       V: FnMut(String) -> VF,
       VF: Future<Output = Vec<ReceiverOutcome>>,
       E: FnMut(Emission),
   {
       let outcomes = next().await;
       let stopping = outcomes.iter().any(|outcome| matches!(outcome, ReceiverOutcome::Stopped { .. }));
       for outcome in &outcomes {
           for emission in emissions_for(outcome) {
               emit(emission);
           }
           if let Some(FollowUp::Verify { org_id }) = follow_up_for(outcome) {
               for verified in verify(org_id).await {
                   for emission in emissions_for(&verified) {
                       emit(emission);
                   }
               }
           }
       }
       stopping
   }

   /// LLR-ygr6gd, LLR-acb5g4. The outcomes of one verification result:
   /// `entry` is the JSON value of the entry `verify_organisation` returns for
   /// it, and `record` the record read back after it (epoch and root), or
   /// `None`. `adopted` is `Updated` with the record read, or
   /// `RecordUnreadable` without one, then the result; `removed` is a
   /// self-delete with no epoch, whatever the record reads, then the result;
   /// every other result is the result alone, never `Updated`.
   pub fn outcomes_for_verification(entry: serde_json::Value, record: Option<(u64, String)>) -> Vec<ReceiverOutcome> {
       let org_id = entry.get("org_id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
       match (VerifiedKind::of(&entry), record) {
           (VerifiedKind::Adopted, Some((epoch, root))) => {
               vec![ReceiverOutcome::Updated { org_id, epoch, root }, ReceiverOutcome::VerificationResult { entry }]
           }
           // REQ-2k7ys4 / REQ-dp95pv: no record, no epoch or root to announce.
           (VerifiedKind::Adopted, None) => {
               vec![ReceiverOutcome::RecordUnreadable { org_id }, ReceiverOutcome::VerificationResult { entry }]
           }
           (VerifiedKind::Removed, _) => {
               vec![ReceiverOutcome::SelfDeleted { org_id }, ReceiverOutcome::VerificationResult { entry }]
           }
           (
               VerifiedKind::InStep
               | VerifiedKind::Behind
               | VerifiedKind::Inconsistent
               | VerifiedKind::Unverified
               | VerifiedKind::Unknown,
               _,
           ) => vec![ReceiverOutcome::VerificationResult { entry }],
       }
   }
   ```

   3b. `app/src-tauri/src/commands.rs`:
   - Add `use org_io::HeldTarget;` if T50 did not add it.
   - Add `verification_outcomes` and `verify_received` near `next_outcomes`.
   - Replace the receiver loop inside `start_receiver`. Only the `loop { … }` block changes; the claim, the `start_receiving` failure path and the guard stay as they are.
   ```rust
   /// LLR-acb5g4, LLR-w7m3d4, LLR-2267hj. One verification through
   /// `verify_and_send` (so an own adoption is sent once and a behind
   /// Organisation requested), with each entry mapped by
   /// `events::outcomes_for_verification`; only an `adopted` entry's record is
   /// read back. The receiver loop's follow-up and the periodic run (T55) both
   /// announce verifications through this function.
   pub async fn verification_outcomes(org_io: &OrgIo, target: Option<HeldTarget>) -> Vec<events::ReceiverOutcome> {
       // `Some` verifies that one target; `None` every target org-io holds, in its order.
       let entries = match target {
           Some(target) => vec![verify_and_send(org_io, target).await],
           None => verify_all_and_send(org_io).await,
       };
       let mut outcomes = Vec::new();
       for entry in entries {
           let entry = serde_json::to_value(&entry).expect("a verification entry is a plain struct of owned scalars");
           let record = match events::VerifiedKind::of(&entry) {
               events::VerifiedKind::Adopted => match entry.get("org_id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(parse_org_id) {
                   Some(Ok(org_id)) => org_io
                       .organisation(org_id)
                       .await
                       .map(|organisation| (organisation.epoch.get(), hex::encode(organisation.root_hash.as_bytes()))),
                   Some(Err(_)) | None => None,
               },
               events::VerifiedKind::InStep
               | events::VerifiedKind::Removed
               | events::VerifiedKind::Behind
               | events::VerifiedKind::Inconsistent
               | events::VerifiedKind::Unverified
               | events::VerifiedKind::Unknown => None,
           };
           outcomes.extend(events::outcomes_for_verification(entry, record));
       }
       outcomes
   }

   /// LLR-w7m3d4: the receiver loop's follow-up for `org_id` (40 hex, as
   /// `events` names it): one verification of that held Organisation.
   async fn verify_received(org_io: &OrgIo, org_id: String) -> Vec<events::ReceiverOutcome> {
       match parse_org_id(&org_id) {
           Ok(org_id) => verification_outcomes(org_io, Some(HeldTarget::Organisation(org_id))).await,
           // Unreachable: `events` wrote this id from an OrgId. Reported, not panicked.
           Err(message) => vec![events::ReceiverOutcome::ReceiveError { message }],
       }
   }
   ```
   The loop inside `start_receiver`'s spawned task, replacing the existing `loop { … }`:

   ```rust
                   },
   ```

   ```rust
   use tokio::time::Instant;

   /// Starts `periodic_runs` with a run that records its start (seconds since
   /// `t0`), counts how many runs are in progress at once, and takes `took(n)`
   /// for its n-th run.
   fn spawn_recorded(
       interval: Duration,
       took: fn(usize) -> Duration,
   ) -> (Arc<Mutex<Vec<u64>>>, Arc<AtomicUsize>, tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>) {
       let t0 = Instant::now();
       let starts = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
       let most_at_once = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
       let running = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
       let (starts_in, most_in) = (Arc::clone(&starts), Arc::clone(&most_at_once));
       let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
           periodic::periodic_runs(
               interval,
               move || {
                   let (starts, most, running) = (Arc::clone(&starts_in), Arc::clone(&most_in), Arc::clone(&running));
                   async move {
                       let n = {
                           let mut starts = starts.lock().unwrap();
                           starts.push((Instant::now() - t0).as_secs());
                           starts.len() - 1
                       };
                       let now_running = running.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst) + 1;
                       most.fetch_max(now_running, Ordering::SeqCst);
                       tokio::time::sleep(took(n)).await;
                       running.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                       Vec::<ReceiverOutcome>::new()
                   }
               },
               |_emission: Emission| {},
           )
           .await;
       });
       (starts, most_at_once, task)
   }

       tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(599)).await;
       assert_eq!(*starts.lock().unwrap(), Vec::<u64>::new(), "no run before one interval has elapsed");
       tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(6)).await; // t = 605
       assert_eq!(*starts.lock().unwrap(), vec![600]);
       tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(1200)).await; // t = 1805
       assert_eq!(*starts.lock().unwrap(), vec![600, 1200, 1800], "one run per interval");
       assert_eq!(most_at_once.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 1, "never two runs at once");
       task.abort();
   ```

   ```rust
   //! The periodic verification (SDD-tgu7dp). While the app runs it asks
   //! org-io, once every verification interval, to verify every Organisation
   //! and provisional founding it holds, through the same body every other
   //! verification runs (`commands::verification_outcomes`, over
   //! `verify_and_send`), and announces each result as the receiver loop
   //! announces one. It decides nothing of the result.

   use std::future::Future;
   use std::sync::Arc;
   use std::time::Duration;

   use org_io::OrgIo;
   use tokio::time::{interval_at, Instant, MissedTickBehavior};

   use crate::commands;
   use crate::events::{self, Emission, ReceiverOutcome};

   /// LLR-3ampqm. `run` once per `interval`, the first time one interval
   /// after this starts, never two at once (each run is awaited before the
   /// next tick). When a run outlasts an interval the next starts as soon as
   /// it ends and the missed ones are not made up (tokio's
   /// `MissedTickBehavior::Delay`). LLR-2267hj: every outcome's events are
   /// emitted in order, as the receiver loop emits them. Runs until the task
   /// is dropped.
   pub async fn periodic_runs<R, F, E>(interval: Duration, mut run: R, mut emit: E)
   where
       R: FnMut() -> F,
       F: Future<Output = Vec<ReceiverOutcome>>,
       E: FnMut(Emission),
   {
       let mut ticker = interval_at(Instant::now() + interval, interval);
       ticker.set_missed_tick_behavior(MissedTickBehavior::Delay);
       loop {
           ticker.tick().await;
           for outcome in run().await {
               for emission in events::emissions_for(&outcome) {
                   emit(emission);
               }
           }
       }
   }

   /// One periodic run (LLR-3ampqm, LLR-fe7umz): every target org-io holds,
   /// verified through `verify_and_send`, so an own adoption is sent once and
   /// a behind Organisation is requested at this run.
   pub async fn periodic_run(org_io: &OrgIo) -> Vec<ReceiverOutcome> {
       commands::verification_outcomes(org_io, None).await
   }

   /// SDD-tgu7dp. Spawned once by `run`'s setup after `AppState::init`, with
   /// the interval `init` decided (LLR-2dpn52) and the emitter the receiver
   /// loop uses.
   pub async fn run_periodic_verification<E>(org_io: Arc<OrgIo>, interval: Duration, emit: E)
   where
       E: FnMut(Emission) + Send,
   {
       periodic_runs(
           interval,
           || {
               let org_io = Arc::clone(&org_io);
               async move { periodic_run(&org_io).await }
           },
           emit,
       )
       .await
   }
   ```

   ```ts
   /**
    * The creation form (CreateOrg.svelte, T56 of
    * docs/plans/2026-10-21-org-io-domain-api.md): the Person proposed if none
    * is held, then the founding, whose `founder` the form shows and hands to
    * the founding-writes list (LLR-6ff735, LLR-rhc555). Tested on the
    * extracted helper `proposeFounding` and on the components' source, never
    * a rendered component (vitest.config.ts).
    */

   import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest';

   const { invoke } = vi.hoisted(() => ({ invoke: vi.fn() }));
   vi.mock('@tauri-apps/api/core', () => ({ invoke }));
   vi.mock('@tauri-apps/api/event', () => ({ listen: vi.fn() }));

   import { proposeFounding, PERSON_ALREADY_HELD } from '../src/lib/founding';
   import formSource from '../src/lib/components/CreateOrg.svelte?raw';
   import pageSource from '../src/routes/+page.svelte?raw';

   const DEVICE = 'cd'.repeat(32);
   const FOUNDER = 'ef'.repeat(32);
   const FORM = { name: 'Alice', surname: 'Smith', handle: 'alice', orgName: 'Acme' };
   const PERSON = { device_public_key: DEVICE, name: 'Alice', surname: 'Smith', status: 'provisional' };
   const FOUNDING = { persona_id: 'ab'.repeat(32), status: 'provisional_founding', founder: FOUNDER };

   /** Each command returns its answer, or is refused with its text as Tauri rejects a command's `Err`. */
   function answer(answers: Record<string, unknown>, refusals: Record<string, string> = {}) {
   	invoke.mockImplementation(async (command: string) => {
   		if (command in refusals) throw refusals[command];
   		return answers[command];
   	});
   }

   function commands(): unknown[] {
   	return invoke.mock.calls.map((call) => call[0]);
   }

   describe('proposeFounding', () => {
   	beforeEach(() => invoke.mockReset());

   	// verifies: LLR-6ff735, LLR-rhc555
   	it('proposes the Person and then the founding, and returns the founder', async () => {
   		answer({ propose_person: PERSON, propose_founding_organisation: FOUNDING });
   		const proposals = await proposeFounding(FORM);
   		expect(invoke.mock.calls).toEqual([
   			['propose_person', { name: 'Alice', surname: 'Smith' }],
   			['propose_founding_organisation', { name: 'Alice', surname: 'Smith', handle: 'alice', orgName: 'Acme' }]
   		]);
   		expect(proposals).toEqual({ person: PERSON, founding: FOUNDING });
   		expect(proposals.founding.founder).toBe(FOUNDER);
   	});

   	// verifies: LLR-6ff735, LLR-rhc555
   	it('a Person held already is not proposed again and the founding is still proposed', async () => {
   		answer(
   			{ propose_founding_organisation: FOUNDING },
   			{ propose_person: `${PERSON_ALREADY_HELD} (${DEVICE}); nothing created` }
   		);
   		const proposals = await proposeFounding(FORM);
   		expect(commands()).toEqual(['propose_person', 'propose_founding_organisation']);
   		expect(proposals).toEqual({ person: null, founding: FOUNDING });
   	});

   	// verifies: LLR-6ff735
   	it('any other refusal of the Person stops before the founding, naming the field', async () => {
   		answer({ propose_founding_organisation: FOUNDING }, { propose_person: 'name: must not be empty' });
   		await expect(proposeFounding({ ...FORM, name: '' })).rejects.toBe('name: must not be empty');
   		expect(commands()).toEqual(['propose_person']);
   	});

   	// verifies: LLR-6ff735
   	it('a refused founding is reported as org-io words it', async () => {
   		answer({ propose_person: PERSON }, { propose_founding_organisation: 'handle: must not be empty' });
   		await expect(proposeFounding({ ...FORM, handle: '' })).rejects.toBe('handle: must not be empty');
   		expect(commands()).toEqual(['propose_person', 'propose_founding_organisation']);
   	});
   });

   describe('the creation form', () => {
   	// verifies: LLR-rhc555
   	it('the creation form shows the founder and hands it to the founding-writes list', () => {
   		expect(formSource).toMatch(/const proposals = await proposeFounding\(\{/);
   		expect(formSource).toMatch(/onProposed\?\.\(proposals\.founding\.founder\);/);
   		expect(formSource).toMatch(/Founder Device key: <code>\{proposed\.founding\.founder\}<\/code>/);
   		expect(formSource).not.toMatch(/createPersona|createOrganisation|create_persona|create_organisation/);
   		expect(pageSource).toMatch(/<CreateOrg \{notifyReload\} onProposed=\{fileProposedFounder\} \/>/);
   		expect(pageSource).toMatch(/proposedFounders = \[founder, \.\.\.proposedFounders\];/);
   		expect(pageSource).toMatch(/<PersonaList \{reloadToken\} \{results\} \{fileResults\} proposed=\{proposedFounders\} \/>/);
   	});
   });
   ```

   ```ts
   /** LLR-g8wfy9: the last verification of an Organisation on this handle (`removed` as amended 2026-10-22). */
   export type VerificationDto =
   	| { status: 'in_step'; epoch: number }
   	| { status: 'adopted'; epoch: number }
   	| { status: 'removed' }
   	| { status: 'behind'; chain_epoch: number }
   	| { status: 'inconsistent'; reason: string }
   	| { status: 'unverified'; reason: string }
   	| { status: 'not_checked' };

   /** LLR-rywe8f, LLR-nkg8sb: one Device's outcome of a send or a request. */
   export type DeviceOutcomeDto =
   	| { device: string; result: 'sent' }
   	| { device: string; result: 'failed'; reason: string };

   /**
    * LLR-n64wvr: a provisional change an adopted epoch left out. org-io reports
    * the request's name and surname, and a revoked Member's Handle, when it
    * still holds them; otherwise the field is `null` (names table OPEN-1).
    */
   export type DiscardedChangeDto =
   	| { kind: 'admission'; invite_id: string; name: string | null; surname: string | null; handle: string }
   	| { kind: 'revocation'; member_id: string; handle: string | null };

   /**
    * LLR-jf63e4 (amended 2026-10-22): which target an entry is for. An
    * Organisation's entry has its `org_id` and no `founder`. Every provisional
    * founding's entry carries `founder`, its founder's Device key (64 hex),
    * beside `org_id` `null` before its proxy is recorded and the proxy's
    * Organisation identifier after.
    */
   export type EntryTarget = { org_id: string; founder?: undefined } | { org_id: string | null; founder: string };

   /** LLR-jf63e4: what a verification settled of an unknown chain write (org-io's `Verified::Settled`). */
   export type WriteLabel = 'adopted' | 'not_executed' | 'deprecated' | 'still_unknown';

   /** LLR-jf63e4: one verification result, tagged by `result`. */
   export type VerificationEntryDto = EntryTarget & { write?: WriteLabel } & (
   		| { result: 'in_step'; epoch: number }
   		| {
   				result: 'adopted';
   				epoch: number;
   				own: boolean;
   				discarded: DiscardedChangeDto[];
   				sends?: DeviceOutcomeDto[];
   				sends_refused?: string;
   		  }
   		| { result: 'removed' }
   		| { result: 'behind'; chain_epoch: number; requests?: DeviceOutcomeDto[]; requests_refused?: string }
   		| { result: 'inconsistent'; reason: string }
   		| { result: 'unverified'; reason: string }
   	);

   /** LLR-j2x9jb: verify every Organisation and provisional founding held; one entry per result. */
   export function verifyOrganisations(): Promise<VerificationEntryDto[]> {
   	return invoke<VerificationEntryDto[]>('verify_organisation');
   }

   /** verification-result: LLR-8grnbb, LLR-84cxpt. One per result of a verification the app ran itself. */
   export function onVerificationResult(cb: (payload: VerificationEntryDto) => void): Promise<UnlistenFn> {
   	return listen<VerificationEntryDto>('verification-result', (e) => cb(e.payload));
   }

   /** LLR-k57uqv: the Person as `propose_person` returns it: its Device key (64 hex), the names stored, its status. */
   export interface PersonDto {
   	device_public_key: string;
   	name: string;
   	surname: string;
   	status: 'provisional';
   }

   /** LLR-k57uqv: propose the user's Person from a name and a surname (no Handle); a refusal names the field. */
   export function proposePerson(name: string, surname: string): Promise<PersonDto> {
   	return invoke<PersonDto>('propose_person', { name, surname });
   }

   /** LLR-6ff735 (amended 2026-10-22): a proposed founding, with its founder's Device key (64 hex). */
   export interface ProposedFoundingDto {
   	persona_id: string;
   	status: 'provisional_founding';
   	founder: string;
   }

   /** LLR-6ff735: propose a founding; its result carries the founder's Device key the founding's write takes. */
   export function proposeFoundingOrganisation(
   	name: string,
   	surname: string,
   	handle: string,
   	orgName: string
   ): Promise<ProposedFoundingDto> {
   	return invoke<ProposedFoundingDto>('propose_founding_organisation', { name, surname, handle, orgName });
   }

   /** LLR-rhc555, LLR-k4rhbs: a write's outcome, tagged by `result`; an included write carries its verification. */
   export type WriteDto =
   	| { result: 'included'; epoch: number; verification: VerificationEntryDto }
   	| { result: 'refused'; reason: string }
   	| { result: 'unknown'; reason: string };

   /** LLR-rhc555: write a held Organisation by `orgId`, or a founding by its `founder`; exactly one. */
   export function writeOrganisationToChain(target: { orgId: string } | { founder: string }): Promise<WriteDto> {
   ```

   3b. `app/src/lib/verification.ts`, the full new content of the renamed file:
   ```ts
   import type { VerificationEntryDto, VerificationDto, WriteLabel } from './api';

   /** LLR-mfzr6z (amended 2026-10-22): the words for a settled write. */
   const WRITE_WORDS: Record<WriteLabel, string> = {
   	adopted: 'write adopted',
   	not_executed: 'write not executed',
   	deprecated: 'write deprecated',
   	still_unknown: 'write still unknown'
   };

   /** The Organisation an entry names, or, for a founding with no proxy yet, its founder (LLR-jf63e4). */
   function subject(entry: { org_id: string | null; founder?: string }): string {
   	return entry.org_id ?? `founding by ${entry.founder}`;
   }

   /** The result's own words, before any write label. */
   function resultLine(result: VerificationEntryDto): string {
   	const name = subject(result);
   	switch (result.result) {
   		case 'in_step':
   			return `${name}: in step at epoch ${result.epoch}`;
   		case 'adopted':
   			return `${name}: adopted epoch ${result.epoch}`;
   		case 'removed':
   			return `${name}: this device was removed`;
   		case 'behind':
   			return `${name}: behind the chain (chain at epoch ${result.chain_epoch})`;
   		case 'inconsistent':
   			return `${name}: inconsistent: ${result.reason}`;
   		case 'unverified':
   			return `${name}: unverified: ${result.reason}`;
   		default: {
   			const unknown = result as { result: string };
   			return `${name}: unverified: unknown result ${unknown.result}`;
   		}
   	}
   }

   /**
    * LLR-mfzr6z: one verification result as one line. The result is org-io's;
    * this only words it. A removed, behind, inconsistent or unverified result
    * is never worded as in step or adopted, and a result this view does not
    * know is shown as unverified (HAZ-9fmhm4). A behind line does not depend
    * on its `requests` report (LLR-zkpsw5). A result carrying a `write` label
    * is its result's line followed by the write's settlement; the label never
    * changes how the result itself is worded.
    */
   export function verificationLine(result: VerificationEntryDto): string {
   	const line = resultLine(result);
   	return result.write ? `${line}; ${WRITE_WORDS[result.write]}` : line;
   }

   /** LLR-njb6mr: an Organisation's last verification as the list shows it. */
   export function verificationLabel(verification: VerificationDto): string {
   	switch (verification.status) {
   		case 'in_step':
   			return 'in step';
   		case 'adopted':
   			return 'adopted';
   		case 'removed':
   			return 'removed';
   		case 'behind':
   			return `behind (chain at epoch ${verification.chain_epoch})`;
   		case 'inconsistent':
   			return `inconsistent: ${verification.reason}`;
   		case 'unverified':
   			return `unverified: ${verification.reason}`;
   		default:
   			return 'not checked';
   	}
   }

   /**
    * LLR-84cxpt: the list of results the view shows, newest first. The
    * entries `verifyOrganisations` returned and a `verification-result`
    * event's entry are filed the same way.
    */
   export function fileVerificationResults(
   	list: VerificationEntryDto[],
   	entries: VerificationEntryDto[]
   ): VerificationEntryDto[] {
   	return [...entries, ...list];
   }

   /**
    * LLR-rhc555 (amended 2026-10-22): the founders whose founding the view
    * offers to write to the chain, each once: those `proposed` (the `founder`
    * of `proposeFoundingOrganisation`'s result, LLR-6ff735) first, then those
    * the filed results' founding entries carry (LLR-jf63e4), newest first, so
    * a restarted app finds every held founding in its first verification. A
    * founder whose newest entry is `adopted` or `in_step` is written and is
    * not offered.
    */
   export function foundingWrites(results: VerificationEntryDto[], proposed: string[]): string[] {
   	const founders = [...proposed, ...results.flatMap((entry) => (entry.founder ? [entry.founder] : []))];
   	return [...new Set(founders)].filter((founder) => {
   		const newest = results.find((entry) => entry.founder === founder);
   		return newest === undefined || (newest.result !== 'adopted' && newest.result !== 'in_step');
   	});
   }
   ```

   ```svelte
   	/** LLR-84cxpt: every verification result shown, newest first. */

   		let torndown = false;

   		subscribeAll([[onVerificationResult, (entry: VerificationEntryDto) => fileResults([entry])]]).then((fn) => {
   ```

   3e. `app/src/lib/founding.ts` (new), full content:
   ```ts
   import { proposePerson, proposeFoundingOrganisation, type PersonDto, type ProposedFoundingDto } from './api';

   /**
    * How org-io's refusal of a second Person begins (`CreateError::PersonAlreadyHeld`,
    * T29: "a Person is held already (<device key>); nothing created"). The
    * command passes org-io's text unchanged (T46's `field_refusal`).
    */
   export const PERSON_ALREADY_HELD = 'a Person is held already';

   /** What the creation form takes. */
   export interface FoundingForm {
   	name: string;
   	surname: string;
   	handle: string;
   	orgName: string;
   }

   /** What the creation form proposed: the Person (`null` when one was held already) and the founding. */
   export interface FoundingProposals {
   	person: PersonDto | null;
   	founding: ProposedFoundingDto;
   }

   /**
    * LLR-6ff735, LLR-rhc555: the creation form's proposals. The Person is
    * proposed first (LLR-k57uqv). org-io holds one Person per device and
    * refuses a second; that refusal alone is passed over, because the Person
    * it names is the one the form needs. Any other refusal is returned as
    * org-io words it, naming the field, and no founding is proposed. Then the
    * founding is proposed; its `founder` is the Device key the founding's
    * "Write to chain" takes. Nothing is written to the chain here.
    */
   export async function proposeFounding(form: FoundingForm): Promise<FoundingProposals> {
   	let person: PersonDto | null = null;
   	try {
   		person = await proposePerson(form.name, form.surname);
   	} catch (refusal) {
   		if (!String(refusal).startsWith(PERSON_ALREADY_HELD)) throw refusal;
   	}
   	const founding = await proposeFoundingOrganisation(form.name, form.surname, form.handle, form.orgName);
   	return { person, founding };
   }
   ```

   ```ts
   /**
    * SDD-xg4nj7: the frontend decisions behind what the Admin and the invitee
    * are shown about admissions and sends. Pure functions; the components
    * render what they return.
    */
   import type { AdmissionRequestedPayload, AdmissionRequestOutcome } from './api';

   /** LLR-47zvjn: one kept admission request as the Admin is shown it. */
   export interface AdmissionConfirmation extends AdmissionRequestedPayload {
   	/** The typed invitee name differs from the request's name and surname. */
   	mismatch: boolean;
   }

   /**
    * LLR-47zvjn: the invitee name typed for the Invite beside the request's
    * name, surname and Device key in full; a mismatch when the trimmed,
    * case-folded invitee name differs from the name and surname joined by one
    * space (case-folded).
    */
   export function admissionConfirmation(request: AdmissionRequestedPayload): AdmissionConfirmation {
   	const typed = request.invitee_name.trim().toLowerCase();
   	const stated = `${request.name} ${request.surname}`.toLowerCase();
   	return { ...request, preferred_handles: [...request.preferred_handles], mismatch: typed !== stated };
   }

   export type AdmissionCheck = { ok: true } | { ok: false; message: string };

   /** LLR-e63yrs: refuses, naming what is missing, until the Admin confirmed the request shown. */
   export function admissionGate(input: { request: AdmissionConfirmation | null; confirmed: boolean }): AdmissionCheck {
   	if (input.request === null) {
   		return { ok: false, message: 'Choose the admission request to admit.' };
   	}
   	if (!input.confirmed) {
   		return { ok: false, message: 'Confirm that this request is from the person you invited before admitting.' };
   	}
   	return { ok: true };
   }

   /**
    * LLR-dhtec7: the Admin's admission requests, one confirmation per
    * `org_id` and `invite_id`. A request both listed and announced, in either
    * order, is shown once; a later one with the same pair replaces the
    * earlier in its place; a new pair is added at the end.
    */
   export function fileAdmissionRequests(
   	shown: AdmissionConfirmation[],
   	requests: AdmissionRequestedPayload[]
   ): AdmissionConfirmation[] {
   	const next = [...shown];
   	for (const request of requests) {
   		const confirmation = admissionConfirmation(request);
   		const at = next.findIndex((c) => c.org_id === request.org_id && c.invite_id === request.invite_id);
   		if (at === -1) next.push(confirmation);
   		else next[at] = confirmation;
   	}
   	return next;
   }

   export interface RequestMessage {
   	severity: 'error';
   	text: string;
   }

   /** LLR-d8998k: an error for an invite another Device used; nothing for any other outcome. */
   export function admissionRequestMessage(outcome: AdmissionRequestOutcome): RequestMessage | null {
   	if (outcome.result === 'invite_used_by_another_device') {
   		return {
   			severity: 'error',
   			text: 'Another Device already used this invite. Contact the person who invited you for a new one.'
   		};
   	}
   	return null;
   }
   ```

   ```svelte
   <script lang="ts">
   	/**
   	 * Story 3: Admit a member (SDD-xg4nj7; markup SDD-6g3wnh's). The kept
   	 * admission requests, listed at start and announced on arrival, each shown
   	 * beside the invitee name typed for its Invite (LLR-47zvjn). The Admin
   	 * chooses one, may choose a Handle (blank: org-io takes the first preferred
   	 * Handle free), confirms, and proposes the admission (LLR-e63yrs): it is
   	 * recorded as a provisional change, written with the next epoch.
   	 */
   	import { proposeAdmission } from '$lib/api';
   	import { admissionGate, type AdmissionConfirmation } from '$lib/notices';

   	interface Props {
   		notifyReload?: () => void;
   		/** LLR-dhtec7: one confirmation per org id and invite id. */
   		requests?: AdmissionConfirmation[];
   	}
   	let { notifyReload, requests = [] }: Props = $props();

   	let selectedKey = $state('');
   	let handle = $state('');
   	let confirmed = $state(false);
   	let admitBusy = $state(false);
   	let admitErr = $state('');
   	let proposed = $state(false);

   	function keyOf(c: AdmissionConfirmation): string {
   		return `${c.org_id}/${c.invite_id}`;
   	}

   	let selected = $derived(requests.find((c) => keyOf(c) === selectedKey) ?? null);
   	let gate = $derived(admissionGate({ request: selected, confirmed }));

   	function choose(key: string) {
   		selectedKey = key;
   		confirmed = false;
   		admitErr = '';
   		proposed = false;
   	}

   	async function doAdmit() {
   		if (!gate.ok) {
   			admitErr = gate.message;
   			return;
   		}
   		if (selected === null) return;
   		admitBusy = true;
   		admitErr = '';
   		try {
   			await proposeAdmission(selected.org_id, selected.invite_id, handle.trim(), true);
   			proposed = true;
   			notifyReload?.();
   		} catch (e) {
   			admitErr = String(e);
   		} finally {
   			admitBusy = false;
   		}
   	}
   </script>
   ```

   ```ts
   /** LLR-k5rf3r: one discarded change of an adopted epoch, kept until dismissed. */
   export interface DiscardedNotice {
   	id: string;
   	org_id: string;
   	epoch: number;
   	change: DiscardedChangeDto;
   	text: string;
   }

   function discardedText(orgId: string, epoch: number, change: DiscardedChangeDto): string {
   	const where = `epoch ${epoch} of …${orgId.slice(-12)}`;
   	if (change.kind === 'admission') {
   		const who = [change.name, change.surname].filter((part) => part !== null).join(' ') || 'the invitee';
   		return `The admission of ${who} (Handle ${change.handle}) was left out of ${where}.`;
   	}
   	const member = change.handle === null ? change.member_id : `${change.handle} (${change.member_id})`;
   	return `The revocation of Member ${member} was left out of ${where}.`;
   }

   /**
    * LLR-k5rf3r: one notice per `discarded` change of an `adopted` result,
    * naming the Member and the kind of change, added after those kept. No
    * count limit drops one, and no later result removes one. An adopted entry
    * names its Organisation (only a founding with no proxy has none).
    */
   export function applyDiscarded(notices: DiscardedNotice[], entry: VerificationEntryDto): DiscardedNotice[] {
   	if (entry.result !== 'adopted' || entry.org_id === null) return notices;
   	const orgId = entry.org_id;
   	const added = entry.discarded.map((change, index) => ({
   		id: `${orgId}/${entry.epoch}/${index}`,
   		org_id: orgId,
   		epoch: entry.epoch,
   		change,
   		text: discardedText(orgId, entry.epoch, change)
   	}));
   	return [...notices, ...added];
   }

   /** LLR-k5rf3r: removes that one notice, and only it. */
   export function dismissNotice(notices: DiscardedNotice[], id: string): DiscardedNotice[] {
   	return notices.filter((n) => n.id !== id);
   }

   export type AdmissionReproposal = { command: 'propose_admission'; org_id: string; invite_id: string; handle: string };
   export type RevocationReproposal = { command: 'propose_revocation'; org_id: string; member_id: string };
   export type Reproposal = AdmissionReproposal | RevocationReproposal;

   /** LLR-md6hhz: the command that proposes the notice's change again; the notice is not touched. */
   export function reproposal(notice: DiscardedNotice): Reproposal {
   	return notice.change.kind === 'admission'
   		? { command: 'propose_admission', org_id: notice.org_id, invite_id: notice.change.invite_id, handle: notice.change.handle }
   		: { command: 'propose_revocation', org_id: notice.org_id, member_id: notice.change.member_id };
   }

   /** What "Propose again" does first (LLR-md6hhz as amended 2026-10-22, LLR-e63yrs). */
   export type ReproposalStep =
   	| { step: 'confirm'; confirmation: AdmissionConfirmation; reproposal: AdmissionReproposal }
   	| { step: 'propose'; reproposal: RevocationReproposal }
   	| { step: 'unavailable'; message: string };

   /**
    * LLR-md6hhz, LLR-e63yrs: an admission is proposed again only through the
    * REQ-88npkt confirmation, beside the kept request for its Organisation
    * and invite (the confirmation the Admin was first shown); with no such
    * request kept nothing can be confirmed, so nothing is proposed. A
    * revocation has no confirmation to repeat. The notice is not touched.
    */
   export function reproposalStep(notice: DiscardedNotice, requests: AdmissionConfirmation[]): ReproposalStep {
   	const again = reproposal(notice);
   	if (again.command === 'propose_revocation') return { step: 'propose', reproposal: again };
   	const confirmation = requests.find((c) => c.org_id === again.org_id && c.invite_id === again.invite_id);
   	if (confirmation === undefined) {
   		return {
   			step: 'unavailable',
   			message: 'The admission request for this invite is no longer kept, so it cannot be confirmed again.'
   		};
   	}
   	return { step: 'confirm', confirmation, reproposal: again };
   }

   /** LLR-fsk4g2: every Device's outcome of the single send, in the report's order; report only, no action. */
   export function sendOutcomes(entry: VerificationEntryDto): DeviceOutcomeDto[] {
   	return entry.result === 'adopted' && entry.sends ? [...entry.sends] : [];
   }
   ```

   ```ts
   	/** LLR-k5rf3r: notices for discarded changes, kept until dismissed. */
   	let notices = $state<DiscardedNotice[]>([]);
   	/** LLR-fsk4g2: each Device's outcome of the last own adoption's send. */
   	let lastSends = $state<{ org_id: string; outcomes: DeviceOutcomeDto[] } | null>(null);
   	let reproposeErr = $state('');
   	/** LLR-md6hhz, LLR-e63yrs: the admission being proposed again, awaiting the Admin's confirmation. */
   	let confirming = $state<{ notice: DiscardedNotice; confirmation: AdmissionConfirmation; again: AdmissionReproposal } | null>(
   		null
   	);
   	let confirmedAgain = $state(false);
   	let gateAgain = $derived(admissionGate({ request: confirming?.confirmation ?? null, confirmed: confirmedAgain }));

   	function recordVerification(entry: VerificationEntryDto) {
   		notices = applyDiscarded(notices, entry);
   		if (entry.result === 'adopted' && entry.sends && entry.org_id !== null) {
   			lastSends = { org_id: entry.org_id, outcomes: sendOutcomes(entry) };
   		}
   	}

   	/**
   	 * LLR-md6hhz: "Propose again". An admission opens the REQ-88npkt
   	 * confirmation (LLR-e63yrs) and proposes nothing yet; a revocation is
   	 * proposed again at once. The notice stays until dismissed.
   	 */
   	async function proposeAgain(notice: DiscardedNotice) {
   		reproposeErr = '';
   		const step = reproposalStep(notice, requests);
   		if (step.step === 'unavailable') {
   			reproposeErr = step.message;
   			return;
   		}
   		if (step.step === 'confirm') {
   			confirming = { notice, confirmation: step.confirmation, again: step.reproposal };
   			confirmedAgain = false;
   			return;
   		}
   		try {
   			await proposeRevocation(step.reproposal.org_id, step.reproposal.member_id);
   			notifyReload?.();
   		} catch (e) {
   			reproposeErr = String(e);
   		}
   	}

   	/** LLR-e63yrs: the admission is proposed again, with confirmed true, only once the Admin confirmed. */
   	async function confirmProposeAgain() {
   		if (confirming === null) return;
   		if (!gateAgain.ok) {
   			reproposeErr = gateAgain.message;
   			return;
   		}
   		const again = confirming.again;
   		try {
   			await proposeAdmission(again.org_id, again.invite_id, again.handle, true);
   			confirming = null;
   			confirmedAgain = false;
   			reproposeErr = '';
   			notifyReload?.();
   		} catch (e) {
   			reproposeErr = String(e);
   		}
   	}

   	/** Closing the confirmation proposes nothing; the notice stays. */
   	function cancelProposeAgain() {
   		confirming = null;
   		confirmedAgain = false;
   	}
   ```

   3a. `app/src/lib/invite.ts`, full new content (`REPLY_WARNING`, `unboundPersonas`, `ReplyCheck` and `replyGate` are deleted):
   ```ts
   /**
    * REQ-2yh3c8 (LLR-qcg6bz, LLR-prh433): what a provisional Member is told
    * before its first admission request, and the decision that gates sending
    * it. There is no Persona to choose: each Member proposal is its own new
    * Persona (org-io's Persona per proposal).
    */

   export const ADMISSION_REQUEST_WARNING =
   	'Nothing has verified who sent this Invite, or the Organisation name it states. ' +
   	'Your admission request will reveal the name, surname and preferred Handles you entered to the Device the Invite names.';

   export type RequestCheck = { ok: true } | { ok: false; message: string };

   /**
    * LLR-qcg6bz: refuses, naming the missing confirmation, until the user
    * confirms the first request. LLR-prh433: a request for a provisional
    * Member whose earlier request the user confirmed is allowed with no
    * confirmation asked again.
    */
   export function admissionRequestGate(input: { confirmedBefore: boolean; confirmed: boolean }): RequestCheck {
   	if (input.confirmedBefore || input.confirmed) {
   		return { ok: true };
   	}
   	return { ok: false, message: 'Read the warning and confirm before requesting admission.' };
   }
   ```

   3b. `app/src/lib/revoke.ts`, full new content:
   ```ts
   export interface RevokeInput {
   	memberIdHex: string;
   }

   export type RevokeCheck = { ok: true } | { ok: false; message: string };

   /**
    * REQ-he8ejb (LLR-csbs5v). Whether a revocation may be proposed, decided
    * from the member identifier alone: 64 hexadecimal characters after one
    * optional `0x`, surrounding whitespace trimmed. No peer address is asked
    * in any mode (REQ-vgr7s2 retired 2026-10-20; org-io holds each Device's
    * addresses).
    */
   export function validateRevokeInput(input: RevokeInput): RevokeCheck {
   	const memberId = input.memberIdHex.trim().replace(/^0x/, '');
   	if (memberId.length !== 64) {
   		return { ok: false, message: `Member ID must be 64 hex characters, got ${memberId.length}.` };
   	}
   	if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]+$/.test(memberId)) {
   		return { ok: false, message: 'Member ID must be hexadecimal.' };
   	}
   	return { ok: true };
   }
   ```

   ```ts
   /** LLR-b7ywy4: an Invite's public fields; nothing is stored. */
   export interface InviteSummaryDto {
   	org_name: string;
   	org_id: string; // 40 hex chars
   	invitee_name: string;
   	issuer_device_key: string; // 64 hex chars
   }

   /** LLR-rg9vc7: the new Persona a Member proposal created. */
   export interface ProposedPersonaDto {
   	persona_id: string;
   	status: string;
   }

   /** LLR-8cz828: org-io's outcome of an admission request, tagged by `result`. */
   export type AdmissionRequestOutcome =
   	| { result: 'delivered' }
   	| { result: 'already_received' }
   	| { result: 'invite_used_by_another_device' }
   	| { result: 'refused' }
   	| { result: 'not_delivered'; reason: string };

   /** LLR-y3zykm: an Invite for this Organisation; no Organisation name and no address are passed. */
   export function issueInvite(orgId: string, inviteeName: string): Promise<string> {
   	return invoke<string>('issue_invite', { orgId, inviteeName });
   }

   /** LLR-b7ywy4: read an Invite Blob; a field that does not parse is named. */
   export function readInvite(blob: string): Promise<InviteSummaryDto> {
   	return invoke<InviteSummaryDto>('read_invite', { blob });
   }

   /** LLR-rg9vc7: a new Persona proposed as a Member from an Invite; sends nothing. */
   export function proposeMember(
   	blob: string,
   	name: string,
   	surname: string,
   	preferredHandles: string[]
   ): Promise<ProposedPersonaDto> {
   	return invoke<ProposedPersonaDto>('propose_member', { inviteBlob: blob, name, surname, preferredHandles });
   }

   /** LLR-q2k9z8: the provisional Member's admission request, only with `confirmed` true. */
   export function requestAdmission(personaId: string, confirmed: boolean): Promise<AdmissionRequestOutcome> {
   	return invoke<AdmissionRequestOutcome>('request_admission', { personaId, confirmed });
   }

   /** LLR-7n4hgr: record a revocation as a provisional change; no peer address. */
   export function proposeRevocation(orgId: string, memberId: string): Promise<void> {
   	return invoke<void>('propose_revocation', { orgId, memberId });
   }
   ```

   3d. `app/src/lib/components/Invite.svelte`, full new content (SDD-6g3wnh's markup over SDD-ckqyh3's decision):
   ```svelte
   <script lang="ts">
   	/**
   	 * Story 2: Invite flow (two sides).
   	 * A (Admin):   issue_invite (LLR-y3zykm) → show/copy the Invite Blob.
   	 * B (Invitee): paste an Invite → read_invite (LLR-b7ywy4) → name, surname
   	 *              and preferred Handles → propose_member (a new Persona,
   	 *              LLR-rg9vc7) → read ADMISSION_REQUEST_WARNING and confirm
   	 *              (LLR-qcg6bz) → request_admission. A retry of a confirmed
   	 *              request asks nothing again (LLR-prh433).
   	 */
   	import {
   		listOrgs,
   		issueInvite,
   		readInvite,
   		proposeMember,
   		requestAdmission,
   		type OrgDto,
   		type InviteSummaryDto,
   		type AdmissionRequestOutcome
   	} from '$lib/api';
   	import { ADMISSION_REQUEST_WARNING, admissionRequestGate } from '$lib/invite';

   	interface Props {
   		notifyReload?: () => void;
   	}
   	let { notifyReload }: Props = $props();

   	// --- Side A: issue an Invite ---
   	let orgs = $state<OrgDto[]>([]);
   	let selectedOrgId = $state('');
   	let inviteeName = $state('');
   	let inviteBlob = $state('');
   	let issueBusy = $state(false);
   	let issueErr = $state('');

   	async function loadOrgs() {
   		try {
   			orgs = await listOrgs();
   			if (orgs.length > 0 && !selectedOrgId) selectedOrgId = orgs[0].org_id;
   		} catch (e) {
   			issueErr = String(e);
   		}
   	}

   	$effect(() => {
   		loadOrgs();
   	});

   	async function doIssueInvite() {
   		if (!selectedOrgId) {
   			issueErr = 'Select an org.';
   			return;
   		}
   		issueBusy = true;
   		issueErr = '';
   		try {
   			inviteBlob = await issueInvite(selectedOrgId, inviteeName.trim());
   		} catch (e) {
   			issueErr = String(e);
   		} finally {
   			issueBusy = false;
   		}
   	}

   	// --- Side B: read the Invite → propose a Member → confirm → request admission ---
   	let pastedInvite = $state('');
   	let read = $state<InviteSummaryDto | null>(null);
   	let readBusy = $state(false);
   	let readErr = $state('');

   	let name = $state('');
   	let surname = $state('');
   	let handles = $state('');
   	let personaId = $state('');
   	let proposeBusy = $state(false);
   	let proposeErr = $state('');

   	/** LLR-prh433: the provisional Members whose request the user confirmed. */
   	let confirmedPersonas = $state<string[]>([]);
   	let confirmed = $state(false);
   	let confirmedBefore = $derived(personaId !== '' && confirmedPersonas.includes(personaId));
   	let gate = $derived(admissionRequestGate({ confirmedBefore, confirmed }));
   	let requestBusy = $state(false);
   	let requestErr = $state('');
   	let outcome = $state<AdmissionRequestOutcome | null>(null);

   	async function doReadInvite() {
   		if (!pastedInvite.trim()) {
   			readErr = 'Paste an Invite first.';
   			return;
   		}
   		readBusy = true;
   		readErr = '';
   		read = null;
   		personaId = '';
   		confirmed = false;
   		outcome = null;
   		try {
   			read = await readInvite(pastedInvite.trim());
   		} catch (e) {
   			readErr = String(e);
   		} finally {
   			readBusy = false;
   		}
   	}

   	async function doProposeMember() {
   		const preferred = handles
   			.split(',')
   			.map((h) => h.trim())
   			.filter((h) => h !== '');
   		proposeBusy = true;
   		proposeErr = '';
   		try {
   			personaId = (await proposeMember(pastedInvite.trim(), name.trim(), surname.trim(), preferred)).persona_id;
   			notifyReload?.();
   		} catch (e) {
   			proposeErr = String(e);
   		} finally {
   			proposeBusy = false;
   		}
   	}

   	async function doRequestAdmission() {
   		if (!gate.ok) {
   			requestErr = gate.message;
   			return;
   		}
   		requestBusy = true;
   		requestErr = '';
   		try {
   			outcome = await requestAdmission(personaId, true);
   			if (!confirmedPersonas.includes(personaId)) confirmedPersonas = [...confirmedPersonas, personaId];
   		} catch (e) {
   			requestErr = String(e);
   		} finally {
   			requestBusy = false;
   		}
   	}

   	function outcomeText(o: AdmissionRequestOutcome): string {
   		switch (o.result) {
   			case 'delivered':
   				return 'Delivered: the Admin will see your request.';
   			case 'already_received':
   				return 'The Admin already has this request.';
   			case 'invite_used_by_another_device':
   				return 'Another Device already used this invite.';
   			case 'refused':
   				return 'The receiving Device refused the request.';
   			case 'not_delivered':
   				return `Not delivered: ${o.reason}`;
   		}
   	}

   	function copy(text: string) {
   		navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
   	}
   </script>

   <section class="panel">
   	<h2>Story 2: Invite Flow</h2>

   	<div class="two-col">
   		<div class="side">
   			<h3>A — Issue Invite (Admin)</h3>
   			{#if orgs.length === 0}
   				<p class="muted">No orgs yet (create one in Story 1).</p>
   			{:else}
   				<label>
   					Org
   					<select bind:value={selectedOrgId}>
   						{#each orgs as o (o.org_id)}
   							<option value={o.org_id}>…{o.org_id.slice(-12)} (epoch {o.epoch})</option>
   						{/each}
   					</select>
   				</label>
   				<label>
   					Invitee's full name
   					<input type="text" bind:value={inviteeName} placeholder="Bob Builder" disabled={issueBusy} />
   				</label>
   				<button onclick={doIssueInvite} disabled={issueBusy}>{issueBusy ? 'Issuing…' : 'Issue Invite'}</button>
   				{#if issueErr}<p class="err">{issueErr}</p>{/if}
   				{#if inviteBlob}
   					<label>
   						Invite (copy to the invitee)
   						<textarea readonly rows="4" value={inviteBlob}></textarea>
   					</label>
   					<button onclick={() => copy(inviteBlob)}>Copy</button>
   				{/if}
   			{/if}
   		</div>

   		<div class="side">
   			<h3>B — Read Invite + Request Admission (Invitee)</h3>
   			<label>
   				Paste Invite
   				<textarea rows="4" bind:value={pastedInvite} placeholder="Paste the Invite here…"></textarea>
   			</label>
   			<button onclick={doReadInvite} disabled={readBusy}>{readBusy ? 'Reading…' : 'Read Invite'}</button>
   			{#if readErr}<p class="err">{readErr}</p>{/if}
   			{#if read}
   				<dl>
   					<dt>Organisation name</dt>
   					<dd>{read.org_name} <span class="warn">(stated by the sender, unverified)</span></dd>
   					<dt>Org id</dt><dd class="mono">{read.org_id}</dd>
   					<dt>Invitee name</dt><dd>{read.invitee_name}</dd>
   					<dt>Issued by Device</dt><dd class="mono">{read.issuer_device_key}</dd>
   				</dl>
   				{#if personaId === ''}
   					<label>Name <input type="text" bind:value={name} disabled={proposeBusy} /></label>
   					<label>Surname <input type="text" bind:value={surname} disabled={proposeBusy} /></label>
   					<label>Preferred Handles (1 to 3, comma-separated) <input type="text" bind:value={handles} placeholder="bob, builder" disabled={proposeBusy} /></label>
   					<button onclick={doProposeMember} disabled={proposeBusy}>{proposeBusy ? 'Proposing…' : 'Propose Member'}</button>
   					{#if proposeErr}<p class="err">{proposeErr}</p>{/if}
   				{:else}
   					{#if !confirmedBefore}
   						<div class="warning-box" role="alert">
   							<p>{ADMISSION_REQUEST_WARNING}</p>
   							<label class="confirm">
   								<input type="checkbox" bind:checked={confirmed} disabled={requestBusy} />
   								I understand
   							</label>
   						</div>
   					{/if}
   					<button onclick={doRequestAdmission} disabled={requestBusy || !gate.ok}>
   						{requestBusy ? 'Requesting…' : confirmedBefore ? 'Request admission again' : 'Request admission'}
   					</button>
   					{#if !gate.ok}<p class="muted">{gate.message}</p>{/if}
   					{#if requestErr}<p class="err">{requestErr}</p>{/if}
   					{#if outcome}<p class="small">{outcomeText(outcome)}</p>{/if}
   				{/if}
   			{/if}
   		</div>
   	</div>
   </section>
   ```

   `org-node/tests/admission_sender.rs`: four new tests replace the cut `a_second_organisation_is_admitted_into_without_touching_the_first`, `the_proxy_account_from_genesis_is_kept_and_handed_back`, `member_ids_are_not_derived_from_keys` and `readmission_with_same_keys_gets_a_fresh_member_id` (the last two keep their names).
   ```rust
   // LLR-exaa9u, LLR-f9x3vf (design gap G2; rewrites
   // `a_second_organisation_is_admitted_into_without_touching_the_first`): a
   // Persona is Proposed until the first adoption in its own store sets it
   // Active (the founding's for a founder, a first admission's for a
   // provisional Member); its Organisation is the one it was given and does
   // not change; and an operation on one store of the service changes no
   // other store. Two stores with one Device key are refused, and an unknown
   // Device key names no store.
   // verifies: LLR-exaa9u, LLR-f9x3vf
   #[test]
   fn the_first_adoption_marks_its_persona_active_and_changes_no_other_store() {
       use org_node::error::OrgNodeError;
       use org_node::verify_org::Verified;
       use org_node::store::PersonaStatus;
       use org_node::{OrgId, OrgService, SigningKeypair};
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       // A founder: Proposed, bound once its proxy is recorded, Active at the
       // founding's adoption.
       let mut a = sweep::found();
       let persona = &sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).persona;
       assert_eq!((persona.status, persona.org_id), (PersonaStatus::Proposed, Some(sweep::the_org())));
       let chain = sweep::founding_state(&a);
       let adopted = sweep::adopt(&mut a, chain);
       assert!(matches!(adopted, Verified::Adopted { own: true, .. }), "{adopted:?}");
       let persona = &sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).persona;
       assert_eq!((persona.status, persona.org_id), (PersonaStatus::Active, Some(sweep::the_org())));

       // A provisional Member of a second Organisation, its store held by
       // the same service as A's founded store.
       let other = OrgId::new([0x0b; 20]);
       let (mut c, _) = sweep::founded_at(other);
       let pending = sweep::admission(&mut c, "Bea", "bea");
       let mut both = OrgService::new(vec![a.reopened_store(), pending.member.clone_store()]).unwrap();
       let bea = pending.member.device;
       assert_eq!(sweep::data(&both, &bea).persona.status, PersonaStatus::Proposed);
       assert_eq!(sweep::data(&both, &bea).persona.org_id, Some(other));
       let a_before = sweep::bytes_of(&both, &a.device);

       // Bea's first adoption, in the shared service: Bea is Active and bound
       // to the Organisation she was given; A's store is byte-for-byte as it was.
       let (checked, change) = both.check_received(&mut OsRng, &bea, c.device, &pending.body).unwrap();
       assert!(matches!(checked, org_node::service::Checked::ProvisionalOrganisationKept { .. }), "{checked:?}");
       assert!(change.is_some(), "the kept provisional organisation is sealed");
       let (verified, change) = both.verify(&mut OsRng, &bea, Some(pending.chain), sweep::at(), sweep::no_secrets).unwrap();
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Adopted { own: false, .. }), "{verified:?}");
       assert!(change.is_some(), "the first adoption is sealed");
       let persona = &sweep::data(&both, &bea).persona;
       assert_eq!((persona.status, persona.org_id), (PersonaStatus::Active, Some(other)));
       assert_eq!(sweep::bytes_of(&both, &a.device), a_before, "A's store is unchanged by Bea's adoption");
       let persona_a = &sweep::data(&both, &a.device).persona;
       assert_eq!((persona_a.status, persona_a.org_id), (PersonaStatus::Active, Some(sweep::the_org())), "never rebound");

       // LLR-f9x3vf: two stores with one Device key, and an unknown key.
       let duplicate = OrgService::new(vec![c.reopened_store(), c.clone_store()]);
       assert!(matches!(duplicate, Err(OrgNodeError::DuplicatePersonaStore { .. })), "{:?}", duplicate.err());
       let unknown = SigningKeypair::generate(&mut OsRng).device_key().unwrap();
       let refused = both.propose_updated_organisation(&mut OsRng, &unknown);
       assert!(matches!(refused, Err(OrgNodeError::PersonaNotHeld { .. })), "{:?}", refused.err());
   }

   // LLR-x5asbx (design gap G2; rewrites
   // `the_proxy_account_from_genesis_is_kept_and_handed_back`): the proxy
   // account `record_founding_proxy` is given is held in the provisional
   // founding, becomes the record's at the founding's adoption, never
   // reaches the disk in clear, is handed back unchanged by `proxy_account`,
   // and no admission, revocation, proposal or later adoption changes it; a
   // record a first admission created holds none.
   // verifies: LLR-x5asbx
   #[test]
   fn the_proxy_account_recorded_for_a_founding_is_kept_and_handed_back() {
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       let mut a = sweep::found();
       let founding = sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).founding.as_ref().expect("a provisional founding");
       assert_eq!(founding.proxy, Some(sweep::the_proxy()), "held in the provisional founding");
       let sealed = a.last.as_ref().unwrap().sealed.as_bytes().to_vec();
       assert!(!sweep::contains(&sealed, sweep::the_proxy().as_bytes()), "never on disk in clear");

       let chain = sweep::founding_state(&a);
       sweep::adopt(&mut a, chain);
       assert_eq!(sweep::record_of(&a).proxy_account, Some(sweep::the_proxy()), "the record's from the adoption");
       assert_eq!(a.svc.proxy_account(sweep::the_org()).unwrap(), Some(sweep::the_proxy()));

       let mut bob = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       assert_eq!(a.svc.proxy_account(sweep::the_org()).unwrap(), Some(sweep::the_proxy()), "an admission leaves it");
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut bob.member, a.device, &bob.body, bob.chain);
       assert_eq!(bob.member.svc.proxy_account(sweep::the_org()).unwrap(), None, "a first admission's record holds none");

       let b_id = sweep::member_id_of(&bob.member);
       let change = a.svc.record_revocation(&mut OsRng, &a.device, b_id).unwrap();
       a.keep(change);
       assert_eq!(a.svc.proxy_account(sweep::the_org()).unwrap(), Some(sweep::the_proxy()), "a recorded revocation leaves it");
       let next = sweep::propose_next(&mut a);
       assert_eq!(a.svc.proxy_account(sweep::the_org()).unwrap(), Some(sweep::the_proxy()), "a proposal leaves it");
       sweep::adopt(&mut a, next);
       assert_eq!(sweep::record_of(&a).proxy_account, Some(sweep::the_proxy()), "an adoption that replaces the record keeps it");

       let sealed = a.last.as_ref().unwrap().sealed.as_bytes().to_vec();
       assert!(!sweep::contains(&sealed, sweep::the_proxy().as_bytes()), "still never in clear");
       let reopened = a.reopened();
       assert_eq!(reopened.proxy_account(sweep::the_org()).unwrap(), Some(sweep::the_proxy()), "and read back from the sealed store");
   }

   // Normal case of REQ-d9g6nt (ported over the new operations, design gap
   // G2; LLR-ag9mgm -> LLR-4rv4kr): the founder's MemberId and an admitted
   // Member's are drawn, not computed from a key, and differ from each other;
   // two foundings with the same details give two founders two identifiers
   // (LLR-rjg3m2).
   // verifies: REQ-d9g6nt, LLR-4rv4kr, LLR-rjg3m2
   #[test]
   fn member_ids_are_not_derived_from_keys() {
       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let founder = sweep::record_of(&a).trie_members[0].clone();
       assert_eq!(sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).persona.member_id, Some(founder.id));
       assert_ne!(founder.id.as_bytes(), founder.member_key.as_bytes(), "the founder's id is its member key");
       assert_ne!(founder.id.as_bytes(), founder.device_keys[0].as_bytes(), "the founder's id is its device key");

       let mut bob = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut bob.member, a.device, &bob.body, bob.chain);
       let admitted = sweep::record_of(&a)
           .trie_members
           .iter()
           .find(|m| m.device_keys.contains(&bob.member.device))
           .expect("Bob is in A's record")
           .clone();
       assert_ne!(admitted.id.as_bytes(), admitted.member_key.as_bytes(), "Bob's id is his member key");
       assert_ne!(admitted.id.as_bytes(), admitted.device_keys[0].as_bytes(), "Bob's id is his device key");
       assert_ne!(admitted.id, founder.id, "Bob's id equals the founder's");
       assert_eq!(sweep::member_id_of(&bob.member), admitted.id, "Bob's Persona holds the id A's record gives him");

       let first = sweep::found();
       let second = sweep::found();
       let id_of = |side: &sweep::Side| sweep::data(&side.svc, &side.device).founding.as_ref().unwrap().members[0].id;
       assert_ne!(id_of(&first), id_of(&second), "two foundings, two founder identifiers");
   }

   // Abnormal case of REQ-d9g6nt (ported, design gap G2; LLR-ag9mgm ->
   // LLR-4rv4kr): the same kept admission request, with the same
   // Member-as-a-group key and DevicePublicKey, proposed twice gets two
   // identifiers; the adopted one is later revoked; and no identifier is ever
   // issued twice across three rounds.
   // verifies: REQ-d9g6nt, LLR-4rv4kr
   #[test]
   fn readmission_with_same_keys_gets_a_fresh_member_id() {
       use org_node::MemberId;
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut issued: Vec<MemberId> = vec![sweep::record_of(&a).trie_members[0].id];
       for round in 0..3 {
           let invite = sweep::invite(&mut a, "Bob");
           let bob = sweep::propose_member(&invite, "Bob", &["bob"]);
           let member = sweep::data(&bob.svc, &bob.device).member.as_ref().unwrap();
           let (member_key, device) = (member.member_key, member.device_key);
           sweep::request_admission(&mut a, &bob);
           let change = a.svc.record_admission(&mut OsRng, &a.device, invite.invite_id, None).unwrap();
           a.keep(change);
           let first = sweep::propose_next(&mut a);
           let second = sweep::propose_next(&mut a);
           let ids = [sweep::proposed_id_of(&a, first, &device), sweep::proposed_id_of(&a, second, &device)];
           assert_ne!(ids[0], ids[1], "round {round}: the same keys proposed twice got one id");
           for id in ids {
               assert!(!issued.contains(&id), "round {round}: an id was issued again");
               assert_ne!(id.as_bytes(), member_key.as_bytes(), "round {round}: id is the member key");
               assert_ne!(id.as_bytes(), device.as_bytes(), "round {round}: id is the device key");
               issued.push(id);
           }
           sweep::adopt(&mut a, second);
           assert!(sweep::record_of(&a).trie_members.iter().any(|m| m.id == ids[1]), "round {round}: adopted under the second id");
           sweep::revocation(&mut a, ids[1]);
           assert!(!sweep::record_of(&a).trie_members.iter().any(|m| m.id == ids[1]), "round {round}: revoked");
       }
   }
   ```
   `org-node/tests/admission_sender.rs`: the G2 ports, each re-created over the new operations under the cut test's name, keeping its in-force IDs and re-pointing the superseded ones.
   ```rust
   // LLR-95av3e, LLR-j6j95z (ported, design gap G2; LLR-38e2kn ->
   // LLR-95av3e): a first admission is attempted only from Organisation
   // information. A's genuine message to provisional Member B, relabelled a
   // revocation, is refused as `OrgNotHeld` by a store holding no record,
   // with nothing kept, the expectation in place and the Persona Proposed;
   // the genuine message is then kept, its snapshot decoded, and adopted.
   // verifies: REQ-d9g6nt, REQ-vxqc5g, LLR-j6j95z, LLR-95av3e
   #[test]
   fn a_revocation_about_an_organisation_not_held_is_refused_before_the_chain() {
       use org_node::error::OrgNodeError;
       use org_node::verify_org::Verified;
       use org_node::store::PersonaStatus;
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut pending = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       let mut relabelled = pending.body.clone();
       relabelled[0] = 1; // the Revocation variant's index (LLR-xr88a8); the Organisation identifier follows unchanged
       let before = sweep::bytes_of(&pending.member.svc, &pending.member.device);
       let refused = pending.member.svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &pending.member.device, a.device, &relabelled);
       assert_eq!(refused.unwrap_err(), OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { org_id: sweep::the_org() });
       assert_eq!(sweep::bytes_of(&pending.member.svc, &pending.member.device), before, "nothing kept");
       let b = sweep::data(&pending.member.svc, &pending.member.device);
       assert!(b.record.is_none(), "no record");
       assert_eq!(b.expected_admissions.len(), 1, "the expectation is kept");
       assert_eq!(b.persona.status, PersonaStatus::Proposed);

       let verified = sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut pending.member, a.device, &pending.body, pending.chain);
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Adopted { .. }), "{verified:?}");
       assert_eq!(sweep::record_of(&pending.member).org_id, sweep::the_org());
   }

   // LLR-34c5y3, LLR-degg8t (ported, design gap G2; LLR-qg9utu -> LLR-34c5y3,
   // LLR-8hdu9x -> LLR-degg8t): A's record takes B's removal only through the
   // adoption of the provisional organisation the chain carries, and the
   // adoption reaches A's disk: one member, the chain's epoch and root, the
   // Sequence number equal to the epoch. The removed Device's message for
   // the epoch is a Revocation holding its notice and nothing else.
   // verifies: LLR-34c5y3, LLR-degg8t
   #[test]
   fn a_revocation_reaches_the_administrators_disk() {
       use org_node::wire::{decode_message, WireMessage};
       use org_node::SequenceNumber;

       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut bob = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut bob.member, a.device, &bob.body, bob.chain);
       let b_id = sweep::member_id_of(&bob.member);
       assert_eq!(sweep::record_of(&a).trie_members.len(), 2, "A and B before the revocation");

       let chain = sweep::revocation(&mut a, b_id);
       let record = sweep::record_of(&a);
       assert_eq!(record.trie_members.len(), 1, "A holds itself only");
       assert_eq!((record.epoch, record.root_hash, record.org_pub_key), (chain.epoch, chain.root_hash, chain.org_pub_key));
       assert_eq!(record.last_seq, SequenceNumber::new(chain.epoch.get()), "the mark is the adopted epoch");

       let messages = a.svc.messages_for_current_epoch(&a.device).unwrap();
       let to_b = messages.iter().find(|m| m.recipient == bob.member.device).expect("a message for the removed Device");
       let WireMessage::Revocation(notice) = decode_message(&to_b.body).unwrap() else {
           panic!("the removed Device is sent a Revocation")
       };
       assert_eq!((notice.org_id, notice.member_id, notice.device), (sweep::the_org(), b_id, bob.member.device));

       let reopened = a.reopened();
       let on_disk = sweep::data(&reopened, &a.device).record.as_ref().expect("the record on disk");
       assert_eq!(on_disk.trie_members.len(), 1, "the removal reached the disk");
       assert!(!on_disk.trie_members.iter().any(|m| m.id == b_id));
       assert_eq!((on_disk.epoch, on_disk.root_hash, on_disk.last_seq), (chain.epoch, chain.root_hash, SequenceNumber::new(chain.epoch.get())));
   }

   // LLR-34c5y3, LLR-g2jeqd (ported, design gap G2; LLR-qg9utu -> LLR-34c5y3,
   // LLR-t4znbk -> LLR-g2jeqd, ledger 84a31b1a): the messages of the adopted
   // removal are built and never delivered; the adopted removal stays in A's
   // record, in memory and on disk, and building the messages twice gives the
   // same bytes and changes nothing: whether an epoch's messages are ever sent
   // changes neither the outcome nor the store.
   // verifies: LLR-34c5y3, LLR-g2jeqd
   #[test]
   fn a_failed_revocation_send_leaves_the_committed_removal_in_place() {
       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut bob = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut bob.member, a.device, &bob.body, bob.chain);
       let b_id = sweep::member_id_of(&bob.member);
       let chain = sweep::revocation(&mut a, b_id);

       let before = sweep::bytes_of(&a.svc, &a.device);
       let first: Vec<Vec<u8>> = a.svc.messages_for_current_epoch(&a.device).unwrap().into_iter().map(|m| m.body).collect();
       assert!(!first.is_empty(), "B's revocation is built");
       drop(first); // never delivered
       let again: Vec<Vec<u8>> = a.svc.messages_for_current_epoch(&a.device).unwrap().into_iter().map(|m| m.body).collect();
       assert!(!again.is_empty());
       assert_eq!(sweep::bytes_of(&a.svc, &a.device), before, "building the messages changes nothing");
       assert!(!sweep::record_of(&a).trie_members.iter().any(|m| m.id == b_id), "the adopted removal stays");
       assert_eq!(sweep::record_of(&a).epoch, chain.epoch);
       let reopened = a.reopened();
       let on_disk = sweep::data(&reopened, &a.device).record.as_ref().unwrap();
       assert!(!on_disk.trie_members.iter().any(|m| m.id == b_id), "and on A's disk");
       assert_eq!(on_disk.epoch, chain.epoch);
   }

   // A first admission writes the chain's Organisation public key (LLR-rys5nx:
   // the key of the chain state handed to `verify`, never a value the message
   // carried), the Organisation private key the message carried, which A's
   // record holds (LLR-qw8tyu), and the Persona's member id, status and
   // Organisation (LLR-exaa9u: Active at the first adoption in its store), in
   // memory and on disk. Ported, design gap G2 (LLR-3fwykc -> LLR-qw8tyu;
   // LLR-e5c9ud -> LLR-exaa9u, ledger 84a31b1a).
   // verifies: LLR-exaa9u, LLR-rys5nx, LLR-qw8tyu
   #[test]
   fn a_first_admission_records_the_chains_key_the_private_key_and_the_member() {
       use org_node::store::PersonaStatus;

       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut bob = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut bob.member, a.device, &bob.body, bob.chain);
       let held_by_a = sweep::record_of(&a).org_private_key_for_test().clone();
       let record = sweep::record_of(&bob.member);
       assert_eq!(record.org_pub_key, bob.chain.org_pub_key, "the chain's key");
       assert_eq!(record.org_private_key_for_test().clone(), held_by_a, "the key the message carried, A's");
       assert_eq!(held_by_a.x25519_keypair().org_public_key().unwrap(), bob.chain.org_pub_key, "the private half of the chain's key");
       let member = record.trie_members.iter().find(|m| m.device_keys.contains(&bob.member.device)).expect("B's Device is listed");
       let persona = &sweep::data(&bob.member.svc, &bob.member.device).persona;
       assert_eq!(persona.member_id, Some(member.id));
       assert_eq!(persona.status, PersonaStatus::Active);
       assert_eq!(persona.org_id, Some(sweep::the_org()));

       let reopened = bob.member.reopened();
       let on_disk = sweep::data(&reopened, &bob.member.device).record.as_ref().unwrap();
       assert_eq!(on_disk.org_pub_key, bob.chain.org_pub_key);
       assert_eq!(on_disk.org_private_key_for_test().clone(), held_by_a);
   }

   // PR-szkat6 (ported, design gap G2; LLR-3fwykc -> LLR-qw8tyu): an admitted
   // Member holds the Organisation private key, the one the founder's record
   // holds and the private half of the chain's key.
   // verifies: LLR-qw8tyu, REQ-szq3ud, REQ-ju6vn2, PR-szkat6
   #[test]
   fn pr_szkat6_an_admitted_member_holds_the_organisation_private_key() {
       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut bob = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut bob.member, a.device, &bob.body, bob.chain);
       let held = sweep::record_of(&bob.member).org_private_key_for_test().clone();
       assert_eq!(held, sweep::record_of(&a).org_private_key_for_test().clone(), "the key the founder holds");
       assert_eq!(held.x25519_keypair().org_public_key().unwrap(), bob.chain.org_pub_key);
   }

   // PR-ve9zw8 (ported, design gap G2; LLR-37cj3n -> LLR-8528ud, LLR-3fwykc ->
   // LLR-qw8tyu): Organisation information whose Organisation private key a
   // relay substituted is refused from the relay (`SenderNotListed`) and,
   // from A's listed Device, kept under the public key derived from the
   // substituted key: no match for the chain, so verification reports Behind
   // and B's record and both keys stay as they were. The genuine message is
   // then kept and adopted with the chain's key. Which record is adopted is
   // decided by the chain state alone, never by the delivering Device.
   // verifies: LLR-8528ud, LLR-qw8tyu, PR-ve9zw8
   #[test]
   fn pr_ve9zw8_an_update_carrying_a_substituted_key_is_refused_on_both_paths() {
       use org_node::error::OrgNodeError;
       use org_node::service::Checked;
       use org_node::verify_org::Verified;
       use org_node::wire::{decode_message, encode_message, WireMessage};
       use org_node::OrgPrivateKey;
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut bob = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut bob.member, a.device, &bob.body, bob.chain);
       let mut b = bob.member;
       let carol = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Carol", "carol");
       let genuine = sweep::message_for(&a, &b.device);
       let WireMessage::OrgInformation { envelope, record_snapshot, .. } = decode_message(&genuine).unwrap() else {
           panic!("Organisation information")
       };
       let substituted = encode_message(&WireMessage::OrgInformation {
           envelope,
           record_snapshot,
           org_private_key: OrgPrivateKey::from([0x42u8; 32]),
       })
       .unwrap();
       let held = sweep::record_of(&b).clone();
       let before = sweep::bytes_of(&b.svc, &b.device);

       let from_relay = b.svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &b.device, sweep::relay_device(), &substituted);
       assert_eq!(from_relay.unwrap_err(), OrgNodeError::SenderNotListed { org_id: sweep::the_org() });
       assert_eq!(sweep::bytes_of(&b.svc, &b.device), before, "nothing kept from the relay");

       let checked = sweep::receive(&mut b, a.device, &substituted);
       assert!(matches!(checked, Checked::ProvisionalOrganisationKept { .. }), "{checked:?}");
       let (verified, change) = b.svc.verify(&mut OsRng, &b.device, Some(carol.chain), sweep::at(), sweep::no_secrets).unwrap();
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Behind { .. }), "no match for the chain: {verified:?}");
       assert!(change.is_none(), "Behind writes nothing");
       let after = sweep::record_of(&b);
       assert_eq!(
           (after.epoch, after.last_seq, after.root_hash, after.org_pub_key),
           (held.epoch, held.last_seq, held.root_hash, held.org_pub_key)
       );
       assert_eq!(after.org_private_key_for_test().clone(), held.org_private_key_for_test().clone());

       let verified = sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut b, a.device, &genuine, carol.chain);
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Adopted { own: false, .. }), "{verified:?}");
       assert_eq!(sweep::record_of(&b).org_pub_key, carol.chain.org_pub_key);
       assert_eq!(
           sweep::record_of(&b).org_private_key_for_test().x25519_keypair().org_public_key().unwrap(),
           carol.chain.org_pub_key
       );
   }

   // LLR-94rzrk (ported, design gap G2; LLR-xn5pwc -> LLR-94rzrk): each
   // adopted epoch gives B's record the key pair A's record holds, the
   // public half the chain's, in memory and on disk; the same message with
   // its key cut off or one byte short does not decode and is refused before
   // anything is kept.
   // verifies: LLR-94rzrk, REQ-ju6vn2
   #[test]
   fn a_committed_update_gives_the_record_the_new_key_pair_on_both_paths() {
       use org_node::error::OrgNodeError;
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut bob = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut bob.member, a.device, &bob.body, bob.chain);
       let mut b = bob.member;
       for name in ["Carol", "Dave"] {
           let next = sweep::admission(&mut a, name, &name.to_lowercase());
           let body = sweep::message_for(&a, &b.device);
           let before = sweep::bytes_of(&b.svc, &b.device);
           for cut in [body[..body.len() - 32].to_vec(), body[..body.len() - 1].to_vec()] {
               let refused = b.svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &b.device, a.device, &cut);
               assert_eq!(refused.unwrap_err(), OrgNodeError::MalformedMessage, "{name}: {} bytes", cut.len());
           }
           assert_eq!(sweep::bytes_of(&b.svc, &b.device), before, "{name}: nothing kept from the cut bodies");
           sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut b, a.device, &body, next.chain);
           let record = sweep::record_of(&b);
           assert_eq!(record.org_pub_key, next.chain.org_pub_key, "{name}");
           assert_eq!(record.org_private_key_for_test().clone(), sweep::record_of(&a).org_private_key_for_test().clone(), "{name}");
           assert_eq!(record.org_private_key_for_test().x25519_keypair().org_public_key().unwrap(), record.org_pub_key, "{name}: a pair");
       }
       let reopened = b.reopened();
       let on_disk = sweep::data(&reopened, &b.device).record.as_ref().unwrap();
       assert_eq!(on_disk.org_pub_key, sweep::record_of(&a).org_pub_key, "on disk");
       assert_eq!(on_disk.org_private_key_for_test().clone(), sweep::record_of(&a).org_private_key_for_test().clone(), "on disk");
   }

   // PR-u4c2vp (ported, design gap G2; LLR-3q63zv -> LLR-283x6f): A's genuine
   // Organisation information about C's admission, relayed to B by a Device
   // B's record does not list, is refused with `SenderNotListed` with nothing
   // kept and no change; the same body from A's listed Device is kept and
   // adopted.
   // verifies: LLR-283x6f, PR-u4c2vp
   #[test]
   fn pr_u4c2vp_an_update_relayed_by_a_non_member_is_refused_on_the_self_delete_path() {
       use org_node::error::OrgNodeError;
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut bob = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut bob.member, a.device, &bob.body, bob.chain);
       let mut b = bob.member;
       let epoch_before = sweep::record_of(&b).epoch;
       let carol = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Carol", "carol");
       let body = sweep::message_for(&a, &b.device);
       let before = sweep::bytes_of(&b.svc, &b.device);
       let refused = b.svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &b.device, sweep::relay_device(), &body);
       assert_eq!(refused.unwrap_err(), OrgNodeError::SenderNotListed { org_id: sweep::the_org() });
       assert_eq!(sweep::bytes_of(&b.svc, &b.device), before, "nothing kept");
       assert!(sweep::data(&b.svc, &b.device).provisional_organisations.is_empty());
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut b, a.device, &body, carol.chain);
       assert!(sweep::record_of(&b).epoch > epoch_before, "from A's listed Device it is adopted");
   }
   ```
