   `org_node_is_sans_io`: the body is unchanged except for its comment's last line, its annotation and the five `why` strings that named LLR-4tcxsu. Re-pointed from LLR-4tcxsu to LLR-g2jeqd: org-node binds no endpoint and sends nothing, so an adoption never waits on a send. The full function:
   ```rust
   // org-node binds no endpoint, sends and receives nothing, opens no file and
   // awaits nothing: it has no transport, no file IO, no async and no keychain
   // (S4, task T14). The transport and its preflight check are org-io's.
   // Subsumes `revocation_and_reconcile_do_no_io` for the whole crate.
   // *Strengthened 2026-10-14 (review round 1 of S4, finding-9):* a grouped
   // `use std::{fs, io}` import and an environment read (`env::var(` and its
   // kin) are caught too (`file_and_environment_reads`).
   // *2026-10-15 (S4 TEST review round 2, finding-1):* the helper is checked on
   // strings first, so a helper that misses grouped imports fails this test.
   // *Re-pointed 2026-10-22 (T60, design gap G2):* LLR-4tcxsu is superseded by
   // LLR-g2jeqd, which states the same of `verify`'s adoption.
   // verifies: LLR-g2jeqd, REQ-x3jrh8
   #[test]
   fn org_node_is_sans_io() {
       assert_the_scan_catches_grouped_file_imports_and_environment_reads();
       for (needle, why) in [
           ("iroh", "LLR-g2jeqd: the transport is org-io's"),
           ("OrgEndpoint", "LLR-g2jeqd: org-node has no endpoint"),
           ("pub mod transport", "LLR-g2jeqd: no transport module"),
           ("crate::transport", "LLR-g2jeqd: no transport module"),
           ("fn bind_endpoint", "LLR-g2jeqd: nothing binds an endpoint"),
           ("fn send_body", "LLR-g2jeqd: nothing sends"),
           ("fn receive_body", "LLR-g2jeqd: nothing receives"),
           ("std::fs", "REQ-x3jrh8: org-node opens no file"),
           ("PathBuf", "REQ-x3jrh8: org-node names no file path"),
           ("tokio", "org-node runs no runtime"),
           ("async fn", "org-node awaits nothing"),
           (".await", "org-node awaits nothing"),
           ("keyring", "org-node never touches the OS keychain (REQ-26mjqa)"),
           ("ODS_DEVICE_SEED", "no seed from the environment: the preflight left with owner ruling 7"),
           ("DeviceSeed", "the device seed is the move-only DeviceSecret"),
           ("fn check_transport", "the transport check is org-io's (owner ruling 7)"),
       ] {
           assert_absent(needle, why);
       }
       for (path, text) in sources() {
           let found = file_and_environment_reads(&text);
           assert!(found.is_empty(), "{} reads a file or the environment: {found:?} (REQ-x3jrh8)", path.display());
       }
       let dependencies = normal_dependencies();
       for crate_name in ["iroh", "tokio", "async-trait", "argon2", "keyring"] {
           assert!(!dependencies.contains(&format!("{crate_name} =")), "org-node depends on {crate_name}");
       }
       let manifest = manifest();
       for needle in ["iroh", "tokio", "transport = [", "\"transport\"", "name = \"preflight\""] {
           assert!(!manifest.contains(needle), "org-node's manifest names `{needle}` (LLR-g2jeqd: no transport, no runtime)");
       }
   }

   `org-node/tests/receive_chain_reads.rs`: three rewrites of the LLR-38e2kn tests (lines 152, 234 and 363 today), each verifying LLR-95av3e. If T5 changed the file's module docs, the new tests sit at the end of the file.
   ```rust
   // LLR-95av3e (rewrites
   // `the_self_delete_path_refuses_an_unheld_organisation_without_a_chain_read`):
   // in a store holding no record, a founding store or a provisional Member's,
   // a revocation is refused with `OrgNotHeld` before any field past its kind
   // and Organisation identifier is decoded: a body whose tail is garbage is
   // refused the same way. Nothing is kept, no record is created, the
   // expectation stays, and the call takes no chain state.
   // verifies: LLR-95av3e
   #[test]
   fn a_revocation_in_a_store_holding_no_record_is_refused_as_org_not_held() {
       use org_node::error::OrgNodeError;
       use org_node::MemberId;
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       // A founding store, its proxy recorded, not yet adopted.
       let mut founder = sweep::found();
       let unrelated = sweep::relay_device();
       let notice = sweep::notice_about(sweep::the_org(), MemberId::new([0x31; 32]), founder.device);
       let before = sweep::bytes_of(&founder.svc, &founder.device);
       let refused = founder.svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &founder.device, unrelated, &notice);
       assert_eq!(refused.unwrap_err(), OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { org_id: sweep::the_org() });
       assert_eq!(sweep::bytes_of(&founder.svc, &founder.device), before, "nothing kept in the founding store");
       assert!(sweep::data(&founder.svc, &founder.device).record.is_none(), "no record created");

       // A provisional Member's store; the notice comes from the issuer.
       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut pending = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       let b = pending.member.device;
       let notice = sweep::notice_about(sweep::the_org(), MemberId::new([0x32; 32]), b);
       let mut garbled = notice[..21].to_vec(); // the kind and the twenty-byte Organisation identifier
       garbled.extend_from_slice(&[0xff; 12]);
       let before = sweep::bytes_of(&pending.member.svc, &b);
       for body in [notice, garbled] {
           let refused = pending.member.svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &b, a.device, &body);
           assert_eq!(refused.unwrap_err(), OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { org_id: sweep::the_org() }, "{} bytes", body.len());
       }
       assert_eq!(sweep::bytes_of(&pending.member.svc, &b), before, "nothing kept in the provisional Member's store");
       let data = sweep::data(&pending.member.svc, &b);
       assert!(data.record.is_none() && data.kept_revocation_notices.is_empty());
       assert_eq!(data.expected_admissions.len(), 1, "the expectation stays");
   }

   // LLR-95av3e (rewrites `revocations_are_refused_without_writing`): in a
   // store holding a record, a revocation about another Organisation, even
   // from a Device the record lists, is refused by `check_notice` with
   // `RevocationNotHeld` naming that Organisation, keeping nothing.
   // verifies: LLR-95av3e
   #[test]
   fn a_revocation_about_another_organisation_is_refused_as_revocation_not_held_and_writes_nothing() {
       use org_node::error::OrgNodeError;
       use org_node::OrgId;
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut bob = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut bob.member, a.device, &bob.body, bob.chain);
       let mut b = bob.member;
       let b_id = sweep::member_id_of(&b);
       let elsewhere = OrgId::new([9; 20]);
       let notice = sweep::notice_about(elsewhere, b_id, b.device);
       let held = sweep::record_of(&b).clone();
       let before = sweep::bytes_of(&b.svc, &b.device);
       let refused = b.svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &b.device, a.device, &notice);
       assert_eq!(refused.unwrap_err(), OrgNodeError::RevocationNotHeld { org_id: elsewhere });
       assert_eq!(sweep::bytes_of(&b.svc, &b.device), before, "nothing written");
       assert!(sweep::data(&b.svc, &b.device).kept_revocation_notices.is_empty(), "nothing kept");
       assert_eq!((sweep::record_of(&b).epoch, sweep::record_of(&b).root_hash), (held.epoch, held.root_hash));
   }

   // LLR-95av3e, LLR-q8emds (rewrites
   // `after_an_unheld_revocation_the_expected_admission_is_still_taken`): a
   // revocation refused by a provisional Member's store leaves its expected
   // admission in place, so the first admission arriving next is kept and
   // adopted; the adoption's one sealed change clears the expectation it
   // matched (LLR-q8emds, one of T5's untested in-force items).
   // verifies: LLR-95av3e, LLR-q8emds
   #[test]
   fn after_a_refused_revocation_the_expected_admission_is_still_in_place() {
       use org_node::error::OrgNodeError;
       use org_node::verify_org::Verified;
       use org_node::MemberId;
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut pending = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       let b = pending.member.device;
       let notice = sweep::notice_about(sweep::the_org(), MemberId::new([0x33; 32]), b);
       let refused = pending.member.svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &b, a.device, &notice);
       assert_eq!(refused.unwrap_err(), OrgNodeError::OrgNotHeld { org_id: sweep::the_org() });
       assert_eq!(sweep::data(&pending.member.svc, &b).expected_admissions.len(), 1, "the expectation stays");

       let verified = sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut pending.member, a.device, &pending.body, pending.chain);
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Adopted { epoch, .. } if epoch == pending.chain.epoch), "{verified:?}");
       let data = sweep::data(&pending.member.svc, &b);
       assert_eq!(data.record.as_ref().map(|r| r.org_id), Some(sweep::the_org()));
       assert!(data.expected_admissions.is_empty(), "settled by the adoption");
   }

   `org-node/tests/organisation_key.rs`: the ports of `a_created_organisation_publishes_a_fresh_key_no_genesis_key_equals` (`:110`) and `the_organisation_private_key_is_kept_only_in_the_encrypted_store` (`:165`), both cut by T5. LLR-3fwykc → LLR-qw8tyu, LLR-sj7cd5 → LLR-9qavm7 and LLR-qjz3q4 → LLR-qw8tyu.
   ```rust
   // Normal case (ported, design gap G2): the founding's public key is the
   // X25519 public key of the private key drawn for it, which the record
   // takes at the founding's adoption; no member or device key of the founding
   // record equals it, and it is neither the member seed nor the Device seed.
   // verifies: REQ-ech45n, LLR-9qavm7, LLR-qw8tyu
   #[test]
   fn a_created_organisation_publishes_a_fresh_key_no_genesis_key_equals() {
       let mut a = sweep::found();
       let chain = sweep::founding_state(&a);
       let device_seed = sweep::seed_bytes(a.secret.as_ref().unwrap());
       sweep::adopt(&mut a, chain);
       let record = sweep::record_of(&a);
       let published = *chain.org_pub_key.as_bytes();
       assert_eq!(*record.org_pub_key.as_bytes(), published, "the record holds the key the founding proposed");
       let key = record.org_private_key_for_test().clone();
       assert_eq!(key.x25519_keypair().public_bytes(), published, "the public key of the private key held");
       for m in &record.trie_members {
           assert_ne!(&published, m.member_key.as_bytes(), "a Member-as-a-group key of the founding record");
           for d in &m.device_keys {
               assert_ne!(&published, d.as_bytes(), "a DevicePublicKey of the founding record");
           }
       }
       let persona = &sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).persona;
       assert_ne!(key.expose_secret(), persona.member_seed_for_test().expose_secret(), "the private key is the member seed");
       assert_ne!(key.expose_secret().as_slice(), device_seed.as_slice(), "the private key is the device seed");
   }

   // The Organisation private key (ported, design gap G2): in the provisional
   // founding and then in the record, it reaches the disk only inside the
   // sealed store, never in clear, and only the Persona's own Device secret
   // opens it.
   // verifies: REQ-ech45n, LLR-qw8tyu
   #[test]
   fn the_organisation_private_key_is_kept_only_in_the_encrypted_store() {
       use org_node::store::PersonaStore;
       use org_node::test_fixtures::device_secret;

       let mut a = sweep::found();
       let before_adoption = a.last.as_ref().unwrap().sealed.as_bytes().to_vec();
       let chain = sweep::founding_state(&a);
       sweep::adopt(&mut a, chain);
       let key = sweep::record_of(&a).org_private_key_for_test().clone();
       assert!(!sweep::contains(&before_adoption, key.expose_secret()), "the founding's key is in the file in clear");
       let write = a.last.as_ref().unwrap();
       assert!(!sweep::contains(write.sealed.as_bytes(), key.expose_secret()), "the record's key is in the file in clear");
       assert!(
           PersonaStore::unseal(&write.sealed, write.device_key, device_secret([0x99; 32])).is_err(),
           "only under the Persona's own device secret"
       );
       let reopened = a.reopened();
       let on_disk = sweep::data(&reopened, &a.device).record.as_ref().unwrap();
       assert_eq!(on_disk.org_private_key_for_test().clone(), key, "the sealed store holds the key");
   }
   ```
   `org-node/tests/service_stories.rs`: the port of `revocation_from_an_unknown_device_leaves_the_record_in_place` (`:307`). LLR-3q63zv → LLR-283x6f; LLR-tx8ruv → LLR-rhsfw9 (ledger 84a31b1a: `accept` only decides, `verify` signs); the out-of-force IDs leave the line.
   ```rust
   // Abnormal input (ported, design gap G2): a revocation notice naming this
   // node's own Device, well formed and for the right Organisation, whose
   // absence proof is genuine under a trie the chain never held, delivered
   // by a Device the record does not list, is refused with `SenderNotListed`
   // and nothing is kept (LLR-283x6f). From A's listed Device it is kept on
   // receipt, and verification, whose `revocation::accept` refuses its proof
   // under the chain's root that still lists B (LLR-rhsfw9), reports InStep,
   // asks for no secret and leaves the record as it was.
   // verifies: LLR-283x6f, LLR-rhsfw9
   #[test]
   fn revocation_from_an_unknown_device_leaves_the_record_in_place() {
       use org_node::error::OrgNodeError;
       use org_node::service::Checked;
       use org_node::verify_org::Verified;
       use org_node::store::PersonaStatus;
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut bob = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut bob.member, a.device, &bob.body, bob.chain);
       let mut b = bob.member;
       let notice = sweep::notice_about(sweep::the_org(), sweep::member_id_of(&b), b.device);
       let held = sweep::record_of(&b).clone();
       let before = sweep::bytes_of(&b.svc, &b.device);

       let refused = b.svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &b.device, sweep::relay_device(), &notice);
       assert_eq!(refused.unwrap_err(), OrgNodeError::SenderNotListed { org_id: sweep::the_org() });
       assert_eq!(sweep::bytes_of(&b.svc, &b.device), before, "nothing kept from an unlisted Device");

       let checked = sweep::receive(&mut b, a.device, &notice);
       assert!(matches!(checked, Checked::RevocationNoticeKept), "{checked:?}");
       let (verified, change) = b.svc.verify(&mut OsRng, &b.device, Some(bob.chain), sweep::at(), sweep::no_secrets).unwrap();
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::InStep), "{verified:?}");
       assert!(change.is_none(), "InStep writes nothing");
       let after = sweep::record_of(&b);
       assert_eq!((after.epoch, after.root_hash, after.trie_members.len()), (held.epoch, held.root_hash, held.trie_members.len()));
       assert_eq!(sweep::data(&b.svc, &b.device).persona.status, PersonaStatus::Active);
   }
   ```
   `org-node/tests/service_lifecycle.rs`: the port of `a_new_persona_is_proposed_with_an_id_derived_from_its_member_key` (`:65`). LLR-tev8h8 → LLR-d4gpxm, LLR-6acxu9; LLR-v82xds → LLR-t2adzg (ledger 84a31b1a), which states both halves: the founding's Persona unbound, the provisional Member's bound to its Invite's Organisation. Then the new test of LLR-t2adzg (fix item 20), `only_the_first_adoption_sets_a_personas_member_id`.
   ```rust
   // A new Persona (ported, design gap G2): `propose_founding` and
   // `propose_member` each draw a member seed and a Device seed apart, keep
   // the member seed and the Device public key and no Device seed, return the
   // Device secret by value, and record the Persona Proposed with no member
   // identifier (the founding's with no Organisation, the provisional
   // Member's bound to its Invite's), its identifier the first sixteen bytes
   // of its member key in lowercase hex; the store survives a reload from the
   // write it returned.
   // verifies: REQ-hzm4kt, LLR-d4gpxm, LLR-6acxu9, LLR-s7yu4k, LLR-t2adzg
   #[test]
   fn a_new_persona_is_proposed_with_an_id_derived_from_its_member_key() {
       use org_node::store::PersonaStatus;
       use org_node::OrgService;

       let hex16 = |bytes: [u8; 32]| bytes.iter().take(16).map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect::<String>();

       let mut svc = OrgService::new(vec![]).unwrap();
       let (device, secret, change) = svc.propose_founding(&mut rand::rngs::OsRng, "Alice", "Smith", "alice", "Acme".to_owned()).unwrap();
       let persona = &sweep::data(&svc, &device).persona;
       assert_eq!((persona.status, persona.org_id, persona.member_id), (PersonaStatus::Proposed, None, None), "LLR-t2adzg: a founding's Persona is unbound");
       assert_eq!(persona.persona_id.as_str(), hex16(persona.member_seed_for_test().x25519_keypair().public_bytes()));
       assert_eq!(persona.device_key, device, "the Device public key is kept");
       assert_eq!(secret.device_key(), device);
       assert_ne!(persona.member_seed_for_test().expose_secret().as_slice(), sweep::seed_bytes(&secret).as_slice(), "the two seeds are drawn apart");
       let mut founder = sweep::Side::new(svc, device, secret, change);
       let reloaded = founder.reopened();
       assert_eq!(sweep::data(&reloaded, &device).persona.handle.as_ref().map(|h| h.as_str()), Some("alice"));

       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let invite = sweep::invite(&mut a, "Bob");
       let mut bob = sweep::propose_member(&invite, "Bob", &["bob"]);
       let persona = &sweep::data(&bob.svc, &bob.device).persona;
       assert_eq!((persona.status, persona.member_id, persona.handle.is_none()), (PersonaStatus::Proposed, None, true));
       assert_eq!(persona.org_id, Some(invite.org_id), "LLR-t2adzg: a provisional Member's Persona is bound to its Invite's Organisation");
       assert_eq!(persona.persona_id.as_str(), hex16(persona.member_seed_for_test().x25519_keypair().public_bytes()));
       assert_ne!(persona.member_seed_for_test().expose_secret().as_slice(), sweep::seed_bytes(bob.secret.as_ref().unwrap()).as_slice());
       let reloaded = bob.reopened();
       assert_eq!(sweep::data(&reloaded, &bob.device).persona.persona_id.as_str(), hex16(sweep::data(&reloaded, &bob.device).persona.member_seed_for_test().x25519_keypair().public_bytes()));
   }
   // LLR-t2adzg (new 2026-10-22, supersedes LLR-v82xds; fix item 20): a
   // founding's Persona is recorded Proposed with no Organisation and no
   // member id; recording its proxy binds it and gives it no member id; a
   // provisional Member's Persona is recorded Proposed, bound to its Invite's
   // Organisation, with no member id; only the first adoption in each store
   // sets the member id, to the one the adopted record gives that Persona's
   // Device, and recording an admission, proposing and a later adoption
   // change it in no store.
   // verifies: LLR-t2adzg
   #[test]
   fn only_the_first_adoption_sets_a_personas_member_id() {
       use org_node::store::PersonaStatus;
       use org_node::OrgService;
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       // The founding: Proposed, unbound, no member id.
       let mut svc = OrgService::new(vec![]).unwrap();
       let (device, secret, change) = svc.propose_founding(&mut OsRng, "Ada", "Lovelace", "ada", "Acme".to_owned()).unwrap();
       let persona = &sweep::data(&svc, &device).persona;
       assert_eq!((persona.status, persona.org_id, persona.member_id), (PersonaStatus::Proposed, None, None));
       let mut a = sweep::Side::new(svc, device, secret, change);

       // Its proxy recorded: bound to the Organisation, still no member id.
       let change = a.svc.record_founding_proxy(&mut OsRng, &a.device, sweep::the_org(), sweep::the_proxy()).unwrap();
       a.keep(change);
       let persona = &sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).persona;
       assert_eq!((persona.status, persona.org_id, persona.member_id), (PersonaStatus::Proposed, Some(sweep::the_org()), None));

       // The founding's adoption, the first in A's store, sets the founder's member id.
       let founder_id = sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).founding.as_ref().unwrap().members[0].id;
       let chain = sweep::founding_state(&a);
       sweep::adopt(&mut a, chain);
       assert_eq!(sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).persona.member_id, Some(founder_id), "the first adoption sets it");

       // A provisional Member: Proposed, bound to the Invite's Organisation, no member id.
       let invite = sweep::invite(&mut a, "Bob");
       let mut bob = sweep::propose_member(&invite, "Bob", &["bob"]);
       let persona = &sweep::data(&bob.svc, &bob.device).persona;
       assert_eq!((persona.status, persona.org_id, persona.member_id), (PersonaStatus::Proposed, Some(invite.org_id), None));

       // Recording Bob's admission and proposing the next epoch set no member id.
       sweep::request_admission(&mut a, &bob);
       let change = a.svc.record_admission(&mut OsRng, &a.device, invite.invite_id, None).unwrap();
       a.keep(change);
       let next = sweep::propose_next(&mut a);
       assert_eq!(sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).persona.member_id, Some(founder_id), "recording and proposing change none");
       assert_eq!(sweep::data(&bob.svc, &bob.device).persona.member_id, None, "no adoption in Bob's store yet");

       // A's second adoption keeps A's member id; Bob's first adoption sets his.
       sweep::adopt(&mut a, next);
       assert_eq!(sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).persona.member_id, Some(founder_id), "a later adoption leaves it");
       let body = sweep::message_for(&a, &bob.device);
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut bob, a.device, &body, next);
       let admitted = sweep::record_of(&bob)
           .trie_members
           .iter()
           .find(|m| m.device_keys.contains(&bob.device))
           .expect("Bob's Device is listed")
           .id;
       assert_eq!(sweep::data(&bob.svc, &bob.device).persona.member_id, Some(admitted), "Bob's first adoption sets his");
   }

   `org-node/tests/verification.rs` (written by T14–T24): the three re-creations of `commit_paths.rs`'s `commit_genesis_creates_the_record_once_the_chain_carries_the_root`, `commit_update_commits_a_provisional_update_the_chain_carries` and `the_revoking_record_takes_the_removal_only_through_commit_update`. Each keeps its in-force IDs and re-points LLR-3fwykc → LLR-qw8tyu, LLR-w3fhhg → LLR-exaa9u, LLR-q3aj8z → LLR-gcm7bq, LLR-dzte8x/LLR-3v5nu9/LLR-drgdy8 → LLR-x5asbx, LLR-4tcxsu → LLR-g2jeqd and LLR-qg9utu → LLR-34c5y3.
   ```rust
   // A founding is adopted once the chain carries its root (ported, design
   // gap G2): a chain state at epoch 1 with another root is no match, so the
   // founding store reports Behind and writes nothing; the founding's own
   // state is adopted, synchronously and with no send, as the record with the
   // chain's root and key, epoch and mark 1, the founding's private key and
   // its proxy; the Persona is Active with the founder's MemberId; the
   // founding is consumed; and the sealed store holds all of it.
   // verifies: REQ-tqap3r, LLR-gcm7bq, LLR-exaa9u, LLR-qw8tyu, LLR-x5asbx, LLR-g2jeqd
   #[test]
   fn a_founding_is_adopted_once_the_chain_carries_its_root() {
       use org_node::verify_org::Verified;
       use org_node::store::PersonaStatus;
       use org_node::{OrgState, RootHash, SequenceNumber};
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       let mut a = sweep::found();
       let chain = sweep::founding_state(&a);
       let elsewhere = OrgState { root_hash: RootHash::new([0x01; 32]), ..chain };
       let (verified, change) = a.svc.verify(&mut OsRng, &a.device, Some(elsewhere), sweep::at(), sweep::no_secrets).unwrap();
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Behind { .. }), "{verified:?}");
       assert!(change.is_none(), "Behind writes nothing");
       assert!(sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).founding.is_some(), "the founding is kept");

       let founder_id = sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).founding.as_ref().unwrap().members[0].id;
       let verified = sweep::adopt(&mut a, chain);
       assert!(matches!(&verified, Verified::Adopted { epoch, discarded, own: true } if *epoch == chain.epoch && discarded.is_empty()), "{verified:?}");
       let record = sweep::record_of(&a);
       assert_eq!(
           (record.org_id, record.root_hash, record.org_pub_key, record.epoch, record.last_seq),
           (sweep::the_org(), chain.root_hash, chain.org_pub_key, chain.epoch, SequenceNumber::new(1))
       );
       assert_eq!(record.org_private_key_for_test().x25519_keypair().org_public_key().unwrap(), chain.org_pub_key);
       assert_eq!(record.proxy_account, Some(sweep::the_proxy()));
       let persona = &sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).persona;
       assert_eq!((persona.status, persona.org_id, persona.member_id), (PersonaStatus::Active, Some(sweep::the_org()), Some(founder_id)));
       assert!(sweep::data(&a.svc, &a.device).founding.is_none(), "the founding is consumed");
       let reopened = a.reopened();
       let on_disk = sweep::data(&reopened, &a.device);
       assert_eq!(on_disk.record.as_ref().map(|r| (r.root_hash, r.proxy_account)), Some((chain.root_hash, Some(sweep::the_proxy()))));
       assert!(on_disk.founding.is_none());
   }

   // An own provisional organisation the chain carries is adopted as a
   // received one would be (ported, design gap G2): the record, epoch, mark
   // and members are written together with the provisional organisation's key
   // pair, keeping no earlier key, and the sealed store returned with the
   // outcome holds them; the adoption sends nothing.
   // verifies: REQ-tqap3r, REQ-jy6ybw, LLR-cja9zv, LLR-g2jeqd
   #[test]
   fn an_own_provisional_organisation_the_chain_carries_is_adopted() {
       use org_node::verify_org::Verified;
       use org_node::SequenceNumber;

       let (mut a, founding) = sweep::founded();
       let key_before = sweep::record_of(&a).org_private_key_for_test().clone();
       let pending = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       let record = sweep::record_of(&a);
       assert_eq!(
           (record.root_hash, record.epoch, record.last_seq, record.trie_members.len()),
           (pending.chain.root_hash, pending.chain.epoch, SequenceNumber::new(pending.chain.epoch.get()), 2)
       );
       assert_ne!(pending.chain.epoch, founding.epoch);
       assert_eq!(record.org_pub_key, pending.chain.org_pub_key, "the provisional organisation's public key");
       let key = record.org_private_key_for_test().clone();
       assert_eq!(key.x25519_keypair().org_public_key().unwrap(), pending.chain.org_pub_key, "and its private half");
       assert_ne!(key, key_before, "no earlier key is kept");
       assert!(matches!(sweep::adopt(&mut a, pending.chain), Verified::InStep), "adopted already: the same state is in step");
       let reopened = a.reopened();
       let on_disk = sweep::data(&reopened, &a.device).record.as_ref().unwrap();
       assert_eq!((on_disk.root_hash, on_disk.epoch, on_disk.last_seq), (record_root(&pending), pending.chain.epoch, SequenceNumber::new(pending.chain.epoch.get())));
       assert_eq!(on_disk.org_private_key_for_test().clone(), key);
   }

   fn record_root(pending: &sweep::Admission) -> org_node::RootHash {
       pending.chain.root_hash
   }

   // The record takes a recorded revocation only through adoption (ported,
   // design gap G2): recording it and proposing the next epoch leave the
   // record listing B; the adoption removes B; the messages built afterwards
   // and never delivered undo nothing; the proxy account is neither read nor
   // changed by any of it.
   // LLR-t4znbk -> LLR-g2jeqd (ledger 84a31b1a).
   // verifies: REQ-tqap3r, LLR-34c5y3, LLR-x5asbx, LLR-g2jeqd
   #[test]
   fn the_record_takes_a_recorded_revocation_only_through_adoption() {
       use rand::rngs::OsRng;

       let (mut a, _) = sweep::founded();
       let mut bob = sweep::admission(&mut a, "Bob", "bob");
       sweep::receive_and_adopt(&mut bob.member, a.device, &bob.body, bob.chain);
       let b_id = sweep::member_id_of(&bob.member);
       let proxy_before = a.svc.proxy_account(sweep::the_org()).unwrap();

       let change = a.svc.record_revocation(&mut OsRng, &a.device, b_id).unwrap();
       a.keep(change);
       assert!(sweep::record_of(&a).trie_members.iter().any(|m| m.id == b_id), "recording changes no record");
       let next = sweep::propose_next(&mut a);
       assert!(sweep::record_of(&a).trie_members.iter().any(|m| m.id == b_id), "proposing changes no record");
       sweep::adopt(&mut a, next);
       assert!(!sweep::record_of(&a).trie_members.iter().any(|m| m.id == b_id), "the adoption removes B");
       let messages = a.svc.messages_for_current_epoch(&a.device).unwrap();
       assert!(messages.iter().any(|m| m.recipient == bob.member.device), "B's revocation is built");
       drop(messages); // never delivered
       assert!(!sweep::record_of(&a).trie_members.iter().any(|m| m.id == b_id), "an undelivered message undoes nothing");
       assert_eq!(a.svc.proxy_account(sweep::the_org()).unwrap(), proxy_before);
   }
   ```

4. **Write the minimal implementation.** Write `org-node/tests/support/sweep.rs` in full, as below. These are the shared scenario steps. Each step is one or a few public `OrgService` calls, and each keeps the last `StoreWrite` its Persona's operations returned, as org-io would write it. T60 makes no ledger edit (step 1).
   ```rust
   //! The scenario steps of plan T60 (design gap G2) over the operations P2
   //! built: each is one or a few `OrgService` calls, values in and values
   //! out, with the chain stood in for by the `OrgState` a step hands
   //! `verify`. A `Side` is one Persona's service and Device key, its Device
   //! secret, and the last sealed write its operations returned (what org-io
   //! writes to that Persona's file).
   #![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, dead_code)]

   use org_node::invitation::Invite;
   use org_node::keys::X25519Keypair;
   use org_node::revocation::RevocationNotice;
   use org_node::service::{Checked, StoreChange};
   use org_node::verify_org::{VerificationTime, Verified};
   use org_node::store::{OrgRecord, PersonaStore, StoreData};
   use org_node::test_fixtures::genesis_trie;
   use org_node::wire::{encode_message, WireMessage};
   use org_node::{ChainAccount, DevicePublicKey, DeviceSecret, Epoch, MemberId, OrgId, OrgService, OrgState, SigningKeypair, StoreWrite};
   use rand::rngs::OsRng;

   /// The Organisation every founding of these tests is written as.
   pub fn the_org() -> OrgId {
       OrgId::new([0x0a; 20])
   }

   /// The pure proxy recorded for every founding of these tests.
   pub fn the_proxy() -> ChainAccount {
       ChainAccount::new([0x5a; 32])
   }

   /// The time every verification of these tests is made at.
   pub fn at() -> VerificationTime {
       VerificationTime(1_790_000_000)
   }

   /// The Device-secret source for a verification that removes nobody: it
   /// must never be called (LLR-qvp7mq, LLR-5tvn7g).
   pub fn no_secrets(_: &[DevicePublicKey]) -> Vec<DeviceSecret> {
       panic!("no Device secret is asked for by a verification that removes nobody")
   }

   /// The seed bytes of `secret`, as org-io's keychain holds them.
   pub fn seed_bytes(secret: &DeviceSecret) -> Vec<u8> {
       let mut bytes = vec![];
       secret
           .lend_to_keychain(|seed| {
               bytes.extend_from_slice(seed);
               Ok::<(), std::convert::Infallible>(())
           })
           .unwrap();
       bytes
   }

   /// Whether `needle` occurs in `haystack`.
   pub fn contains(haystack: &[u8], needle: &[u8]) -> bool {
       haystack.windows(needle.len()).any(|window| window == needle)
   }

   /// A Device key no store lists.
   pub fn relay_device() -> DevicePublicKey {
       SigningKeypair::generate(&mut OsRng).device_key().unwrap()
   }

   /// The store `device` names in `svc`.
   pub fn data<'s>(svc: &'s OrgService, device: &DevicePublicKey) -> &'s StoreData {
       svc.store_data(device).expect("the store is held")
   }

   /// The encoded `StoreData` of the store `device` names: equal bytes, equal
   /// store (the behind marker is not encoded).
   pub fn bytes_of(svc: &OrgService, device: &DevicePublicKey) -> Vec<u8> {
       postcard::to_allocvec(data(svc, device)).unwrap()
   }

   /// One Persona: its service, Device key, Device secret and last sealed write.
   pub struct Side {
       pub svc: OrgService,
       pub device: DevicePublicKey,
       pub secret: Option<DeviceSecret>,
       pub last: Option<StoreWrite>,
   }

   impl Side {
       pub fn new(svc: OrgService, device: DevicePublicKey, secret: DeviceSecret, change: StoreChange) -> Self {
           let mut side = Self { svc, device, secret: Some(secret), last: None };
           side.keep(change);
           side
       }

       /// Keeps the write a store change carries, as org-io writes it.
       pub fn keep(&mut self, change: StoreChange) {
           let StoreChange::Sealed(write) = change;
           assert_eq!(write.device_key, self.device, "a change for this Persona's store");
           self.last = Some(write);
       }

       /// The last sealed write, opened again under a copy of the Device
       /// secret.
       pub fn clone_store(&self) -> PersonaStore {
           let write = self.last.as_ref().expect("a sealed write");
           let bytes = seed_bytes(self.secret.as_ref().expect("the Device secret"));
           let secret = DeviceSecret::from_keychain_bytes(zeroize::Zeroizing::new(bytes)).unwrap();
           PersonaStore::unseal(&write.sealed, write.device_key, secret).expect("the sealed store opens")
       }

       /// The last sealed write, opened again: the store as it reached disk.
       pub fn reopened_store(&mut self) -> PersonaStore {
           self.clone_store()
       }

       /// A service over the store as it reached disk.
       pub fn reopened(&mut self) -> OrgService {
           OrgService::new(vec![self.reopened_store()]).expect("one store")
       }
   }

   /// The current record of `side`'s store.
   pub fn record_of(side: &Side) -> &OrgRecord {
       data(&side.svc, &side.device).record.as_ref().expect("a current record")
   }

   /// The MemberId an adoption gave `side`'s Persona.
   pub fn member_id_of(side: &Side) -> MemberId {
       data(&side.svc, &side.device).persona.member_id.expect("an adopted Persona")
   }

   /// A founder whose founding is proposed and whose proxy is recorded for
   /// `org_id`, not yet adopted.
   pub fn found_at(org_id: OrgId) -> Side {
       let mut svc = OrgService::new(vec![]).unwrap();
       let (device, secret, change) = svc.propose_founding(&mut OsRng, "Ada", "Lovelace", "ada", "Acme".to_owned()).unwrap();
       let mut side = Side::new(svc, device, secret, change);
       let change = side.svc.record_founding_proxy(&mut OsRng, &device, org_id, the_proxy()).unwrap();
       side.keep(change);
       side
   }

   pub fn found() -> Side {
       found_at(the_org())
   }

   /// The chain state a written founding leaves: its root and key at epoch 1.
   pub fn founding_state(side: &Side) -> OrgState {
       let founding = data(&side.svc, &side.device).founding.as_ref().expect("a provisional founding");
       OrgState { root_hash: founding.root, org_pub_key: founding.org_pub_key, epoch: Epoch::new(1) }
   }

   /// Verifies `side` against `chain`, keeping any write.
   pub fn adopt(side: &mut Side, chain: OrgState) -> Verified {
       let (verified, change) = side.svc.verify(&mut OsRng, &side.device, Some(chain), at(), no_secrets).unwrap();
       if let Some(change) = change {
           side.keep(change);
       }
       verified
   }

   /// A founder at `org_id` whose founding is adopted, and the chain state.
   pub fn founded_at(org_id: OrgId) -> (Side, OrgState) {
       let mut side = found_at(org_id);
       let chain = founding_state(&side);
       let verified = adopt(&mut side, chain);
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Adopted { own: true, .. }), "{verified:?}");
       (side, chain)
   }

   pub fn founded() -> (Side, OrgState) {
       founded_at(the_org())
   }

   /// Proposes the next epoch from the held provisional changes and returns
   /// the chain state a write of it leaves.
   pub fn propose_next(side: &mut Side) -> OrgState {
       let change = side.svc.propose_updated_organisation(&mut OsRng, &side.device).unwrap();
       side.keep(change);
       let own = data(&side.svc, &side.device).provisional_organisations.last().expect("the own provisional organisation");
       OrgState { root_hash: own.root, org_pub_key: own.org_pub_key, epoch: own.epoch }
   }

   /// The MemberId the provisional organisation for `chain` gives `device`.
   pub fn proposed_id_of(side: &Side, chain: OrgState, device: &DevicePublicKey) -> MemberId {
       data(&side.svc, &side.device)
           .provisional_organisations
           .iter()
           .find(|p| p.root == chain.root_hash && p.org_pub_key == chain.org_pub_key)
           .expect("the provisional organisation for that state")
           .members
           .iter()
           .find(|m| m.device_keys.contains(device))
           .expect("the Device is a member of it")
           .id
   }

   /// An Invite issued by `inviter` for `invitee`, with no addresses.
   pub fn invite(inviter: &mut Side, invitee: &str) -> Invite {
       let (invite, change) = inviter.svc.build_invite(&mut OsRng, &inviter.device, invitee.to_owned(), vec![]).unwrap();
       inviter.keep(change);
       invite
   }

   /// A provisional Member of `invite`'s Organisation, in a service of its own.
   pub fn propose_member(invite: &Invite, name: &str, handles: &[&str]) -> Side {
       let mut svc = OrgService::new(vec![]).unwrap();
       let (device, secret, change) = svc.propose_member(&mut OsRng, invite, name, "Member", handles).unwrap();
       Side::new(svc, device, secret, change)
   }

   /// `member`'s admission request, kept by `inviter`.
   pub fn request_admission(inviter: &mut Side, member: &Side) {
       let request = member.svc.build_admission_request(&member.device, vec![]).unwrap();
       assert_eq!(request.recipient, inviter.device, "the request goes to the Invite's issuer");
       let (checked, change) = inviter.svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &inviter.device, member.device, &request.body).unwrap();
       assert!(matches!(checked, Checked::AdmissionRequest { .. }), "{checked:?}");
       inviter.keep(change.expect("the kept request is sealed"));
   }

   /// Receives `body` from `from`, keeping any write.
   pub fn receive(side: &mut Side, from: DevicePublicKey, body: &[u8]) -> Checked {
       let (checked, change) = side.svc.check_received(&mut OsRng, &side.device, from, body).unwrap();
       if let Some(change) = change {
           side.keep(change);
       }
       checked
   }

   /// Receives an Organisation-information `body` and verifies against `chain`.
   pub fn receive_and_adopt(side: &mut Side, from: DevicePublicKey, body: &[u8], chain: OrgState) -> Verified {
       let checked = receive(side, from, body);
       assert!(matches!(checked, Checked::ProvisionalOrganisationKept { .. }), "{checked:?}");
       let verified = adopt(side, chain);
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Adopted { .. }), "{verified:?}");
       verified
   }

   /// The body of `inviter`'s current epoch for `recipient`.
   pub fn message_for(inviter: &Side, recipient: &DevicePublicKey) -> Vec<u8> {
       inviter
           .svc
           .messages_for_current_epoch(&inviter.device)
           .unwrap()
           .into_iter()
           .find(|m| m.recipient == *recipient)
           .expect("a message for that Device")
           .body
   }

   /// An admission adopted by its inviter and not yet received by the new
   /// Member: the Member's side, the chain state, and the body it is sent.
   pub struct Admission {
       pub member: Side,
       pub chain: OrgState,
       pub body: Vec<u8>,
   }

   /// `inviter` invites `name`, keeps the request, records the admission,
   /// proposes and adopts the next epoch.
   pub fn admission(inviter: &mut Side, name: &str, handle: &str) -> Admission {
       let invite = invite(inviter, name);
       let member = propose_member(&invite, name, &[handle]);
       request_admission(inviter, &member);
       let change = inviter.svc.record_admission(&mut OsRng, &inviter.device, invite.invite_id, None).unwrap();
       inviter.keep(change);
       let chain = propose_next(inviter);
       let verified = adopt(inviter, chain);
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Adopted { own: true, .. }), "{verified:?}");
       let body = message_for(inviter, &member.device);
       Admission { member, chain, body }
   }

   /// `inviter` records the revocation of `member_id`, proposes and adopts.
   pub fn revocation(inviter: &mut Side, member_id: MemberId) -> OrgState {
       let change = inviter.svc.record_revocation(&mut OsRng, &inviter.device, member_id).unwrap();
       inviter.keep(change);
       let chain = propose_next(inviter);
       let verified = adopt(inviter, chain);
       assert!(matches!(verified, Verified::Adopted { own: true, .. }), "{verified:?}");
       chain
   }

   /// A well-formed revocation notice body about `org_id` naming `member_id`
   /// and `device`, its absence proof genuine under a trie no chain holds.
   pub fn notice_about(org_id: OrgId, member_id: MemberId, device: DevicePublicKey) -> Vec<u8> {
       let trie = genesis_trie(&X25519Keypair::generate(&mut OsRng), &SigningKeypair::generate(&mut OsRng));
       let proof = trie.prove_absent(&member_id, &device).unwrap();
       encode_message(&WireMessage::Revocation(RevocationNotice { org_id, member_id, device, proof })).unwrap()
   }
   ```
   `zeroize` is a normal dependency of org-node, so the tests can name it. If `cargo` reports otherwise, use `DeviceSecret::from_keychain_bytes` the way `service_lifecycle.rs`'s `secret_from` does today.

4. **Bring each README overview table and each item's `Code:` paths up to the in-force items.** Write two read-only scripts in your scratchpad (never in the repository) and run each with `python3 -I`, one call per unit (`org-node`, `org-io`, `app`, `on-chain-client`).

   `t61_readme.py` lists the in-force SDDs of a unit's ledgers that no README table row names, and the table IDs that are not in force:
   ```python
   import glob, re, sys
   root, unit = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   item = re.compile(r'^\*\*([A-Z]+-[a-z0-9]{6})\*\*')
   in_force = set()
   for path in sorted(glob.glob(f'{root}/{unit}/docs/architecture/*.md')):
       if path.endswith(('README.md', 'soup.md')):
           continue
       lines = open(path).read().split('\n')
       for i, line in enumerate(lines):
           match = item.match(line)
           if not match or not match.group(1).startswith('SDD-'):
               continue
           j = i + 1
           while j < len(lines) and not item.match(lines[j]) and not lines[j].startswith('#'):
               j += 1
           block = '\n'.join(lines[i:j])
           if not re.search(r'^(superseded-by|retired):', block, re.M):
               in_force.add(match.group(1))
   readme = open(f'{root}/{unit}/docs/architecture/README.md').read().split('\n')
   table = set(re.findall(r'SDD-[a-z0-9]{6}', '\n'.join(l for l in readme if l.startswith('|'))))
   print('in force, in no README table row:', sorted(in_force - table))
   print('in a README table row, not in force:', sorted(table - in_force))
   ```

           if not match:

           j = i + 1
           while j < len(lines) and not item.match(lines[j]) and not lines[j].startswith('#'):

           block = '\n'.join(lines[i:j])
           if re.search(r'^(superseded-by|retired):', block, re.M) or 'Code:' not in block:

The comment above the variable gains a line: `2026-10-22 (worktree-org-io-domain-api, task T61): the six targets T28 deleted leave, the eight T1 registered join, and keychain_contract (on the verify line, missing here before) joins, matching the verify line.` org-node and the app have no coverage target and none is added.

   Then measure with the floors at 0, overriding them on the command line, one command each:
   - `make coverage-org-io ORG_IO_LINES=0 ORG_IO_REGIONS=0`
   - `make coverage-branch-org-io ORG_IO_BRANCHES=0`
   - `make coverage-on-chain-client ON_CHAIN_CLIENT_LINES=0 ON_CHAIN_CLIENT_REGIONS=0`
   - `make coverage-branch-on-chain-client ON_CHAIN_CLIENT_BRANCHES=0`

   **How to read the figures.** The two statement figures are on the `TOTAL` row of `cargo llvm-cov`'s summary: the regions *Cover* column (the third) and the lines *Cover* column (after *Lines* and *Missed Lines*). The branch figure is the line `org-io: <covered> of <count> branches, <percent>% (floor 0%)` that `judge_branches` prints.

   **How to set the new floor (house rule: one point below the measurement, rounded down).** The new floor is the measured percentage minus one, rounded down to an integer. For example, 81.24% lines gives 80, and 79.94% regions gives 78. The floors ratchet:
   - If the result is above the current floor (`ORG_IO_LINES := 80`, `ORG_IO_REGIONS := 78`, `ORG_IO_BRANCHES := 82`, `ON_CHAIN_CLIENT_LINES := 46`, `ON_CHAIN_CLIENT_REGIONS := 47`, `ON_CHAIN_CLIENT_BRANCHES := 99`), raise the floor to it.
   - If the result is at or below the current floor but the measurement still meets the current floor, leave the floor as it is (a floor is never lowered).
   - If the measurement is below a current floor, the gate fails. Do not lower the floor. Stop, write the shortfall (the file-by-file figures from `cargo llvm-cov … --summary-only` without the floor override, i.e. its per-file table, read for the files this change wrote) into the plan's Progress section, and ask the owner, whose decision goes into the merge's verification record.

   Record each measurement as a dated row in the comment above its floor, in that comment's format (`measured 2026-10-22 … lines regions (n of N lines; m of M regions)`, and for branches `<covered> of <count> branches, <percent>%`), with the toolchain (`rustc --version`, `cargo llvm-cov --version`, `cargo +nightly-2026-10-03 --version` for the branch run) and one sentence naming the shell files left uncovered.

   Then run the four targets with their floors: `make coverage-org-io`, `make coverage-branch-org-io`, `make coverage-on-chain-client` and `make coverage-branch-on-chain-client`. Expected: each exits 0 and prints its figure at or above its floor.

6. **Run every gate.** As in T60 step 7 (on-chain-client, org-node, org-io, app, every line), then:
   - `.guardrails/scripts/check-units.sh`
   - for each of the four units, `GR_CONFIG=<unit>/.guardrails/config.yaml .guardrails/scripts/check-trace.sh`
   - for each of the four units, `GR_CONFIG=<unit>/.guardrails/config.yaml .guardrails/scripts/check-ids.sh`

   Expected:
   - every test line green, clippy clean, `npm` check and test green;
   - the coverage targets of step 5 green;
   - check-trace exit 0 with no OUT-OF-FORCE-VERIFIES and no MISSING-TEST for an item of this change, and only the UNRESOLVED-PR / UNMET-EXPECTATION advisories for untouched items;
   - check-ids exit 1 for each unit, printing only that unit's expected `DRAFT-FILE` lines (the DRAFT ledger files merge-change renames) and nothing else; any other line is a defect to fix here.

   Record the results, the new floors and the SOUP and README outcomes in the plan's Progress section.

7. **Commit.**

   `git add on-chain-client/docs/architecture/README.md org-node/docs/architecture/README.md org-io/docs/architecture/README.md app/docs/architecture/README.md org-io/docs/architecture/soup.md org-node/docs/architecture/2026-10-16-domain-api.md org-io/docs/architecture/2026-10-16-domain-api.md app/docs/architecture/2026-10-16-domain-api.md Makefile docs/plans/2026-10-21-org-io-domain-api.md`

   Add `on-chain-client/docs/architecture/2026-10-20-domain-api.md` only if step 4 edited it (PLAN DELTA above). Leave out any listed file the steps left unchanged; `git status --short` shows which.

   `git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -m "chore(sweep): SOUP and manifests agree, README tables and Code paths match the in-force items, coverage target lists and floors re-set"`

## 3. Design gaps

Found while outlining and in the detail pass; none is resolved by inventing behaviour. **Status at plan assembly (2026-10-22): G1–G5 and every DESIGN GAP the detail writers raised are resolved in the ledgers (commits `ddc965ec`, `84a31b1a`, `f127e2ec`) or by the dispatcher's fix list; the four items left open at assembly (O1–O4) are decided by the dispatcher (2026-10-22) and applied in ledger `9b037db` and this plan; O3's source of the webview's founder key, which could not be applied as first stated, is decided again by the dispatcher (2026-10-22) and applied in ledger `983f25c` and this plan (below). No design gap is open.** The G2 supersessions and ledger `84a31b1a` put 29 more annotations out of force (334 → 349 → 363; O4's supersessions in `9b037db` one more, 364); the coverage table and the counts in §1 and §2 are regenerated for them (§2, *Coverage*), with rows for the eight G2 successors and the three new LLRs of `84a31b1a`.

- **G1** — resolved (ledger `ddc965ec`); T45 implements LLR-gh4rw3; T1 has nothing to restore.

## 4. Prerequisites and environment notes

- Work in this change worktree or the task worktree `develop-change` gives you. Commits are unsigned in worktrees: `git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -m "…"`; never a `Co-Authored-By` line; one plain git command per shell call, no compound lines mentioning git.
- Never edit a file with `sed`, Rust test files above all; use the editor.
- Cargo: the root workspace (`-p org-node`, `-p org-io`) builds with the default home. Every `cargo` line with `--manifest-path on-chain-client/Cargo.toml` or `--manifest-path app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` runs with `CARGO_HOME=/tmp/cargo_home_fuzz` prefixed: their standalone lockfiles name crates the read-only `~/.cargo` lacks (`anyhow 1.0.102`, `quinn-udp 0.5.16`), and the default home fails with "failed to download … Operation not permitted". Any line that must fetch a crate not in a lockfile uses the same home (none expected: `rand_core` 0.6 with `getrandom`, `keyring` and `tokio` are already in org-io's lockfile).
- A fresh worktree has no `app/node_modules`: run `npm --prefix app ci` once before `npm --prefix app run check` / `npm --prefix app run test`.
- `org-io/tests/endpoints.rs`'s `a_seventeenth_connection_waits_for_a_slot_while_sixteen_stall` is timing-sensitive under load: in the baseline it failed once while parallel builds ran and passed alone. If it fails in a gate run, re-run it alone (`cargo test -p org-io --features test-support --test endpoints a_seventeenth_connection_waits_for_a_slot_while_sixteen_stall`) and report both runs; a failure alone is a real failure.
- The quint gate (org-node's verify lines) runs with `QUINT_HOME` set to a scratch directory; `~/.quint` is read-only by design.
- on-chain-client's chopsticks-dependent targets (`write_genesis_e2e`, `scenario_a_full`, `off_chain_genesis_ceremony`, …) are outside `verify_commands`; T2's `SubxtWriteOps` fetches meet a chain only there.
- Red first: write the test, run it, paste the failure, implement, paste the green run; a compile-time red counts when the API does not exist yet.
- Every test carries `// verifies: <IDs>` on the line directly above `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` (or the vitest `it(`), naming the LLR; tests open with `#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]`.
- Re-pinned golden bytes are derived by the format rule with a dated comment, never captured from the code (T26).
- The `gpg` signing check cannot be verified in the sandbox; the squash merge is signed by `merge-change` in the owner's terminal.
- Merge LOCAL master at the merge's first step (verify ancestry with `git merge-base`).

### Guideline reviews — round 1 (2026-10-25)

Seven read-only reviewers. There is one guidelines file per kind (the `.guardrails/templates/` defaults govern every path), and TEST and CODE were split by unit for depth. Findings above low are listed below; dispositions are added as each fix merges. Low findings are fixed where cheap, or else noted in the fix report.

**CODE, app + on-chain-client + Makefile** (5 medium, 4 low). C-A1: single-letter names (Names 1). C-A2: TypeScript DTO names differ from the Rust DTOs; `verifyOrganisations` vs `verify_organisation` (Names 4). C-A3: `parse_founder` repeats `parse_32_bytes` (Simplicity 4). C-A4: the JSON round trip in `verification_outcomes` adds untested `Unknown` and unparsable-id arms (Simplicity 1). C-A9: comments that narrate the change, with task numbers and dates, in code, Cargo.toml and the Makefile (Comments 2). T57's listing-label note: not present (own label at +page.svelte:119); a rejected subscription leaves it unshown (low C-A8).
**CODE, org-node** (9 medium, 9 low). C-N1, C-N2: change narration and task numbers in service.rs comments (Comments 2). C-N4: single-letter names (Names 1). C-N5: `filter_map(.. data().ok())` drops `OrganisationRemoved` with no reason given (Errors 2). C-N6: peer-input decode failures reported as `OrgNodeError::Chain` (Errors 1). C-N7: person_store repeats the store's AEAD constants and unseal sequence (Simplicity 4). C-N8: verify_org repeats `set_address` with retain+push, and the copies have drifted (Simplicity 4). C-N9: wire kind indices and the `kind > 5` literal repeated in service.rs (Simplicity 4). C-N14: "device key", "Device secret" and "person key" in prose and user text (Names 4).
**CODE, org-io** (9 medium, 7 low). C-O1: change narration and task numbers in comments and Cargo.toml (Comments 2). C-O2: dead `send_body_to_device` and test-only `send_body` behind `allow(dead_code)` (Simplicity 3). C-O3: a `kept_acknowledgements` error ends the delivery task silently (Errors 2). C-O4: `accepted()` drops org-node's refusal and the store-write failure (Errors 1/2). C-O5: a bind failure is reduced to "the direct bind failed" (Errors 1). C-O6: `list_removed` / `list_stores` errors become empty lists (Errors 2). C-O7: org-node query errors dropped across verify, send, lib, exchange, write and persona (Errors 2). C-O11: two `holder_of` functions with different rules (Names 4). C-O12: `remove_store` removes only `removed-` files (Names 3).
**TEST, app + on-chain-client** (1 high, 5 medium, 1 low). T-A1 (high): the founding test fakes org-io's "a Person is held already" text, with no contract test pinning it (Doubles 3). T-A2: `FakeOps` `free_balance` / `mapped_account` have no contract against `SubxtWriteOps` (Doubles 3). T-A3: webview tests regex-match component source instead of rendering (UI 1/3); a false green is possible on the admission gate. T-A4: T58's error-label test is annotated LLR-5mw2dj, which states no such label (Seams 1). T-A5: periodic, verification and receiver tests call helpers no LLR names (Seams 2). T-A6: periodic.rs asserts source text of owned calls (Doubles 1). T48's ~60 s ipc test: accepted, since no clause limits duration.
**TEST, org-node** (7 medium, 19 low). T-N1: `seal_removal_for_test` below the seam (Seams 1). T-N2: support fixtures hand-build states the operations no longer produce (no change set, no revoked entry) (Seams 1 / Owned services 2). T-N3: an LLR-f9x3vf test checks only through `store_data`. T-N4: sealed_store tests seal through `seal_for_test`. T-N5, T-N6: absences scans pin private call chains and `stores.retain(`. T-N7: no abnormal test for an undecodable Organisation answer snapshot (LLR-kd7u2r). T27 note (c): confirmed and recorded as a note (add `acknowledgement_accepted` to the nonce sweep).
**TEST, org-io** (7 medium, 19 low). T-O1: six endpoints tests cut "for T60" were never re-created (PR-8qsnhx, PR-47aycj, PR-tcd2ta regressions; LLR-d2pzzk, LLR-z35vbh) (Existing suites 1). T-O2: three normal-case tests cut from expectations_met.rs (REQ-x6kdse, qza96g, v6r2gd; RC-d8dbxs, RC-jgyd6m). T-O3: an REQ-2xgsbn test drives org-node directly. T-O4: store_files and rng_source tests call `store_for_test`. T-O5: a direct test of `next_round_after` with no LLR. T-O6: `FakeChain` `create_proxy` / `found_at` have no contract test; write.rs's step mapping and `h160_of` never run. T-O7: keychain.rs:235 was re-annotated to LLR-kna4zj, which does not state its rule. T44's guard: low T-O26 (untested false side; reachable through `drop_store`).
**ARCHITECTURE** (7 medium, 2 low). A1: org-io production reads `list_orgs()` (`&OrgRecord`) and `PersonStore::data()`, values that carry key fields, instead of key-free views (LLR-8ru6mv). A2: org-io's error enums carry `OrgNodeError`, and the app matches it exhaustively. A4: "Device key" in user-facing labels. A5: "not executed" is a glossary _Avoid_ synonym of Deprecated, used for a different outcome. A6: public terms missing from docs/CONTEXT.md (revocation notice, unknown write, removal acknowledgement, kept admission request). A7: the removed-Persona deletion rule is written three times inline in IO code. A8: SDD-83un8g states two responsibilities (Boundaries 3).

Intent:
- api.ts gains wrappers for `propose_updated_organisation` and `cancel_invite`, with the commands' exact arguments.

- **MR3-N1 — owner's ruling, revised 2026-10-30.** This replaces the earlier "accept only the issuer"; n10 made no edit under that ruling.
  - Organisation information is accepted from anyone. The tentative mechanism is reused: verification adopts one provisional organisation and the others are discarded.
  - The new rule: every verification, whether or not it adopts, compares each provisional organisation received from another Device, at epoch E, with the chain's epoch C, and discards it when:
    1. E < C;
    2. E > C + 1;
    3. E = C, and its root and key do not match;
    4. E = C + 1, and more than 5 minutes (300 s) have passed since the first verification that saw it at C+1 stamped it with that verification's `verified_at`.
  - The 5-minute limit covers new joiners and Members receiving updates.
  - Exempt, by the owner's ruling:
    - this node's own proposals (origin Own);
    - the Admin's batched provisional changes, which carry no members root, since the root is calculated only when the next epoch is proposed, shortly before it is written.
  - A Device whose information is discarded keeps waiting.
  - This is task n11, followed by round 4 (a reviewer for org-node).

- **MR3-N1, rule 4: the owner's clarification, 2026-10-30.** The 5-minute limit is not a passive expiry. Within 5 minutes the chain is read again, and that reading decides:
  - If the chain has reached E, the information is judged by the normal match: adopted if it matches, discarded if not.
  - If the chain is still at C, it is discarded.
- Within one verification, the freshly read chain is judged first (adopt, then rules 1–3). The 300 s limit then applies only to what is still at C+1.
- Mechanism, across three units:
  - org-node: a verification that leaves a received C+1 held reports the earliest re-check due time, the stamp plus 300 s. This is task n11, extended.
  - org-io: passes that time on in its verification outcome.
  - app: schedules a verification of that Organisation for the due time, beside its periodic runs.
  - The org-io and app parts are a follow-up task after n11, before round 4.

- **MR3-N1, rule 4: the owner's decision, 2026-10-30.** It replaces the 5-minute limit and the scheduled re-check.
  - The C+1 time limit is a parameter of org-node's `verify`, passed in by the caller.
  - The app passes twice its verification interval, so at least two chain reads fall inside the limit whatever the interval is: the default 600 s gives 1200 s.
  - A received provisional organisation still at C+1 is discarded by a verification more than that limit after its stamp.
- No re-check report is needed: the periodic verification makes the reads.
- Tasks:
  - n11 does org-node. It passes a temporary org-io constant, 1200 s, so org-io still compiles.
  - A follow-up task makes org-io take the limit from the app, and the app pass twice its interval.

- **n11 — MR3-N1, by the owner's final ruling (merged 2026-10-30):**
  - `OrgService::verify` takes `ahead_limit: AheadLimit` (seconds; `org_node::AheadLimit`).
  - After the chain state is read and before `judge`, the pure `verify_org::discard_unadoptable` applies four rules to received provisional organisations (origins `Received` and `Answer`), with E their epoch and C the chain's:
    - Rule 1: E < C is discarded.
    - Rule 2: E > C+1 is discarded.
    - Rule 3: E = C is discarded unless it matches the chain (the `matches_chain` rule of LLR-8528ud).
    - Rule 4: E = C+1 is stamped `first_ahead_at` by the first verification that sees it, and the stamp never moves. It is discarded once more than `ahead_limit` has passed since the stamp. Exactly at the limit it is kept.
  - Exempt: Own proposals, the provisional changes, and the provisional founding.
  - With no chain state, nothing is discarded or stamped.
  - InStep, Behind and Inconsistent now seal one store change when a rule changed the store. No sender restriction was added, and a Device whose information is discarded keeps waiting.
  - Store layout: `first_ahead_at: Option<VerificationTime>` is appended to `ProvisionalOrganisation`. GOLDEN_ACTIVE_STORE is re-derived by the format rule, with one `00` per provisional organisation, so it is now 2108 bytes.
